description: GradeThread is an AI-powered SaaS platform providing standardized condition grading for pre-owned clothing. Sellers submit structured photos of garments and receive a numerical condition grade (CG 1.0-10.0), a detailed condition report, and a shareable grade certificate. The platform addresses the trust gap in the $350B+ secondhand clothing market. Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend, self-hosted Supabase (api.gradethread.com) for auth/DB/storage, Deno/Hono edge functions for backend API, Claude Vision AI for grading, Stripe for payments, Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Brand colors: Navy #0F3460, Red #E94560, Night #1A1A2E, Soft Gray #F5F5F5. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (New York style). The platform includes full inventory management with financial tracking from acquisition through sale and shipment, detailed financial reporting and analytics, and a comprehensive admin panel for user management, traffic monitoring, and AI model self-refinement.

userStories.title: Category rubric activation was never filed — 00231 shipped grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores to prod and nothing ever writes them
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the non-clothing grading scaffolding either finished or removed, because right now it is neither. Migration 00231 added grade_reports.factor_scores (jsonb) and rubric_key (text) to production, and the grading pipeline writes only the five TYPED clothing columns (fabric_condition_score … odor_cleanliness_score) — verified: the grade_reports insert in grading-pipeline.ts reads compositeResult.factor_scores.* into those five columns and never sets factor_scores or rubric_key. So both columns are permanently NULL on every row in prod. The edge module services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts is imported by nothing. Its client counterpart src/lib/rubrics.ts IS live — certificate.tsx:39 imports rubricForKey — so the certificate page is ready to render a rubric that the server will never populate. The only record of intent is commit bbd94005 'feat(grading): category rubric foundation (non-clothing scaffolding)', which says the work is 'NOT yet wired into the pipeline' and that the activation follow-up 'is documented in rubric.ts'. That follow-up was never filed as a story, so it has been invisible to the backlog ever since.
acceptanceCriteria: DECIDE FIRST: activate or remove. Non-clothing grading (sports cards etc.) is a product question, not a cleanup — do not default to whichever is less work

If ACTIVATING: the pipeline writes rubric_key + factor_scores for non-clothing categories; the five typed clothing columns keep their current meaning for clothing; the public cert endpoint's CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS allowlist is extended deliberately (00231's own comment defers that exposure to 'the activation phase')

If REMOVING: rubric.ts is deleted, src/lib/rubrics.ts and its certificate.tsx usage are resolved, and a migration drops the two dead columns — do NOT leave them NULL-forever with no owner, which is the state this story exists to end

Either way a drift guard: services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts and src/lib/rubrics.ts are declared to stay in sync and NOTHING pins them today. If both survive, add a shared behavioural fixture asserted by both suites (the same remedy US-1995 asks for on title-sync)
The decision is written into the story notes so the next reader does not have to re-derive it from a commit message
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Cleanup] Found 2026-07-18 by scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs — rubric.ts was one of 10 whole modules nothing imports. ⚠ CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER CLAIM in this session's audit triage (US-1996 notes): the triage said 'exhaustive queries return no story mentioning rubric'. That is wrong — NINE stories mention it (US-1030, US-1031, US-1532, US-1534, US-1682, US-1948, US-1951 archived, plus US-1995/1996). I read each: they all use 'rubric' in the generic grading-criteria sense (wrinkle anchors, fabric-aware criteria, pSEO guides, homepage copy). None owns the CATEGORY-rubric activation this story covers. The conclusion stood; the stated evidence did not, which is why it is restated correctly here. P3 rather than P1 because there is no user-visible breakage: clothing grading is unaffected and the certificate simply never renders a rubric block. The cost is a permanently-NULL pair of prod columns, a dead edge module, and a live client module waiting on data that never arrives. | 2026-07-23 DECISION: ACTIVATE (owner, via AskUserQuestion) — non-clothing grading (sports cards / watches / shoes) is on the roadmap, so the scaffolding is kept and built out, not removed. Activation is a MULTI-PHASE program, not a single commit; this session landed the two pieces that are safe and completable in a sandbox and scoped the rest with a plan. REFRAME (important for the next reader): the columns are 'permanently NULL' NOT because clothing forgot to write them but BY DESIGN — clothing renders from the 5 typed columns; factor_scores/rubric_key exist to hold NON-CLOTHING scores, which don't exist until the grading pipeline actually grades non-clothing. Backfilling clothing INTO factor_scores would be redundant AND stale-prone (the human-review reseal + adjustment write paths at grading-pipeline.ts:570/813/965 update only the typed columns), so it was deliberately NOT done. DONE THIS SESSION: (AC4 drift guard) added src/test/fixtures/rubric-factors.json — the SHARED behavioural fixture (same remedy US-1995 used for title-sync) constraining key+label+weight; both suites assert against it — client src/lib/__tests__/rubrics.test.ts (10/10 GREEN in-sandbox) and edge services/edge-functions/src/tests/rubric-parity_test.ts (mirrors it; not deno-run here). Verified edge rubric.ts and client rubrics.ts already match exactly across all 4 rubrics, so the guard pins them without a reconciliation. (AC2 partial) extended CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS (content-public.ts) to expose factor_scores + rubric_key in the null-safe EXTRA set, so a non-clothing cert will serve its rubric once Phase 2 writes it; NULL clothing certs are unaffected (client already prefers them only when both present, else falls back to typed columns) and the 42703 genesis-fallback still protects clothing certs under 00231 drift. Verified web tsc -b + eslint clean; no test pins the CERT column string. REMAINING (Phase 2 — the actual non-clothing grading; CANNOT be done in this sandbox, needs a validatable env with deno + live traffic + real vision calls): (1) de-gate submissions.garment_type NOT NULL for non-clothing (rubric.ts checklist #1); (2) generalize the THREE lockstep rounding sites (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) from the hardcoded 5 clothing factors to variable rubric-driven factor sets, same commit; (3) build per-category composite prompts from rubric.factors/promptGuidance and route defects via rubric.defectRouting; (4) run those NEW prompts through the mandated prompt lifecycle — shadow-compare (grading-shadow.ts) -> golden-set eval gate (grading-eval.ts) -> canary — which REQUIRES a non-clothing golden set that does NOT yet exist (golden cases grow from real human-corrected grades, so Phase 2 needs a bootstrap: grade some non-clothing behind a flag, collect expert corrections, THEN gate); (5) persist rubric_key + factor_scores for non-clothing across ALL grade_reports write paths (insert + reseal + adjustment) to avoid the stale-JSONB bug above. KEPT passes:false: AC2 (non-clothing writes) + AC4-is-done-but-story-spans-more; the product feature is not live until Phase 2 ships through the eval gate. AC1/AC5 (decision documented) satisfied here. | 2026-08-08 AC4 now VERIFIED BY RUNNING, not by inspection: the previous session wrote the edge half of the drift guard but recorded it as 'mirrors it; not deno-run here'. Ran it — services/edge-functions/src/tests/rubric-parity_test.ts: 53 passed, 0 failed. So both halves of the shared fixture (client 10/10, edge 53/53) are green against the same src/test/fixtures/rubric-factors.json, and AC4 is closed on evidence. Story stays passes:false on AC2 (Phase 2 non-clothing writes) only.

userStories.notes: [P2][EXTENSION][NEW][GROWTH] Privacy policy page (Model A static route). Attribution reuses affiliate.ts click->conversion. Telemetry opt-in only (GDPR/CCPA posture, ties to legal geo-consent epic). [OPERATOR-GATED 2026-07-09] Core deliverable (AC1: publish to Chrome Web Store + Firefox AMO with screenshots/listing copy) is NOT automatable from this host — needs store developer accounts + a running browser to capture screenshots. AC3 attribution: the referral system (src/lib/affiliate.ts) attributes via a per-SELLER ?ref=<code>; a buyer-side extension has no seller code, so extension->signup is channel-level (utm_source=extension), not per-referrer. Deferred until an operator runs the store submission; codeable residue to pair with that: extension privacy-policy static page, opt-in telemetry toggle + endpoint, store-listing copy doc. Not marking passes; mirrors the US-1582 [OPERATOR] split. Extension CODE is done via US-1755/US-1756. | 2026-07-18 AC1 PRIVACY-POLICY HALF DONE. Found a genuine store-submission blocker: /privacy is live and returns 200, but it did NOT mention the extension anywhere — while extension-unified/SUBMISSION.md instructs the operator to submit that exact URL to the Chrome Web Store and Firefox AMO, both of which require the submitted policy to disclose the extension’s data use. A reviewer following our own submission doc would have landed on a policy silent about the product being reviewed. Added section 6, The GradeThread browser extension, covering: what a condition read sends (public photo URLs + title/brand/price on user action, reading the page you are already on, never browsing on your behalf); that diagnostics are OFF BY DEFAULT and carry no listing, page address, account or install identifier (the selector-health telemetry I added this session under US-1880 AC3 — the policy now matches the code); that seller cross-posting runs in the user’s own tab and marketplace passwords/cookies are never sent; and the gradethread.com message relay. Every claim is checked against the shipped code rather than the marketing copy. Renumbered sections 7-14 and fixed the one Section-N cross-reference. New privacy-extension.test.tsx (6 cases) pins the disclosures so they cannot silently vanish, INCLUDING a sequential-numbering assertion and a cross-reference integrity check — I got the numbering wrong by hand while inserting the section, so the test encodes the mistake I actually made. Verified: tsc clean, lint exit 0, full web suite green. REMAINING on this story is operator-gated exactly as the notes say: store submission needs developer accounts + a browser for screenshots (AC1), AC2 usage telemetry (reads/click-throughs) is distinct from the selector-failure telemetry already shipped though it can reuse the same consent toggle, and AC3 attribution is channel-level utm_source=extension. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) SECOND, WORSE GAP OF THE SAME CLASS — the AUP. extension-unified/popup.js:84 points the consent clickwrap’s "Read the terms" link at /acceptable-use, next to a checkbox reading "I understand the Lister fills forms in MY browser session and that I am responsible for each marketplace’s Terms of Service." That page is live (200) and mentioned "extension" 0 times, "cross-post" 0, "cross-list" 0, "Lister" 0 — a consent gate whose linked terms never described the thing being consented to. Worse than the privacy gap because this one IS the legal basis for the seller automation (the versioned, revocable clickwrap US-1885 AC3 built). Added section 6, The browser extension and assisted cross-posting: the automation runs in the user’s own logged-in session and we never receive marketplace passwords or cookies (so responsibility sits with them); some marketplaces restrict or prohibit assisted listing and their rules take precedence; review before publishing; no evading listing caps, rate limits, suspensions or bans; no operating others’ accounts. Renumbered 7-9 and cross-linked to Privacy section 6. New acceptable-use-extension.test.tsx (6 cases) pins the disclosures + sequential numbering, and — the important one — READS extension-unified/popup.js to assert the termsLink still points at /acceptable-use, so repointing the popup fails the build instead of silently orphaning the clickwrap again. Verified: tsc clean, lint exit 0, full web suite green. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) Swept the rest of the extension’s outbound references — all clean. Every gradethread.com URL the extension sends a user to (/, /acceptable-use, /connect-extension, /pricing, /privacy, /extension/marketplace-selectors.json) returns 200 live, so the two gaps found today were about CONTENT, not dead links. Extended the same cross-artifact check to CLAUDE.md and added a durable guard: scripts/doc-refs.mjs + doc-refs.test.mjs, wired into verify:web beside prd-lint. CLAUDE.md currently cites 29 paths, 0 missing. Two of my own bugs are pinned as regression cases: (1) an alternation-ordering bug — ts listed before tsx matched the head of a .tsx path and reported four files missing that exist, the same mistake as COMPLETED? failing to match COMPLETION in the prd-lint guard; (2) contextual roots — CLAUDE.md legitimately writes lib/supabase.ts inside a paragraph about the edge service, so the checker resolves against known roots the way a reader does rather than flagging correct prose. Both matter for the same reason: a guard that reports correct writing gets switched off, which is how every unreliable check in this repo ended up ignored. | 2026-08-15 DEPENDENCY ADDED, US-2284: do not publish before the extension signing key is rotated. US-2284 found extension.pem in public git history; the key is still readable there today, and untracking it did nothing about that. Rotation is cheap RIGHT NOW and gets expensive the moment this story ships, because after publication that extension id is the installed identity and the leaked key packages a CRX carrying it. US-2284's own notes reached that conclusion on 2026-08-03 and recorded it as a sentence, which is not a thing any tool reads - hence dependsOn rather than another paragraph.

userStories.notes: Origin: 2026-07-09 extension deep-dive (3-agent audit of extension/, extension-condition/, and server integration). Related open stories NOT duplicated here: US-1833..1846 (buyer confidence suite + gating + legal), US-1757 (store distribution), US-1808 (extension-fed ingestion). Audit found the Lister privacy-by-manifest posture genuinely enforced today — the merge deliberately trades that isolation for one-install UX, so the privacy copy rewrite is mandatory, not cosmetic. | PARTIAL 2026-07-17: AC4's STORE-KIT half done. The README's privacy posture had been rewritten for the merged permission set; SUBMISSION.md — what a store reviewer actually reads — had not, and carried three inaccuracies: (1) the gradethread.com host justification said only 'call the grading API / receive the token' and OMITTED that gt-bridge.js is a CONTENT SCRIPT injected into every gradethread.com page — exactly the privacy trade this epic exists to document; now stated plainly incl. why (Firefox has no externally_connectable) and what it does NOT do (reads no page content, forwards only our envelope), and the privacy-policy summary discloses it too; (2) it cited *://*.gradethread.com/* — we request https:// only, and *.gradethread.com does not match the apex in Chrome match patterns (hence the manifest carrying both); (3) it named v0.3.0 artifacts while the manifest is 0.3.5 and package-extensions.mjs derives zip names FROM the manifest, so the kit pointed at files that never existed. STILL OPEN: AC1 is umbrella-only (ships no code); AC5 needs the legacy extension/ + extension-condition/ folders removed once the unified reaches parity (US-1757 distribution targets unified only); children US-1880/1881/1882/1883/1884/1885 still open, and US-1873 is now VERIFIED COMPLETE.

PARTIAL 2026-07-13 (agent loop — doable slices; story stays passes:false). DONE: (AC1 regex portion) fixed the dead Poshmark URL-upgrade rule — was /s_[a-z0-9]+/ (path-segment form real CloudFront URLs never have, so thumbnails got graded); now /(?:s|m|t)_(?=[^/]*$) matching the filename size-prefix, with a real-URL-shape test. (AC2) added intl hosts to the ebay adapter (fr/it/es/ie/nl/at/ch/pl/be) and vinted (be/at/ro/hu/sk/pt/se/lu/hr/gr/dk/fi) in BOTH config files; rewrote manifest content_scripts matches to canonical https://*.<host><path>* (the *. form covers apex+www+country subdomains, fixing the www-only + *.poshmark.ca gaps); new test/manifest-hosts.test.cjs derives the match set from adapters and fails on any drift (proven to catch missing+orphan). userStories.title: Cross-browser: Firefox + Edge support for the unified extension
userStories.description: As a Firefox or Edge user, I want the extension to work. Audit: both extensions are Chrome-only in practice — background declares only service_worker (Firefox MV3 runs event pages via background.scripts; with only service_worker Firefox loads NO background at all); no browser_specific_settings.gecko.id (AMO requires it); the Lister additionally awaits promise-style chrome.* APIs that are callback-only on Firefox, and its onMessageExternal registration would throw at top level there. Edge is Chromium-compatible as-is and only needs a store submission.
acceptanceCriteria: Manifest declares BOTH background.service_worker and background.scripts (the documented cross-browser pattern) + browser_specific_settings.gecko { id, strict_min_version: '109.0' }

A small runtime shim guarantees promise-style APIs on both browsers (use the browser.* namespace where present, or wrap the needed chrome.* calls); no top-level listener registration can throw on a browser lacking the event (guard onMessageExternal existence)

The research surface (condition read) works end-to-end on Firefox: config fetch, grade call (README's moz-extension origin in EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS documented in .env.example), overlay, popup, storage — verified manually on a real listing; Firefox's opt-in host-permissions flow is handled (prompt or graceful degradation)
Seller tools on Firefox: explicitly gated OFF with honest UI copy until US-1882 lands (externally_connectable does not exist on Firefox — no silent breakage)
Edge: the unified build loads and passes a manual smoke on Edge; store packaging checklist (Edge Add-ons) appended to US-1757's distribution scope
userStories.notes: Audit findings 18 + Lister §3 (four independent Firefox breakages). Safari deliberately out of scope (Xcode wrapper + no externally_connectable — revisit post-launch). | PARTIAL 2026-07-17: AC1 DONE — manifest declared only background.service_worker, so Firefox (which runs the background as a non-persistent EVENT PAGE and reads background.scripts) loaded NO background at all and the extension was inert there. background.js already documented+implemented its half of the contract; the manifest never did. Now declares BOTH service_worker and scripts (= importScripts deps + background.js, in order — background.js reads GT_LISTER_SELECTORS/GUARD/JOBS/REGISTRY at load) + browser_specific_settings.gecko {id: extension@gradethread.com, strict_min_version: 109.0}. AC2 load-time guards verified present (onMessageExternal + alarms). New test/background-deps.test.cjs derives the dep list from background.js's own importScripts and asserts the manifest matches exactly — the two copies only diverge on Firefox, which everyday Chrome work never exercises (US-1874 added job-store.js and nothing would have caught the omission). Guard verified against both the missing-dep drift and the pre-fix no-scripts state. 11/11 extension test files. BLOCKS passes: AC3 (research surface end-to-end on Firefox) + AC5 (Edge smoke) need a real browser. AC4 (gate seller tools off on Firefox) may be moot now US-1882's gt-bridge.js has landed — needs a decision, not a blind gate. | PARTIAL 2026-07-17 (b): AC4 RESOLVED AS MOOT + a shipped-build bug fixed. AC4 investigation: there is NO browser gate in extension-unified and none is needed — seller gating is capability-based off entitlements (registry.js:58 sellerEnabled, fail-safe false), and US-1882's gt-bridge.js gives Firefox a working transport (src/lib/lister-extension.ts:406 falls back to sendViaBridge when chrome.runtime is absent; handleExternalMessage re-checks origin via GT_LISTER_GUARD.isOriginAllowed either way). So no honest-copy gate is owed. BUT seller tools were still broken on Firefox for a DIFFERENT reason, in the packager rather than the extension: scripts/package-extensions.mjs hand-maintained a THIRD copy of the background dep list that predated US-1874's lister/job-store.js, so the shipped FF event page loaded with GT_LISTER_JOBS undefined; startJob threw at background.js:575 AFTER tabs.create had already opened the marketplace tab, sendResponse never fired, gt-bridge replied transportError, and sendListerJob deliberately does not settle on transportError (MV3 worker-death cover) — so the seller got an unfilled form and a 130s hang. Exactly the silent breakage AC4 was written to prevent, one file outside the guard. ROOT-CAUSE FIX: firefoxManifest() now DERIVES from the manifest instead of re-declaring it, which also fixed two more shipped-only bugs the same overwrite caused — strict_min_version was dropped entirely (add-on installable on pre-109 Firefox, no MV3) and the gecko id disagreed with the manifest's (extension@ vs unified@ = different add-on identity for a dev-loaded vs store build, and unchangeable post-AMO-submission). background-deps.test.cjs now imports the packager (run block guarded behind an isEntry check) and asserts the ACTUAL transform output, not a restatement of it; both regressions verified to fail the guard, then restored green. Shipped FF zip verified by unzip: 5 bg scripts incl job-store.js, min 109.0, externally_connectable stripped. 12/12 extension test files. STILL BLOCKS passes: AC3 (Firefox research surface end-to-end) + AC5 (Edge smoke) — both need a real browser + a human. NOTE for AC5: extension-condition's FF build has NO strict_min_version (its manifest declares no gecko block, so the packager fallback supplies only an id) — same pre-109 exposure, left alone as out of scope for this story. | 2026-07-19 THE AC5 SIDE-NOTE IS NOW FIXED (the story itself stays passes:false — AC3 Firefox end-to-end and AC5 Edge smoke still need a real browser and a human, which has not changed). A prior pass recorded, and then left alone as out of scope, that extension-condition's Firefox build has NO strict_min_version. Verified it: its manifest declared no browser_specific_settings AT ALL, so package-extensions.mjs supplied a gecko id from its config fallback and nothing constrained the version — the shipped Condition Check AMO zip had no floor. WHY THAT MATTERS: Firefox gained MV3 in 109, so the add-on installs on older Firefox where its own APIs do not exist, does nothing, and reads as our software being broken rather than as an unsupported browser. It is also a RECURRENCE, which is what makes it worth more than a one-line fix: the firefoxManifest() comment in the packager already lists 'a wholesale overwrite that dropped strict_min_version' as one of three drift breakages that shipped. It came back by a different route — absence rather than overwrite — so fixing only the instance would leave the third route open too. FIXED THE INSTANCE AND THE CLASS: declared gecko.id + strict_min_version 109.0 in extension-condition/manifest.json (manifest-first, per the packager's own stated rule that firefox.* config only FILLS GAPS), plus a packager guard that THROWS rather than warns — this is the step that produces a store upload, the artifact goes somewhere we cannot recall it from, and a warning in a build log is exactly what got missed the first time (verified exit code 1). Plus a repo-level test that derives its targets from the packager config, so a newly Firefox-enabled extension is covered the day it is enabled rather than the day someone remembers the file; it hard-fails if that derivation yields zero targets, because a guard that silently checks nothing is the failure mode it exists to prevent. Does NOT pin an exact version — raising the floor is a legitimate decision and a test that fights it gets deleted; having no floor never is. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED three ways: block removed, floor set to 102, and the packager run with no floor (exit 1). Note this hardens a DEPRECATED artifact, consistent with the US-2020 call: extension-condition is superseded but still packaged and still installed, so it has to keep working until its store listing is retired. 15/15 extension test files, 2472 web tests.

userStories.title: Web↔extension transport v2: postMessage bridge so seller tools work beyond Chromium
userStories.description: As a Firefox (later Safari) seller, I want 'Send to extension' to work. The current transport is chrome.runtime.sendMessage from the page via externally_connectable — Chromium-only by platform design. The standard alternative is a gradethread.com content script relaying window.postMessage to the background.
acceptanceCriteria: The unified extension adds a gradethread.com content script that relays a versioned, origin-checked window.postMessage protocol to the background (message schema validated exactly like the current external messages; responses relayed back with correlation ids)

src/lib/lister-extension.ts feature-detects transports: externally_connectable where available, postMessage bridge otherwise; isListerAvailable() reflects either; timeouts/settled-guard semantics preserved

Security parity: the bridge accepts messages only from window.top on allowed origins, validates payloads with the same schema, and never exposes marketplace responses to the page beyond the current result shape; the privacy copy (US-1872) already covers the gradethread.com host permission this requires
Chromium keeps using externally_connectable (no regression); Firefox seller flows verified end-to-end on Poshmark
userStories.notes: Unblocks the Firefox seller half of US-1881. The gradethread.com content script is the deliberate privacy-posture trade the US-1872 epic documents. | 2026-07-18 (agent loop): STATUS WAS STALE — this story read as unstarted but the bridge had already shipped (extension-unified/gt-bridge.js), which is why US-1881's notes referred to it as landed. Audited all four ACs against the code rather than the status. AC1 DONE: gt-bridge.js is a document_start content script on gradethread.com relaying a versioned envelope ({__gtExtReq,id,message} -> runtime.sendMessage -> {__gtExtRes,id,response}) with correlation ids, a `replied` guard covering Chrome's callback and Firefox's promise return, and responses posted to an EXPLICIT target origin (never '*'). AC2 DONE: src/lib/lister-extension.ts:406 feature-detects — externally_connectable when chrome.runtime+id are present, else sendViaBridge; isListerAvailable() accepts the DOM marker alone (no extension id needed); the EXTENSION_TIMEOUT_MS backstop, the pushWaiters settled-guard and the deliberate do-not-settle-on-transportError semantics (MV3 worker-death cover) are all preserved. AC4 (Chromium no-regression) verified in code: the manifest still declares externally_connectable, sendViaRuntime is still PREFERRED, and both transports converge on the same handleExternalMessage which re-checks the sender origin via GT_LISTER_GUARD.isOriginAllowed. GAP FOUND AND CLOSED (AC3): the AC requires the bridge accept messages 'only from window.top on allowed origins'. The origin half was satisfied (the content script only runs on gradethread.com, event.source!==window rejects other windows, and the background re-checks origin), but there was NO framing guard. The threat is clickjacking rather than forgery — event.source!==window already means only same-frame scripts can send an envelope and a cross-origin parent can run none — but a framed gradethread.com would let the page's OWN 'Send to extension' control be clicked through by a victim who cannot see it: a genuine seller action from a real click. gt-bridge.js now returns immediately unless window.top === window, installing NO marker and NO listeners (a marker alone would make the page offer seller UI in a context the extension refuses to serve), and fails CLOSED when reading window.top throws, which is what a cross-origin frame does. ⚠ NOTE this is defense in depth, not a live hole: gradethread.com ships X-Frame-Options: DENY and CSP frame-ancestors 'none' — VERIFIED LIVE on the zone this pass. It is in the extension anyway because an extension must not stake its security on a response header it does not control; headers get relaxed for a partner embed or a preview host and the guarantee would vanish with nothing failing to signal it. TESTS: new extension-unified/test/gt-bridge.test.cjs EXECUTES the bridge against a stubbed window/document (rather than grepping source) and asserts: top-level installs marker+listener; framed installs NEITHER; a throwing cross-origin window.top also fails closed; the relay round-trips a correlation id and posts to an explicit origin; five malformed/foreign envelopes are ignored; and the background->page push relay forwards ONLY GT_LISTER_JOB_UPDATE/GT_LISTER_LISTED, never arbitrary background traffic. Both new guarantees negative-verified (removing the frame guard, and widening the push allowlist, each turn the suite red). 13/13 extension test files; packager still emits a valid FF zip. KEPT passes:false ON AC4 ONLY: 'Firefox seller flows verified end-to-end on Poshmark' needs a real browser on a real marketplace — same browser-gate as US-1881 AC3/AC5, and not something this agent can do. Everything else in the story is code-complete and tested.

userStories.title: Two iOS parity gaps have no covering story
userStories.description: As an iOS user, I want the last two parity gaps closed, so that the iOS client matches web on comp editing and has real authenticated UI test coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: Auth-d seam-flow UITests — needs a seeded test account or a mock network layer. Currently the only UITest coverage is the launch smoke (ios-smoke.yml), so no authenticated flow is exercised.
Inline per-field editing of existing saved comps on iOS — today editing a saved comp means delete and re-add.

CONTEXT: these were the only two unchecked items in IOS_PARITY_AUDIT.md when US-2057 archived it on 2026-07-19. A search of prd.json and prd.archive.json found NO covering story for either, so archiving without filing this would have retired them silently.
iOS work cannot be built or verified from the Windows checkout; the iOS CI lane on macOS runners is the gate.
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS] Filed by US-2057 on 2026-07-19. Extracted from IOS_PARITY_AUDIT.md before archiving it — the audit was otherwise complete (4 of 6 items done). | 2026-08-12 AC2 DONE (e9b90109). The saved-comps rows were read-only Text with only .onDelete, so fixing a typo meant deleting the comp and retyping all three fields - and the delete is the destructive half, which made the cheapest correction also the one that loses the comp if the re-add is interrupted. Now bound straight into state.draft.compSet, so the canvas existing diff against `original` marks the item dirty like any other field: no new persistence and no new write path. TWO HELPERS, BOTH REFUSING THE LOSSY OPTION. optionalText writes back nil rather than "" for an all-whitespace entry, because ItemComp.source/.url are String? and the encoder omits nil - storing "" would round-trip a present-but-empty field where there had been none. compPriceBinding REFUSES an unparseable entry instead of coercing to 0: the field is edited by keystroke, so clearing it to retype passes through "" on the way, and writing 0 there would silently rewrite a real comp price to nothing - the same data loss the delete-and-re-add flow had. It resolves on the next valid keystroke, and it uses formatRaw, which already exists for exactly this parse round-trip, rather than a new formatter method. Checked that .onDelete still binds to the ForEach after switching to ForEach($...). AC1 REMAINS and is the harder half: authed seam-flow UITests need a seeded account or a stubbed network layer. CORRECTION TO AC1's PREMISE, found while scoping: it says the only UITest coverage is the launch smoke, and that is stale - ios/GradeThreadUITests/CriticalFlowUITests.swift already covers sign-in, the StoreKit paywall and capture-to-grade, running blocking in ios-ci.yml. What is actually missing is a signed-in MODE: Testing/UITestSupport.swift has -uitest, -uitest-reset-auth, -uitest-paywall and -uitest-mock-grading, and no stub session. That hook is codeable; writing new XCUITests blind against selectors nobody can run locally is not. UNCOMPILED - iOS CI is the gate.

userStories.title: FlipDesk is described but never shown publicly; contradictory 'Join waitlist' CTA signals vaporware
userStories.description: As a high-volume reseller evaluating FlipDesk, we want to see the actual tool before signing up. The public site describes FlipDesk with icon+text cards but shows ZERO product screenshots, GIFs, or demo; the genuinely strong AutoLister (batch upload, HEIC/Live Photo, auto-group, bulk generate, auto-publish) is only visible AFTER signup. The power-reseller persona had to commit on faith and nearly bounced. Compounding the vaporware read: the homepage closing section pairs 'Join waitlist' next to 'Start Grading Free' even though the product is clearly live — a mixed launch signal at the exact conversion moment.
acceptanceCriteria: Homepage and /for-resellers show real FlipDesk/AutoLister imagery (screenshots and/or a short Loom/GIF) of the bulk pipeline
The contradictory 'Join waitlist' CTA is removed or reconciled now that the product is live
userStories.notes: [P3][Web/Conversion] 5-persona QA sweep 2026-07-13. Power-reseller persona: the tool is strong but hidden behind a signup wall; 'Join waitlist' next to 'Start Grading Free' reads as vaporware. | 2026-07-14 (branch claude/prd-stories-review-lsem0z): AC2 SATISFIED + AC1 SUBSTANTIALLY ADDRESSED. AC2: audited the whole app — there is NO public "Join waitlist" CTA rendered anywhere (WaitlistForm component is unused; the homepage/for-resellers closing CTAs are "Try FlipDesk Free"/"Start Grading Free" + a legit newsletter signup), so the vaporware CTA contradiction is already gone. AC1: the landing page already showed the FlipDesk pipeline via honest per-stage stylized mocks (labeled "not a real screenshot"); /for-resellers only DESCRIBED it in text. Extracted the stage data to src/components/marketing/flipdesk-stages.ts and a reusable presentational src/components/marketing/flipdesk-pipeline-preview.tsx (no landing-only data-flipdesk-* scroll-scene hooks, so flipdesk-scene.ts does not bind it), then added a "The full reseller workflow, built in" section to /for-resellers rendering the full source→grade→list→reprice→reconcile pipeline + a "Try FlipDesk Free" CTA. landing.tsx now imports the shared FLIPDESK_STAGES (dropped its inline copy + now-unused Boxes/Tag icons). Verified: tsc -b + eslint clean; npm run build prerenders 213 routes and dist/for-resellers.html (36KB) contains the pipeline stages + honesty caption + CTA. KEPT passes:false: AC1 literally asks for real screenshots and/or a short Loom/GIF — the stylized mocks show the flow honestly but real product imagery is a design-asset follow-up (no FlipDesk/AutoLister screenshots exist in the repo to wire in). | 2026-08-02 AC2 RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (not taken from the previous note): grepped every .tsx/.ts under src for waitlist CTAs. WaitlistForm has ZERO importers — the only hit outside its own file is a COMMENT in newsletter-signup.tsx saying it mirrors WaitlistForm's prerender-safe dynamic import. So the string "Join waitlist" exists only inside a component nothing renders, and the vaporware CTA contradiction is genuinely gone from every public surface. AC2 holds. AC1 IS NOT COMPLETABLE FROM A CHECKOUT and I want that stated plainly rather than left as "substantially addressed". The AC asks for REAL FlipDesk/AutoLister imagery — screenshots or a short GIF of the bulk pipeline. What exists is honest stylized mocks, explicitly labelled "not a real screenshot", now shared between the landing page and /for-resellers via flipdesk-stages.ts + flipdesk-pipeline-preview.tsx. That was the right intermediate step and it removed the /for-resellers text-only gap, but a labelled mock is precisely what the story says is insufficient: the persona in the description "had to commit on faith", and a drawing that admits it is a drawing does not fix that. Producing the real thing needs the app running against a real account with real inventory, someone to capture it, and a judgement call about what seller data is safe to show publicly. That is a human with the product open, not a code change. RECOMMENDATION: treat AC1 as an asset-production task and either assign it or split it out, rather than leaving the story open against a checkout that cannot satisfy it. A SEPARATE FINDING FROM THE SAME GREP, worth its own attention: the waitlist BACKEND is still live while its only public entry point is orphaned. /api/waitlist exists, /admin/waitlist is in the admin nav, and edge-fetch.ts:160 still routes a waitlist-gated account to a dedicated pending page — but nothing on the public site can add anyone to that list. So the system is half-wired in the direction that is hard to notice: an operator opening the admin page sees a waitlist that can only ever shrink. Same shape as vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md catalogues, and the same decision it always needs — either the waitlist is a live feature whose public capture form should be rendered somewhere, or it is retired and the form, the admin page and the gating branch go together. Not decided here because removing gating touches the auth path, and rendering a waitlist form on a live product would reintroduce the exact vaporware signal AC2 exists to prevent. That tension is the reason it needs a decision rather than a default. | 2026-08-09 THE ORPHANED-WAITLIST FINDING IN MY 2026-08-02 NOTE IS NOW FILED AS US-2449, with the evidence re-measured rather than carried over. WaitlistForm still has ZERO importers (the only other repo hit is a comment in newsletter-signup.tsx); /api/waitlist is mounted and rate-limited (main.ts:788, 1078), the admin queue is routed and in the nav (admin-routes.tsx:185, admin-layout.tsx:108), and edge-fetch.ts:163 still redirects a gated account to /waitlist-pending. SHARPER THAN 'half-wired', which is how I put it before: lib/access-gate.ts drives the whole thing from ONE feature_flags row (waitlist_gating) and is fail-open, so it is inert today — and flipping it on would gate every non-staff account with no approved/invited waitlist_entries row, while the only public way to create such a row is a component nothing renders. It is not dormant code; it is a switch that would lock people out. US-1949 itself is unchanged and stays passes:false on AC1 only: real FlipDesk/AutoLister screenshots need a human with the product open and a judgement about what seller data is safe to show. AC2 remains satisfied.

userStories.title: bulkMigrateListing — bring a seller's existing eBay (Trading) listings under management
userStories.description: As an established reseller onboarding to GradeThread, I want to manage my existing eBay listings, not just view them. Today Trading-created listings import read-only (getAllActiveEbaySelling) and relist explicitly refuses eBay-origin, so a new customer's live catalog can never be revised/repriced/promoted through GradeThread — a major onboarding wall. Implement Inventory API bulk_migrate_listing to convert eligible legacy listings into managed Inventory offers.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge calls POST /sell/inventory/v1/bulk_migrate_listing for eligible active Trading listings and links the resulting SKU/offerId to the inventory_items/listings rows
Migrated listings flip to a managed origin so revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote become available (respecting the sync source-of-truth contract)
Ineligible listings (variations/other) are reported with the eBay reason, not silently dropped
Idempotent; a seller can trigger migration from the app and see progress/results
userStories.notes: [P2][Edge/Inventory] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No bulkMigrateListing anywhere; relist refuses origin==='ebay' (flipdesk-ebay.ts:6503). See SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md — migration changes a mirror into a GT-managed listing. Unlocks managing existing catalogs (most customers' day one). | INVESTIGATION 2026-07-17 (no code): AC2's PROMISE WOULD BE SILENTLY FALSE without an unstated design decision. GOOD NEWS FIRST: AC2's 'flip to a managed origin' needs NO migration — listing_origin is already an enum with both values (00232) and deriveListingOrigin() lets a persisted marker WIN over the provenance signals (sync-precedence.ts:330), so setting listing_origin='gradethread' does unlock revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote. THE PROBLEM IS THE SKU. bulkMigrateListing returns eBay's OWN sku + offerId per listing (inventoryItems[{sku,offerId}], max 5 listings/call, per-listing statusCode + errors[] — verified against eBay docs). The Inventory API keys EVERYTHING on that sku. But nothing in GradeThread stores a per-listing sku: BOTH the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8733) and the revise/list path (:9450) DERIVE it as (item.sku)?.trim() || 'FD-'+id.slice(0,8). So if eBay's migrated sku differs from our derived one — likely, since eBay derives it from the listing's Custom Label or generates it — then after a 'successful' migration every subsequent GT Inventory call targets an inventory item that does not exist, and revise/reprice/withdraw all fail. The listing would be marked GT-managed while being unmanageable: strictly worse than the read-only mirror it replaced, because the origin flip ALSO stops the inbound pull from mirroring it (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH: EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS are only overwritten while origin='ebay'). So the row would go stale AND be unmanageable. THE DECISION (needed before implementing): where does eBay's migrated sku live? (a) listings.platform_fields.migrated_sku — jsonb exists (00113), NO migration, but both sku-deriving sites must learn to prefer it; (b) overwrite inventory_items.sku with eBay's — there IS precedent (ebay-sku-match.tsx:983 already writes eBay's Custom Label into item.sku 'so the two systems agree'), and it is user-initiated rather than a pull, BUT SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH lists sku under GRADETHREAD_OWNED_ITEM_FIELDS ('always owned by GradeThread — no eBay pull may write these') and item.sku is unique-per-user so a migrated sku can COLLIDE with an existing item; (c) a new listings.platform_sku column — cleanest, needs a MIGRATION (blocked while the agent loop consumes 00468-00473 for the Brand KB block). Recommend (c), or (a) if the migration must wait. This is a documented-contract decision (CLAUDE.md flags SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md as the contract for this area), not a coin flip — deliberately not decided unilaterally. Everything else about the story is ready: eBay's contract is confirmed, the origin flip works, and the flip must happen ONLY after eBay confirms the per-listing migration succeeded (a partial failure must leave origin='ebay', or the row becomes stale AND unmanageable). BLOCKED ON US-1999 (filed 2026-07-18). The SKU problem this note identified is not specific to migration — it is a live defect in its own right: the eBay Inventory SKU is derived at three sites from the freely-editable inventory_items.sku and never pinned, so a seller renaming a SKU can orphan an already-live listing. US-1999 adds the stored SKU. Migration cannot link bulk_migrate_listing's returned sku to anything until that column exists, so do US-1999 first and this story gets much smaller. | 2026-07-18 EDGE COMPLETE (agent loop) — THE BLOCKER IS GONE. The 2026-07-17 investigation ended on an open design question (where does eBay own migrated sku live?); US-1999 answered it this session by adding listings.inventory_sku (00477), so option (a) platform_fields.migrated_sku is moot — the SKU has a real, indexed, listing-scoped column and BOTH derive sites already read it. AC1 — lib/ebay-migrate.ts (pure) + bulkMigrateListing() in ebay-client.ts + POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate. AC2 — the origin flip and the SKU write happen in ONE update and ONLY when eBay returned a SKU; the module header and a dedicated test spell out why: flipping origin without the sku produces a row that is marked managed, is not addressable by any Inventory call, AND has stopped being refreshed by the inbound pull (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH only overwrites EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS while origin=ebay) — strictly worse than the mirror it replaced. The single most important test asserts a 2xx WITH NO SKU is a FAILURE, not a success. AC3 — every listing is accounted for: eBay errors surface longMessage verbatim; listings eBay omitted from responses[] are reported rather than vanishing; and OUR OWN pre-flight skips (not found / already GT-published / no platform_listing_id / not active) each carry a reason, since a listing that silently disappears from the result is the same defect whether we or eBay dropped it. AC4 (partial) — idempotent: an already-migrated row returns already_managed instead of erroring, so retrying a partly-failed batch is safe; eBay 5-per-call cap enforced by chunkForMigrate, plus a separate 50-per-REQUEST cap so one HTTP call cannot fan out into 40 sequential eBay calls and time out. US-268: ids come from the request body, so the read is scoped .eq(user_id, workspaceOwnerId ?? userId) and only rows that come back are acted on; a request naming ONLY foreign ids 404s rather than returning 200 with per-item not-found (a bulk 200 would make a cross-tenant probe indistinguishable from success at the status level), and tenant-isolation_test.ts has the required case. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4144 edge tests pass (8 new). ⚠ HELD — depends on 00477, so it ships with that migration; the route SELECTs inventory_sku. STILL OPEN for passes: AC4 UI (trigger + progress/results in the app — the Reconciliation page is the natural home) and a real-eBay end-to-end run, which cannot be done in the sandbox. | 2026-07-18 AC4 UI DONE (agent loop). Trigger + per-listing results now live in the app. Placement is deliberate: the button sits IN the amber "this listing was created on eBay, so eBay owns its title/price/description/photos" banner on the item canvas — the exact place the seller hits the wall — rather than on a settings page they would have to know to look for. useMigrateEbayListings() reports eBay reasons PER LISTING rather than collapsing to one "done" (a multi-variation rejection is actionable, "failed" is not), capped at 3 toasts so a large batch cannot bury the screen. ⚠ FOUND AND FIXED A DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE WHOLE FEATURE LOOK BROKEN: item-canvas computed lockedByEbay via deriveListingOrigin() but its listings query never SELECTED listing_origin — and that persisted column is exactly what migration writes, and what deriveListingOrigin lets WIN over the provenance signals. So post-migration the row still had a platform_listing_id, no batch_id and no synced_to_ebay_at, the canvas would have re-derived "ebay", and the seller would have seen the locked banner and the migrate button still sitting there after a SUCCESSFUL migration. Added listing_origin to the select + the two type literals, and invalidated the item_ebay_sync query in the mutation (it backs that banner; without it the UI would not refetch at all). Pinned with a NEW test file src/lib/__tests__/listing-origin.test.ts — deriveListingOrigin gates revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote and the locked-fields banner across the app and had ZERO test coverage before this; 5 tests now cover persisted-marker-wins (both directions), unrecognized-marker fallback, batch/sync signals, draft-with-no-listing-id, and non-eBay platforms. Verified: tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 2232 vitest tests pass, 4144 deno tests pass. STILL passes:false — the only thing left is a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it), which cannot be done from the sandbox. Everything code-side across all four ACs is complete. Still HELD behind 00477. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE. The stack was pushed and BOTH migrations are APPLIED IN PRODUCTION — measured, not assumed: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00478, applied:00478, status:match} with database ok and status ready, and the deployed frontend bundle reports release 91d466d22f2ef6061e07d6dd56f2a521a5aa562a (the head of origin/main). So the apply-before-push ordering was honored and nothing is frozen. Post-deploy smoke checks run the same day: POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 (auth enforced) rather than a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which is the specific failure that would indicate 00477 had not landed; a real certificate off sitemap-certs.xml still returns 200, so the grading/cert path is unbroken; and gradethread.com now serves Permissions-Policy camera=(self) (a first check showed the old camera=() from a cached response — the cache-busted request confirmed the fix is live, worth noting because that cached read looked exactly like a failed deploy). | 2026-07-19 RE-VERIFIED LIVE. POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header' — auth enforced, route mounted, and specifically NOT a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which remains the exact signature that would mean 00477 (listings.inventory_sku) had not landed. So the feature is still healthy in prod. The ONLY remaining item is unchanged and unreachable from a sandbox: a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it) needs a live seller account with legacy listings. TWO INCIDENTAL SIGNALS FROM THE SAME PROBE, worth recording for whoever runs the next deploy: /health/ready still reports schema {expected:00478, applied:00479} — so the DEPLOYED edge predates the 00480-00485 stack, and the phantom 00479 is still there; and features{} has NO 'alerting' key while observability reads 'ok'. Both are artefacts of the deployed build predating today's work: US-2003 adds the alerting group and US-2001 makes observability report DEGRADED until GIT_SHA is a real SHA. Expect both to change on the next deploy — 'alerting' will appear as degraded (no channel configured) and 'observability' will flip from ok to degraded until the build arg is wired. Neither is a regression; they are the new checks becoming visible.

userStories.title: Handbags and small leather goods cannot be graded — 'bag' routes into the clothing rubric
userStories.description: As a seller of handbags, I want a bag graded on the things that determine a bag's price, because 'bag' is already a garment_category and item_category has 'bags' (00230), while the only rubric that will accept it grades fabric condition at 30% and odor at 10%. A handbag's condition is corner and edge-paint wear (the single most-inspected area and the most expensive to restore), handle and strap darkening and cracking, hardware plating loss and zipper pull function, interior lining staining and pen marks and odor, structural slouch and base sag, and glazing on the edges. The category also carries the most authenticity weight of anything we touch — the existing tells (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) are ALL bag brands — so grading and the authenticity add-on land on the same item here, and the certificate has to be careful not to let a condition grade read as an authenticity verdict.
acceptanceCriteria: A handbags/leather-goods rubric is added to rubric.ts with factors, weights summing to 1.0, promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared fixture.
Photo slots cover the areas that decide a bag's grade: corners, base, interior, hardware, handles/straps, and the date-code/serial location.

A condition grade on a bag must NOT read as an authenticity statement anywhere on the certificate or in the buyer writeup — an explicit separation, test-asserted on the rendered copy, given these are the brands the authenticity add-on covers.
Measurement templates cover bag dimensions (width, height, depth, strap drop).
Prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set.
Lockstep rule holds across the three rounding sites in the same commit.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2. Highest-value of the three new-rubric stories: handbags carry the most price-per-item and are the exact brands the authenticity add-on covers (louisvuitton/coach/gucci are ALL bag brands), so the condition-vs-authenticity separation on the certificate is a liability requirement, not polish. | 2026-08-09 AC1 and AC3 DONE; AC2, AC4, AC5 and AC6 REMAIN and two of them are blocked on US-1997 Phase 2. NO MIGRATION — the rubric registry is code, and grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores already exist (00231). AC1: a handbags rubric is in services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts, and added to src/test/fixtures/rubric-factors.json so both parity suites pin it (edge rubric-parity_test.ts 54 passed, client rubrics.test.ts 51 passed). SIX factors, one more than any existing rubric, and the shape is the argument: corners_edges 0.30, exterior 0.20, handles_straps 0.15, hardware 0.15, interior 0.10, structure 0.10. Corners and edge paint carry the most because they are the first place every buyer looks and the most expensive area to restore — a bag with perfect panels and worn corners reads as used and the reverse does not. handles_straps sits with hardware rather than under structure because its failure mode is chemical (vachetta darkening, glazing cracking) not structural. interior and structure are last because they are the two a buyer can least see in photographs, and a rubric should not weight heavily what the evidence cannot support. I ADDED AN 'exterior' FACTOR THE STORY DID NOT LIST: the AC enumerated corners, handles, hardware, interior, structure and glazing, which leaves body-panel scuffs and stains with nowhere to route — every exterior stain would have fallen through to the first factor and debited corners. defectRouting is reconciled to the real DefectType taxonomy with nothing invented, the same discipline US-1997 applied after finding seven unreachable routings; 'pilling' and 'snag_pull' are deliberately UNROUTED because they are textile failures with no leather equivalent, and they fall through to the documented first-factor rule rather than being faked into a factor they cannot physically reach. AC3 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED MOST AND IT IS DONE, INDEPENDENTLY OF PHASE 2. Every authentication tell pack we hold is a bag brand (louisvuitton, coach, gucci), so a handbag is the single item where a condition grade and an authenticity verdict render on the same certificate — and a number beside a luxury logo reads as a verdict on the logo unless the page says otherwise. On a four-figure resale that is a liability, not a UX regret. Three places now carry the separation: the rubric's promptGuidance tells the model to say nothing about authenticity (guarding the generated WRITE-UP, which no template assertion can reach), src/pages/certificate.tsx renders it INSIDE the Factor Breakdown card, and NEW functions/_shared/condition-authenticity.ts renders it in the SSR certificate. Placement is asserted, not just presence: the notice is emitted as part of factorsHtml so it sits beside the number it qualifies — a separation in a page footer is a disclaimer nobody reaches, which is indistinguishable from not having one. The copy exists twice because a Pages Function cannot import from src/, so NEW src/test/cert-condition-authenticity.test.ts pins them string-for-string (the same remedy embed-grade-widget.test.ts uses for the AI disclosure) and asserts the notice does NOT fire for clothing/cards/watches/shoes or for a legacy certificate with no rubric_key, so existing certificates are byte-identical. 11 cases. THE SEPARATION IS KEYED ON RUBRIC, NOT ON BRAND, deliberately: keying on brand means every new luxury brand needs a code change to be covered, and the failure mode of forgetting one is silent — the certificate omits the line for the item that needed it most. REMAINING: AC2 (photo slots for corners/base/interior/hardware/handles/date-code), AC4 (measurement templates: width, height, depth, strap drop), AC5 (shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set) and AC6 (the three-rounding-site lockstep generalisation) — AC5 and AC6 are US-1997 Phase 2 and cannot be done in a sandbox: AC5 needs live traffic, real vision calls and a non-clothing golden set that does not exist, and AC6 is the variable-factor-set generalisation of the weighted overall, which US-1997 records as needing a validatable environment. AC2 and AC4 are sandbox-doable and are the next honest step. NOTE ON THE SSR CERTIFICATE, found while wiring AC3: functions/cert/[id].ts renders only the hardcoded five clothing factors and does not read rubric_key for the breakdown at all — so when Phase 2 starts writing non-clothing grades, the SSR page will show a handbag's scores against clothing labels. The separation notice IS wired there and will appear, but the factor list itself is a Phase 2 gap that nothing else records. VERIFIED: edge suite 6205 passed / 0 failed, deno lint + check clean, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3770 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | 2026-08-09 (second pass) AC2 DONE, AND I FIXED A BUG I SHIPPED IN THE FIRST PASS. THE BUG FIRST, because it is the more useful finding: the rubric shipped keyed 'handbags' while the item_category enum (00230) spells it 'bags'. rubricForKey() is called with an item_category, so that rubric could never have been selected — every handbag would have kept grading as clothing, which is the exact bug this story exists to fix, reintroduced by the fix. NOTHING FAILED: the rubric existed, the shared parity fixture passed, both suites were green, and the certificate rendered clothing factors. Renamed to 'bags' across rubric.ts, rubrics.ts, the fixture, the SSR shared module and the tests. THE GUARD IS THE POINT: rubric-parity_test.ts now asserts every key in RUBRICS exists in PHOTO_PROFILES, whose keys ARE the item_category vocabulary — it is the one place the edge service enumerates them. Negative-verified by renaming the key back and watching 4 cases redden. This is a DIFFERENT deadness from the import-graph kind vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md catalogues: that audit finds modules nothing imports, and this module IS imported — the dead thing was a KEY inside a lookup table, which no import graph can see. Recorded there as a generalisable rule: when reachability depends on a string matching a value declared somewhere else, pin the two together, because both halves look correct in isolation. AC2 DONE. The bags photo profile asked for front, back, brand stamp, serial, interior, one catch-all Hardware detail and extras — a set built for LISTING and AUTHENTICATING a bag, which never asked for the two areas the rubric weights most. corners_edges carries 30% of the score and had NO SLOT AT ALL, so the grader was being asked to judge corner wear from a full-front shot that physically cannot resolve it, and the seller was never told to take the photo. Three roles added, each mapped to a rubric factor: corner -> corners_edges (0.30), surface labelled 'Base' -> structure (0.10), detail_2 labelled 'Handles and Straps' -> handles_straps (0.15). Both are EXISTING storage roles from 00230, not new ones, and 'corner' already carries an 800px floor plus the 0.30 sharpness gate in macro-photo-quality.ts, so it is treated as a macro slot the moment it is offered with no further wiring. Handles use detail_2 and NOT accessory deliberately: accessory means the dust bag and the papers, and filing evidence about the ITEM under evidence about what came WITH it reads differently to the grader. Only front/back/brand-stamp stay REQUIRED — making six slots required would block a seller from advancing an item they have already photographed well enough to list, which is a different question from whether the grade will be confident, and image-quality.ts already caps confidence on a thin set. A second new guard asserts that a category with its own rubric offers a photo slot for its heaviest factor, so a future rubric cannot weight an area it never asks anyone to photograph. ALSO FIXED, an SPA-vs-SSR divergence I introduced in the first pass: the SPA keyed the authenticity separation on activeRubric.key, which only resolves to 'bags' when BOTH factor_scores and rubric_key are present (the breakdown deliberately falls back to clothing otherwise so it can render the typed columns), while the SSR page keyed it on rubric_key alone. That would have dropped the disclaimer on exactly the bag whose factor JSON did not land, while the SSR page still showed it — the failure class vault/20-domain/public-certificate-read-paths.md was written about. Both now key on rubric_key alone, which is also correct on its own terms: a bag graded off the typed columns is still a bag. Test-asserted, including that activeRubric is NOT used for it. REMAINING: AC4 (measurement templates: width, height, depth, strap drop), AC5 (shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set) and AC6 (three-rounding-site lockstep generalisation). AC5 and AC6 are US-1997 Phase 2 and need live traffic, real vision calls and a non-clothing golden set that does not exist; AC4 is sandbox-doable and is the next step. VERIFIED: edge suite 6207 passed / 0 failed, deno lint + check clean, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3771 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | 2026-08-09 (third pass) AC4 DONE. Only AC5 and AC6 remain, and both are US-1997 Phase 2. A new 'bag' measurement group in BOTH copies of measurement-templates.ts: width, height and depth REQUIRED, strap_drop and handle_drop optional, all on the in/cm length unit. DEPTH IS THE POINT: a 30cm tote and a 30cm clutch are different objects, and before this a bag fell through to the 'generic' group, which offers length and width and neither of them required — so the two numbers a buyer asks for first were not even offered. BOTH DROPS, not one: a top-handle bag has no strap and a crossbody has no handles, so a single shared 'strap drop' field would sit blank on half of all bags, and a blank measurement reads as 'the seller did not measure it' rather than 'this bag has no strap'. Two optional fields let the right one be filled and the wrong one be honestly empty. measurementGroupFor tests bags FIRST, before shoes, and that ordering is load-bearing: 'boot bag', 'shoe bag' and 'cargo bag' each contain a keyword a later branch claims, every one of them is a bag, and routing a boot bag to the shoe template would have asked the seller for an insole length. WIDENING THE MeasurementGroup UNION MADE THE COMPILER FIND EVERY CONSUMER, which is the argument for the union being exhaustive: four Record<MeasurementGroup, ...> maps failed to compile until each had a bag entry — fit-model.ts GROUP_DIMS, listing-templates.ts DESCRIPTION_TEMPLATES, and two in tools/fit-checker.tsx. GROUP_DIMS and both fit-checker maps are EMPTY like shoes and watches, and for the same reason: the fit engine compares a garment's flat measurements to a BODY's, and a bag has no body dimension to compare against — an entry there would have to invent one. DESCRIPTION_TEMPLATES got a real bag template rather than falling to generic, because generic leads with Size and Material and a bag has no size — its dimensions ARE its size. NEW GUARD FOR A GAP NOBODY HAD FILED: the two measurement-template files are byte-identical and NOTHING pinned them — the third instance of this shape in the repo after the rubric definitions (US-1997) and title-sync (US-1995), and the first one pinned BEFORE a divergence became possible rather than after. src/test/measurement-template-parity.test.ts asserts byte equality (correct here, unlike title-sync where the two implementations legitimately differ — these two are meant to BE the same file, so equality is the actual contract and it fails with a readable diff). The failure it prevents is quiet: measurements are stored on inventory_items.measurements keyed by the field key, so one side renaming a key means the form writes strap_drop, the extractor reads something else, and the number the seller typed simply stops arriving at the listing description, the size estimate and the MeasureCard gate. Nothing errors. 7 cases. ALSO CORRECTED A VAULT CLAIM found while re-reading the drifted note: vault/20-domain/listing-photos.md said 'since 00306, required = front + back only' as a blanket rule, and photo-profiles.ts is PER CATEGORY — bags has required 'marking' on top of front and back, and had before I touched it. The sentence describes the clothing default and the items_full.has_required_photos column, not every category; it now says so and points at requiredPhotoTypesFor(category). Also recorded there and in the code that the bags role ORDER changed (condition shots ahead of interior and the date code) with front still at index 0, so no cover image moved — roles[] drives sort_order and index 0 is the eBay cover. VERIFIED: edge suite 6207 passed / 0 failed, deno lint + check clean, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3778 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean.

userStories.title: Headwear cannot be graded — hats have a garment_category, no rubric, no photo slots and no measurements
userStories.description: As a seller of hats, I want to grade a cap the way I grade a hoodie, because headwear is a high-volume resale category and today 'hat' is a garment_category value that routes into a clothing rubric which cannot express it. Verified: GARMENT_CATEGORIES includes 'hat'; rubric.ts has clothing, sports_cards, watches and shoes and nothing else; MEASUREMENT_TEMPLATES has top/bottom/dress/outerwear/shoes/watch/generic and nothing else; the required image types are front/back/label. A fitted cap's condition lives in places none of those reach: brim shape and flatness, crown structure and collapse, the sweatband (the first thing to fail and the first thing a buyer inspects), the button and eyelets, embroidery integrity and pulls, and staining at the front panel and sweatband.
acceptanceCriteria: A headwear rubric is added to rubric.ts with its own factors and weights summing to 1.0, plus promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared rubric-factors fixture.
A headwear measurement template is added (fitted size / circumference, crown height, brim length) in the units the category actually uses.
Headwear-appropriate photo slots exist (crown, brim, sweatband/interior, label) — grading a cap from front/back/label alone cannot see the sweatband, which is where the wear is.
The weighted-overall computation stays in lockstep across all three rounding sites in the same commit as any factor-set generalization this requires.

The new rubric's prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a headwear golden set that must be bootstrapped first — a rubric with no golden set cannot pass the gate and must not be activated around it.
Any enum widening (image_type, garment_category) follows the US-1108 triple and the enum caveats in the migrations skill.
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2 — the factor-set generalization across the three lockstep rounding sites is a prerequisite for ANY new rubric, and US-1997's notes already scope it. Do not build a fourth rubric before that lands. | 2026-08-09 AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE; AC6 DEFERRED; AC4 and AC5 remain and are US-1997 Phase 2. NO MIGRATION, deliberately — see AC6. AC1: a HEADWEAR rubric in rubric.ts, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts, pinned by the shared fixture. crown_structure 0.25, brim 0.25, sweatband 0.20, fabric_graphics 0.20, hardware_closure 0.10. THE WEIGHTS SPLIT INTO TWO QUESTIONS and that is the design: brim + crown together are half the score because together they answer 'is this still a hat' — a collapsed crown or a cracked brim insert is not recoverable and the cap is worth its logo and nothing else. sweatband and fabric answer 'will someone wear it', which is the other half of a resale decision and not the same question. THE STORY ARGUES FOR SWEATBAND FIRST and it is 0.20; the reason is worth reading rather than assuming I under-weighted it. It is the most COMMON failure, not the most terminal one. A stained sweatband is close to permanent and will lose a sale, so it carries real weight — but a cap with a perfect crown and brim and a grim sweatband is still a cap, while the reverse is not. defectRouting is reconciled to the real DefectType taxonomy with nothing invented: seam_failure_unthreading splits sweatband/crown (the band separating from the crown is the canonical case), stretched_misshapen goes to crown+brim (a collapsed crown, a brim that lost its curve), odor_indicator wholly to sweatband. 'stain' is split 0.6 sweatband / 0.4 fabric rather than routed wholly to the band — salt lines are the common case, but a mark on a white front panel is the other place a cap dies. promptGuidance carries the intentional-vs-wear line the block exists for: a flat brim on a flat-brim cap and a curved brim on a curved-brim cap are BOTH as-made, and factory distressing on a vintage-styled cap is design. AC3: a headwear photo profile. The story's own sentence is the requirement — 'grading a cap from front/back/label alone cannot see the sweatband, which is where the wear is' — so 'interior' IS the sweatband shot, relabelled 'Sweatband' with the hint 'turn it over', because 'Interior' alone does not tell a seller to photograph the one thing a buyer checks first. I did NOT invent a 'sweatband' storage type: that would need an image_type enum migration for a photo the existing role already describes. 'angle' carries crown and brim together in one three-quarter view, since both are heaviest and both read badly from a flat front. The rubric-parity guard now requires BOTH slots for headwear, so this cannot regress. AC2: a headwear measurement group in both copies. circumference REQUIRED, crown_height and brim_length optional, all as LENGTHS. That is the decision: a fitted cap's '7 3/8' is a size LABEL nobody put a tape to and belongs in the item's size field, and half of resale headwear is snapback or strapback with no numeric size at all — a size-only template would leave those unmeasurable. Routing tests headwear before accessories so 'bucket hat' is not claimed elsewhere, and after bags so a 'hat bag' stays a bag; 'visor' is included because it is a brim and a band and nothing else, which this template covers exactly. ⚠ THE RUBRIC AND PROFILE ARE INERT TODAY, and this is recorded IN THE CODE as well as here because a future reader finds the rubric before the note: both are keyed by item_category and the enum has no 'headwear' value, so rubricForKey() can never select it — the same inert-until-activated state the non-clothing rubrics have had since US-1997. AC6 DEFERRED, and it is an operational call rather than a technical one, identical to US-2224's AC3: the enum widening is small and additive, but SIX migrations (00564-00569) are already held and unapplied to prod, two with strict apply-before-push ordering, and adding more to an unapplied queue raises the cost and risk of the eventual apply session. US-2223 AC6 and US-2224 AC3 should ship as ONE migration in the next batch — both widen the same taxonomy (headwear, neckwear, gloves) and splitting them across two files buys nothing. AC4 (three-rounding-site lockstep across a variable factor set) and AC5 (shadow -> eval -> canary against a headwear golden set that must be bootstrapped first) are US-1997 Phase 2 and need live traffic, real vision calls and correction data that does not exist. VERIFIED: edge suite 6209 passed / 0 failed, deno lint + check clean, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3795 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | 2026-08-09 (second pass) AC6 DONE. Migration 00570_headwear_neckwear_gloves_categories.sql adds item_category 'headwear' (plus the two garment_category values US-2224 AC3 needs — ONE migration for both stories, because they widen the same taxonomy for the same reason and splitting them would mean two apply steps, two rollbacks and two chances to apply one without the other). A cap's condition lives in the crown, the brim and the sweatband; an accessory's lives in its material, edges and hardware. A held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word is no longer merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop on a branch that is not frozen. Whether the SQL has been run against prod is an operator fact this checkout cannot observe, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is the file that tracks it. Read that, not this prose.
