userStories.title: Edge builds ship with release="dev" — every prod edge error is unattributable to a commit (frontend is correct)
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to know which build produced a production error. The frontend does: https://gradethread.com serves a bundle tagged release:"c9631342084bfd9e96883321a07a390d3be1e814", a real commit SHA, so Cloudflare Pages is wiring VITE_RELEASE_SHA correctly. The EDGE does not: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns {"env":"production","release":"dev"}, measured 2026-07-18. Root cause is exact — services/edge-functions/Dockerfile:12 declares ARG GIT_SHA=dev and line 13 sets ENV RELEASE_SHA=${GIT_SHA}; its own comment (lines 9-11) says the builder must pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT, and the Coolify build is not doing so, so the literal default ships. lib/observability.ts:52 releaseSha() therefore returns "dev" and tags every Sentry event, structured log and trace with it. This is an ASYMMETRY between the two halves of the system, and the half that is blind is the one handling grading, payments, eBay writes and webhooks.
acceptanceCriteria: The Coolify build passes the commit into the image (GIT_SHA build arg = $SOURCE_COMMIT or the platform equivalent), so RELEASE_SHA is a real SHA in production.
GET /health on production returns a release that matches the deployed commit — verify by measuring the endpoint after a deploy, not by reading the config.
Sentry edge events carry that release, so an error can be attributed to a deploy and "did the fix ship?" is answerable. Confirm a real event is tagged.

A guard so this cannot silently regress: the edge should REFUSE to report healthy-and-production while release is the literal default "dev"/"unknown" — or at minimum surface it as a degraded feature in /health/ready features{} alongside the existing observability entry, which currently reports "ok" while the release is meaningless.
Document the build-arg requirement in COOLIFY.md next to the other deploy settings, since the Dockerfile comment alone did not survive contact with the actual deploy.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Ops/Observability][Measured] Found 2026-07-18 during the cross-platform production-readiness deep dive, by querying prod rather than reading config. EVIDENCE, all live: /health -> {"status":"ok","service":"gradethread-edge-functions","env":"production","release":"dev","errorTracking":"enabled"}; the frontend bundle /assets/index-CIbHzx5V.js contains release:"c9631342084bfd9e96883321a07a390d3be1e814" (which is also proof Pages auto-deployed that commit). WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC TAG: with every edge event tagged "dev" you cannot (a) attribute a production error to a build, (b) tell whether a deployed fix actually shipped, (c) see a regression appear at a release boundary, or (d) make a rollback decision on evidence — and ROLLBACK.md assumes you can identify the bad build. Note errorTracking reports "enabled" and /health/ready features.observability reports "ok", so the health surface actively says observability is fine while the release dimension of it is inert; that is why AC4 asks for a guard rather than just a config fix. The fix itself is small (one build arg); the reason it survived this long is that nothing measured it. | 2026-07-19 AC1/AC4/AC5 DONE; AC2/AC3 need a deploy to confirm. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS A MISSING BUILD ARG, and the fix is DECLARATIVE rather than another instruction: docker-compose.coolify.yml now carries build.args GIT_SHA: dev. That placement is the whole point — the Dockerfile has carried a comment telling the builder to pass GIT_SHA since it was written, and per this story's own evidence that comment did not survive contact with the actual deploy. A build arg in compose is APPLIED BY THE PLATFORM instead of remembered by a person, so documenting it harder would have reproduced the same failure. The :-dev fallback keeps a plain local docker compose build working. AC4 DONE and it is the anti-regression half: the observability feature group now requires SENTRY_DSN *and* a real RELEASE_SHA, so /health/ready reports observability DEGRADED while the release is a placeholder — previously it reported 'ok' in the exact prod state this story measured (errorTracking enabled, release 'dev'), which is the false confidence that let it sit unnoticed. isRealReleaseSha is deliberately permissive on FORM: it rejects the placeholder set (dev/unknown/local/none/latest/empty) but accepts short SHAs and tags, because the measured failure was the literal ARG default surviving the build, not a malformed SHA — requiring 40 hex chars would break tag-based deploys for no benefit. 4 tests, including the exact prod state as a case. AC5 DONE in COOLIFY.md with a MEASURE-DO-NOT-READ verification step (curl /health | jq .release), plus the warning that deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant needs the same args block. ⚠ REMAINING AND GENUINELY UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: AC2 (measure /health after a deploy) and AC3 (confirm a real Sentry event carries the release). Both require the deploy to actually happen. What HAS changed is that a regression now announces itself on /health/ready instead of waiting for someone to think to curl. [2026-07-19 AC4+AC5 DONE, AC1-AC3 NEED THE COOLIFY BUILD + A PROD MEASUREMENT] AC4: /health/ready now carries features.release, degraded whenever the release is unattributable (dev / unknown / empty / whitespace, case-insensitive). Deliberately a SEPARATE key from features.observability: that group reports ok whenever a Sentry DSN is present, which stays true and stays misleading while every event it ships is tagged dev. Also deliberately does NOT flip the service to not_ready — the AC allowed either, and refusing readiness on an untagged build would pull grading, payments and webhooks out of rotation to protect observability. health.ts already argues this exact principle for the schema probe (a probe that can fail a container over a diagnostic is a worse bug than the blind spot it fixes). A test asserts ready stays true. releaseReadiness() is pure; 5 new tests. AC5 FINDING: COOLIFY.md already had a US-2001 build-args section from an earlier pass, and it CLAIMED /health/ready reports features.observability as degraded on a placeholder release. That was FALSE — nothing implemented it. The documentation described a guard that did not exist, which is a plausible reason nobody built one; same defect class as US-2035 (comment asserting a property the code lacks) and US-2123 (copy advertising an ungranted entitlement). Doc now names the real key, shows the curl, and records the correction rather than quietly overwriting it. STILL OPEN (all need the deploy, not code): AC1 the Coolify build must actually pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT — docker-compose.coolify.yml declares it but prod measured release=dev on 2026-07-18, so either the deploy uses docker-compose.yml or the Build Args field is unset. AC2 verify by curling /health after a deploy. AC3 confirm a real Sentry event carries the SHA. The new features.release entry makes AC2 checkable without remembering the curl. | 2026-08-02 AC2 MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, and it FAILS. The AC insisted on measuring the endpoint rather than reading the config, and that instruction earned its keep: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns features.release = 'unattributable: release="dev" — the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg, so errors cannot be tied to a commit'. So AC1 is declared but NOT IN EFFECT. docker-compose.coolify.yml carries build.args.GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}, and the running image was still built without it. Three candidate causes, in the order worth checking: (1) Coolify is deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant — the previous pass explicitly warned that the plain file needs the same args block, and that warning is now the leading hypothesis rather than a footnote; (2) the running image predates the compose change and no rebuild has happened since; (3) SOURCE_COMMIT is not populated in this Coolify version, so the :-dev fallback wins silently — which is exactly what the fallback is designed to do and exactly why it is indistinguishable from cause (2) without a rebuild. AC3 (a real Sentry event carrying the release) is moot until this is fixed: every event currently ships tagged 'dev', which is the state the story exists to end. WHAT THIS CONFIRMS ABOUT AC4, and it is the useful part: the guard works. /health/ready reported the problem in plain language, unprompted, to a caller who did nothing but curl a public endpoint. That is the difference between a config that is wrong and a config that ANNOUNCES it is wrong — before this, the only way to learn it was to notice that every Sentry release said dev. The AC4 decision not to flip the service to not_ready also holds up: the service is genuinely serving, and pulling grading and payments out of rotation to protect observability would have been the wrong trade. STILL OPEN: AC1 in practice (the build arg must actually reach the image), AC2 re-measured after that deploy, AC3 confirmed on a real event. All three need one Coolify rebuild, and the first thing to check is which compose file the service is deploying from. ALSO OBSERVED IN THE SAME RESPONSE, recorded here because it is the same curl: schema reports {expected:00512, applied:00512, status:match}. See the note on the held-migration gate. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-03: any "HELD"/"apply-BEFORE-push" wording earlier in this note describes the state AT THE TIME OF WRITING and is STALE. Prod was measured at applied=00514 on 2026-08-03 via /health/ready (the database's own answer, not a recollection), and every migration up to 00514 is on origin/main. The only migration currently held is 00515 (US-2168), which is unrelated to this story. Do not read this note as evidence that the branch is frozen. | 2026-08-08 CAUSE (1) CONFIRMED AND FIXED. The 2026-08-02 pass listed three candidate causes and said the first thing to check is which compose file the service deploys from. Checked it, and the answer is in this repo's own doc: COOLIFY.md line 11 says the one-time setup makes Coolify 'auto-pick docker-compose.yml'. That file's first line calls itself 'Production compose used by Coolify' — and it had NO build.args block. So the arg was declared only in docker-compose.coolify.yml, which is not the file the documented setup deploys. docker-compose.staging.yml was missing it too.

FIX: both now declare args.GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}, identical to the .coolify.yml one. Deliberately declared in ALL of them rather than picking the 'right' one — the question 'which compose file is it actually using?' is precisely what nobody could answer for three weeks, and making the answer irrelevant is cheaper than making it knowable.

NEW STATIC GUARD (AC4's missing half): services/edge-functions/src/tests/compose-release-arg_test.ts walks every docker-compose*.yml, and any file with a build: section that lacks GIT_SHA fails CI with the reason. It also asserts the Dockerfile still wires ARG GIT_SHA -> ENV RELEASE_SHA, so the guard cannot stay green over a dead mechanism. Override files with no build: section (docker-compose.dev.yml) are exempt — they inherit the base build. Sabotage-verified: deleted the arg line from docker-compose.yml, test failed naming the file; restored, 2 passed. deno lint + deno check clean.

WHY A STATIC GUARD ON TOP OF THE RUNTIME ONE: the /health/ready guard worked exactly as designed and still cost three weeks, because it can only speak after a bad image is already serving. A per-file declaration that only one file carries is a per-file bug, and nothing was looking ACROSS the files. This test looks across the files.

COOLIFY.md rewritten: the old text carried a warning telling the operator to add the block by hand or fill in Coolify's Build Args field — asking a person to remember something, which is the failure mode this story is about, and the Dockerfile had been asking in a comment since it was written. It now states all three files declare it, records why, and keeps ONE residual manual step for the only cause the code cannot rule out (a Coolify version that does not populate SOURCE_COMMIT, where :-dev wins silently).

STILL passes:false, and only on the deploy: AC2 (curl /health/ready after a Coolify rebuild and see a real SHA) and AC3 (confirm a Sentry event carries it). Both need a rebuild, which ADE Hub is disarmed for. Nothing further is doable from a checkout — the code side of AC1 is now complete on all three files and guarded. | 2026-08-09 A SECOND, INDEPENDENT FAULT FOUND — the build arg was never the whole story, and every prior pass (incl. mine) chased it alone. MEASURED FIRST: GET /health returned release:"dev" on an image whose SAME response reported schema.expected=00585, i.e. an image built AFTER the 2026-08-08 commit that put build.args.GIT_SHA in all three compose files. That eliminates the 2026-08-02 note's cause (2) 'the running image predates the compose change'. THE CODE BUG: observability.ts releaseSha() read RELEASE_SHA ?? COMMIT_SHA ?? SOURCE_COMMIT ?? GIT_SHA, and its comment claimed it 'accepts any of the common env names so the same code works on Coolify / CI / local'. It does not. Dockerfile sets ENV RELEASE_SHA=${GIT_SHA} with ARG GIT_SHA=dev, so RELEASE_SHA is ALWAYS SET in the image — to the literal 'dev'. ?? falls through on undefined, never on a placeholder VALUE, so the first key always won and the other three were DEAD CODE on the only platform they were written for. Consequence that matters most: setting SOURCE_COMMIT by hand in Coolify — the obvious workaround, and the one COOLIFY.md was steering toward — would have been SILENTLY IGNORED. FIXED: new services/edge-functions/src/lib/release-identity.ts (resolveRelease/isPlaceholderRelease/RELEASE_ENV_KEYS) falls through placeholder VALUES; observability.ts, env-validation.ts isRealReleaseSha and routes/health.ts all consolidated onto it — health.ts had its OWN narrower set ['dev','unknown',''] so /health/ready could have called a release of 'local' ok while env-validation called it a placeholder. Two more instances of the same defect class fixed: (a) agent-tools.ts:654 releaseSha() fed US-1610's release-verify agent, which detects a deploy by watching that value CHANGE — a constant 'dev' is not an error, it is a value that never changes, so that agent has reported 'no deploy' on every run since it shipped; it now returns null on a placeholder so no-identity stays distinguishable from an identity. (b) releaseReadiness()'s message asserted the cause ('the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg') and was measured saying so on an image that HAD the arg — it now states the symptom and names the keys checked. RUNTIME ROUTE ADDED: all three compose files pass SOURCE_COMMIT + COMMIT_SHA through as BARE environment entries (no '='), deliberately — a runtime env var overrides the image ENV, so the safer-looking '- SOURCE_COMMIT=${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}' would clobber a correctly stamped image whenever the host lacks the var. So setting SOURCE_COMMIT in Coolify now fixes prod WITHOUT a rebuild, which is the fastest thing to try. VERIFIED BY SABOTAGE, 5/5: restoring the original ??-chain, dropping the runtime pass-through, writing it in the clobbering '=' form, narrowing the placeholder set, and reverting isRealReleaseSha to read RELEASE_SHA alone each redden a named test. ⚠ THE FIFTH SURVIVED AT FIRST — no test covered the disagreement case (health says unattributable while Sentry events are correctly tagged), which is exactly the state that would send someone to fix a build arg that already works. Added that case. Full edge suite 6359 passed / 0 failed; deno lint + deno check clean; web tsc -b + eslint clean. DOCS: COOLIFY.md now records that the build arg was insufficient and gives the no-rebuild fix first. vault/10-ops/rollback.md gained a warning that GET /health cannot currently identify the running build, which that runbook's step 3 depends on — identify it from Coolify's deployment history instead; the same caveat is in the admin rollback runbook (src/lib/admin/runbooks.ts) since that is what gets read mid-incident. vault/10-ops/env-reference.md now documents the precedence and the placeholder fall-through. STILL passes:false on AC2/AC3, unchanged: both need a deploy or an env-var change on the Coolify side, then re-measure /health. What changed is that the fix no longer requires a rebuild. | 2026-08-12 AC2 MEASURED AGAINST PROD, AND IT STILL FAILS. GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns {"env":"production","release":"unknown","errorTracking":"enabled"}. So the declarative fix from 2026-07-19 - build.args GIT_SHA in docker-compose.coolify.yml - has NOT taken effect across every deploy since, and the value moved from the literal "dev" to "unknown", which is the same problem wearing a different word. AC1 is therefore NOT done: something in the Coolify build is not substituting the arg, and the next step is to look at how Coolify expands build.args rather than to add another instruction somewhere. AC4 IS CONFIRMED WORKING, and this is the part worth keeping: /health/ready now reports features.release as "unattributable: release="unknown" - none of RELEASE_SHA, COMMIT_SHA, SOURCE_COMMIT, GIT_SHA held a real commit, so errors cannot be tied to a build. Either the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg or none of those vars is set at runtime (see COOLIFY.md, US-2001)". That is the guard doing exactly its job - it names the defect, names the candidates, and points at the doc - and it is why this was measurable in one GET instead of another deep dive. AC3 (a real Sentry event carrying the release) is moot until AC1 lands, since the release it would carry is the broken one. ALSO MEASURED IN THE SAME CALL, recorded so the sweep is not lost: features.observability reports "set but not satisfied - every var is present; see the observability check", and features.hostWatchdog reports "unconfigured: no host watchdog has ever checked in" (US-2447 working as designed - the absence is visible). Schema is {expected:00589, applied:00589, status:match}.

userStories.title: Category grading criteria cover 8 of 20 garment categories — 12 categories grade with no category guidance at all
userStories.description: As a seller of a shirt, a coat or a skirt, I want the grader to know what matters on my category, because the ones that do get it are measurably better guided. Verified: ai-grading.ts:320 GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA has exactly 8 keys (jeans, pants, shorts, jacket, sweater, hoodie, t-shirt, dress) while src/lib/constants.ts GARMENT_CATEGORIES has 20 values. The 12 with no entry — shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf, other — fall through to the generic prompt with only DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE. Each of the missing ones has real category-specific signal the model is currently not told to look for: collar and cuff fray and yellowing on shirts, seam slippage and pulls on blouses, lining and shell separation and pilling on wool coats, zipper and hem and lining on skirts, and for footwear the outsole and midsole entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Every value in GARMENT_CATEGORIES has a criteria entry, or the fallback is made explicit and deliberate for the ones that genuinely have none.
Each new entry follows the existing voice: what is INTENTIONAL design on this category vs what is genuine wear, since that distinction is the whole point of the block.
The prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, not a silent edit — this changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once.
Golden-set cases exist for the newly-covered categories before activation, tagged so the eval report can slice per category.
Categories already covered produce byte-identical prompts, test-guarded, so the eval measures only the new coverage.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). 8 of 20 categories covered. Cheapest coverage win in the epic (prompt data, no schema), but it changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once so it needs a real eval cycle and per-category golden cases first. | 2026-08-08 AC1/AC2/AC5 DONE. AC3 IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS WRITTEN, and that is the finding. AC4 unchanged and still blocking.

AC1: all 11 remaining categories written (shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf). "other" is DELIBERATELY left uncovered and the absence is now pinned by a test: it is the value assigned when the category is UNKNOWN (garment-mapping.ts maps five of six garment types to it), so an "other" item may be any of the twenty and there is no honest guidance to give. Generic filler there would restate DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE and make coverage look complete while the real gap is upstream classification.

AC2: each entry draws the design-vs-defect line, and a test fails any entry that names only defects. The calls worth having are the ones a generic prompt gets backwards: midsole yellowing on sneakers is OXIDATION not soil (and some releases ship pre-yellowed), vachetta patina on a bag is supposed to darken, leather patina on boots is desirable aging, the molded footbed impression on sandals is permanent use that affects resale, and the fold crease at the worn hole is the defining signal on a belt.

AC3 CANNOT BE SATISFIED — verified, not assumed. The AC says ship through shadow -> golden-set eval -> canary. That lifecycle covers the SYSTEM prompt ONLY. GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA is interpolated into the per-image USER message by buildUserPrompt, and: an ai_prompt_versions row carries one prompt_text which becomes the system block, so no override can reach it; canary picks between two system texts; runEval overrides system text only, so the criteria are ambient on BOTH legs of its comparison; grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only AND reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path at all. Worse, PerImageAnalysis carries no version field, so PER_IMAGE_PROMPT_VERSION never reaches a grade record — bumping it would have looked like compliance and changed nothing.

So the change ships ENV-FLAG GATED (GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2, default OFF), which is the only gate the architecture offers and is the same pattern GRADING_BASELINES / GRADING_TAG_OCR already use. The eleven entries live in a SEPARATE map from the shipped eight, so byte-identity is a property of the file rather than a claim a reviewer has to diff. Composite grades attributed with a +cat2 suffix, appended last per the stated ordering rule.

AC5 DONE and strengthened: byte-identical for the eight with the gate ON, AND a no-op for all twenty with it OFF, so deploying this commit changes no grade. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED four ways — dropped a category entry (AC1 + coverage + disjoint reddened), flipped the gate to default-on (the no-op test reddened), duplicated a key into both maps (only the source-scan caught it, which is exactly why that test is a source scan and not behavioural), and moved +cat2 out of last position (ordering test reddened).

STILL passes:false: AC4 (golden-set cases for the newly-covered categories, tagged for per-category slicing) needs real human-corrected grades on those categories, which do not exist yet — the same bootstrap problem US-1997 Phase 2 has. Until then the flag stays off, and the flag being off is why that is safe rather than merely convenient. The structural fix for AC3 is US-2432.

Also corrected in the same commit: vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md claimed each block appends a suffix "so accuracy-tracking can attribute an era per block". The suffix records a block PRESENCE, not its CONTENT — editing FABRIC_CRITERIA still reports +fabric — and the per-image stage is not attributed at all. The note now carries the versioned-vs-not split as a third axis alongside trusted/untrusted. | 2026-08-08 AC3 IS NO LONGER IMPOSSIBLE. The note above says the shadow/eval/canary lifecycle CANNOT reach GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA because it is interpolated into the per-image USER message, and names US-2432 as the structural fix. That fix shipped as US-2438: category_criteria is now one of two blocks in a versioned registry (ai_prompt_block_versions, migration 00563), and runEval takes a blockCandidate that pins exactly that block while the system prompt stays active. So the eval-gate leg of AC3 is available today. TWO CAVEATS, both real: the SHADOW leg is still missing — grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only and reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path to run a category-criteria candidate through, and that is US-2438 AC2 rather than a wiring task here. And AC4 is unchanged and still blocking on its own: a per-category golden set has to come from real human-corrected grades on those categories, which do not exist yet. So GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 stays OFF and this story stays passes:false — what changed is that the gate is now buildable rather than architecturally unreachable. | 2026-08-09 CORRECTION: THE SHADOW BLOCKER NAMED IN THE NOTE ABOVE IS GONE. That note said 'the SHADOW leg is still missing — grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only and reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path to run a category-criteria candidate through, and that is US-2438 AC2 rather than a wiring task here.' US-2443 shipped that path today: services/edge-functions/src/lib/grading-shadow-per-image.ts re-analyzes every photo under a challenger per-image artifact and re-composites, and ai_prompt_block_versions gained is_shadow / shadow_sample_rate / shadow_daily_cap (migration 00566, HELD) specifically so a BLOCK candidate — which category_criteria is — can be sampled. So all three legs of AC3's lifecycle now exist: shadow (US-2443), eval gate (US-2438), canary (US-896). Recording this because a stale blocker is the specific failure this repo keeps paying for — someone picking this story up would have read the note above, concluded the lifecycle was architecturally unreachable, and stopped. WHAT STILL BLOCKS, unchanged and genuinely: AC4. A per-category golden set has to come from real human-corrected grades on those twelve categories, and they do not exist. Shadow can now MEASURE a category-criteria candidate on live traffic, but AC3 also requires the golden-set eval gate, and a gate with no cases for the new categories cannot pass or fail them — it would report on the eight already covered and say nothing about the twelve this story is about. Also note the per-image shadow path is OFF by default and costs a vision call per photo plus a composite per sampled submission (PER_IMAGE_SHADOW_DAILY_VISION_CAP), so running it is a spend decision, not just a flag flip. GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 stays OFF and this story stays passes:false on AC4. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (second half of the day): the HELD-migration claim in this story's notes is now STALE. Migrations 00563 and 00566 are on origin/main - verified with git ls-tree against a freshly fetched origin/main, not inferred - and the branch has zero unpushed commits. A held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word is no longer merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop on a branch that is not frozen. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: pushed is not applied. Whether the SQL has been run against prod is an operator fact this checkout cannot observe, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is the file that tracks it. Read that, not this prose. Recorded because prd-lint caught it the same hour the branch moved, which is the guard working as intended - it went unactioned for weeks before, and a stale freeze cost real sessions.

OPERATOR: on the prod DB host, install the backup cron and confirm a dump plus its .sha256 lands in the offsite bucket, then run restore-postgres.sh against a REAL offsite dump on a scratch host and record the measured timing (AC1, AC2, AC4). userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/DR][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. It is an ACTIVATION gap: a runbook step marked MANUAL that was never performed, and a checklist that honestly records it was never performed. AC3 says "either stand up wal-g PITR or amend the stated RPO to the honest figure — do not leave a documented RPO the infrastructure cannot deliver." WHY THIS WAS WORTH DOING WHILE THE REST IS BLOCKED: AC1, AC2 and AC4 all need someone on the prod host and are genuinely operator work. AC3 is the only half that is a claim rather than an action, and a runbook is read during an incident by someone who will not re-derive it — which is precisely when an overstated recovery point does its damage. The shape is worth remembering and is written into the callout: this is not a missing mechanism. The scripts exist, they work, the restore was drilled on 2026-06-12. userStories.title: Every alert channel is optional and silently no-ops — nothing proves anyone gets paged
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a SEV1 to reach a human. Today every channel degrades to silence when unconfigured. .github/workflows/uptime.yml:46 marks UPTIME_ALERT_WEBHOOK 'Optional' and scripts/ops/uptime-check.mjs:188 logs 'not set — skipping webhook channel' then continues. Edge-side, ops-events.ts:104-108 falls back to MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, which ENV_REFERENCE.md:168 marks as not set. ops-events.ts:242-244 records an ops_event.alert_undelivered metric when neither channel exists — a metric that itself has no alert. INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:42-46 asserts all three sources 'must point at the same on-call channel before launch', which is an instruction, not a verified state; LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264-268 leaves it unchecked. The only channel that works with zero config is the GitHub uptime issue fallback, which pages only if repo-watch mobile notifications happen to be on.
acceptanceCriteria: Set UPTIME_ALERT_WEBHOOK and MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, then RUN THE DRILL: break a target, confirm the message arrives on a phone, record the date in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md. Configuration is not evidence.

Make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric — fail at boot (or emit at critical) when production has no alert channel configured. A monitoring system that cannot page is worse than none, because it produces false confidence.
Confirm Sentry alert routing actually delivers (LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264) — see also the webhook dead-letter story, which routes ONLY to Sentry.
Measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target in INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:33 — a 10-minute GitHub cron plus jitter can consume most of it before a human is notified.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Alerting][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Pairs with the backup story: that one is about surviving a disaster, this one is about LEARNING there is one. Every other alerting improvement is worthless until these two secrets are set and drilled, because they are the last mile for all of them. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (partially — see below); AC1/AC3/AC4 still need you. AC2 asked to make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric, because 'a monitoring system that cannot page is worse than none, because it produces false confidence'. Added an 'alerting' feature group to env-validation: in PRODUCTION ONLY, a deploy with none of MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL set now reports DEGRADED on /health/ready and warns at boot, instead of the current state where every channel silently no-ops and nothing says so. Non-production is exempt via enabledWhen — a dev box has no business paging anyone, and warning there would train people to ignore the warning. ANY channel satisfies it, deliberately: the failure being caught is 'none of them', not 'not the one I expected'. I did NOT make it fatal at boot, which AC2 offered as an option. Refusing to start the edge because no webhook is configured would convert a monitoring gap into a total outage — strictly worse than the problem, and the opposite of the fail-open reasoning applied in US-2013. Degraded-and-loud is the right severity for 'we cannot tell you when things break'. STILL BLOCKED ON YOU and this is the launch-blocker part: AC1 (set the two secrets, break a target, confirm the message reaches a phone, record the date in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md), AC3 (confirm Sentry routing delivers) and AC4 (measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target). Configuration is not evidence and neither is a degraded-flag — this story stays open until a human has watched an alert arrive. Note US-2004's cron stall detector is now proven to detect, so it is queued up behind exactly this last mile. | 2026-08-02 MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, and fixed a reporting bug the measurement exposed. AC2's health surface WORKS: GET /health/ready reports features.alerting = "ok", so at least one channel (MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL) IS configured in prod. That is worth recording plainly, because AC1's framing assumed none were set. What is still unproven is whether a message actually ARRIVES — AC1's drill is about delivery, not configuration, and a configured webhook pointing at a dead endpoint reports "ok" here forever. THE BUG THE SAME CURL FOUND: features.observability returned the literal string "missing: " — nothing after the colon. The cause is a group whose satisfiedWhen fails while every var it LISTS is present. observability requires SENTRY_DSN plus a real RELEASE_SHA; the DSN is set, so the `miss` array is empty, and the message named nothing. An operator reading that at 3am is told something is missing and refused the name of it, which is worse than no line at all because it costs them the time to go looking. FIXED in computeFeatureReadiness and warnMissingFeatureGroups: when nothing is literally absent, the message now says the vars are all present and the check still rejected one, instead of an empty list. Two tests pin both paths — the all-present case, and the regression that a genuinely absent var must still be NAMED, which is the whole value of the line for every other group. WORTH BEING PRECISE ABOUT WHAT observability's DEGRADED MEANS, since "missing" read alarmingly and I nearly reported it that way: Sentry IS configured and IS receiving events. The group is degraded solely because RELEASE_SHA is "dev" — US-2001's problem, reported here as a second symptom. So the dead-letter path in US-2011 does reach Sentry; its events are simply untagged and unattributable to a commit. One Coolify rebuild with the GIT_SHA build arg clears BOTH this line and US-2001. STILL OPEN AND ALL OPERATOR WORK: AC1's drill (break a target, confirm the page lands on a phone, date it in the launch checklist), AC3 (confirm Sentry routing delivers — see US-2011, which routes ONLY to Sentry), AC4 (measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target; a 10-minute cron plus jitter can consume most of it before a human is notified). userStories.title: eBay Media API: video upload for listings
userStories.description: As a clothing seller, I want to add video to my listings to lift conversion. Today images are passed as external URLs only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls) and there is no video support. Integrate the eBay Media API (/commerce/media) to upload video and attach it to listings.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge can createVideo -> uploadVideo -> poll getVideo to a terminal status, and attach the resulting id via product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem

TRANSCODE DECISION MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN: eBay accepts .mp4 H.264/AVC only, and iPhones record HEVC by default. Either the client transcodes before upload, or the edge does, or HEVC is rejected with a message that tells the seller how to fix it. Silently failing on the most common input is not an option

PUBLISH-ORDERING DECISION MADE: processing is async and terminal status is not immediate, so either publish waits for LIVE, or publish proceeds without video and a later revise attaches it. Whichever is chosen, a seller never ends up with a listing that permanently lacks the video they added
BLOCKED is handled as a moderation outcome, not an error: it is terminal and expected, and the seller is told their video was rejected rather than shown a retry that cannot succeed
Video upload gets its own validation path. The US-276 hardening (validateImageUpload / stripImageMetadata) is image-only and does NOT cover video, which also carries GPS/EXIF-equivalent metadata
iOS/web can add a video during compose and see it reflected on the published listing
Respects the Media API POST rate limit (50 requests / 5 seconds, per user)
userStories.notes:
[P3][Edge/Media] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No Media API; images external-URL only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls). Nice-to-have; video is a real apparel conversion lever. 

INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18. Confirmed greenfield: no videoId / commerce-media / uploadVideo reference anywhere in services/edge-functions/src or src. Two findings change the shape of this story.

FINDING 1 — NOT SCOPE-BLOCKED, contrary to the obvious assumption. The Media API's createVideo requires sell.inventory, which is ALREADY in our production grant (ebay-client.ts:233). This story therefore does NOT depend on US-1421 (restricted-scope acquisition) and does not need a new seller consent round. Attachment is also on the path we already use: product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem — a sibling of the product.imageUrls we already send at ebay-client.ts:2163 — NOT a Trading-API-only feature as the AddItem/VideoDetails docs might suggest. So the integration surface is much smaller than the P3 implies: the eBay side is three new calls plus one extra field on a payload we already build.

FINDING 2 — THE REAL COST IS TRANSCODING, AND IT LANDS ON AC2. eBay accepts .mp4 MPEG-4 Part 10 / AVC (H.264) only. iPhones have defaulted to HEVC / H.265 since iOS 11 unless the user changed Camera > Formats to 'Most Compatible'. AC2 specifically promises iOS compose. So the single most likely real-world input is a format eBay will not accept, and the failure would surface late — after upload, as PROCESSING_FAILED — which is the worst place to discover it. Whoever picks this up should size the transcode decision FIRST, because it dominates the estimate: client-side transcode, server-side transcode (ffmpeg in the Deno container, which is a real image-size and CPU change on Coolify), or explicit rejection. The eBay calls are the easy part.

FLOW: createVideo returns 201 with the video id in the Location header -> uploadVideo sends the bytes -> poll getVideo. Statuses PENDING_UPLOAD -> PROCESSING -> LIVE, with BLOCKED and PROCESSING_FAILED as the other terminal states. BLOCKED is a moderation verdict rather than a fault, so it needs its own message; a generic retry there loops forever. Rate limit is 50 POSTs / 5s per user.

ALSO: AC3's original wording ('routes through the hardened fetch path') is misleading and has been rewritten. Our upload hardening is image-specific — validateImageUpload magic-byte-sniffs for images and stripImageMetadata drops EXIF/GPS from images. Neither does anything for an .mp4, which carries its own location metadata. Video needs a parallel validator, not a reuse of the image one.

NOT CONFIRMED, flagged rather than guessed: max file size, max duration, and how many videos a single listing accepts. eBay's docs point at Seller Center for those numbers and I could not retrieve them (developer.ebay.com WebFetch timed out twice; the above is from eBay doc search summaries, not the doc pages read directly). Confirm those three numbers against the live docs before implementing, since max-duration in particular shapes the compose UX. | 2026-08-12 THE THREE UNCONFIRMED NUMBERS ARE CONFIRMED, AND AC2 IS DECIDED. SOURCING CAVEAT FIRST, because it matters for how much weight to put on these: developer.ebay.com WebFetch timed out a THIRD time (createVideo, managing-video-media, uploadVideo, and the edp.ebay.com mirror all exceeded 60s), so these come from search-result summaries of those same doc pages plus eBay seller help, not from the pages read directly. Multiple independent results agreed on every number below, but re-check them against the live docs when you have a browser. MAX FILE SIZE: 150 MB, stated as exactly 157,286,400 bytes. MAX DURATION: 1 minute. VIDEOS PER LISTING: exactly 1 - so the compose UX is add-or-replace, never a gallery, which simplifies AC6 considerably. FORMAT: .mp4, H.264 video with AAC audio (eBay seller help also names .mov, but that is the web UI which transcodes for you; the API path is the mp4/H.264 one this story already assumed). A FOURTH FACT NOBODY HAD, and it is load-bearing: createVideo takes the byte size as metadata and the uploaded stream must match it EXACTLY, or the video does not upload and eBay may block the seller from uploading. PROCESSING_FAILED is documented as covering all three of corrupted / too large / size does not match the metadata - so a size mismatch surfaces as the SAME terminal status as a genuinely broken file, which means the edge has to know its own byte count precisely rather than trusting a client-declared length, and cannot distinguish the two after the fact. Status flow confirmed as PENDING_UPLOAD -> PROCESSING -> one of LIVE / PROCESSING_FAILED / BLOCKED, with BLOCKED documented as malware or the video moderation feature - i.e. a verdict, which is exactly what AC4 assumed. AC2 DECISION: TRANSCODE ON THE CLIENT THAT CAUSES THE PROBLEM, REJECT EVERYWHERE ELSE WITH A MESSAGE. Not server-side ffmpeg, and the reason is concrete rather than aesthetic: it would add ~70-100 MB to the Deno image and put a CPU-heavy transcode of a file up to 150 MB on a single-replica edge that per US-2010 still has no second replica and strands in-flight work for 6-15 minutes on every deploy. Buying a transcoder with that is the wrong trade. iOS has AVAssetExportSession natively and is the platform whose HEVC default creates the problem in the first place, so iOS transcodes before upload; Android has androidx.media3.transformer if it ever composes. Web and every other input gets sniffed and, if it is not H.264 mp4, REFUSED with a message naming the fix (Camera > Formats > Most Compatible on iOS, or export as H.264). That satisfies AC2 third branch honestly rather than silently failing on the most common input, which is the one thing the AC rules out. WHAT IS LEFT is the build itself and it spans three trees: the edge three-call flow plus product.videoIds (AC1), a video-specific validator since US-276 hardening is image-only and an .mp4 carries its own location metadata (AC5), the publish-ordering decision (AC3), and iOS/web compose (AC6), plus the 50-POST/5s per-user limiter (AC7). The estimate is no longer blocked on unknowns. | 2026-08-12 AC5 SUBSTANTIALLY DONE, AND I STOPPED DELIBERATELY BEFORE AC1 - the reason is the useful part. WHAT SHIPPED (0d0997c0 + follow-up): the codec gate. My own brief called AC5 greenfield and that was WRONG - validateVideoUpload has existed since US-1763 and already sniffs magic bytes, enforces a format allowlist, and caps bytes and duration, and grade.ts:543 already uses it. What it did NOT do is read the CODEC, which is the case AC2 is actually about: eBay takes H.264 only and an .mp4 container says nothing about what is inside it. isoBmffVideoCodec walks moov > trak > mdia > minf > stbl > stsd and checks each trak hdlr for "vide", skipping audio tracks - reading trak[0] blindly returns mp4a and calls a good H.264 file non-H.264. Fail-open on an unreadable header, matching the duration parser, because a faststart-less file hides moov behind mdat and refusing on unknown would block valid uploads. Exposed as an opt-in allowCodecs option so the existing US-1763 grading path does NOT start rejecting HEVC; the refusal message names Camera > Formats > Most Compatible, because catching this before a 150 MB upload is pointless if the seller is not told how to fix it. Nine cases, five sabotages each watched failing (hdlr check dropped, HEVC folded into the H.264 set, sample entry read four bytes early, the allowlist made inert, the allowlist inverted). WHY I STOPPED AT AC1 RATHER THAN CONTINUING: it needs somewhere to record the eBay video id and its status per listing, and listings.platform_fields is explicitly NOT that - 00113 own header says "The eBay draft keeps its dedicated columns" and the blob is keyed by NON-eBay platform. So AC1 needs a migration, and there is already ONE held migration (00590) blocking the push. Adding a second, for code that nothing can call until AC6 ships client compose, would be shipped-but-unwired with a prod-apply attached - the exact combination vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md exists to warn about. WHAT IS LEFT, in the order it should be built: AC1 (createVideo -> uploadVideo -> getVideo plus product.videoIds, and the storage decision - a new listings column or a small table), AC3 (publish proceeds WITHOUT the video and a DURABLE job attaches it on LIVE; the AC requirement that a seller never permanently lacks the video they added is exactly why it must be a locked job with retries and a terminal state, not a fire-and-forget promise), AC4 (BLOCKED is a moderation verdict, terminal, and needs its own message - PROCESSING_FAILED is a different one because the docs also use it for a size mismatch), AC7 (50 POSTs / 5s per user), AC6 (iOS/web compose). THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL FOR WHOEVER BUILDS AC1: createVideo takes the byte size as metadata and the uploaded stream must match EXACTLY, and a mismatch surfaces as the same PROCESSING_FAILED as a corrupt file - so the edge must compute its own byte count and never trust a client-declared length. VERIFIED: deno lint 1505 files, deno check, full edge suite 6566 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-15 THE HELD-MIGRATION WORDING ABOVE IS HISTORICAL, RESOLVED. The owner applied every outstanding migration and pushed main; origin/main and local are the same commit, PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md lists no HELD section, and the session-context hook reports none. So nothing in this story is waiting on a prod apply and the branch is not frozen on its account. Recorded as an appended correction rather than by editing the sentence, because these notes are append-only and prd-lint resolves by segment order. WHY THIS GETS ITS OWN NOTE INSTEAD OF BEING LEFT TO ROT: HELD is not a status, it is an instruction to stop, and a stale one tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not. That has cost real sessions in this repo (US-2286's 2026-08-09 note says so explicitly). VERIFY IT RATHER THAN TRUST THIS: curl -fsS https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready | jq .schema — US-2603 added a missing[] listing versions this build ships that the database never recorded, which is the check a bare status:match cannot do. | 2026-08-15 STATUS CORRECTION, formal: no migration named in this story is held. Every outstanding migration is applied to prod and main is pushed (origin/main == local). The previous segment said this in words prd-lint does not recognise, so the guard kept warning; this one uses the token it reads.

userStories.title: Authenticity tell coverage follows brand-pack order, not counterfeit prevalence
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want tell coverage driven by what actually gets faked, because an add-on a seller can buy for any brand currently has real depth for three (CANONICAL_TELLS: louisvuitton, coach, gucci) and legacy free-text {tell, detail} rows for the rest, which brand-authenticity.ts coerces to category 'other' with no redFlag and which therefore contribute almost nothing to the verdict. The 37 migrations that mention authentication_tells were written in brand-pack order — luxury first because that pack came first — not from any ranking of counterfeit exposure. Nike, adidas, Supreme, BAPE, Moncler, Canada Goose, The North Face and Patagonia are among the most-counterfeited apparel brands in the world and sit in packs whose tells were never structured. US-2139 fixes the SHAPE and the depth of what we have; this story fixes WHICH BRANDS we invest in next and why.
acceptanceCriteria: A written, sourced prioritization of brands by counterfeit exposure crossed with our own submission volume, recorded in the vault as a decision note rather than in a commit message.
The top-ranked brands get structured, sourced, verified tells with redFlags — not free-text rows.

The add-on's purchasability is reconciled with coverage: a brand with no verified tells either cannot be purchased for, or is sold with an explicit stated limitation. Silent degradation to generic reasoning is not acceptable for a paid add-on.
Coverage is measurable: a query or admin view reports verified-tell count per brand so the gap is visible instead of anecdotal.
No claim about detection accuracy is published anywhere until the authenticity golden set (US-2131) can support it.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Authenticity/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Coverage today follows brand-pack authoring order, which put luxury first. Nike/adidas/Supreme/BAPE/Moncler/Canada Goose/TNF/Patagonia sit in packs whose tells were never structured. Pairs with US-2139 (shape) — this one is about which brands get invested in next. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED except AC1's sourced ranking and AC2's seeding (both deferred with reasons). Commit 2c95f59, no migration.
THE PREMISE WAS UNDERSTATED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE MAIN RESULT. The story says coverage follows brand-pack authoring order. The real state is worse and more precise: ALL 179 seeded authentication_tells payloads across the packs use the LEGACY {tell, detail} shape, and ZERO use the structured one. coerceTell maps a legacy entry to category "other" with no redFlag, so those 179 payloads are PROSE THE PROMPT READS AND THE VERDICT CANNOT USE. On top of that CANONICAL_TELLS holds 7 structured tells across 3 brands, every one sourced to "seed:... (unverified — review in admin)". So the distinction that actually matters is between HAVING TELLS and HAVING USABLE TELLS, and almost the entire corpus is on the wrong side of it. A test pins the 179/0 split and instructs the next reader to UPDATE its floor rather than delete it when US-2139 re-shapes the rows.
THAT REFRAMED THE STORY. The useful question was not "which brands to prioritize" but "what does a PAID add-on owe a buyer when it has almost nothing to check against" — because before this, a brand with no usable tells still produced a confident-looking assessment from generic reasoning and NOTHING in the output said so. That is the part a buyer would object to, and it needed no new data to fix. AC3 DONE and it is the substance of this commit. AC4 DONE: classifyTellCoverage reports level/total/actionable/categories, which is the per-brand measurement the AC asked for.
DECISION TAKEN AND RECORDED (vault/20-domain/authenticity-coverage-priority.md, type: decision, revisit_by 2026-10-31): DISCLOSE AND CAP RATHER THAN BLOCK THE SALE. Two answers were defensible — refuse the purchase when coverage is thin, or sell with a mandatory disclosure plus a confidence cap. Took the second: a general construction-and-finishing assessment has real value to some buyers even without brand tells, and what is NOT defensible is charging for it while IMPLYING brand-specific authentication. purchaseDisclosure() returns a non-null string the offer surface cannot render without. Blocking remains available and is a PRODUCT call, not an engineering one — revisit if buyers report the disclosure is insufficient.
CAPS: 0.6 with no tells, 0.75 with inert ones, composing by MIN with US-2218's reference cap. Two coarse bands again rather than a gradient, same reasoning: we know an assessment with nothing to check against rested on generic reasoning and we do NOT know how much that costs; the golden set (US-2131) is what should set real numbers. Never raises. The limitation text is written in terms of what WE hold, never the garment — a test asserts it contains no counterfeit/fake/suspect/inauthentic/replica.
ONE TRAP AVOIDED, worth knowing: the new `tells` parameter on normalizeAuthenticityAssessment is OPTIONAL and absent means "NOT MEASURED", not "none". Defaulting it to [] would have classified every existing caller as having zero coverage and silently capped them all — the exact silent-degradation failure this story exists to end, reintroduced from the other direction. A test pins that an existing caller passing no tells is byte-identical.
AC1 DEFERRED, WITH THE REASON WRITTEN DOWN. The AC asks for a SOURCED ranking by counterfeit exposure crossed with our submission volume. Half is available — volume is in our own database and scripts/brand-style-coverage.mjs --db already shows that query's shape. The other half is not: counterfeit-exposure figures need external sources I could not obtain from this sandbox, and a ranking assembled from recollection would be precisely the failure this corpus documents as its most dangerous (the RN 17257 / Longchamp trap — a real record, the right brand string, completely the wrong company). So the RANKING is deliberately NOT recorded; the METHOD is, plus one observation needing no external source: the packs' own headers repeatedly note that Nike, adidas, Supreme, BAPE, Moncler, Canada Goose, The North Face and Patagonia are heavily counterfeited, and every one of them sits in a pack whose tells were written in the legacy shape. That is where the corpus itself points for the first pass.
AC2 DEFERRED (seeding verified tells is the same sourcing project). AC5 HOLDS: nothing in this commit publishes an accuracy number, and the caps are explicitly documented as placeholders until the golden set can measure them.
VERIFICATION: 4703 edge tests pass, 15 new in authenticity-coverage_test.ts; the 8 failures are the same pre-existing imagescript-FFI / network-timeout sandbox artifacts confirmed against a clean tree in US-2210. deno lint clean; zero new type errors.

userStories.title: Authentication tells are text-only — there is no known-genuine reference imagery to check a font, stitch or stamp against
userStories.description: As a reviewer or a grading model, I want a picture of what genuine looks like, because half our tell taxonomy is VISUAL and cannot be verified from prose. Verified: brand-authenticity.ts defines 11 tell categories including stitching, font, stamp, hardware and construction, and CANONICAL_TELLS's own text admits the gap — the Louis Vuitton stamp tell says to 'compare letter spacing/shape to a KNOWN-GENUINE REFERENCE' and no such reference exists anywhere in the system. A tell whose check instruction depends on an artifact we do not have is not a checkable rule. This is distinct from US-2139 (tell DEPTH and counterfeit-side modelling) and US-2138 (decoder cross-checks): this is the missing evidence layer both of those assume.
acceptanceCriteria: A reference-image store exists for tells, with per-image provenance (source, rights, brand, style, tell category) — reference imagery must be licensed or owned, never scraped into a public surface.
Reference images are private by default and served only through signed URLs, consistent with the submission-images posture; they are NEVER placed in the public item-photos bucket.

The authenticity pass can present the relevant reference alongside the suspect region for a comparison, and a tell with no reference is explicitly marked as unverifiable-visually rather than silently scored.
Seller-submitted photos are NEVER promoted into the reference corpus without explicit consent — the few-shot exemplar privacy rule (US-1067) applies with equal force here.
Absence of a reference widens limitations and lowers confidence; it must not produce a confident verdict from generic reasoning.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Authenticity/Evidence] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Distinct from US-2139 (tell depth + counterfeit-side modelling) and US-2138 (decoder cross-checks) — this is the missing EVIDENCE layer both assume. Self-evident from CANONICAL_TELLS's own text: the LV stamp tell instructs a comparison against a known-genuine reference we do not have. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED (table starts empty; seeding real imagery is the sourcing half). Commit a0fc163, migration 00500 (HELD). AC1 DONE: authenticity_references stores brand_key, style, tell_category, storage_path, caption, source, rights, confidence, verified. RIGHTS IS NOT NULL WITH NO DEFAULT — a reference cannot exist without a stated licence/ownership basis, and a nullable column would have made omitting provenance the easy path. Scraped brand or marketplace imagery is precisely what that column exists to prevent. AC2 DONE: PRIVATE bucket (public=false, load-bearing not a default), reads only via createSignedUrl with TTL 900s matching the submission-images rule, never getPublicUrl, never item-photos; a test pins all of it. AC3 DONE: assessTellVerifiability pairs each tell with the references for its category; an unreferenced VISUAL tell is marked in the prompt as "report it as UNVERIFIED rather than as a confirmed match or a discrepancy" — it is NOT dropped, because the claim is still useful context, it just cannot carry a confident finding. AC4 DONE: no FK to submission_images, no code path, and a test asserts the EXECUTABLE SQL never names it. AC5 DONE: referenceLimitation names the specific categories we could not check, and referenceConfidenceCap caps confidence.
THE DESIGN DECISION THAT MATTERS: ABSENCE LOWERS CONFIDENCE, IT NEVER RAISES SUSPICION. A visual tell we cannot check is a gap in OUR evidence, not a mark against the garment. So the cap is applied to authenticity_confidence and verdict_confidence ONLY and deliberately NOT to counterfeit_risk — converting our own incompleteness into an accusation about a seller's item would be the worst possible failure mode for this feature. A test asserts the limitation text contains none of counterfeit/fake/suspect/inauthentic. The cap composes by MIN and can only lower (grading-engine contract).
THE CAP IS TWO COARSE BANDS, NOT A FORMULA (0.6 when no visual tell is referenced, 0.8 when some are). A fine-grained curve would imply a precision we do not have: we know a visual tell without a reference was reasoned about from model memory rather than checked, and we do NOT know how much that costs. Two honest bands beat a fabricated gradient, and the numbers should move once the authenticity golden set (US-2131) can measure them.
ONLY VISUAL CATEGORIES REQUIRE IMAGERY — stitching, font, stamp, hardware, construction. A date code, serial, packaging or material tell is read, measured or handled, so marking it unverifiable would dilute the limitation text until reviewers learn to skip it. That restraint is what keeps the disclosure meaningful.
STRICTLY ADDITIVE: with no references the tells block is byte-identical to the US-1769 grounded block (test-pinned), and normalizeAuthenticityAssessment's new verifiability parameter defaults to empty so every existing caller and test is unchanged.
WHAT IS NOT DONE: the table is EMPTY. Acquiring licensed or owned known-genuine photographs is a sourcing project, not a coding one — the same shape as the RN gap (US-2211), the era provenance gap (US-2212) and the extended-sizing gap (US-2215). Until rows exist, every visual tell is unverifiable, which is exactly what the code now says out loud instead of quietly guessing. Also NOT done: presenting the reference image ALONGSIDE the suspect region in a reviewer UI. referenceCaptionBlock deliberately ships only the CAPTIONS to the text pass — inlining reference photos into every authenticity call would multiply its cost for a benefit nobody has evaluated. signReferenceUrl exists precisely so the reviewer-facing surface can be built separately.
TWO SELF-INFLICTED BUGS, both caught and worth remembering. (1) The confidence cap first landed in normalizeAuthenticityAssessment while referencing a variable defined in its CALLER — deno check caught it. Fixed by passing verifiability in as a defaulted parameter, which is the better shape anyway because the pure function is now testable on it. (2) TWO TESTS FAILED ON THEIR OWN DOCUMENTATION: the prose explaining "never getPublicUrl" and "no link to submission_images" contains those exact strings, so a naive substring check flagged the code that implements the rule. The tests now strip comments first — and the SQL stripper matches through the CLOSING QUOTE (';) rather than the first semicolon, because comment prose contains semicolons. That is the identical trap that broke the US-2216 pack parser; if you write a third source-grepping test, strip comments first and terminate string-bearing statements on the quote.
VERIFICATION: 4688 edge tests pass, 19 new; the 8 failures are the same pre-existing imagescript-FFI / network-timeout sandbox artifacts confirmed against a clean tree in US-2210 (a mid-run count of 15 was my regression and is fixed). deno lint clean; no new type errors. 00500 not executed against a live DB (no Docker), so it is proven by parsing only. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-07-29: the HELD-migration claim above is STALE and should not be acted on. Every migration this story names is on origin/main and applied to prod (schema at 00503); PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is empty and the branch is not frozen. | 2026-08-15 WHY THIS IS STILL OPEN WITH EVERY AC MARKED DONE, recorded because an all-ACs-done story that stays open reads as an oversight and this one is not. The five criteria are about the MECHANISM - a store with mandatory provenance, private-by-default serving, the unverifiable marking, the no-seller-photos rule, and the confidence cap - and all five hold. The story's TITLE is about the outcome: authentication tells are text-only. They still are, in production, because authenticity_references is empty and nothing in a checkout can fill it. Licensed or owned reference imagery is a sourcing project, exactly like US-2215's plus/petite/tall seeding: the dimension is the prerequisite, not the deliverable. Closing on the mechanism would put a story in the archive whose stated problem is unsolved for every real submission, and the next reader looking for why tells are still text-only would find it marked passes:true. THE SHAPE TO WATCH, since this is now a live instance of it: with an empty table every visual tell reports UNVERIFIED and the confidence cap sits at 0.6 on every authenticity pass carrying one. That is the designed behaviour rather than a bug - absence lowers our confidence and never raises suspicion - but it means the feature is currently paying its whole cost and returning none of its benefit. Seeding even a handful of references for the most-counterfeited brands would change that, and US-2219's own note observes which brands those are. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: references seeded for at least the visual categories on the brands that carry the most counterfeit risk, with rights recorded, and one authenticity pass observed presenting a reference rather than reporting UNVERIFIED.

userStories.title: brand_styles covers a fraction of the KB's brands — model-level identity is what sets price and it is mostly missing
userStories.description: As a seller, I want GradeThread to name the MODEL, not just the brand, because 'Barbour jacket' and 'Barbour Bedale' are different listings at different prices. Verified: 70 migration statements insert into brand_knowledge (about 177 canonical brands) but only 36 insert into brand_styles, and the style rows that exist concentrate on flagship lines. brand_styles already has the right shape for this (style_name, aliases, product_line, department, category, visual_fingerprint, fabric_tech, era, msrp_band, keywords) — it is under-populated, not under-designed. The knock-on is real: without a style row there is no visual_fingerprint for the extractor to disambiguate against, no msrp_band for comping, and no style-level anchor for the condition baseline (see the companion story on garment_baselines).
acceptanceCriteria: Style coverage is prioritized by actual submission and listing volume per brand, not by KB seeding order — name the query that produced the priority list.
Every new style row carries visual_fingerprint and keywords populated (those are what make a style row usable by the extractor), plus source_url and confidence.
A golden-harness case per seeded style asserts the style is recoverable from a representative description/photo-derived field set, extending the existing brand-knowledge-golden_test.ts pattern.
Styles are seeded as DATA (brand_styles rows via migration) reusing the existing pack conventions — no new code path per brand.

The decoder bar is NOT relaxed to hit style coverage: a style name recovered from a graphic or a season notation is informational, never a decoder. Record refusals in vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-negative-findings.md.
Migrations follow the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Grading/Knowledge] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). 70 brand_knowledge inserts vs 36 brand_styles inserts. brand_styles is under-populated, not under-designed — the shape (visual_fingerprint, fabric_tech, msrp_band, keywords) is already right. | 2026-07-28 PARTIAL — AC1 DONE, premise CORRECTED, AC2/AC3/AC4 deliberately left open as sourcing work. Commit 86ecbaa, no migration.
THE PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THAT IS THE MAIN RESULT. The story says brand_styles "covers a fraction of the KB's brands" and cites "70 migration statements insert into brand_knowledge but only 36 insert into brand_styles". Those are FILE counts, not coverage — one migration seeds many brands. Counted properly: 188 brands in brand_knowledge, 706 brand_styles rows across 178 brand keys, so 178 of 188 brands (about 95%) already have at least one style, median 4 each. Ten have none and two have exactly one. Bulk seeding was therefore the wrong response, and had I taken the premise at face value it would have driven a large amount of unnecessary and unsourced data entry.
AC1 DONE: scripts/brand-style-coverage.mjs IS the named query, in both forms it can take. With --db it ranks uncovered brands by ACTUAL volume (inventory_items + submissions brand counts, the only place volume exists) and joins that against current style counts. Without a database it does a static pass over the migrations and reports coverage only — and it REFUSES to rank, saying so explicitly, rather than substituting seeding order, which is the exact substitution AC1 forbids. I could not run --db here (no prod access from this sandbox), so the volume ranking is built and unexercised; the static mode is what produced the numbers above.
COUNTING THE PACKS IS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS, and this is the reusable lesson. THREE tuple layouts occur across the packs: one tuple per line ("  ('zara', ..."), tuple on the values line ("values ('nike', ..."), and tuple opened with the key on the next line ("values (\n  'lululemon', ..."). My first parser handled only the line-anchored form. It reported 53 unparsed brand_knowledge statements, counted 162 brands instead of 188, and produced a "brands with no styles" list that WAS WRONG (it omitted carharttwip and mis-stated the totals). The script now reports unparsed statements on every run, and a test asserts the unparsed count is ZERO across all five brand tables — because a silent floor is exactly how a wrong premise gets believed. If you write another script that counts these packs, make it report what it could not parse.
GUARD SHIPPED: brand-style-coverage_test.ts fails when a NEW brand ships a brand_knowledge row with no styles (the regression that would quietly widen the gap), AND fails when an allowlist entry outlives the gap it names, so the list cannot rot into a lie that hides the next real regression. Same shape as rls-guard / cron-registry. It also pins the coverage ratio above 90% so the "a fraction" reading cannot quietly return.
AC2/AC3/AC4 NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY. Seeding style rows means writing style_name, visual_fingerprint, keywords, source_url and confidence. Producing those from model memory with invented source_urls is precisely the trap this corpus already documents as its most dangerous failure (vault: "RN 17257 is not Longchamp" — a real federal record, the right brand string, completely the wrong company). I will not manufacture sourced-looking brand data. This is a sourcing project needing real references, exactly like the RN coverage gap in US-2211 and the extended-sizing gap in US-2215.
WHICH GAPS ARE REAL, so the next person does not seed the wrong ten. The uncovered brands are aeropostale, carharttwip, eddiebauer, gildan, guess, hanes, harleydavidson, hollister, nautica, poloralphlauren. NOT ALL OF THESE ARE GAPS: Gildan and Hanes are BLANKS MANUFACTURERS whose garments have no model identity worth naming, and a style row for them would be noise in every prompt that resolves their pack — their absence is probably correct and should not be "fixed". Aeropostale, Hollister and Guess are mall brands whose value does not turn on the model. The four genuinely worth seeding are EDDIE BAUER, NAUTICA, HARLEY-DAVIDSON and POLO RALPH LAUREN, each of which has named, collectible lines. That reasoning is recorded in the allowlist comment and in vault/20-domain/brands/brand-taxonomy-overview.md.
AC5 holds trivially (no decoder was seeded because no style was seeded). AC6 not applicable (no migration).
VERIFICATION: 4656 edge tests pass, 5 new in brand-style-coverage_test.ts; the remaining failures are the same pre-existing imagescript-FFI / network-timeout sandbox artifacts confirmed against a clean tree in US-2210. deno lint clean.

userStories.title: No international size-system conversion, and no plus / petite / tall / big-and-tall charts as first-class
userStories.description: As a seller listing an EU 42 jacket or a women's 18W, I want the size read off the tag mapped to the system a US buyer searches in, because a size the buyer cannot interpret is functionally an unsized item. Verified: the SizingChart shape (sizing-charts.ts) has department (Women/Men/Unisex/Kids) and a free-text garment scope — there is no size-system dimension. International equivalence lives only as per-brand prose in note strings (the 00456 pack shows the pattern: BAPE charts embed 'JP L (approx US M)' INSIDE the size label because there was nowhere structured to put it, and 00455 notes 'IT 42' at least announces itself). Extended sizing is likewise absent: plus, petite, tall and big-and-tall have their own grading-relevant fit and failure points and no chart carries them.
acceptanceCriteria: A size-system dimension (US / UK / EU / IT / FR / JP / AU / intl-alpha) is added to the chart shape and to brand_size_charts, so an equivalence is structured data rather than a substring inside a size label.

A deterministic conversion layer maps between systems where the mapping is genuinely regular, and REFUSES where it is brand-specific — the decoder-bar discipline applied to sizing: a wrong conversion is worse than none, and refusals are recorded in the vault.
Plus, petite, tall and big-and-tall are representable and seeded for the brands that actually sell them, rather than folded into the standard chart.
Existing per-brand prose that encodes a conversion inside a size label (BAPE, luxury IT sizing) is migrated to the structured field with the prose kept as the note.
Migration follows the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Grading/Sizing] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Evidence is in the packs themselves: 00456 embeds 'JP L (approx US M)' inside the size LABEL because the shape had nowhere structured to put an equivalence, and 00455 notes IT sizing 'at least announces itself'. Both are workarounds for a missing dimension. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED except AC3's seeding half (a sourcing gap, see below). Commit 56247cd, migration 00499 (HELD, generated). AC1 DONE: size_system (US|UK|EU|IT|FR|JP|AU|alpha) and size_class (standard|plus|petite|tall|big_and_tall|maternity) are now fields on SizingChart and columns on brand_size_charts. 137 of 292 charts have a readable system. AC2 DONE AND IT IS THE HEART OF THE STORY: the conversion table was DERIVED FROM THE CORPUS, not recalled. Every size label stating both sides was extracted and checked for contradictions, which yielded exactly four clean rules: FR|Women +32, IT|Men +10, IT|Women +36, UK|Women +4 — six data points each, zero contradictions. TWO tests guard it in both directions: one re-derives all four from SIZING_CHARTS and fails if the corpus stops agreeing, another fails if a conversion is ever added with no paired data behind it. So the table cannot drift away from its own evidence, and it cannot grow by assertion. AC4 DONE, with a deliberate limit: the structured field is added BESIDE the prose and the prose is KEPT. A test asserts 00499 touches neither `rows` nor `note`. Re-authoring the 115 charts that encode their system inside the size label is a separate, riskier change — those strings are what the model actually reads, so rewriting them deserves its own eval rather than riding along here. AC5 DONE (idempotent / EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 00499 same commit / self-record footer / PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md).
THE REFUSALS ARE THE FEATURE, and every one has a reason recorded in vault/20-domain/size-system-conversions.md. EU: no paired data anywhere in the corpus, and EU womenswear numbering differs by country — a German 38 and an Italian 38 are not the same garment and a tag reading 'EU' does not say which. JP: the corpus's only JP mapping is BAPE's, which 00456 explicitly records as a BRAND fact (BAPE runs small), so 'JP L = US M' is true of BAPE and not of Japan; generalising it would mis-size every other Japanese label. alpha: S/M/L is not a numbering system, and Essentials' 'M drapes like a US L' is a DESIGN fact (00456), not a conversion. UK/FR men's and AU: no paired data — UK men's tailoring often equals US, and 'often' is not a rule the corpus vouches for. Any result <= 0: the offset has been applied outside the range it was derived from, which is inventing a size. A refusal returns null, meaning 'we do not know', and the caller shows the original label.
DETECTION READS, IT DOES NOT GUESS. detectSizeSystem returns a system only where the labels state one. A chart of bare numbers stays NULL because a bare '6' could be US or UK and nothing in the row says which — and NULL means 'not recorded', never an implied US. A chart mixing systems across its rows is also NULL rather than reduced to one. A test walks the whole corpus asserting no chart claims a non-alpha system without a label saying so.
AC3 IS HALF DONE, DELIBERATELY. The dimension is representable, which was the shape gap the AC identified. It is almost entirely UNPOPULATED, and that is accurate rather than lazy: the corpus contains EXACTLY ONE extended chart — Talbots, whose garment scope reads 'Misses (US numeric 2-18) / Petite (0P-16P) / Plus (14W-26W)'. That single chart IS the folding this dimension exists to end, so detectSizeClass returns null for it rather than collapsing it to one class that would be false for two thirds of its rows. Seeding real plus/petite/tall/big-and-tall charts for the brands that sell them is a SOURCING project of the same kind as the RN coverage gap in US-2211 — the dimension is the prerequisite, not the deliverable. Do not read the empty column as a bug.
TWO THINGS THE NEXT READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) NOTHING READS THESE COLUMNS YET. This story lands the dimension and the conversion layer; putting a converted US size onto a certificate is a later, deliberate step, and it should go through the same trusted-block discipline as US-2213's verified size. (2) A test bug worth remembering, the second of its kind this session: I first asserted labelNumber('W30 L32') === 30. The CODE was right and the TEST was wrong — 'W30' is a waist measurement in inches, not a place in a national size sequence, and returning 30 would let it be handed to an offset and come back as a meaningless 'US 26'. The test now pins the refusal and explains why.
VERIFICATION: 4650 edge tests pass, 27 new (25 in size-systems_test.ts, 2 added to sizing-chart-parity_test.ts); the 8 failures are the same pre-existing imagescript-FFI / network-timeout sandbox artifacts confirmed against a clean tree in US-2210. deno lint clean; zero type errors in the new module. 00499 was NOT executed against a live DB (no Docker here), so it is proven by generation + parsing only. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-07-29: the HELD-migration claim above is STALE and should not be acted on. Every migration this story names is on origin/main and applied to prod (schema at 00503); PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is empty and the branch is not frozen. | 2026-08-15 SAME SHAPE AS US-2218, recorded so the pair are read together rather than each looking like an oversight. Every AC is marked DONE and the story is still open on one thing: AC3's seeding half. The size-system dimension, the four corpus-derived conversions and the refusals all shipped; what is missing is CHARTS - the corpus holds exactly one extended chart (Talbots), so plus, petite, tall and big-and-tall are representable and unpopulated. That is a sourcing project, not code, and the dimension was the prerequisite rather than the deliverable. THE ONE THING WORTH RE-CHECKING BEFORE ANYONE SEEDS: the previous note records that NOTHING READS THESE COLUMNS YET - the conversion layer exists and no surface calls it. So seeding charts would populate a dimension that still changes nothing a seller or buyer sees. If this story is picked up, do the reading half in the same pass or the seeding is shipped-but-unwired with a sourcing bill attached. Putting a converted US size on a certificate is the deliberate step named there, and it should go through the same trusted-block discipline as US-2213's verified size.

userStories.title: Single edge replica with no graceful shutdown — every deploy strands in-flight work for 6-15 minutes
userStories.description: As a seller mid-batch, I do not want a deploy to silently stall my work. SCALING.md:8-9 states the edge runs as a single Coolify container so a deploy is a brief full outage, and :14 marks 2+ replicas as MANUAL/not done. There is no signal handling at all — no SIGTERM / addSignalListener / shutdown anywhere in main.ts (1638 lines) — so in-flight requests are KILLED, not drained. Recovery is by sweep rather than drain: flipdesk-autolister.ts:114 JOB_STALE_MS = 6min, :117 BATCH_STALE_MS = 15min, reclaim crons at */5. The ~30s outage documented at SCALING.md:26-30 is understated for anyone whose job was running: their work sits in 'running' for 6-15 minutes before reclaim.
acceptanceCriteria: Scale to 2+ replicas — the prerequisite is already cleared (Supavisor pooling done, SCALING.md:22).
Add a SIGTERM handler that stops claiming NEW jobs and lets in-flight ones finish before exit.
Verify by deploying during an active grading batch and confirming no job enters the stale-reclaim path.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Ops/Reliability] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive.
