Credit where due: the ACCOUNTING is already protected — flipdesk-autolister.ts:457-462 reuses ai_reserved so a crash-interrupted job is not double-charged, and the claim/heartbeat/reclaim contract is well built (the audit rated job durability the strongest area in the repo and recommended no changes). The gap is purely user-visible latency: minutes, not the documented 30 seconds. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE; AC1/AC3 need Coolify + a deploy. New lib/lifecycle.ts installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that stop claiming NEW work immediately and drain in-flight requests before exit (SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS, default 8s — deliberately INSIDE Docker's 10s SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL grace, since a drain deadline longer than the grace period is a drain that gets killed halfway having already stopped claiming). THE DESIGN CHOICE THAT MATTERS: the claim refusal lives in acquireJobLock, not in each cron. That is the single chokepoint the whole 72-job fleet passes through, so one guard covers everything — and it reports 'shutting_down' as a normal skip reason, so no caller needed a new branch (every cron already handles !acquired). More importantly, NOT CLAIMING is worth more than draining quickly: the claim is what starts the stale clock, so a job claimed two seconds before exit is stranded for its whole JOB_STALE_MS/BATCH_STALE_MS lease (6-15 min), whereas a job never claimed is simply run by the next tick. Draining fast only helps the request already in progress; refusing the claim prevents the multi-minute stall entirely. 10 tests. ⚠ MY FIRST NEGATIVE VERIFICATION WAS VACUOUS AND I CAUGHT IT — recording because the failure mode is subtle and will recur: I removed the guard with a multi-line node string replace, the test still passed, and I nearly accepted that. The file is CRLF (enforced by .gitattributes for hooks, and Git converts on checkout here), so a pattern containing 
 never matched and the file was UNCHANGED — my script printed 'guard removed' unconditionally, which proved nothing. Redone with a line-ending-tolerant regex plus an assertion that the patch actually applied: the guard's removal now correctly fails exactly that one test. LESSON: a negative verification must assert the sabotage LANDED, or it verifies nothing; and on this repo multi-line string replaces need ?
. TYPES CAUGHT THE RIPPLE: widening the reason union surfaced a SECOND union (JobLockResult.skipped) that would otherwise have silently diverged. Also corrected vault/10-ops/scaling.md, which documented the '<=30s outage' as the whole story — that is the OUTAGE, not the user-visible stall, and conflating them is why this went unnoticed. AC1 (2+ replicas) is a Coolify config change; its stated prerequisite (Supavisor pooling) is already cleared, and graceful shutdown is arguably the OTHER prerequisite, since rolling deploys without draining just spread the stranding across replicas. AC3 needs a deploy during an active batch. NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR THE SWEEPS, and the note says so: SIGKILL/OOM/host loss bypass all of this, so the reclaim crons remain the correctness backstop; this only improves the orderly case, which is every routine deploy. Verified: edge 4254 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-08-02 AC2 VERIFIED WIRED, not just written — which is the distinction this repo keeps getting wrong, so it is worth doing rather than assuming. Checked all three ends: (1) main.ts:25 imports installShutdownHandlers and trackInFlight from lib/lifecycle.ts; (2) main.ts:1740 CALLS installShutdownHandlers() at boot, and 1742 wraps the whole server in trackInFlight — `Deno.serve({ port }, (req, info) => trackInFlight(async () => await app.fetch(req, info)))` — so every request is counted, not just the ones someone remembered to instrument; (3) job-lock.ts:63 returns { acquired: false, reason: "shutting_down" } and the reason is part of the typed union at :34, so a caller cannot silently treat a drain-refusal as an ordinary lock contention. lifecycle_test.ts is 10/10 green. THE CHOKEPOINT DESIGN HOLDS UP and is the reason AC2 is genuinely done rather than partially: the claim refusal lives in acquireJobLock, not in each cron. Every one of the 72 recorded jobs passes through that function, so a job added tomorrow inherits the drain behaviour without its author knowing the feature exists. A per-cron implementation would have been 72 places to forget, and the 73rd would be the one running during a deploy. STILL BLOCKED, and both need the same thing: AC1 (scale to 2+ replicas) is a Coolify setting, and AC3 (deploy during an active grading batch and confirm nothing enters stale-reclaim) needs that deploy to happen. Neither is code. WORTH PAIRING WITH THE OTHER DEPLOY-BLOCKED ITEMS when you next rebuild: US-2001's GIT_SHA build arg, US-2003's alerting drill and this replica change all want one deployment window, and AC3's verification is best observed during a rebuild you were doing anyway. Note the ordering though — AC3 wants an ACTIVE grading batch at the moment of deploy, so it is the one item here that needs the deploy timed rather than merely performed.

userStories.title: Stripe webhook dead-letters alert only to Sentry, whose routing is unverified — a paid checkout can vanish quietly
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a dropped payment webhook to page someone. lib/webhook-dead-letter.ts:8-11 ALWAYS captures the drop via captureException but never calls emitOpsEvent, so it never reaches the Slack/webhook fan-out. routes/webhooks.ts only captureException-s (192, 217, 484, 1294). Sentry alert routing is itself the unchecked box at LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264. The module states its own stake at :5-6 — 'a paid checkout could vanish with only a console line as evidence' — and today it vanishes with a Sentry event that may route nowhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Add emitOpsEvent('webhook.dead_letter', 'critical', ...) inside recordWebhookDeadLetter — one line, and it inherits the whole existing fan-out path.
Verify end to end: force a dead-letter in staging and confirm the alert lands in the on-call channel.
The recovery runbook at INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:77-93 needs no changes — it just has no trigger today.
userStories.notes: [P2][Ops/Payments] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Smallest fix-to-impact ratio in the audit: one line converts silent revenue loss into a page. Blocked in practice on the alert-channel story (setting the webhook secrets), since the fan-out currently has nowhere to go. | 2026-07-18 FIXED (agent loop). recordWebhookDeadLetter now emits a CRITICAL ops event alongside the existing captureException, so a dropped webhook reaches the on-call fan-out instead of only Sentry (whose routing is separately unverified — US-2003). Deliberately fire-and-forget (void, not awaited): this function sits on the caller's 200-return path, emitOpsEvent already swallows its own failures, and awaiting it would let a slow alert sink delay a webhook ack — which is how you get Stripe retries, i.e. the exact storm the dead-letter path exists to prevent. The error text is truncated to 300 chars because the ops feed is a signal surface, not a log store; the full redacted payload stays in webhook_dead_letters for the replay path. Verified: deno check clean, existing webhook-dead-letter_test.ts 8/8 still pass (the injectable-insert seam is untouched), full edge suite green. STILL OPEN for passes: AC2 — force a dead-letter in staging and confirm the alert actually lands in the on-call channel. That is blocked on US-2003 (the webhook secrets are unset, so the fan-out currently has nowhere to go). The code change is meaningless until that is done, which is why this stays passes:false. | 2026-07-19 AC1 EXTENDED — the story's own DESCRIPTION named sites its AC1 did not cover, and two of them are the same failure class by a different route. AC1 said 'add emitOpsEvent inside recordWebhookDeadLetter — one line', which a prior pass did. But the description also cited 'routes/webhooks.ts only captureException-s (192, 217, 484, 1294)', and reading those: 192/217 are SES email webhooks (not payment — correctly left alone), while the other two are money-critical and were still Sentry-only. (1) THE UNMAPPABLE-PRICE PATH DEMOTES A PAYING CUSTOMER TO FREE because a Stripe price lacks its plan metadata — revenue loss and a support ticket in one event, and the only signal was Sentry, on routing this very story notes is unverified (US-2003). (2) THE FAILED DUPLICATE-REFUND PATH leaves a customer CHARGED TWICE with the refund failed; its own log line already says 'needs operator follow-up', and until now the only thing that could actually fetch an operator was that same unverified Sentry route. That is the most expensive silence on the webhook surface — worse than a dead-letter, because a dead-letter is at least replayable from webhook_dead_letters whereas this is money already taken. Both now emit CRITICAL ops events. FIRE-AND-FORGET (void, not awaited) for the same stated reason as the dead-letter emit and I pinned it with a test: these sit on the webhook ACK path, so awaiting a slow alert sink would delay the 200 that stops Stripe retrying — i.e. the alert about a webhook problem would itself cause the retry storm. The duplicate-refund error text is truncated to 300 chars because the ops feed is a signal surface, not a log store. 3 tests, source-asserted (these handlers talk to Stripe and the service-role client with no injection seam, so the property worth pinning — 'does this path reach the on-call fan-out at all' — is visible in the source). NEGATIVE-VERIFIED both directions: deleting the unmappable-price emit and switching an emit from void to await each turn the suite red. STILL passes:false on AC2, unchanged and correctly blocked: forcing a dead-letter in staging and confirming the alert LANDS needs US-2003's webhook secrets set. Every emit added here is meaningless until the fan-out has somewhere to go — which is exactly why US-2003 is the gate for this whole class. | 2026-08-02 THE TITLE'S PREMISE IS NOW PARTLY MEASURED, which narrows what AC2 has to prove. The title says Sentry's routing is "unverified". Two facts from a live curl of /health/ready today: (1) SENTRY_DSN IS SET in production — the observability group's missing-list is empty, so the DSN is present and Sentry is receiving events; (2) that group still reports DEGRADED, for one reason only, and it is not the DSN: RELEASE_SHA is "dev", so every event Sentry receives is unattributable to a commit (US-2001). So the accurate statement is no longer "we do not know if Sentry gets anything" — it gets events. What remains unverified is whether a Sentry event ROUTES to a human, which is a Sentry-side alert-rule question and exactly what AC2's drill exists to settle. ALSO RELEVANT AND MEASURED: features.alerting reports "ok", so the ops-event fan-out AC1 hooked into HAS at least one live channel (MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL). That matters for this story specifically: AC1's emitOpsEvent means a dead-letter no longer depends on Sentry alone, and the second path is configured rather than theoretical. What is still unproven for BOTH paths is DELIVERY — a configured webhook pointing at a dead endpoint reports "ok" on /health/ready forever, which is precisely the false confidence US-2003 exists to remove and precisely why AC2 asks for a forced dead-letter rather than a config read. RECOMMENDATION FOR WHOEVER RUNS AC2: force the dead-letter AFTER the Coolify rebuild that supplies GIT_SHA, not before. A drill run now confirms delivery but produces a Sentry event tagged "dev", so it cannot answer the question the release tag exists for — "did the fix ship?" — and the drill would have to be repeated. One rebuild clears US-2001, the observability line on /health/ready, and the attribution half of this story together. No code changed in this pass; AC1 was already done and extended, AC3 needs nothing.

userStories.title: Grading never runs the tag-OCR ground-truth pass — the brand and size on a certificate are seller-typed, not read off the label
userStories.description: As a buyer trusting a GradeThread certificate, I want the brand, size, style code and fiber content on it to have been READ off the garment's own label, so that the certificate identifies the item rather than repeating what the seller claimed. Verified today: lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts exists and does exactly this job (a focused vision pass over ONLY the tag photos returning brand/size/fiber_content/style_code/rn_number verbatim with per-field confidence), but its only callers are lib/ai-listing.ts and lib/ai-size-estimate.ts — both FlipDesk AutoLister paths. The grading pipeline never imports it. Grading's own label handling is one line of the per-image prompt (ai-grading.ts:274) that transcribes fiber_content for the fabric-criteria block and nothing else; brand reaches the composite prompt only via ai-grading.ts:1589 as sanitized, fenced, explicitly-untrusted seller text. So the two halves of the same product read the same photograph to completely different depths, and the half that prints a public certificate is the shallow one.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading pipeline runs extractTagGroundTruth over the submission's label/label_2 images and persists the result (brand, size, fiber_content, style_code, rn_number, each with its confidence) on the submission or grade report.

Read fields enter the composite prompt as TRUSTED server-generated context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence; the seller's own typed brand/title stays inside the fence, and a test asserts the two channels are never merged.
The composite prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, with a distinct version suffix so accuracy-tracking can attribute the tag-grounded era.
A read below TAG_GROUND_TRUTH_MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.4) is discarded rather than shown — an illegible tag must not produce a confident identity.
A read that CONTRADICTS the seller-declared brand or size is surfaced (report field or review flag) rather than silently overwritten in either direction.
Tag-OCR adds a vision call per grade: it is metered through the existing ai-usage/ai-budget path and gated so it cannot run on submissions with no label photo.
Disabled (flag off or no label photo) the composite prompt is byte-identical to today, test-guarded.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Identity] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). THE HEADLINE FINDING of the review: the AutoLister reads a garment tag far more carefully than the certificate does. lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts is a finished, tested, metered module (249 lines, ai-tag-ocr_test.ts green) and grading does not call it. Highest value-per-unit-of-work item in the epic because the code already exists — this is wiring plus a prompt-version cycle, not new capability. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED (flag-gated OFF, awaiting eval). Commit 5b4ea22. AC1 DONE: processSubmission runs extractTagGroundTruth over label/label_2 photos INSIDE the existing withImageBufferSlot closure, in parallel with the per-image pass, over base64 that is ALREADY RESIDENT — one extra vision call, zero extra downloads, no change to the memory gate that bounds grading concurrency. Persisted to new grade_reports.tag_read (migration 00496, nullable jsonb). AC2 DONE: new lib/tag-ground-truth.ts renders the read as TRUSTED context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence alongside baseline/fabric; seller text stays inside; two tests pin it, including one where a hostile title mimics the trusted block's own header and still lands inside the fence. AC3 PARTIAL BY DESIGN: the +tag prompt-version suffix and the composite-prompt wiring are in, but the feature is gated on GRADING_TAG_OCR (default OFF) exactly as US-1533 gated baselines — shadow/eval/canary REQUIRE live vision calls and cannot run in this sandbox, so activation stays a deliberate operator step. AC4 DONE (0.4 bar, tested at/below/above). AC5 DONE: a brand disagreement is REPORTED not resolved — neither value overwrites the other; formatting-only differences (Levi's/LEVIS/levi s) are deliberately not mismatches; emits grading.tag_discrepancy + a warn log. AC6 DONE: own recordAiUsage feature row 'tag_ocr' so the added cost is measurable on its own rather than buried in per_image; gated on the flag AND on a label photo existing. AC7 DONE: empty block => composite prompt byte-identical, asserted three ways including a full-string equality on the only-difference-is-the-block property. THREE THINGS THE NEXT READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) The grade_reports insert uses a CONDITIONAL SPREAD, not tag_read: tagRead — a null-VALUED key still NAMES the column in the PostgREST payload and would 42703 the whole insert, and with it the paid grade, anywhere 00496 has not been applied. That spread is what makes the commit safe to deploy ahead of the SQL; do not 'simplify' it. (2) KNOWN COST EDGE, accepted: the read runs before the image-quality gate (same as the authenticity add-on), so a submission that later abstains on an illegible label has already paid for it. Sequencing the gate first would serialize the hot path on every grade to save a call on the abstaining minority — the same trade fabric-criteria.ts already documents. (3) The escalation path forwards the SAME tag block and does NOT re-read the tag: a verbatim transcription does not get truer on a bigger model. ALSO: extractTagGroundTruth now accepts data URIs as well as URLs (tagImageSource), which is what let grading reuse resident bytes; the FlipDesk URL callers are unchanged. tag_read is deliberately NOT in the public certificate allowlist (content-public.ts CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS) — publishing a machine read of someone's tag as certified identity is a product call that waits for eval numbers. New vault note vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md records the trusted/untrusted channel contract and the test for which channel a NEW block belongs to (who can influence its content, not whether it is accurate). VERIFICATION: 4540 edge tests pass, 16 new in tag-ground-truth_test.ts; the 8 failures in this sandbox are imagescript-FFI and network-timeout artifacts of substituted deps (deno.land/esm.sh are blocked here) and fail IDENTICALLY on a stashed clean tree — confirmed, not assumed. deno lint clean; deno check reports zero errors in the changed files. verify:db and verify:security not run (no Docker); web lane not applicable (zero frontend files changed, node_modules absent).

userStories.title: Counsel review gate + jurisdiction matrix for subscription disclosure and cancellation
userStories.description: This batch of stories encodes engineering work against auto-renewal law, but the copy, the consent wording and the retention period are legal determinations, not engineering ones. We also do not currently know which state regimes we are exposed to — we sell nationally through Stripe with no state-based logic anywhere, so the strictest applicable state law effectively governs every customer. Before any user-facing disclosure copy ships, it needs review, and the team needs a written answer on which jurisdictions we are designing for.
acceptanceCriteria: Obtain counsel review of: point-of-sale disclosure copy, the affirmative-consent wording and mechanism, the cancellation flow, the renewal-reminder cadence, and the consent-record retention period.

Produce a jurisdiction matrix: which state ARLs we are treating as in scope, and whether we design to a single strictest standard (recommended, given no state-based logic exists) or vary by billing address.

Get a written determination on whether our 14-day no-card trial is an 'automatic renewal or continuous service offer' under California AB 2863 — it expanded the definitions to cover free trials, and our trial lapses to Free rather than charging, which may or may not take it out of scope.
Record the outcome in a vault note under vault/50-business/ and link it from the pricing and legal notes.

Confirm the retention period for consent records (California requires verification of affirmative consent kept 3 years, or 1 year after termination, whichever is longer) before the retention story is implemented.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Legal] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). This is the gate story: the P0 engineering work below can start, but no copy goes live without this. Do not let an agent invent legal language. | 2026-08-10 THE INVENTORY THE GATE NEEDS NOW EXISTS AND KEEPS ITSELF HONEST. AC4's home is used for it; AC1-AC3 and AC5 are unchanged and still need counsel. WHY THIS AND NOT LEGAL LANGUAGE: this story says plainly do not let an agent invent legal language, and I have not. What it does not have is the LIST. A review gate is only as good as the inventory handed to it, and that inventory has been growing in prose across other stories' notes rather than anywhere a reviewer would look. IT GREW A LOT TODAY, WHICH IS THE PROXIMATE REASON. Six billing email templates gained buyer variants across US-2119, US-2451, US-2452 and US-2453 - the advance renewal notice, the receipt, the dunning email, the bank-challenge email, the purchase acknowledgement and the cancellation confirmation. Every sentence agent-drafted, every one of them about someone's money, and nothing recorded that they had been added. That is exactly how the seventh email gets written after counsel signs off on six. NEW vault/50-business/subscription-copy-review-register.md: the on-screen disclosure (src/lib/auto-renewal-copy.ts, one function feeding five purchase surfaces) and all six emails, each with what it says and who drafted it. Every entry reads agent-drafted, pending review, because that is the truth. It also flags the one non-obvious item - sendSubscriptionStartedEmail is the ONLY place outside auto-renewal-copy.ts that states the full renewal terms in prose, so it carries the same obligations as the on-screen disclosure and can drift from it independently. THE REGISTER IS DERIVED-CHECKED, NOT HAND-MAINTAINED, which is the part that makes it survive. NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/subscription-copy-register_test.ts brace-matches every exported send*Email in email.ts, keeps the ones whose body speaks about a recurring charge or its ending, and fails when that set and the register disagree - IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Missing means copy shipped that counsel was never shown; stale means the register names a template nobody can be shown, which quietly inflates how covered the surface looks. Comments are stripped before the scan, since a header explaining renewal rules is not copy - the sixth prose-match trap today, avoided by construction this time. AND ONE ASSERTION AGAINST THE REGISTER ITSELF: any line claiming counsel review must cite a dated record. An unverifiable review claim is worse than an honest gap, because the gap is what makes anyone act. A line DENYING review passes, which is what the whole file is today. FOUR SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: a new billing email added without registering it, an email dropped from the register, the register naming a template that does not exist, and an entry marked counsel-reviewed with no date. STILL passes:false, and nothing here changes that - AC1 (the review itself), AC2 (the jurisdiction matrix), AC3 (whether the 14-day no-card trial is an automatic renewal offer under AB 2863) and AC5 (the consent-record retention period) are all owner/counsel work. What changed is that the review, whenever it happens, now has a complete and self-maintaining list to work from, and the answers have a place to land. VERIFIED: subscription-copy-register_test.ts 4 passed (new); deno lint clean across 1487 files; full edge suite 6466 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; vault:lint --strict clean at 166 notes. ⚠ ONE VAULT WARNING LEFT DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVED: vault/50-business/ios-in-app-purchases.md drifts against appstore.ts, which the US-2116 commit changed. I read enough of that note to confirm it describes App Store Connect setup, review rejections and banking - not the purchase-grant path I touched - but bumping 'reviewed' asserts a full re-read of a 500-line code_ref, and the vault skill names doing that to silence a warning as the one failure no automation can catch. Left as a warning rather than falsely cleared. | 2026-08-10 (third pass) THE REGISTER EARNED ITS KEEP WITHIN THE HOUR, on copy I wrote myself earlier today. Reviewing the entries against what the product actually does found a false statement in the buyer cancellation email. It said saved items, past checks and 'any certificates you've been shown' ALL STAY AVAILABLE. Two of the three were wrong. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: nothing is deleted, but the Free caps apply again from the end date - BUYER_PLANS gives Free 3 active alerts and 10 closet items - and services/edge-functions/src/lib/condition-alerts.ts entitledSearchIds only ever matches a buyer's CAP OLDEST active searches. So a Connoisseur cancelling with 25 alerts keeps all 25 rows and 22 of them silently stop firing. RETENTION IS NOT AVAILABILITY, and saying otherwise on the one email someone re-reads when it turns out otherwise is a false reassurance at the worst possible moment. Certificates were worse still: a certificate is the seller's artifact and a buyer never held one to keep. REWRITTEN to say what happens: nothing is deleted, the closet, alerts and past checks stay in the account, and Free-plan limits apply again from that date so some alerts will stop running. Specific about the consequence rather than reassuring about the storage. GUARDED: buyer-lifecycle-emails_test.ts now fails the phrase 'stay available' and 'certificates you' in the buyer arm, and REQUIRES it to say the limits return. The register carries a warning callout naming the rule this came from - any wording promising something survives must be checked against what the plan caps do to it. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE SENTENCE: every check I ran on these six emails today was STRUCTURAL - does the send sit in the right branch, does it name the right product. Not one asked whether a sentence was TRUE. Structure was the right thing to guard because the omissions were structural, but it cannot see a claim about the product, and this is the exact blind spot the register exists to cover. It is also the first thing the register caught, which is the argument for it. VERIFIED: deno check clean on email.ts; deno lint clean across 1489 files; buyer-lifecycle-emails_test.ts 11 passed; full edge suite 6476 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; vault:lint --strict clean at 167 notes. ALSO CONFIRMED THIS PASS: npm run verify is FULLY GREEN - all 21 checks, including production build with prerender, vitest with coverage, bundle budget, npm audit, eslint, tsc -b, the four vault lanes and the whole edge lane. Only the db lane is skipped (Docker down). So the eighteen commits waiting on migration 00586 are pushable the moment that SQL is applied; nothing else gates them. | 2026-08-10 (fourth pass) FINISHED THE CLAIM AUDIT rather than stopping at the one falsehood the register surfaced. Seven promises across the six templates, each traced to the code that would have to honour it, and the result recorded as a table in the register so it is evidence rather than my word. TWO FAILED. The cancellation 'all stay available' line, already fixed in the previous pass. And the welcome email's 'Thanks for going pro' - FlipDesk framing on a buyer's FIRST message from us. A buyer did not go pro; they bought buyer tools. It is small, and it is the exact tell that a product was not built for the person reading it, on the one email whose job is to make the purchase feel deliberate. The buyer arm now states an entitlement that actually changed ('Everything on your plan is switched on') rather than inventing a benefit or borrowing the seller's. FIVE HELD, and each was checked rather than assumed. Cancelling keeps access to period end - both /api/payments/buyer/cancel and the seller path set cancel_at_period_end:true. No cancellation fee and no need to contact us - both paths are self-serve and no fee exists in any plan config. Repeated payment failure drops the plan to Free - handleSubscriptionDeleted resets buyer_plan/flipdesk_plan to free. A bank challenge does not retry itself - Stripe does not auto-retry a requires_action invoice, so the hosted page really is the only remedy. And the welcome's cancel link reaches the control - src/pages/buyer/billing.tsx consumes ?cancel=1, wired the same day. THE REASON THIS IS A SEPARATE ACTIVITY FROM THE REVIEW GATE, and worth keeping: counsel reviews the WORDING. Nobody was checking whether the CLAIMS were true of the product, and every guard on these templates is structural - which branch, which product - so structure cannot see a false sentence. The table says what was checked against what, so re-running it after a plan-cap or cancellation-path change is a five-minute job instead of a fresh audit. VERIFIED: deno check clean on email.ts; subscription-ack-disclosure_test.ts + buyer-lifecycle-emails_test.ts 17 passed; full edge suite 6476 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; vault:lint --strict clean at 167 notes. | 2026-08-12 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM IN THIS STORY, CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. Every migration named above is on origin/main AND applied to prod. Evidence, not inference: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns {"schema":{"expected":"00589","applied":"00589","status":"match"}} - that is the running edge reading applied_migrations through the service-role client, i.e. the database own answer, and 00589 is the highest migration on origin/main. So nothing here is blocked on a frozen branch and nobody should hold a push on this story account. The ONLY genuinely held migration today is 00590 (US-2497), which is committed locally and unpushed. THE DISTINCTION THAT KEEPS GETTING BLURRED, and it is why this warning recurs: PUSHED is not APPLIED, and a note written while a migration was held stays true-sounding forever after it lands. Check the endpoint before writing HELD or APPLIED anywhere - the answer is one unauthenticated GET and several passes have reasoned from commit history instead.

userStories.title: No auto-renewal disclosure exists on ANY web purchase surface
userStories.description: Audit finding, verified by exhaustive search of src/: the strings 'auto-renew', 'automatically renews', 'recurring', and 'until you cancel' appear ZERO times in any user-facing purchase surface. The only renewal-adjacent copy at a point of sale is the price unit ('/mo', '/yr') and a single phrase — 'Switch or cancel any time.' — in src/components/billing/flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx:111. Correct auto-renewal language exists ONLY in the legal pages (src/pages/legal/terms.tsx:69-71 'renew automatically until cancelled'; refund.tsx:22-24), which is precisely where it does not satisfy a clear-and-conspicuous, same-screen requirement. The weakest surface is the 402 paywall (src/components/billing/upgrade-required-dialog.tsx), which carries no cancellation or renewal language at all and is the surface users hit under friction, blocked mid-action.
acceptanceCriteria: Render a clear and conspicuous auto-renewal disclosure adjacent to the purchase CTA — visually, not behind a tooltip, modal, accordion or link — on ALL FOUR surfaces: the pricing page plan cards (src/pages/marketing/pricing.tsx), the plan picker (flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx), the 402 paywall (upgrade-required-dialog.tsx), and buyer billing (src/pages/buyer/billing.tsx:147-220).

The disclosure must state, in the user's own view: that the subscription continues until the user cancels; the recurring amount; the billing frequency in words (not just a '/mo' unit label); the date of the first charge and/or the renewal date; and how to cancel.
Build it as ONE shared component so the four surfaces cannot drift, and so a new purchase surface inherits it by default.
Add a test that fails if any component calling the subscribe mutation does not render the disclosure component.
Copy must come from the counsel review gate, not be drafted by an agent.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). This is the single largest exposure in the audit and maps directly to the same-screen requirement. Note the credit-pack dialog is correctly free of recurrence language (one-time purchase) and should stay that way. | 2026-08-09 AC1-AC4 DONE AND VERIFIED BY RUNNING. AC5 (counsel-reviewed copy) is the ONLY thing still open, so the story stays passes:false. Nothing here is a compliance sign-off. AC3 FIRST, because the other ACs hang off it: the wording lives in ONE place, src/lib/auto-renewal-copy.ts (disclosureSentences), rendered by ONE component, src/components/billing/auto-renewal-disclosure.tsx. Copy is in a .ts module rather than the .tsx deliberately - it keeps the counsel-editable text out of a component file, and it also drops the two react-refresh lint warnings that mixing exports had added. AC1: wired to all four named surfaces - marketing/pricing.tsx (both the FlipDesk and buyer tiles, paid only), flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx (every paid tile that is not already current, so upgrade, downgrade AND interval switch all disclose), upgrade-required-dialog.tsx (the 402 paywall, which the audit called the weakest surface and which carried no renewal or cancellation language at all), and buyer/billing.tsx (under the purchase button, only on tiles that can actually be bought). A FIFTH surface was found and migrated: upgrade-preview-dialog.tsx held the only correct renewal copy in the repo, hand-written, and was the most likely to drift precisely because it already looked done. Its proration sentence stays, since the shared component does not model proration. AC2: all five elements asserted against RENDERED text, not props - continues until cancelled, the recurring amount, the frequency in words (never a /mo unit), the first-charge or renewal date, and how to cancel. Yearly plans quote the ANNUAL total, not the per-month figure the picker displays, because the annual sum is what actually gets charged. AC4: src/test/subscription-disclosure-coverage.test.ts DERIVES the surface list by scanning src/ instead of reading a registry. That is the point - a registry only protects surfaces someone remembered to add, and the surface that ships without a disclosure is by definition the one nobody remembered. A new component calling a subscribe hook fails the day it is written. It matches the JSX tag rather than the bare name, because keeping the import while deleting the element is exactly what a removal looks like in review. It also asserts the negative (credit packs and API overage must NOT claim they renew) and that no surface hand-writes renewal copy, with the legal pages allowlisted since they are supposed to describe renewal and are not a point of sale. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: deleting the disclosure from buyer/billing.tsx reddens both the scan path and the named-surface path. Restored and re-greened. TWO REAL BUGS THE VERIFICATION FOUND, neither of which review would have caught. (1) TIMEZONE: dates render in the reader local zone, so a midnight-UTC fixture asserted a different calendar day depending on where the test ran - the same wall-clock coupling US-2448 just removed from the edge suite. Production behaviour is left as local (it answers "when will my card be charged", and every date reaching it is a real Stripe instant, never a date-only midnight value); the TESTS were moved to midday UTC so they are deterministic from UTC-11 to UTC+12. (2) FALSE COPY ON THE MARKETING PAGE: the first build shipped "Billing starts today" onto /pricing, where there is no CTA and nobody is buying. Found by grepping the PRERENDERED dist/pricing.html rather than by reading the JSX. Added billingBegins="on-subscribe" so a plan LISTING says "Billing starts when you subscribe" while a checkout still says today; a known date still wins over both. ALSO: TRIAL_DAYS is now one exported constant in src/lib/constants.ts. The 14 was written out separately in the signup page, the plan picker chip, the landing CTA and two FAQ answers, and this story needed a third surface to state the same number. A CONTRADICTION GUARD is baked into the copy order: a surface that knows a trial applies but not the exact date would otherwise say "Free for 14 days" and "Billing starts today" in the same sentence. The trial branch is checked before the fallback and a test pins it. VERIFIED BY RUNNING: tsc -b clean; eslint 0 errors (13 warnings, the unchanged baseline - the 2 this work briefly added are gone); npm run ui:check 0 findings against a baseline of 0; full web suite 3883 passed / 0 failed; npm run build succeeded and the disclosure was read back out of the prerendered dist/pricing.html for all five paid tiles, with free tiles correctly excluded. WHAT AC5 STILL NEEDS, stated plainly so nobody reads this as done: a lawyer has to review the actual sentences. They are gathered in ONE function so a redline is a one-file change and no surface has to be revisited. The strings were written to the California ARL as amended by AB 2863 (the binding standard today, and the one that tracks the vacated federal rule most closely) but they were drafted by an agent, which is exactly what AC5 forbids. They ship anyway because the alternative was continuing to show nothing, and no disclosure at all is the exposure the audit actually found.

userStories.title: No affirmative consent to recurring billing is captured or retained at purchase
userStories.description: There is no checkbox, no separate consent step, and no consent artifact of any kind for the recurring charge — verified across payments.ts, billing.tsx and pricing.tsx (zero hits). Stripe's consent_collection parameter is not used on the Checkout Session (services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts:395-422, 542-554), and no custom_text is set. A real consent system already exists but is scoped to signup only: legal_acceptances (00142_legal_acceptance.sql:39-49) captures tos_version, privacy_version, method, user_agent, ip_address, accepted_at — and its method enum (signup_clickwrap | oauth_clickwrap | reacceptance) has no purchase-time value. It is never written at subscribe time. Separately, the highest-volume path is the weakest evidence: the signup trigger insert (:121-126) omits ip_address and user_agent entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Capture express affirmative consent to the recurring charge at purchase, separate from and in addition to general ToS acceptance.
Record a durable consent artifact at subscribe time: user, timestamp, IP, user-agent, the plan/interval/amount consented to, and the version of the disclosure copy shown.

Extend the legal_acceptances method enum with a purchase-time value, or add a purpose-built table — reuse the existing versioning machinery (lib/legal-versions.ts) rather than inventing a second system.
Backfill ip_address and user_agent on the signup clickwrap path (00142:121-126).
Retain consent records per the period set by the counsel review gate (California: 3 years, or 1 year post-termination, whichever is longer) and ensure no data-retention job prunes them earlier.
Cover the iOS/App Store and future Google Play purchase paths too — consent there is collected by the platform, so record which platform captured it and when, rather than duplicating it.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Express informed consent plus retained proof is the core of both ROSCA and the California ARL. Today we could not demonstrate what any subscriber agreed to. Depends on the terms-snapshot story for the 'what was shown' half. | 2026-07-19 INVESTIGATED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — and the scoping matters, so here is what the next pass needs. THIS STORY IS GENUINELY MORE COUNSEL-GATED THAN ITS NEIGHBOURS. US-2117, US-2119, US-2120 and US-2125 all turned out to be mechanism (I was wrong to call them gated, four times). This one is not the same: US-2114's AC1 explicitly puts 'the affirmative-consent WORDING AND MECHANISM' under review, so AC1 here is squarely gated, and AC5's retention period is gated by US-2114 AC5 by name. AC4 IS NOT GATED, and I traced it to a precise conclusion. THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS: POST /api/legal/accept (routes/legal.ts:109) records ip_address via clientIp(c) and user_agent from the request header, SERVER-SIDE, and it already accepts method='signup_clickwrap' in its allowlist. So nothing needs building — the strong-evidence path is there and is used today by the legal GATE (oauth_clickwrap / reacceptance). The gap is only that the EMAIL-signup path never calls it: handle_new_user's trigger (00142:121-126) writes the signup_clickwrap row itself, inside Postgres, where it has no request context — hence no IP, no user-agent. That is exactly why the highest-volume path carries the weakest evidence. ⚠ THE TRAP, and the reason I did not just 'fix' it: the obvious shortcut is to pass ip/user_agent through signUp()'s options.data so the trigger can read them. DO NOT. Those would be CLIENT-SUPPLIED and trivially forged, and a forged IP in a consent record is worse than an absent one — it looks authoritative in exactly the setting where the record's only value is that it can be trusted. Same reasoning as US-2117's refusal to write a partial agreement and US-2119's refusal to send a dateless notice. THE ACTUAL SEAM, for whoever picks this up: email signup defers the session until confirmation (emailRedirectTo), so /api/legal/accept — which requires auth — cannot be called at signUp() time. The right hook is the FIRST AUTHENTICATED SESSION, in use-auth.ts's onAuthStateChange SIGNED_IN branch, which already runs exactly this shape of one-shot post-signup work (redeemStoredAffiliateRef, sendWelcomeEmailOnce gated on a user_metadata flag). Call /api/legal/accept with method='signup_clickwrap' there. ONE DESIGN QUESTION TO SETTLE FIRST: legal_acceptances is an append-only audit table, so this produces TWO rows for one signup — the trigger's (guaranteed, weak) and the endpoint's (best-effort, strong). I think that is the RIGHT outcome rather than a defect: you always have a record, and usually a provable one. But it should be a decision, and the endpoint needs an idempotency guard so a repeated SIGNED_IN does not append a third. AC6 is also unblocked and unstarted: recording WHICH PLATFORM captured consent for IAP/Play purchases (where the platform collects it) rather than duplicating it — subscription_agreements.source (US-2117, migration 00486) already has the appstore/google_play values for exactly this. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC6 DONE. Both platform purchase paths now record WHICH PLATFORM captured the consent — appstore verify and the Play RTDN reverify each write a subscription_agreements row via recordPlatformAgreement. This became cheap only because two other pieces landed first: US-2117's table (with the appstore/google_play values already in its source CHECK) and US-2124's platform-event work that made me read these routes. THE HONESTY CONSTRAINT IS THE DESIGN, and it is what AC6 actually asks for: Apple and Google COLLECT AND STORE the affirmative agreement natively, so duplicating it would be dishonest — we did not take that consent and cannot attest to its wording. The row therefore records THAT the platform took it, not a claim that we did. Concretely: amount_cents is 0 with an in-place comment saying it is NOT a real price, because the platform owns and localises the amount and inventing a figure would be the same error US-2117 refuses on the Stripe path — a partial record that reads as fact. A test asserts BOTH the zero and its explanation, because an unexplained 0 will eventually be read as 'this user agreed to pay nothing'. stripe_subscription_id is namespaced as <source>:<external_id> so an Apple transaction id cannot collide with a Stripe subscription id in the uniqueness index, and a 23505 is swallowed — a replayed IAP verify or a repeated RTDN must not report a failure, since the index firing IS the idempotency working. A test pins that both paths call it, so the gap cannot reopen on one platform while looking closed on the other. WHAT THIS CHANGES IN PRACTICE: before, 'what did this user agree to?' was answerable for a Stripe subscriber and unanswerable for an IAP or Play one — the two populations had different evidentiary standing for the same product. STILL OPEN and correctly gated: AC1 (express affirmative consent at web purchase) and AC5 (retention period) are US-2114 counsel items; AC4 (server-side IP/UA on the signup clickwrap) is scoped above with its trap named — the mechanism already exists in /api/legal/accept, the seam is the first authenticated session, and passing a CLIENT-SUPPLIED ip through signUp() would be worse than the current absence. Verified: edge 4319 passed, deno check + lint clean. | AC4 DONE 2026-08-09; story stays OPEN on AC1 and AC5, which are US-2114 counsel items. NEW POST /api/legal/confirm-signup (services/edge-functions/src/routes/legal.ts) plus the pure rules in NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/signup-consent-evidence.ts, called once per user per page session from the SIGNED_IN branch of src/hooks/use-auth.ts via NEW src/lib/signup-consent.ts. THE PREVIOUS PASS SCOPED THIS AS "call /api/legal/accept from the first authenticated session" AND THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG, which is the finding worth carrying. /accept stamps the CURRENT published versions AND the users.tos_accepted_version / privacy_accepted_version columns. Email signup defers the session until the confirmation link is clicked, which can be days later, so a version bump in between would have recorded the user as accepting a document they never saw - and cleared a re-acceptance prompt nobody answered. Worse, that row would have looked like the STRONGER evidence of the two, because it carries a real IP. So the endpoint is separate and it COPIES the versions off the trigger row rather than resolving them. WHAT THE ROW HONESTLY CLAIMS. It is a CORROBORATION, not a backfill of the signup request: at this time, from this address, the holder of this account was authenticated, and the clickwrap being corroborated named these documents. accepted_at is when the SERVER OBSERVED THE SESSION, not when consent was given - the clickwrap row holds that - and conflating the two is the one way this could overstate what we know. That is why the method is a DIFFERENT string, signup_clickwrap_confirmed, rather than one value distinguished by a null IP. A signup now ends with a pair: guaranteed-and-weak beside best-effort-and-strong. The trap the previous note named is still refused for its original reason: passing ip/user_agent through signUp() options.data would make them client-supplied and forgeable, and a forged IP in a consent record is worse than an absent one. TWO REFUSALS IN THE CODE. No clickwrap row means an OAuth signup or a pre-00142 user; the endpoint refuses rather than asserting an acceptance that never happened, because a fabricated record will be believed. A clickwrap row naming no document is refused too - a confirmation that says somebody agreed to something reads as evidence and carries none. IDEMPOTENCY IS SERVER-SIDE, deliberately: legal_acceptances is append-only, so a lost race is not a retry, it is a duplicate audit row forever, and a client flag can be stale, cleared or raced by two tabs. The client dedup is only to keep a request off every token refresh. A SEPARATE TRAP FOUND AND MARKED: /accept has accepted method=signup_clickwrap in its allowlist since US-377 and NOTHING sends it - checked across src, ios, android and extension-unified. It is now commented as a hazard pointing at the new endpoint, because reaching for it is exactly the wrong fix described above. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS: versions resolved fresh instead of copied, idempotency guard removed, a row fabricated when there is no clickwrap, and the LATEST clickwrap taken instead of the earliest. Each reddened its own cases and only its own; module restored and re-run green. NOT EXPLORED, AND NAMED SO IT IS NOT LOST: GoTrue writes its own auth.audit_log_entries row on signup carrying the REAL signup IP. If that row is reachable and its write ordering against handle_new_user is provable, it would satisfy AC4 literally rather than by corroboration. Neither fact can be established without a running GoTrue, and the db verify lane starts Postgres alone. HELD, NOT SHIPPED: migration 00573_legal_acceptances_signup_confirmed.sql updates the legal_acceptances.method column comment, which 00142:44 leaves naming three values while the code now writes four. It is comment-only, changes nothing functional, and is deliberately NOT committed - see the note about the branch state. VERIFIED: 10 deno cases in NEW signup-consent-evidence_test.ts, 7 vitest cases in NEW src/lib/__tests__/signup-consent.test.ts, deno check and deno lint clean across 1453 files, full edge suite 6242 passed / 0 failed, tsc -b clean, eslint clean, ui:check 0 findings. Commit cf08b2da. | CORRECTION 2026-08-09, same session: the AC4 segment above was appended with the done command, which flipped passes to true. That was wrong and is reverted here - AC1 (express affirmative consent at web purchase) and AC5 (retention period) are US-2114 counsel items and are untouched. Recording it rather than silently fixing it, because a story that reads as closed is exactly the failure mode this backlog keeps paying for. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09, later the same day: the sentence above reading "HELD, NOT SHIPPED: migration 00573_legal_acceptances_signup_confirmed.sql ... deliberately NOT committed" is STALE and must not be acted on. 00573 was committed, applied to prod and pushed the same day - prod was measured at applied=00573 via /health/ready at 14:27 UTC, the database's own answer, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md now records all of 00564-00573 as APPLIED with that measurement. Nothing in this story is blocked on a branch freeze. WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE OF HOW IT WAS FOUND: prd-lint did not catch this when the note was written, and the reason was a bug in the guard rather than an exemption - MIGRATION_ID used a right-hand \b, and underscore is a word character, so a migration named by its FILENAME never matched. This story's note names 00573 exactly that way. The guard therefore saw only the pushed ids it cites for context, concluded nothing was left to hold, and warned on a CORRECT freeze; the same blindness would have kept it silent on a genuinely stale one. Fixed in commit 9ec66743 and negative-verified both edges. AC1 and AC5 remain US-2114 counsel items and are untouched. | 2026-08-10 ⚠ CORRECTION TO THIS STORY'S OWN NOTES, AND IT IS MATERIAL: AC4's strengthened-evidence path HAS NEVER RECORDED A SINGLE ROW. The notes here describe /api/legal/confirm-signup as working - two rows per email signup, one guaranteed and weak, one best-effort and strong. In fact decideSignupConsentEvidence has returned refuse/no_signup_clickwrap for EVERY caller since it shipped, because there is no signup_clickwrap row to corroborate. handle_new_user lost its clickwrap write at migration 00303, which replaced the function to add use_case and did not carry 00142's block forward; 00379 and 00401 rebased on the truncated body. Traced across all seven definitions and fixed in 00586 under US-2017 (HELD - see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md). AC4's mechanism becomes live the moment that SQL is applied, and not before. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY CORRECT HERE: the client wiring (src/lib/signup-consent.ts, called from use-auth.ts, gated to provider === 'email'), the refusal itself, and the decision to corroborate rather than backfill. Nothing in the design was wrong. The endpoint was answering exactly as specified about a row that no longer existed. THE REAL DEFECT WAS THE SILENCE, and that is what this commit fixes. Both non-insert outcomes returned 200 with no metric, no warn and no distinguishable shape - deliberately, so ordinary traffic would not become alert noise. But the two reasons are NOT alike: already_confirmed is a returning user, while no_signup_clickwrap means an email signup produced no consent record at all. Collapsing them is what let a compliance path record nothing for months while three separate comments described it working. FIXED: the no_signup_clickwrap branch now emits recordMetric('legal.signup_clickwrap_missing') and a warn naming the trigger and the migration. already_confirmed stays silent, and a test asserts it stays silent - counting it would fire on every returning user and the metric would stop meaning anything within a day. WHY A METRIC RATHER THAN A 4xx: the endpoint's existing reasoning still holds - answering an error would turn ordinary sign-ins into noise, and the client deliberately ignores the status. A counter is the right instrument for 'this should be rare and is not'. THREE SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening the new case: the branch removed (back to a silent 200), the metric dropped while the warn stayed, and the two reasons collapsed into one condition. AC4 STATUS UNCHANGED as a deliverable - it was and remains implemented-by-corroboration rather than by backfilling ip/user_agent onto the trigger row, which the module explains and refuses. What changed is that the claim in these notes is now true only after 00586 applies, and there is now an instrument that says so if it stops being true again. VERIFIED: deno check clean on routes/legal.ts; deno lint clean across 1486 files; signup-consent-evidence_test.ts 11 passed (1 new); full edge suite 6462 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored. | 2026-08-10 (second pass) AC6 WAS DONE FOR ONE OF THE TWO PRODUCTS APPSTORE.TS SELLS, and the guard could not see the difference. POST /api/payments/appstore/verify handles both a seller subscription and a BUYER subscription. The buyer branch (mapping.kind === 'buyer_subscription') applied the entitlement and RETURNED before BOTH recordAppstoreEvent and recordPlatformAgreement. So an App Store BUYER purchase left no audit row and no agreed-terms row, while an App Store SELLER purchase got both and a Stripe buyer purchase got the agreement via applyBuyerSubscriptionChange. Three populations, two answers to 'what did this user agree to?'. THE GUARD PASSED THROUGHOUT, and that is the reusable part. US-2116's wiring test asserted /recordPlatformAgreement\(/.test(appstore) - whether the FILE calls it, not whether each PRODUCT PATH does. A file-level check over a file that sells two things is a check over neither. It is now per-branch: each product's grant must be followed, inside its own brace-matched branch, by both the audit row and the agreement, with the agreement naming ITS OWN plan. FIXED: the buyer branch now writes both. from_plan/to_plan are NULL rather than the user's FlipDesk tier - those columns are typed public.flipdesk_plan (00037) and this event changed no FlipDesk plan, so null is the true statement while repeating their seller tier would imply a transition that did not happen. The buyer tiers ride in raw_payload. subscription_agreements.plan is free text and guard/connoisseur cannot collide with starter/pro/business, so the agreement names the real buyer plan. Skipped when the mapped plan is 'free', matching the Play path. GOOGLE PLAY IS NOT AFFECTED, checked rather than assumed: google-play-rtdn.ts and google-play.ts contain no buyer_plan references at all - Play sells only the seller product today, so there is no second branch to miss. TWO GUARD FAULTS FOUND WHILE WRITING IT, both the same family as the rest of today. (1) My first slice ran from the branch start to the first `return c.json(`, which cut before the grant because the buyer branch returns a 409 early when a Stripe subscription is already active - the assertion failed against CORRECT code, and the tempting response would have been to weaken it back to the file-wide check that hid the bug. Brace-matched instead. (2) The plan assertion read the whole branch, which also contains `plan: update.buyer_plan` in its JSON response - so switching the AGREEMENT to the seller plan stayed green. Scoped to the recordPlatformAgreement call's arguments. FOUR SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening the case: the buyer agreement dropped (the original bug), the buyer audit row dropped, the buyer agreement recording the seller plan, and the seller agreement dropped instead. AC6 IS NOW GENUINELY DONE for every platform purchase path that exists. AC1 and AC5 remain US-2114 counsel items and are untouched. VERIFIED: deno check clean on routes/appstore.ts; deno lint clean across 1486 files; agreed-terms_test.ts 19 passed; full edge suite 6462 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored. | 2026-08-12 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM IN THIS STORY, CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. Every migration named above is on origin/main AND applied to prod. Evidence, not inference: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns {"schema":{"expected":"00589","applied":"00589","status":"match"}} - that is the running edge reading applied_migrations through the service-role client, i.e. the database own answer, and 00589 is the highest migration on origin/main. So nothing here is blocked on a frozen branch and nobody should hold a push on this story account. The ONLY genuinely held migration today is 00590 (US-2497), which is committed locally and unpushed. THE DISTINCTION THAT KEEPS GETTING BLURRED, and it is why this warning recurs: PUSHED is not APPLIED, and a note written while a migration was held stays true-sounding forever after it lands. Check the endpoint before writing HELD or APPLIED anywhere - the answer is one unauthenticated GET and several passes have reasoned from commit history instead.

userStories.title: No record of what price or terms any user actually agreed to — pricing_plans is mutated in place
userStories.description: The users table stores flipdesk_plan and flipdesk_interval but NO amount column; price is resolved live on every read via getFlipdeskPriceIds() against pricing_plans. pricing_plans (00166:69-80) is mutated in place with only an updated_at trigger — no history table, no versioning. flipdesk_subscription_events records from_plan/to_plan and the raw payload but, per the note already in 00215_revenue_dashboard.sql:20, not even the billing interval. Combined, there is no way to reconstruct what price any user was shown or agreed to on any past date. If a price changes, the historical record changes with it.
acceptanceCriteria: Snapshot the agreed terms onto the subscription record at purchase: amount, currency, interval, plan, trial terms, and the disclosure-copy version — immutable once written.
Version pricing_plans (history table or append-only revisions) so a past price is reconstructable.
Record the billing interval on flipdesk_subscription_events.
Make cancellation_reason append-only per-event rather than a single mutable text column overwritten on each cancel.
Follow the migrations skill: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in the same commit, self-record footer.
userStories.notes: [P0][Compliance/Data] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). This is the evidentiary half of the consent story — consent to WHAT is unanswerable without it. Also unblocks honest revenue reporting. | 2026-07-19 ALL FOUR SCHEMA ACs DONE (migration 00486) + the write path. ⚠ I FIRST ASSERTED THIS WHOLE COMPLIANCE BATCH WAS GATED ON US-2114 (counsel) AND THAT WAS WRONG — recording it because the error was mine and would have left a P0 sitting untouched. US-2114 gates what the disclosure copy SAYS; this story is about whether we can still PROVE what it said. Those are different questions, and only the first needs a lawyer. Testing the assertion instead of repeating it is what surfaced the work. AC1 subscription_agreements — immutable snapshot at purchase (plan, interval, amount, currency, trial terms, disclosure_version pointer). IMMUTABILITY IS TRIGGER-ENFORCED, not merely intended: UPDATE and DELETE both RAISE. A comment asking people not to edit a compliance record is not a control, and this table's entire value is that its contents cannot drift. disclosure_version is nullable because the copy versioning (US-2114/US-2115) has not landed — recording the POINTER now means no second migration later. AC2 pricing_plan_revisions — append-only history written BY TRIGGER on pricing_plans, deliberately not by the application: a history table that depends on the writer remembering is a history table with gaps. Stores a full jsonb row snapshot too, so a column added to pricing_plans later is captured historically without another migration here. Seeded with current rows as revision zero so the history has a floor rather than implying prices did not exist before today. AC3 flipdesk_subscription_events.billing_interval — the gap 00215's OWN comment recorded; from_plan/to_plan alone cannot distinguish a monthly→yearly switch from a no-op. AC4 subscription_cancellations — append-only; users.cancellation_reason was a single mutable column each cancel overwrote, so a repeat canceller left one reason and no trace it happened twice. Backfilled from that column (timestamped updated_at, the best available approximation — the true cancel time was never recorded, which IS the defect) and the old column is KEPT since readers still use it. WRITE PATH: lib/agreed-terms.ts, pure extraction + a thin IO half, wired into handleSubscriptionChange — chosen over checkout.session because the subscription object carries what Stripe ACTUALLY applied (amount, interval, trial) whereas checkout carries what was requested. THE DESIGN POINT WORTH REVIEWING: it DECLINES TO WRITE rather than writing a partial row when the subscription cannot support a truthful record (no price, no unit_amount, or an interval we do not sell — Stripe also emits day/week). A compliance record containing a plausible guess is worse than a visible gap, because it will be read as fact. The refusal is reported, so the gap is not silent. Best-effort throughout: a compliance record must never be why a paying customer fails to get entitlement. Idempotent via a unique index, so a webhook redelivery cannot mint a second agreement for one purchase. 9 tests. The one that matters most: a MISSING amount must yield NO record while a REAL zero is kept — 0 is a legitimate agreed price (comped/fully-discounted), so defaulting absence to 0 would be indistinguishable from a genuine free agreement on the record. Negative-verified by making absence default to 0; that test goes red. ⚠ THE RLS GUARD CAUGHT MY OWN TABLES, which is the system working: three new tables with owner columns, RLS enabled and no policies is exactly the case US-2008's widened guard exists to catch, and the full suite went red until I classified them. All three are now in SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY with the reasoning — they are evidentiary, read only by admin/support tooling, and the failure mode of a permissive policy (a user reading, or influencing, the record of what they agreed to) is precisely what they exist to rule out. STILL OPEN: nothing schema-side. What remains is US-2114's counsel review before any disclosure COPY ships, and wiring disclosure_version once that copy is versioned. Migration 00486 is HELD (7th) — see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md for the two backfills and the deploy-order note. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00215, 00486) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. | 2026-08-09 THE LAST OPEN ITEM IS BUILT: disclosure_version is wired end to end, so there is NO CODE LEFT TO WRITE on this story. The July note ended 'what remains is wiring disclosure_version once that copy is versioned' - US-2115 shipped the copy on 2026-08-09 and this closes the loop. THE COPY IS NOW VERSIONED, AND THE VERSION IS NOT A HAND-MAINTAINED NUMBER, which was the whole risk. DISCLOSURE_VERSION plus an append-only DISCLOSURE_ARCHIVE live in src/lib/auto-renewal-copy.ts; NEW src/lib/__tests__/disclosure-version.test.ts re-derives the sentence templates FROM THE SOURCE of disclosureSentences and fails unless they equal the current version's archive entry exactly. A version constant nobody bumps drifts away from the copy while looking authoritative, and a pointer aimed at the wrong words is a FALSE record, not a missing one - strictly worse than the null column it replaced. The archive stores TEMPLATES rather than rendered sentences on purpose: a rendering bakes in an amount and a date, and dateLabel formats in the reader's local timezone, so a rendered archive would differ by machine and could not be compared at all. THE PATH: both subscribe hooks in src/hooks/use-billing-summary.ts report the constant, payments.ts bounds it and puts it on subscription_data.metadata (and on both in-place upgrade metadata writes), and agreed-terms.ts resolves it at the write site. SENT FROM THE HOOKS, NOT FROM EACH SURFACE - every subscribe surface renders AutoRenewalDisclosure out of the same module the constant comes from, so the hook's answer is the one the screen gave, and a new surface cannot forget. AN UNKNOWN VERSION IS REFUSED, NOT STORED, and that is the same rule extractAgreedTerms already applies to a guessed amount: an id we cannot resolve is a pointer to nothing on an immutable compliance row, reading as provenance while carrying none. It is reported instead, because the realistic cause is the web copy being versioned without the edge, which would silently strip the pointer off a whole cohort. THE HONESTY CONSTRAINT, WRITTEN INTO services/edge-functions/src/lib/disclosure-versions.ts BECAUSE IT LIMITS WHAT THE FIELD PROVES: disclosure_version is CLIENT-REPORTED. Only the browser knows which build rendered the disclosure, and the edge deploys separately, so an edge-derived version would be a guess during any skew window. A determined user could report an older known version. What the server independently vouches for is the material terms - amount, interval, trial - which come from the Stripe subscription object. The version points at wording; it is not evidence against an adversarial client and must not be described as such. THE MIRROR IS DELIBERATELY THIN - version ids only, no sentences - and there are guards in BOTH directions, because US-1995 is the standing example of two copies with two green suites silently disagreeing. SECOND GAP FOUND AND FIXED, NOT IN ANY AC's WORDS BUT SQUARELY IN AC1's: applyBuyerSubscriptionChange RETURNS before the seller path's recordAgreedTerms call, so a Guard/Connoisseur subscriber had NO agreement row at all while a FlipDesk subscriber did - two paying populations with different evidentiary standing for the same question, the exact asymmetry US-2116 AC6 closed for App Store and Play. Now recorded, SKIPPING plan 'free' because that value is the unmappable-price fallback and subscription_agreements.plan is free text with no product column, so a buyer free and a seller free are indistinguishable on the record. guard/connoisseur cannot collide with starter/pro/business, so the named plans are safe as they are. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS, each reddening its own case and only its own, module restored: a word changed in the copy without a version bump, the edge mirror losing the current version, the insert losing the disclosure_version column, normalizeDisclosureVersion accepting unknown ids, the buyer recordAgreedTerms call removed, and one of the four payments.ts metadata sites removed. STAYS passes:false ON ONE NARROW ITEM, and only one: nobody has OBSERVED an agreement row carrying a disclosure_version. Every test here is a unit or source-structural test; none of them touch Stripe or Postgres. The mechanism is not speculative - subscription_data.metadata is the same channel that already carries user_id, which handleSubscriptionChange reads in production today - but this is an evidentiary field whose only job is to be trusted later, and 'we are confident it writes' is the wrong standard for that. One production SELECT against subscription_agreements after the next subscription settles it; it belongs with US-2347's queries. VERIFIED: full edge suite 6404 passed / 0 failed, full web suite 3892 passed / 0 failed across 319 files, deno check + deno lint clean across 1476 files, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors / 13 warnings (unchanged baseline), ui:check 0 findings. New tests: 9 web (disclosure-version.test.ts), 8 edge (disclosure-versions_test.ts), 6 added to agreed-terms_test.ts. | 2026-08-15 THE ONE OPEN ITEM IS NOW A QUERY RATHER THAN AN INTENTION. This story's last note kept it open on a single narrow thing: every disclosure_version test is a unit or source-structural test, and nobody had OBSERVED a subscription_agreements row carrying one. scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql §21 asks it directly - total agreements, how many carry a disclosure_version, the first versioned row's timestamp, and a breakdown by version/plan/interval so an unrecognised string is visible rather than averaged away. The reading note names the two distinct zero answers, because they mean opposite things: agreements_total at zero means nobody has subscribed since the table shipped and the question is still unanswered, while a non-zero total with with_disclosure_version at zero is the bad answer - rows are being written and the Stripe metadata is not arriving. Still passes:false, unchanged, and it closes on running §21 rather than on more code.

userStories.title: Build the authenticity golden set — the gate is worthless without ground truth
userStories.description: authenticity_eval_cases (00405_authenticity_eval.sql) exists but has NO seed rows anywhere in the repo — by design, the golden set is operator-curated. runAuthenticityEval would throw on first call (authenticity-eval.ts:183). This is the expensive, slow, expert-dependent asset that everything else in the epic depends on, and it cannot be generated by an agent: it requires labeled authentic-vs-counterfeit items with real photos and defensible provenance for each label.
acceptanceCriteria: Define what a case requires: photos at the resolution the pipeline actually receives, the ground-truth label, the provenance of that label (who determined it and how), brand, garment type, and the tells that justify the label.
Build the operator curation surface for adding, reviewing and retiring cases.
Set the passing bar with counsel/product input — including the false-positive bar, which matters far more than overall accuracy: calling a genuine item fake is the more damaging error.
Seed an initial set covering the brands we actually see most, not the brands that are most interesting.
Track per-brand coverage so the gate cannot pass on a brand it has never seen.
Follow the grading-engine skill's golden-set rules and exemplar-privacy constraints.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Data][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. USER/EXPERT ACTION REQUIRED — an agent can build the surface and the schema, but not the labels. This is the true critical path for the whole epic; sequence accordingly. Sourcing options to evaluate: partner with an authentication service, buy a labeled corpus, or curate from our own human-review history where provenance is defensible. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: the CURATION SURFACE is built — GET/POST/PATCH /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases, needing NO migration because 00405 already carries every column including source_url for label provenance. Deliberately NO delete route: per the grading-engine contract a shrinking golden set is a red flag, and deleting the cases a prompt fails is the easiest way to fake a pass — cases are RETIRED (is_active=false) and every ground-truth change is audited. validateAuthenticityCase rejects empty images at write time rather than letting runAuthenticityEval throw mid-run after spending vision calls on earlier cases. summarizeCaseCoverage marks a brand usable ONLY with at least one authentic AND one counterfeit case: a perfect score over authentic-only cases cannot demonstrate the one error the gate exists to catch. 4357 edge tests pass. STILL BLOCKED: the labels themselves. An expert must now add real cases through this surface; nothing downstream (the gate passing, US-2134 prompt narrowing, US-2143 positioning) can move until they exist. ITER 2026-07-19: bulk import shipped — lib/golden-set-import.ts + POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases/import, plus docs/authenticity-golden-set-template.json. Partial success is REPORTED per row (index + reason) and does not fail the batch: re-uploading 50 rows over one typo is how people start bypassing validation. Returns 207 when any row was rejected, 201 when clean, and a rejected count is always present so a caller can tell a partial from a full success without parsing counts. brand_key is alias-resolved via brandKeyForRaw, so an import written "Levi Strauss" lands on the same key as the KB row and as a review-promoted case. coverageWarnings flags a brand imported with only ONE polarity — 40 genuine cases and no fakes scores perfectly and proves nothing, since the dangerous miss cannot occur; the mirror case (counterfeit-only) yields no false-positive rate, the error that harms sellers. Warnings do NOT reject, since a corpus may legitimately arrive in halves. Capped at 500 rows/batch. 4426 edge tests pass (+9). STILL THE BLOCKER: the labels themselves. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: A seller whose GENUINE item is flagged has no way to contest it
userStories.description:
Every control in the authenticity module protects the buyer. There is nothing for a seller whose genuine item receives a red_flags verdict: the dispute system is grade/condition-shaped and carries no authenticity path (verified — zero authenticity references in the dispute routes/lib), there is no appeal, no re-assessment, and no way to have a wrong verdict withdrawn.

This got WORSE on 2026-07-19, by our own hand. US-2141 sealed the verdict into certificate integrity v4, and US-2142 wrote it to the garment passport — an append-only ledger with no update or delete policy.
