So a wrong verdict is now durable, tamper-evident, and by design cannot be erased. We made the record permanent before building the correction path.

Three things compound it: the pass has never cleared an accuracy gate (US-2130/2131), so we cannot state an error rate; confidence is capped but not zero when no macro evidence exists (US-2134), so thin-evidence verdicts still publish; and this is the error direction a financial guarantee would NOT cover (Entrupy-style guarantees pay out on fakes sold as real, not on genuine items called fake), so the seller bears it entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: A seller can contest an authenticity verdict from the surfaces where they see it, with a defined SLA and a human decision — not a form that goes nowhere.

Define what the certificate and passport show WHILE an appeal is open. The passport is append-only, so a withdrawal is a superseding event, never a deletion — decide and document what the public view renders for a superseded verdict.

Wire the outcome through the existing authenticity review path (US-2140) so an upheld appeal produces a reviewer verdict, and a wrongly-flagged genuine item becomes an 'authentic' golden-set case — the most valuable label we can get.
Reseal the certificate on withdrawal (integrity v4 covers the verdict, so a change without a reseal breaks verification).
Notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published, not only when they happen to look. They cannot contest what they never saw.
Counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording — fold into US-2133 rather than running a separate review.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Fairness][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Publicly attaching 'red flags' to a real person's item, from a model with no measured error rate, has a defamation-adjacent shape that belongs in the counsel review. Sharpest open exposure in the module. Sequence with US-2133; do not let an agent draft the notice language. PARTIAL 2026-07-19 (mechanics only): migration 00489 adds disputes.kind (grade|authenticity, default grade) — EXTENDING the existing disputes table rather than building an appeals table, since disputes is already generic at the schema level (grade_report_id, user_id, free-text reason, status, resolution_notes) and only its RESOLUTION path is grade-shaped. One lifecycle, one admin queue, one place a user looks. HELD; packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. lib/authenticity-appeal.ts encodes three decisions worth review: (1) an upheld appeal CLEARS the verdict rather than flipping it to likely_authentic — the assessment should never have been published, which is not the same as positively vouching for the item, and asserting that would be the same overreach reversed; (2) the reseal carries the SCORES through untouched, because an authenticity appeal says nothing about condition and silently re-deriving a grade would change a number nobody contested; (3) a REJECTED appeal produces NO golden-set case — upholding the original verdict is not a human independently confirming counterfeit (the reviewer may just have found the appeal unpersuasive), and treating it as ground truth would seed the golden set with unverified labels. An upheld appeal DOES yield an authentic case, which is a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE — the most valuable label available, and the error direction US-2146 exists to measure. 4408 edge tests pass (+7). DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED, still needs you + counsel (US-2133): what the certificate and passport RENDER while an appeal is open, the SLA, the seller notification wording, and whether a published red_flags verdict should notify the seller proactively. No routes shipped yet — the lib is pure logic + tests, so nothing is user-reachable until those decisions land. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (in my own iteration-4 work): withdrawAssessment cleared only verdict/verdict_confidence, but the PUBLIC certificate view (00172, carried through 00307) does NOT read verdict — it derives what a buyer sees from authenticity_confidence (-> confidence band), counterfeit_risk (-> risk label) and summary (rendered verbatim). So an upheld appeal would have cleared the internal verdict while the certificate kept publicly showing an elevated counterfeit risk and the original red-flag summary: the seller wins and stays flagged, which is exactly the failure this story exists to fix. Now clears every projected field, moves the original under withdrawn_original (operator-side; no view projects it) so the record of what was said survives, and exports PUBLICLY_PROJECTED_ASSESSMENT_FIELDS with a test that iterates it — if the view ever learns a new field, that test fails rather than a seller silently staying flagged. Also confirmed: the edge-SSR cert page renders no authenticity at all (SPA-only), and authenticity_checked in the public view derives from image_authenticity (PHOTO-EDIT, 00061), which is a different signal from the brand add-on and must not be conflated. 4412 edge tests pass. SELLER ROUTE 2026-07-19: POST /api/grade/authenticity-appeal shipped, implementing the approved §1a/§1b decisions. Files as disputes.kind=authenticity (00489) rather than a parallel table. Ownership verified through the submission (grade_reports has no user_id) and a miss reports 404 so an id probe cannot distinguish does-not-exist from not-yours; viewers are blocked, matching the grade-dispute route. Hiding the verdict while an appeal is open is REVERSIBLE — hideAssessmentForAppeal clears the publicly-projected fields and stashes the originals under appeal_hidden_original, so a rejected appeal restores exactly what was there and hiding is not a quiet way to lose a verdict; hiding twice does not bury the original (tested). Rate limited to 5 open appeals per seller, which exists BECAUSE hiding is free otherwise: unlimited appeals would suppress every verdict indefinitely at no cost. CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: the first version called the reseal before the update landed, so it would have hashed the OLD verdict and written a signature verifying against nothing — resealAfterAuthenticityChange now takes the NEXT assessment explicitly, which makes that mistake impossible rather than merely fixed. If hiding fails the appeal is still recorded (better a visible verdict with a filed appeal than a silent appeal nobody actions). 4431 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: the admin resolve route, seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (needs the SLA number + counsel). ADMIN RESOLVE 2026-07-19: GET /authenticity/appeals (open queue, OLDEST FIRST — while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty) + POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve. Step-up gated: upholding withdraws a published verdict and reseals a certificate, rejecting republishes one. Upheld -> withdrawAssessment (permanent, clears every publicly-projected field); rejected -> restoreAssessmentAfterAppeal (exactly what was hidden, since the reviewer finding the appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item). Both reseal with the NEXT assessment. An upheld appeal also records an authentic reviewer verdict through the US-2140 path, because a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE is the most valuable label available and the error direction nothing else measures — the model_verdict snapshot reads from appeal_hidden_original, since the live field was nulled when the appeal was filed. Already-resolved appeals 409 rather than double-applying. 4431 edge tests pass. REMAINING on this story: seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (SLA number + counsel). | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00061, 00172, 00307, 00489) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. NOTIFICATION 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-notify.ts, fired from the pipeline at finalize. Implements the approved §1a decision — red_flags ONLY, never on inconclusive (not a finding; telling a seller invites appeals against nothing) and never on likely_authentic. SLA of 5 business days is stated in the notice, per the decision: an appeal with no stated turnaround cannot be planned around, and while it is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade. COPY IS DELIBERATELY NON-ACCUSATORY and tested to stay that way — it says the check flagged details it COULD NOT CONFIRM, calls itself an automated photo estimate and not a determination, and a test asserts the words counterfeit/fake never appear, because the pass has no measured error rate and must not assert what it cannot support. Rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a type the users notification preferences do not know about, which would have made it unsuppressable. Best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. ⚠ COPY STILL NEEDS COUNSEL REVIEW under US-2133 — flagged in the module header; it should be reviewed alongside the certificate copy, not separately. 4453 edge tests pass (+22). | 2026-08-02 THE APPEAL PIPELINE IS BUILT AT BOTH ENDS AND HAS NO SELLER-FACING BUTTON. Verified by grep, not inferred. The SELLER endpoint exists and is complete: POST /authenticity-appeal at routes/grade.ts:1301 — it verifies the caller owns the submission, 422s when the grade has no authenticity assessment to contest, and rate-limits deliberately (the comment says why: hiding the verdict while an appeal is open means an unlimited appeal is a free way to suppress every verdict indefinitely — that is a well-reasoned control, not boilerplate). The ADMIN side exists too: GET /authenticity/appeals is the open queue oldest-first and POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve closes them, and the queue's ordering carries its own reasoning (while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty). AND NOTHING IN src/ CALLS THE SELLER ENDPOINT. A grep for "authenticity-appeal" across every .ts and .tsx under src returns ZERO hits. So an operator opening the appeals queue sees a list that can only ever be empty, and a seller whose genuine item was flagged still has exactly what the story title says: no way to contest it. THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THIS SESSION KEPT FINDING, and it is the third instance today — the waitlist backend with no public capture form, the grade-card switch writing columns nothing read, and now this. Each time the expensive half was built and the cheap half was not, and each time the missing half is the one a USER touches. Worth naming explicitly on a story about a seller being unable to defend a genuine item: the backend being done makes this look further along than it is, and anyone reading the route file would conclude the feature ships. WHAT REMAINS FOR AC1 is therefore smaller than the AC implies but not trivial: the surfaces where a seller SEES the verdict (the certificate view and the submission detail) need a contest action that POSTs to the existing endpoint, plus the open-appeal state AC2 asks about — and AC2 is a real design question, not wiring, because the passport is append-only so a withdrawal is a superseding entry rather than an edit. AC5 (notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published) is also still open and is arguably prior to AC1: they cannot contest what they were never told about. AC6 needs counsel. I did not build the UI — the certificate and passport display rules in AC2 have to be settled first, and shipping a contest button before deciding what the certificate shows while an appeal is open would put a seller in a state nobody has defined. | 2026-08-02 AC1 AND AC2 DONE — the seller can now contest a verdict. MY EARLIER BLOCKER DISSOLVED ON INSPECTION, and that is worth recording because I nearly left this unbuilt on it: I said AC2 (what the certificate shows while an appeal is open) had to be settled first. It already was, server-side, and I had not read far enough. hideAssessmentForAppeal (lib/authenticity-appeal.ts:106) NULLS verdict, verdict_confidence, authenticity_confidence, counterfeit_risk and summary, sets under_appeal + appeal_opened_at, and stashes the original in appeal_hidden_original — guarded against stashing a stash on a second appeal, which would make the original unrecoverable. The endpoint then RESEALS (AC4) because integrity v4 covers the verdict, and its own comment explains why the reseal passes the HIDDEN assessment rather than the stored one. So AC2 and AC4 were shipped; only the button was missing. SHIPPED: NEW src/components/grade/authenticity-appeal-dialog.tsx and a "This is genuine — contest this result" action on submission-detail.tsx, the surface where the seller actually sees the verdict. THREE DETAILS THAT ARE NOT DECORATION. (1) The page now renders an UNDER-REVIEW card when under_appeal is set, instead of the normal card. Without it the seller sees a row of blanks where the verdict was — which reads as a bug, and is worse than not shipping the button at all, because it makes them think their appeal broke something. (2) The dialog is mounted at the PAGE root, not inside the authenticity card, so it is not unmounted the instant the card swaps to its under-review state on a successful file. (3) MIN_REASON = 20 mirrors the server's validateAppeal floor deliberately, and the client copy spends it telling the seller what a reviewer needs before they type: being rejected after writing is how someone abandons an appeal they were entitled to. The 429 path surfaces the SERVER's message rather than a generic retry, because that cap is a deliberate control (an unlimited appeal is a free way to suppress every verdict) and a retry prompt would send the seller round the same loop. GUARD: NEW src/test/authenticity-appeal-wired.test.ts — something must POST to the endpoint, the dialog must be RENDERED somewhere rather than merely defined, the seller surface must handle under_appeal, and the client minimum must match the server's. A route with no caller is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to every test that exercises the route directly, so only a scan catches it. STILL OPEN: AC3 (wire an upheld appeal through the US-2140 reviewer path), AC5 (notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is PUBLISHED — arguably prior to all of this, since they cannot contest what they were never told), AC6 (counsel, folded into US-2133). VERIFIED: full web suite 248 files / 3154 tests 0 failed, build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors. | 2026-08-02 CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTE ABOVE, and a better outcome than expected. I wrote that AC5 was "still open" and "arguably prior to all of this, since they cannot contest what they were never told". THAT IS WRONG. AC5 IS DONE. notifyAuthenticityFlagged (lib/authenticity-notify.ts:71) is called from grading-pipeline.ts:2785, fires only on a red_flags verdict, and is best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. It had reached the same design conclusion I was about to: it rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a notification type the user's preferences do not know about — an appeal IS a dispute. Its copy is careful in a way worth preserving: "our authenticity check flagged details it could not confirm ... an automated estimate from photos, not a determination", because saying the item IS counterfeit would assert something an ungated photo-only estimate cannot support. THE FLOW IS NOW END-TO-END, which is the actual news: the notice links to /dashboard/submissions/{id}, and that is exactly the page where the contest button I added this session lives. So the loop closes — red_flags verdict fires a notification, the seller clicks through, and the button is there. Before today the notification landed on a page with nothing to do. That is the same defect one level up from the one I fixed: the notice was built, the endpoint was built, and the two were never joined. HOW I GOT IT WRONG: I asserted AC5 was open from the AC text plus the absence of any UI, without grepping the pipeline for a notify call. The lesson is the one this session kept re-learning in the other direction — I checked whether the ENDPOINT had a caller and correctly found none, then failed to run the same check on the NOTIFICATION and assumed. Absence of a caller is a thing you verify, not infer, in both directions. REMAINING ON THIS STORY: AC3 (wire an upheld appeal through the US-2140 reviewer path so a withdrawal produces a reviewer verdict) and AC6 (counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording, folded into US-2133). AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC5 all stand. | 2026-08-02 AC3 IS ALSO ALREADY DONE — checked rather than assumed this time, having just been wrong about AC5. POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve takes an outcome of upheld or rejected, refuses to re-resolve an already-closed appeal, and splits correctly: UPHELD withdraws the verdict permanently, REJECTED restores exactly what was hidden — with the reasoning stated inline that a reviewer finding an appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item, so the original stands rather than being re-derived. It reseals, updates the dispute status, and when plan.reviewerVerdict is set it feeds the outcome through the same review path so it counts toward accuracy and can be promoted, which is precisely what AC3 asked for. SO US-2145 STANDS AT: AC1 done (the contest button, this session — the only piece that was actually missing), AC2 done, AC3 done, AC4 done, AC5 done, AC6 outstanding and needing counsel on the notice and appeal wording, folded into US-2133 per the AC itself. THE SHAPE OF THIS STORY IS WORTH KEEPING, because it is the clearest example of the pattern this whole session kept hitting: FIVE of six criteria were fully implemented — endpoint, hiding, reseal, reviewer path, notification — and the story read as untouched because the one missing piece was a button. Every file a reader would open to check suggested the feature shipped, and the seller still could not contest anything. The expensive halves were all built; the cheap half, the one a user touches, was not. A route with no caller is invisible to tsc, to lint, and to any test that exercises the route directly, which is why it survived. RECOMMENDATION: close on AC1-AC5 and let AC6 travel with US-2133, or leave open pointing there — an owner call, and specifically not one I should make by writing a note that sounds like agreement on a story with a legal-review criterion.

userStories.title: EPIC: Grading depth — identity, sizing, brand knowledge and product coverage
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the grading pipeline to identify WHAT it is grading as rigorously as it grades CONDITION, and to cover the product categories sellers actually list, because today the two halves of the product are lopsided: the condition engine is deep (5 weighted factors, defect taxonomy with mm tolerances, fabric-aware criteria, confidence caps, shadow/eval/canary lifecycle) while identity is thin (brand and size on a certificate are whatever the seller typed) and coverage is clothing-only (a hat, a tie, a belt and a handbag all have a garment_category and no way to be graded).
acceptanceCriteria: Every child story in this epic names the exact module, table or enum it changes — no story in this epic may be closed on prose alone.
Identity work does not weaken US-346: label-read fields are server-derived and TRUSTED; seller-typed brand/size stay fenced and untrusted, and neither channel may move a factor score.
Any change to a grading prompt in this epic goes through the mandated lifecycle (new version name -> shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary), never a silent edit.

Any new rubric added by this epic keeps the three weighted-overall rounding sites in lockstep (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, admin/reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) in the same commit.
Epic closes only when its children close; it carries no implementation of its own.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Epic] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Parent for US-2210..US-2225. Scope split six ways: tag identification (2210-2212), sizing (2213-2215), brand styles/models (2216-2217), authenticity evidence + coverage priority (2218-2219), brand breadth (2220-2221), product coverage beyond clothing (2222-2225). DELIBERATELY NOT DUPLICATED: US-2130..2148 already own the visual-authenticity epic (eval gate, golden set, capture quality, decoder cross-checks, tell depth/counterfeit modelling, appeals, accuracy tracking); US-1997 owns non-clothing rubric ACTIVATION for the three rubrics that already exist (sports_cards/watches/shoes) and its Phase-2 notes already scope the factor-set generalization every new rubric here depends on; US-2107 owns publishing measurable tolerances.

userStories.title: In-place plan upgrade charges a prorated amount on a single click with no confirmation
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts:326-380: if a user already has a subscription, clicking a higher tier calls stripe.subscriptions.update with proration_behavior: 'create_prorations' — charging immediately with NO Stripe Checkout page, no price confirmation, no interstitial and no disclosure. The click IS the purchase. Every other purchase path at least passes through Stripe's hosted checkout, which renders the recurring price; this one renders nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: Show an explicit confirmation step before an in-place upgrade that states the prorated amount charged today, the new recurring amount, the new billing frequency, and the next renewal date.
Capture the same affirmative consent artifact as a new subscription.
Apply the same treatment to downgrades and interval switches if they charge or change terms.
Test asserting the upgrade mutation cannot fire without the confirmation step.
userStories.notes:
[P1][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). A charge with no disclosure and no confirmation is the clearest Section 5 / ROSCA exposure in the codebase after the missing disclosures themselves. | 2026-07-19 SCOPED, DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT — and the reason is the story's own logic, not capacity. AC1 needs a confirmation stating the PRORATED AMOUNT CHARGED TODAY, the new recurring amount, the new frequency and the next renewal date. Those numbers do not exist anywhere yet: payments.ts has fetchUpcomingInvoice (US-400) but that returns the CURRENT subscription's upcoming invoice, not a simulation of what a CHANGE would cost. Getting the real figure needs Stripe's proration preview — invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the PROPOSED subscription_items plus a subscription_proration_date — which is a new endpoint, and one whose output I cannot verify from this sandbox (the Stripe MCP connector is unauthorized; see US-2033, blocked the same way). WHY THAT BLOCKS RATHER THAN MERELY SLOWS: a confirmation dialog that states a WRONG prorated amount is worse than the current no-dialog state. Today the defect is an OMISSION — the click is the purchase and nothing is stated. A dialog showing an unverified number converts that into an AFFIRMATIVE MISSTATEMENT about a charge, on the exact surface this compliance batch exists to fix. That is the same reasoning applied in US-2117 (refuse to write a partial agreement), US-2119 (refuse to send a notice with no date) and US-2116 (refuse to record a client-supplied IP): on an evidentiary or money surface, a plausible-looking wrong value is worse than an acknowledged gap. WHAT THE NEXT PASS NEEDS, so it is short: (1) a preview endpoint wrapping invoices.retrieveUpcoming with the target plan's price id, returning prorated-now / new-recurring / interval / next-renewal; (2) a confirmation dialog — DowngradePreviewDialog is the established pattern to mirror, and AC3's 'apply the same treatment to downgrades' is already satisfied by it, which is why upgrades being bare is the anomaly rather than the norm; (3) route the upgrade mutation through it; (4) AC4's test that the mutation cannot fire without confirmation. AC2 (capture the same consent artifact as a new subscription) is now CHEAP because US-2117 landed: subscription_agreements + recordAgreedTerms already exist, and an in-place upgrade produces a customer.subscription.updated event that already flows through handleSubscriptionChange — which now calls recordAgreedTerms. So an upgrade ALREADY writes an agreement row with the new plan/interval/amount. Worth verifying rather than assuming, but the plumbing is in place. The FIGURES are the blocker, and they need a Stripe session — not more code reading. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h); edge unvalidated in-sandbox (no deno), CI + a real Stripe test env confirm. The in-place upgrade (payments.ts /flipdesk/subscribe, existing paid sub → higher tier) called stripe.subscriptions.update with create_prorations on a single click — no disclosure, no consent. AC1: new POST /flipdesk/upgrade-preview computes the real proration via stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming (simulating the item swap with subscription_items + subscription_proration_behavior) and returns amount_due_today_cents, currency, new_recurring_cents, interval, next_renewal_at (current_period_end). AC4 (server-enforced, the strong guarantee): the in-place path now refuses unless the body carries confirmUpgrade:true — returns 409 { code:'UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED', requiresConfirmation:true } and does NOT mutate; the gate sits BEFORE subscriptions.update. AC2: on a confirmed change it writes a consent artifact to flipdesk_subscription_events (event_type 'in_place_change_confirmed', from/to plan, raw_payload with prices+interval+source) — the equivalent of Checkout's disclosure. Web: new UpgradePreviewDialog (mirrors the existing DowngradePreviewDialog) fetches the preview and discloses amount today / new recurring rate+frequency / next renewal before confirming; the plan picker's upgrade CTA opens it for a paid→higher change and calls subscribe with confirmUpgrade:true on confirm. A free→paid upgrade still goes straight to Stripe Checkout (which discloses on its own hosted page), so it skips the dialog. AC3: downgrades already route through DowngradePreviewDialog and interval switches through the Stripe billing portal (both disclose/confirm) — the upgrade path was the only gap, now closed. TESTS: edge upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts asserts (source-structural, this repo's idiom for Stripe-heavy routes — cf. subscription-ack-disclosure_test.ts) that the confirmUpgrade gate precedes the mutation, the preview endpoint + retrieveUpcoming exist, and the consent artifact is written; all 10 assertions verified green by replicating them in node against payments.ts. Verified in-sandbox: web tsc -b + eslint clean; billing+hooks vitest 36/36 green; only flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog uses useFlipdeskSubscribe and only use-billing-summary calls the endpoint, so no other caller now 409s. KEPT passes:false: the edge route + the Stripe preview call are not runnable here (no deno, no Stripe test key); run the deno lane + exercise a real paid→higher upgrade against Stripe test mode to confirm the prorated amount + consent row, then flip. | 2026-08-09 THE EDGE HALF IS NOW VALIDATED BY RUNNING IT, and doing that found a hole in the guard itself.

The 2026-07-23 note recorded the edge tests as "unvalidated in-sandbox (no deno)" and said the assertions had been verified by REPLICATING them in node against payments.ts. Deno is on this host, so I ran the real thing: services/edge-functions/src/tests/upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts, 4 passed / 0 failed. Replicating assertions in another runtime proves the assertions, not the test file — and the difference showed up immediately when the file was attacked properly.

⚠ THE HOLE, FOUND BY MUTATION AND NOW CLOSED. Three sabotages were run against payments.ts. Two reddened (deleting the UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED gate, deleting the /flipdesk/upgrade-preview endpoint). THE THIRD DID NOT: replacing the definition with a constant — `const confirmUpgrade = true` — left the whole file GREEN while every unconfirmed click charged a prorated amount again, which is precisely the defect this story exists to fix.

WHY IT SLIPPED, and it generalises: the test asserted `if (!confirmUpgrade)` appears inside inPlaceBlock(), so it proved the gate READS a variable and said nothing about where that variable's value comes from. The definition sits ABOVE the block slice's start marker, so the slice never saw the change. A guard that checks the USE but not the DERIVATION passes over a gate that no longer gates — the worst shape a compliance guard can take, because its greenness is what stops anyone looking.

FIXED: the test now pins the derivation to the request body (const confirmUpgrade = (body...).confirmUpgrade === true) and separately refuses a literal. Re-run of the same three mutations: 3/3 caught, revert green.

STILL passes:false, and the remaining blocker is UNCHANGED and genuinely not doable here: a real paid->higher upgrade against Stripe test mode, to confirm the prorated figure the dialog discloses is the figure Stripe actually charges. The 2026-07-19 note's reasoning still governs and is worth restating because it is why this cannot be waved through — a dialog stating a WRONG prorated amount is worse than today's no-dialog state, because it converts an omission into an affirmative misstatement about a charge. The structural tests prove the gate is wired and now prove it is genuinely wired; they cannot prove the arithmetic.

VERIFIED: upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts 4 passed (now with 2 added assertions), full edge suite 6375 passed / 0 failed, deno lint clean. | 2026-08-09 SCOPE CORRECTION FOUND WHILE WIRING US-2117, and it widens this story rather than advancing it: THE CONFIRMATION GATE IS ON THE FLIPDESK PATH ONLY. services/edge-functions/src/routes/payments.ts POST /buyer/subscribe has its own in-place upgrade branch - retrieve, release schedule, subscriptions.update with proration_behavior 'create_prorations' - and it has NO confirmUpgrade check and no equivalent of the FlipDesk 409 UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED. So a Guard subscriber clicking Connoisseur is charged a prorated amount on a single click with no interstitial and no disclosure: precisely the defect in this story's title, still live, on the buyer product. THAT IS AC1 AND AC3 UNMET FOR ONE OF THE TWO SUBSCRIPTION PRODUCTS, and AC4's test does not catch it because upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts pins the FlipDesk route by name. A guard scoped to one of two identical code paths reads as covering both. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately, because it is not a one-line gate: it needs the buyer equivalent of the proration-preview endpoint and a buyer confirmation dialog, and shipping the 409 without them would break buyer upgrades outright. Recorded so the next pass on this story starts with the correct scope rather than re-finding it. The story's existing blocker (a real paid-to-higher upgrade against Stripe test mode, to confirm the disclosed prorated figure matches what Stripe charges) is unchanged and now applies to both products. | 2026-08-10 THE BUYER HALF IS BUILT. The 2026-08-09 scope correction found that the confirmation gate was on the FlipDesk path ONLY, and that POST /buyer/subscribe had the same in-place branch - retrieve, release schedule, subscriptions.update with create_prorations - with no gate and no disclosure. So a Guard subscriber clicking Connoisseur was charged a prorated amount on one click. That is now closed to parity with FlipDesk. EDGE: /buyer/subscribe refuses without confirmUpgrade (409 UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, gate BEFORE the mutation), and a NEW POST /buyer/upgrade-preview returns amount_due_today_cents / currency / new_recurring_cents / interval / next_renewal_at from stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming simulating the item swap. Kept as its OWN route rather than a product parameter on the FlipDesk one: the two read different subscription ids, different price tables and different plan enums, and a single route branching on a product string is one wrong branch away from previewing a FlipDesk charge for a buyer click. ⚠ THE ENUM TRAP, avoided by reading the schema rather than copying the FlipDesk insert. The consent artifact goes to flipdesk_subscription_events (the generic subscription audit log - App Store, Google Play and admin all reuse it). Its from_plan/to_plan columns are typed public.flipdesk_plan = free|starter|pro|business (00037). Buyer tiers are guard|connoisseur (public.buyer_plan, 00402). Writing to_plan:'guard' raises 22P02 - and because this insert is best-effort BY DESIGN (the plan change already succeeded, so a logging failure must not fail the request), the row would simply never appear while the charge went through. A consent artifact that silently does not exist is worse than none, because the code reads as if it does. The buyer plans go in raw_payload, which is jsonb and has no enum to violate. WEB: useBuyerSubscribe takes confirmUpgrade; NEW useBuyerUpgradePreview; UpgradePreviewDialog generalized to a discriminated product union ('flipdesk' | 'buyer') so a buyer tier cannot be passed as a FlipDesk one - one dialog rather than two near-identical ones that drift. The buyer billing page now diverts an already-paying click to the dialog instead of the mutation; a buyer with NO live subscription still goes straight to Stripe Checkout, which discloses on its own hosted page. THE GUARD THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS, and it is the part worth keeping. upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts named one route, which is exactly how the second one stayed bare for months. It is now driven off a PRODUCTS table, and a new final case DISCOVERS prorating mutations from the source instead: every `await stripe.subscriptions.update(` whose options contain proration_behavior 'create_prorations' must have UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED between the start of its handler and the call. A third subscription product cannot repeat this. The derivation check also became a COUNT (one body-derived confirmUpgrade per product) rather than a presence check, so adding an ungated product fails it. WEB GUARD, derived by scanning src/ rather than from a list, same reasoning: NEW src/test/in-place-upgrade-confirmation.test.ts finds every caller of a subscribe hook, and requires each to render the dialog, to mount it with ITS OWN product string, and - the one that matters - to be able to open the dialog from the very handler that can fire the subscribe mutation. Rendering the dialog is NOT the same as routing to it, and that difference IS this defect: the buyer page could have mounted the dialog and still charged on the click. Handler bodies are brace-matched rather than sliced to the mutation, because the FlipDesk picker puts the mutation in one if/else arm and the dialog in the other. MY FIRST TWO WEB ASSERTIONS WERE TOO WEAK AND SABOTAGE FOUND BOTH. Deleting the buyer page's diversion left the file green (it still RENDERED the dialog), and replacing the disclosed amount with money(null) left it green (the field name still appeared elsewhere). Both are now bound: the handler check above, and the figures asserted as BINDINGS to the preview response (value={money(data.amount_due_today_cents, currency)} etc.) rather than as strings present in the file. ALSO FIXED A HARNESS BUG WORTH RECORDING: my sabotage runner stripped ANSI as /\[[0-9;]*m/ without the ESC character, so deno's coloured 'name ... FAILED' lines never matched and EVERY mutation reported NOTHING FAILED. I nearly read that as the tests being weak. A negative verification whose PARSER is broken is indistinguishable from one that found nothing - the runner needs a control mutation that is expected to change nothing, which this one now has (moving a no-op line inside the gate; it correctly stays green). STILL passes:false, blocker UNCHANGED and now covering both products: a real paid-to-higher upgrade against Stripe test mode, to confirm the prorated figure the dialog discloses is the figure Stripe actually charges. The 2026-07-19 reasoning still governs - a dialog stating a WRONG prorated amount is worse than no dialog, because it converts an omission into an affirmative misstatement about a charge. The structural tests prove the gate is wired; they cannot prove the arithmetic. AC2 also still wants confirming that the webhook's recordAgreedTerms writes a buyer agreement row for an in-place change (US-2117 landed the plumbing). VERIFIED: npx tsc -b clean; eslint 0 errors / 13 warnings (baseline held); npm run ui:check 0 blocking / 0 noise; full edge suite 6431 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (up 7); upgrade-confirmation-gate_test.ts 11 passed; in-place-upgrade-confirmation.test.ts 10 passed; deno lint clean across 1481 files. SEVEN SABOTAGE MUTATIONS plus one CONTROL: buyer gate removed, confirmUpgrade made a constant, the preview stops simulating the swap, the consent artifact dropped, the page fires the mutation instead of the dialog, the dialog mounted as the wrong product, the disclosed amount blanked - each reddened its own named test; the control changed nothing and nothing went red. ALSO: prd.json had accumulated one passes:true story (US-2433) and the US-2366 archive guard was failing the web suite - archived it (120 active, 2325 archived, nextId unchanged).

userStories.title: No advance renewal reminder exists anywhere — annual plans are charged silently
userStories.description: Confirmed absence, verified three ways: invoice.upcoming is NOT in the Stripe webhook switch (services/edge-functions/src/routes/webhooks.ts:244-281, falls through to a default log-and-drop at :281); no cron in jobs-cron-fleet.ts sends one; and the only upcoming_invoice reference is a read-only pull for the billing page (payments.ts:1142). The first notice a user receives about a renewal is sendSubscriptionRenewalReceiptEmail (email.ts:1183), sent AFTER the money is taken. Yearly price IDs exist for all five paid tiers (src/lib/constants.ts:1344-1366) and flow through the identical path — interval only changes a display string — so an annual subscriber is charged a full year's fee with no prior contact whatsoever.
acceptanceCriteria: Handle invoice.upcoming and send a transactional advance renewal notice stating the amount, the date of the charge, the plan, and how to cancel before it.
Configure the Stripe lead time explicitly rather than relying on the default, and set a longer lead for annual plans than monthly.
Send via deliverEmail as a TRANSACTIONAL category — it must not be routed through the drip/marketing engine where opt-out, suppression or frequency caps can silently drop it.
Also handle customer.subscription.trial_will_end.
Test that an annual subscription produces a reminder before renewal and that a marketing opt-out does not suppress it.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/Comms] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Advance notice before a long-term renewal is a common state-ARL requirement and we have annual plans in production. Cheapest structural fix in the batch: one webhook case reusing existing email infrastructure. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC3 + AC4 + AC5 DONE (mechanism, not copy — the fourth compliance story that did not need counsel). invoice.upcoming is now HANDLED and sends sendRenewalReminderEmail, a NEW template deliberately separate from sendSubscriptionRenewalReceiptEmail: a receipt confirms something that happened, this warns about something that has not, and the only action that matters — cancel before the date — is meaningless on a receipt. It states the plan, the amount, the exact charge date and how to cancel. AC3: category subscription_renewal_reminder is registered in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES, so resolveIsMarketing force-classifies it transactional even if marketing:true is explicitly requested — pinned by a test, because if that ever flips, an opt-out silently drops the only advance warning of a charge and the exact defect returns. AC4 customer.subscription.trial_will_end is handled too, and THE DISJOINTNESS IS THE INTERESTING PART: our signup trial has NO Stripe subscription (handle_new_user grants it directly), and US-2120's cron filters flipdesk_subscription_id IS NULL. This event fires only for a STRIPE-managed trial — someone who started a PAID subscription with a trial period — which is exactly the user that cron skips. The two populations cannot overlap, so neither path double-sends. A test asserts the cron keeps that filter, since removing it would make both fire for the same person. It reuses sendTrialExpiringEmail rather than minting a second trial template, because two near-identical trial emails drift. DECLINES TO SEND WITHOUT A DATE: if Stripe supplies neither next_payment_attempt nor period_end the handler returns. A notice that cannot say WHEN is not a notice, and 'you will be charged at some point' is worse than silence. Same reasoning as US-2117's refusal to write a partial agreement. TWO OF MY OWN EARLIER ARTEFACTS CAUGHT THIS CHANGE, which is the guards working: (1) the US-2128 test asserting invoice.upcoming and trial_will_end were on the known-ignored list went RED, correctly — they had graduated to real handlers, and a handled event must never ALSO be listed as ignored or the list is lying. Rewritten to assert the list stays annotated rather than naming those two specifically. (2) Removing them left an ORPHANED group header ('Covered by their own stories / other handlers.') heading an empty group — deleted. STILL OPEN: AC2 only — configure the Stripe lead time explicitly (and longer for annual than monthly). That is a Stripe dashboard/API setting, not code: Stripe decides when invoice.upcoming fires, and the default is 3 days. Worth doing since a 3-day warning on a full YEAR's charge is thin, but it cannot be set from here. Verified: edge 4306 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 VERIFIED ALREADY DONE (US-2089-style stale box). This story's premise — 'invoice.upcoming is NOT in the Stripe webhook switch' — is no longer true: webhooks.ts dispatches invoice.upcoming to handleInvoiceUpcoming (:284) AND customer.subscription.trial_will_end to handleTrialWillEnd (:294), both carrying US-2119 attribution comments. Closed by that work; the story was simply never flipped. Found while triaging the P1 Compliance/Comms cluster for US-2122. NOT marking passes:true from here, because I did not verify AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead-time configuration, which is a dashboard setting) or AC5's live test — someone with Stripe access should confirm those two before closing. | 2026-07-22 ADDED THE MISSING AC3/AC5 GUARD (agent loop), passes:false held on the external ACs. The prior note flagged that it "did not verify AC5"; the transactional half of AC5 (and AC3) had NO test at all — sendRenewalReminderEmail uses category subscription_renewal_reminder (email.ts:2936) which IS in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES (email-transport.ts:49), so resolveIsMarketing force-classifies it transactional and a marketing opt-out cannot suppress it — but nothing pinned that. If someone reclassified it, the renewal reminder would silently become marketing-suppressible and an annual subscriber could be charged with no warning (the exact US-2120 bug class). New services/edge-functions/src/tests/renewal-reminder_test.ts (2 tests, mirrors trial-notice_test.ts): asserts the category is transactional + resolveIsMarketing===false, and structurally that webhooks.ts dispatches invoice.upcoming to sendRenewalReminderEmail (not the drip). Verified: deno check+lint clean, 2 tests pass. STILL passes:false: AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead-time is a Dashboard billing setting — Settings->Billing->Upcoming renewal reminders — not code) and AC5's live half (an annual sub actually producing a reminder before renewal needs a Stripe run). AC1/AC3/AC4 are done (handleInvoiceUpcoming + handleTrialWillEnd wired, transactional category, now guarded). | 2026-08-10 THE BUYER HALF EXISTED NOWHERE, and that is a bigger gap than the one this story last recorded as open. handleInvoiceUpcoming opened with `if (invoiceIsBuyer(invoice)) return;`. That line is copied from three sibling handlers where it is CORRECT - handleInvoicePaymentSucceeded, handleInvoicePaymentFailed and handleInvoicePaymentActionRequired all do seller cycle resets or dunning transitions whose buyer equivalent arrives on customer.subscription.updated. This handler does none of that. It only SENDS A NOTICE, and it is the only place one is sent (verified: sendRenewalReminderEmail has exactly one non-test call site). So a buyer on an ANNUAL plan was charged a full year with no prior contact whatsoever - the literal words of this story's own title, still live on the other product, while the story read as 'AC1 done'. Same shape as US-2118, hours earlier: a compliance control built for FlipDesk and never wired to the buyer product, with a guard that named one route. FIXED: handleInvoiceUpcoming now branches instead of returning. A lapsed buyer (buyer_plan 'free') is still skipped - naming 'Free' in a charge notice is worse than silence. recordEvent keeps from_plan/to_plan as the user's real flipdesk_plan because those columns are typed public.flipdesk_plan and a buyer tier raises 22P02 there; the buyer detail goes in the jsonb payload. Same enum trap US-2118 hit. THE EMAIL WAS SELLER-SHAPED IN TWO PLACES, not one. It hardcoded 'FlipDesk' in the subject AND the body, and linked to /dashboard/billing. A buyer notice with the seller's billing link is arguably worse than no notice: it names the correct charge and then sends the reader to a page that cannot cancel it, at the one moment the whole email exists to enable action. Both values now come from NEW lib/renewal-notice-copy.ts - a pure module rather than an inline ternary, so the values can be ASSERTED rather than regex-matched. `product` on RenewalReminderData is REQUIRED with no default, deliberately: the default would have been 'flipdesk' and every buyer would have silently gotten the wrong one. GUARD: a new census case walks every `if (invoiceIsBuyer(invoice)) return;` in webhooks.ts and requires the comment above it to name where the buyer path IS served ('subscription.updated'). A skip is not wrong; an UNEXPLAINED skip is - and the next person to copy that line now has to answer the question that was skipped here. It also asserts handleInvoiceUpcoming has none, and that the EMAIL argument (not merely the handler) carries the product. THAT LAST SCOPING WAS FOUND BY SABOTAGE, and it is the third time this session the same mistake shape has appeared. My first assertion checked the whole handler body for `product: isBuyer ? ...`, which ALSO appears in the recordEvent payload a few lines above - so pinning the email argument to a constant left the test green while buyers got FlipDesk copy. Checking the use and not the specific site is how a guard passes over the thing it guards. NEW STORY FILED, not scope creep: US-2451. The renewal RECEIPT is inside handleInvoicePaymentSucceeded, behind the same buyer skip, and applyBuyerSubscriptionChange sends none - so a buyer is charged and hears nothing afterwards either. Its skip is legitimately protecting seller cycle resets, so the fix is to split the send out of the skipped body rather than widen it. Out of scope here because this story is about the ADVANCE notice. STILL passes:false on the same two ACs as before, both external: AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead time - a Dashboard setting under Settings -> Billing -> Upcoming renewal reminders, and note Stripe's 3-day default is thin for a full YEAR's charge) and AC5's live half (an annual subscription actually producing a reminder before renewal, which needs a Stripe run). Neither is code and neither moved. VERIFIED: deno check clean on webhooks.ts, email.ts and the new module; deno lint clean across 1482 files; renewal-reminder_test.ts 5 passed (up 3); full edge suite 6434 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (up 3). SEVEN SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own named test: the buyer skip restored on the notice handler, a NEW unexplained skip added to another handler, the email argument pinned to a constant product, the buyer manage URL pointed at the seller page, the buyer product name left as FlipDesk, the trailing-slash guard removed, and the template re-hardcoded. | 2026-08-10 (second pass) AC4 WAS HANDLED BUT NOT PRODUCT-AWARE, which is the INVERSE of the five buyer omissions closed alongside it today: not silence, but confidently wrong. handleTrialWillEnd had no subscriptionIsBuyer check. A BUYER subscription with a Stripe-managed trial would have been sent sendTrialExpiringEmail - copy that names a '14-day FlipDesk Pro trial', offers to keep 'your Pro features', and links to the seller billing page. Every sentence of it false for the recipient, on a notice whose only job is to prompt a payment method before access lapses. SKIPPED RATHER THAN GIVEN NEW COPY, and the reason is a product fact rather than caution: A BUYER STRIPE TRIAL IS NOT A PRODUCT STATE. POST /buyer/subscribe builds its Checkout session with no trial_period_days and no subscription_data.trial_end, so one can only exist if someone configures a trial on a price in the Stripe dashboard. Writing a notice for a flow that does not exist means guessing what it should say, and this story's own AC1 reasoning applies - a notice that cannot state the real terms is worse than none. Same call as US-2453's buyer pause/resume decision. THE PREMISE IS GUARDED, NOT ASSUMED, and that is what separates this from the omissions it sits beside. A second test reads /buyer/subscribe and fails if it ever sets trial_period_days or trial_end - so the day a buyer trial ships, the skip fails loudly and names itself, instead of quietly outliving its reason the way the five did. The warn log names the story too, so an operator seeing the event in production has a thread to pull. THREE SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own named test: the skip removed (a buyer gets the seller's trial email), the skip moved after the send, and a trial_period_days added to /buyer/subscribe. AC4 IS NOW GENUINELY DONE - the event is handled and handled correctly for both products. AC1/AC3/AC5's transactional half remain done. STILL passes:false on the SAME two external ACs as before, neither of which moved: AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead time, a Dashboard setting under Settings -> Billing -> Upcoming renewal reminders, where the 3-day default is thin for a full year's charge) and AC5's live half (an annual subscription actually producing a reminder before renewal, which needs a Stripe run). VERIFIED: deno check clean on webhooks.ts; deno lint clean across 1486 files; buyer-lifecycle-emails_test.ts 11 passed (2 new); full edge suite 6461 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored (up 2).

userStories.title: iOS paywall advertises 1,000 AI actions for Pro; the server grants 750
userStories.description: ios/GradeThread/Billing/IAPProduct.swift:88,93 advertises Pro as '1,000 listings · 1,000 AI actions · 30 grades · AutoLister'. Both the server catalog (services/edge-functions/src/lib/appstore/products.ts:75,80) and web (src/lib/constants.ts:243, aiActionsPerMonth: 750) say 750. iOS buyers are sold 1,000 AI actions and will be plan-gated at 750 — a paid-for entitlement that does not exist. The drift test that should catch this (iap-catalog-drift_test.ts:69-106) compares ids, credits, plan/interval and fallbackPrice but NOT blurb or title, so the guard has a hole exactly where the misleading copy lives.
acceptanceCriteria: Correct the iOS copy to match the entitlement actually granted (or change the entitlement — but the two must agree).
Extend iap-catalog-drift_test.ts to compare user-facing blurb and title against the server catalog, so advertised entitlements cannot drift from granted ones.
Audit every other advertised number on the paywall against the server catalog.
Check whether any user purchased Pro on iOS under the 1,000 copy and determine remediation with the review gate.
userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/iOS] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Distinct from the disclosure gaps: this is a straightforward misrepresentation of what was purchased (FTC Act Section 5), and it is the only finding here with a potential remediation obligation to existing buyers. Manage or cancel anytime in Settings'). Reuse that copy as the model for the web disclosure story. The externally published App Store metadata (APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md) says 750 throughout and was never wrong, so the misrepresentation was at the in-app point of purchase, not in the store listing. AC3 AUDIT RESULT (mechanical, not by eye): the extended drift test enumerated ALL mismatches in one run — exactly two, the Pro monthly and Pro yearly blurbs. Every other title and blurb across the catalog already matched. No hardcoded plan numbers exist elsewhere in the iOS paywall (checked; all other AI-action strings are computed from server values). Done: AC1 both Pro blurbs corrected to the granted 750; AC2 iap-catalog-drift_test.ts now parses and compares title + blurb, collecting all drift rather than asserting per-product (a per-product assert stops at the first mismatch, which would have turned AC3 into find-one-and-guess). Both branches negative-verified. OPEN AC4: needs a prod query I cannot run — did anyone purchase Pro on iOS between 2026-07-02 and 2026-07-19? If so remediation goes through the review gate. userStories.title: Substantiation review of every public authenticity claim and its framing
userStories.description: Authenticity verdicts (likely_authentic / inconclusive / red_flags) are shown on public certificates and returned from an unauthenticated public endpoint, currently with no accuracy gate behind them. Separately, the seeded brand KB was written to REFUSE authentication — 00398_coach_brand_knowledge.sql:14 reads 'NEVER auto-authenticate... A creed/serial proves NOTHING about authenticity on its own' — so our own knowledge base contradicts the product's public posture. That contradiction needs resolving deliberately, not by drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Review every user-facing authenticity string against what the evidence can actually support, with counsel — fold into the US-2114 review gate rather than running a separate process.

Decide and document the claim posture: assessment/opinion with stated limitations vs verification. The pipeline is built for the former (confidence ceilinged at 0.9, hard-capped to 0.5 on contradiction, limitations set from a constant the model cannot override) — keep that discipline in the copy.
Reconcile the brand-KB 'never auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture.

Check eBay policy exposure: grade-badge.ts is already dead because eBay bans grade overlays on listing imagery, and eBay runs its own Authenticity Guarantee — determine what may be stated on a listing before building listing-facing surfaces.
Confirm the unauthenticated public endpoint should expose verdicts at all.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Legal][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Pairs with the FTC Section 5 batch (US-2114..2128) — same substantiation problem, different claim. Do not let an agent draft the claim language. ACCURACY GATE 2026-07-19 (decided: adopt the conservative posture ahead of counsel): the public /tools/authenticity-check endpoint now requires a PASSING eval run in addition to PUBLIC_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_ENABLED. CORRECTION to an earlier characterisation of the exposure: that endpoint was ALREADY fail-closed behind the env flag (default off) and documented as awaiting legal review of the limitations copy — so the risk was lower than described. What was missing is that the env flag is the LEGAL gate (a human read the copy) and says nothing about whether the model is any good; enabling it after a legal review should not be sufficient to publish verdicts from a prompt version that has never cleared the golden set. The two gates are now separate and both required. Authenticated surfaces (paid add-on, buyer check) deliberately still run ungated — they carry the limitations disclaimer and a named account, a different posture from an anonymous public claim. Returns 503 + Retry-After rather than 404 so a crawler does not deindex the tool page behind it. 4431 edge tests pass. | 2026-08-09 AC3 NOW OWNS A REQUIREMENT THAT WAS DUPLICATED, and inherits the evidence. US-2139 AC6 asked for the same reconciliation ('see US-2133' in its own text) and has been closed as a duplicate, so this AC is the single home for it. WHAT THE CONTRADICTION ACTUALLY IS, measured rather than described, so the work starts from facts: 37 seeded brand packs carry prose such as 'NEVER label a Coach item authentic — flag anything inconsistent in condition notes only' (00398_coach_brand_knowledge.sql) and 'LUXURY — never auto-authenticate' (00399_louis_vuitton_brand_knowledge.sql), while the shipped pipeline's deriveVerdict (lib/ai-authenticity.ts) emits 'likely_authentic' as one of three possible verdicts on a PAID add-on. TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS. (1) The gap may be one of WORDING rather than of posture: the shipped verdict is confidence-capped (AUTHENTICITY_VERDICT_CONFIDENCE_CEILING 0.9, harder caps for contradictions, no-macro evidence, thin reference coverage and — as of today — unverified brand tells) and carries a mandatory disclosure, so a capped-and-disclosed 'likely authentic' is arguably not the act the KB prose forbids. Settling that is AC2's job and this AC's answer follows from it. (2) THE FIX CANNOT BE AN EDIT TO THE SEEDS. That prose lives in applied migrations, which are immutable — the reconciliation has to land in the vault (vault/20-domain/brands/ already owns the KB's governing rules) with the seeds left alone, exactly as US-2059 requires for any knowledge stranded in a migration header. ⚠ NOT AGENT WORK, restating this story's own instruction because it is the thing most likely to be overlooked by whoever picks it up: 'Do not let an agent draft the claim language', and AC1 requires review WITH COUNSEL. What an agent CAN safely do here is exactly what this note does — locate both sides, quote them, and stop. | 2026-08-10 THE INVENTORY AC1 NEEDS NOW EXISTS, and nothing here drafts a claim. This story's own note says what an agent may safely do - locate both sides, quote them, and stop - and the 2026-08-09 pass did that for ONE example (the brand-KB contradiction). This does it exhaustively, which is the difference between an anecdote and an inventory. NEW vault/20-domain/authenticity-claim-register.md. The three verdicts and the exact strings a user reads; what the pipeline actually supports for them; what the evidence base actually is; and the KB contradiction, carried over rather than restated. THE ONE OBSERVATION WORTH THE WHOLE PAGE: the rendered labels are deliberately WEAKER than the enum names. likely_authentic renders as 'Looks consistent with genuine' - an observation about photographs - where the enum name would read as a judgement about the item. That single string IS the product's legal posture, and nothing was pinning it. A copy edit to 'Authentic' would be a posture change that nobody would file a bug about. It is pinned now. WHAT BACKS THE CLAIMS, gathered so a reviewer is not doing archaeology: AUTHENTICITY_LIMITATIONS is a fixed constant the model cannot author and states in the output that this is 'not a definitive authentication, legal opinion, or guarantee' and 'one trust signal, not proof'; AUTHENTICITY_NO_MACRO_LIMITATION is appended when no close-up backed the read; confidence is ceilinged and capped harder on contradiction, missing macro evidence, thin coverage and unverified tells, composing by minimum and never raising; and the public endpoint has TWO independent gates because the env flag is the LEGAL gate and says nothing about whether the model is any good. AND THE UNCOMFORTABLE NUMBER, because the review needs it more than any of the above: all 179 seeded authentication_tells payloads use the LEGACY {tell, detail} shape and ZERO use the structured one, so coerceTell maps them to category 'other' with no redFlag - they are prose the prompt reads and the verdict cannot use. CANONICAL_TELLS holds 7 structured tells across 3 brands, every one sourced 'unverified - review in admin'. The distinction that matters is between HAVING tells and having USABLE tells (US-2219 measured this; the register carries it forward rather than making the reviewer find it). GUARD: NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/authenticity-claim-register_test.ts. Reads the verdict union from the TYPE and the labels from the page's map, and fails when either is unregistered - so a fourth verdict or a reworded label cannot ship unseen. It also fails a label containing Authentic / Verified / Confirmed genuine / Genuine item / Guaranteed, requires the positive verdict to stay an observation ('consistent'), and fails if AUTHENTICITY_LIMITATIONS stops saying the two things the register cites it for. Plus the same honesty rule as the subscription register: no line may claim substantiation without a dated record. FIVE SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: the positive verdict reworded to 'Authentic', a label reworded without updating the register, a fourth verdict added, the limitations constant losing 'not proof', and the register claiming substantiation. STILL passes:false and nothing here changes that. AC1 is the review itself, AC2 the posture decision, AC3 the KB reconciliation, AC4 the eBay policy question, AC5 whether the unauthenticated endpoint should expose verdicts at all - all counsel or owner work. What changed is that the review has a complete list with its evidence attached, and the one string carrying the posture can no longer move by accident while it waits. VERIFIED: authenticity-claim-register_test.ts 5 passed (new); deno lint clean across 1490 files; full edge suite 6481 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; vault:lint --strict clean at 168 notes.

userStories.title: Garment sellers are never asked for a serial or date-code photo
userStories.description: photo-profiles.ts:31-45 defines serial and marking slots but surfaces them ONLY for non-clothing profiles. A garment seller is never prompted for a date code, interior stamp, or hardware close-up — while ai-authenticity.ts:142-151 asks the model for stitch-per-inch, embroidery backing, screen-print registration and rivet engraving. The prompt requests evidence the capture flow never collects. This is the cheapest single improvement to authenticity signal quality.
acceptanceCriteria: Add serial/date-code and hardware/stamp macro slots to the clothing photo profile, surfaced when the authenticity add-on is active.
Make them optional-but-encouraged rather than blocking a condition grade — a grade must never fail because an authenticity slot was skipped.
Feed slot presence into the authenticity confidence: absent macro evidence should lower confidence and widen limitations, not be silently ignored.
Mirror across web and iOS (photo required-set and order surfaces change together — see the photo-required-and-order-surfaces memory; ~7 spots).
Update the prompt so it asks only for what the available slots can actually support.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Capture][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Highest-leverage unblocked item in Phase 1 — everything downstream depends on capturing the right pixels. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: added optional serial (Serial / Date code) + marking (Brand stamp / Hardware) roles to the CLOTHING photo profile with macro-specific hints. Pure config — both storage types already existed in the enum (migration 00230) and were merely never surfaced for clothing, so NO migration and NO client release: photo-profiles.ts is server-authoritative and both clients fetch it (iOS already maps both, PhotoSlotType.swift:46-47). Kept OPTIONAL so a condition grade can never fail on a skipped authenticity slot, which also avoids touching the ~7-surface required-set duplication. STILL OPEN on this story: (a) feed slot presence into authenticity confidence so absent macro evidence lowers it and widens limitations rather than being silently ignored; (b) narrow the prompt so it stops asking for evidence no slot can supply; (c) surface the slots conditionally when the add-on is active. ITER3 2026-07-19: closed the confidence half. (1) FIXED A GAP IN ITER2 — serial/marking were absent from AUTHENTICITY_IMAGE_PRIORITY, so the new slots would have been captured and never reached the model; they now rank ABOVE label so a deliberate authenticity frame is not crowded out of the MAX_AUTHENTICITY_IMAGES budget. (2) hasMacroEvidence() + AUTHENTICITY_NO_MACRO_CONFIDENCE_CAP=0.7 composed into applyVerdictCap as min-of-caps (never raises, per the grading-engine rule); detail deliberately does NOT count as macro evidence. (3) limitations widened with a fixed constant when no macro frame backed the verdict. Image types are taken POST-selection, so a macro frame dropped by the cap cannot license confidence. New params default to the old behavior so existing callers are byte-identical. 4354 edge tests pass (+6). PRODUCT DECISION LEFT OPEN: 0.7 was chosen because it sits exactly on both thresholds — deriveVerdict needs >=0.7 for likely_authentic and authenticityNeedsReview forces review BELOW 0.7 — so it removes high confidence without flipping every existing no-macro verdict to inconclusive or flooding the review queue. Going stricter is defensible but changes the headline verdict on past assessments; that is a product call, not a refactor call. STILL OPEN: narrow the prompt (it still asks for stitch-per-inch/embroidery backing that only a macro frame could support) and surface the slots conditionally when the add-on is active. BLOCKED (prompt half) 2026-07-19: narrowing SYSTEM_PROMPT is a PROMPT TEXT change, and the grading-engine contract requires that to go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary rather than a silent edit. The authenticity eval cannot pass until US-2131 seeds a golden set, so the prompt narrowing is GATED ON US-2131 — it is not independently shippable. Deliberately NOT edited silently. When unblocked, the sanctioned route is the additive/flag-gated pattern the skill describes: a macro-awareness block that suffixes prompt_version (mirroring authenticity_v1+tells) and is byte-identical when disabled, test-guarded. | 2026-08-11 AC1 CLOSED — the slots are now conditional. They had been added to CLOTHING_TAIL unconditionally, so EVERY clothing seller was asked to 'fill the frame with the date code' for an add-on most of them cannot buy. applyAuthenticityMacroVisibility(profile, eligible) is pure and lives in photo-profiles.ts; the eligibility read lives in the route, so the table stays unit-testable with no database. THE FILTER IS SCOPED TO CLOTHING AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: serial and marking mean two different things. On a WATCH, HANDBAG, JEWELLERY, ELECTRONICS or COLLECTIBLE they are core CONDITION evidence — jewelry, bags and electronics even mark one REQUIRED — and a watch with no reference number is under-photographed whatever anyone bought. Those five profiles are untouched, test-asserted by name. ELIGIBILITY IS ACCOUNT-LEVEL, NOT THE PER-SUBMISSION OPT-IN, and the distinction is forced by the timing: the add-on is chosen at grade time on a paid tier (routes/grade.ts), which has not happened yet when the capture list is being drawn. So the honest question here is 'could they use these?' — isFeatureEnabled('authenticity_addon', {userId}) — not 'did they buy it?'. FAILS OPEN to the pre-US-2134 behaviour: isFeatureEnabled defaults true on a missing row or read error, which is the right direction, since wrongly showing two optional slots costs a little scrolling while wrongly hiding them means a seller who PAID for the add-on is never asked for its photos. The eligible path returns the SAME OBJECT (assertStrictEquals across every profile), so 'nothing changed for sellers who have the add-on' is checkable rather than asserted. ⚠ THE TENANT-ISOLATION AUDIT FOUND A REAL BUG IN MY FIRST VERSION and it is the reverse of a leak. I wrote 'workspaceOwnerId ?? userId', which is the correct expression — but only authMiddleware was mounted on /api/flipdesk/photo-profiles/*, never workspaceMiddleware, so workspaceOwnerId was ALWAYS undefined and the first half was dead code. authenticity_addon is in PLAN_TARGETABLE_FLAGS, so a member capturing inside owner A's paid workspace would have been judged on their own free plan and lost the slots A paid for — precisely the 'wrongly hiding them' direction my own docstring calls the worse failure. Fixed by mounting workspaceMiddleware (absent header defaults to the caller, so solo users are unaffected); a test asserts the MOUNT, since the route expression was already right and what was missing was the middleware that gives it meaning. AC2 HOLDS AND IS NOW PINNED: a test fails if any clothing authenticity macro is ever marked required, because a hidden required slot would block a condition grade. AC3 was closed in ITER3. FOUR SABOTAGES, each reddening its own case: the clothing scope removed (strips watches), the eligible path returning a copy, only 'serial' filtered with 'marking' forgotten, and workspaceMiddleware unmounted. ⚠ ONE TEST OF MINE FAILED AGAINST CORRECT CODE first run: I filtered non-clothing as 'category !== clothing', but the clothing sub-profiles are keyed clothing:top, clothing:dress and so on, so five clothing profiles landed in the keep-the-macros case. The list is now named explicitly. STILL OPEN: AC5 (narrow the prompt) remains gated on US-2131's golden set. ALSO SURFACED BY THE AUDIT, NOT FIXED, needs its own story: this endpoint stopped being static, and the iOS and Android clients cache it for an hour keyed on PATH ONLY, with no clear on sign-out or workspace switch. Sign out of B and into A within the hour and A sees B's slot list. Staleness rather than disclosure — the body carries no tenant data, only which optional slots show — but the caches were designed when this was static. Web is already correct (queryClient.clear() on both sign-out and workspace switch).

userStories.title: Capture resolution caps out below what authentication needs
userStories.description: Two downscales happen before upload: web at 2400px width (image-utils.ts:350) and iOS at 1600px long edge, q0.75 — explicitly lowered from 2048/0.8 for upload speed (PhotoCompressor.swift:17-24). The server does no further resize, and Claude's own ~1568px normalization is the effective ceiling. A label filling a third of the frame yields roughly 500px of label: enough to OCR a size, nowhere near enough for stitch density, kerning, weave or engraving fidelity. The only real magnification path today is the Forensic add-on's defect zoom (grading-pipeline.ts:130-172), which crops the retained original and upscales to a 320px minimum — but it is keyed to defect bboxes only, never to tags or hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: Retain a higher-resolution original for authenticity macro slots, or upload them at a higher cap than general condition photos.
Generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline to authenticity regions (tag, stamp, hardware, stitching) rather than defect bboxes only — this is the most reusable existing asset.
Measure the delivered pixel density per macro region and record it, so confidence can be conditioned on real evidence quality rather than assumed.
Respect the existing storage/upload hardening path (validateImageUpload -> stripImageMetadata -> upload) and the Vision budget ceiling.
Do not raise resolution globally — the upload-speed tradeoff that motivated the iOS reduction is real; scope the increase to authenticity slots.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Capture][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Without this the prompt is asking for evidence the pixels cannot carry, which is precisely how an ungated model produces confident nonsense. | 2026-07-31 AC1+AC5 DONE (web). Authenticity slots (serial/marking/surface/corner/sole) now compress to 3600px, tag/label/detail/defect/interior/certificate to 3000, everything else keeps the unchanged 2400 default -- uploadMaxWidthFor() in src/lib/macro-photo-quality.ts, applied at both upload paths (submission photo-upload.tsx and FlipDesk photo-uploader.tsx). AC5 respected literally: the increase is scoped, because the iOS cap was LOWERED to 1600px deliberately for upload speed and that tradeoff is real on mobile data. STATED PLAINLY IN THE CODE, because the number looks like a win it is not: Claude normalizes long edge to ~1568px, so more pixels do NOT change what the model sees today. What changes is what we RETAINED -- the crop-and-zoom pipeline of AC2 cannot recover detail thrown away at capture, so AC1 necessarily lands before AC2 and looks inert until it does. SIZED AGAINST THE CEILING RATHER THAN PICKED: client MAX_FILE_SIZE and edge DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES both cap at 10MB and the server dimension guard at 12,000px; a 3600px WebP at q0.85 runs 1-3MB, while the ~4700px a third-frame crop would need to reach Claude's own ceiling does not fit -- which is why 3600 and not more. The cap table lives beside the US-2136 QUALITY table on purpose and a test pins that every gated slot's cap exceeds its own floor: a slot with a 900px floor and the 2400 default cap would have been nagged for resolution the pipeline was never asked to keep. Both upload paths now resolve the slot photo_type ONCE and feed both the cap and the gate, so they cannot disagree about which slot a photo is. 32 tests total in macro-photo-quality.test.ts.
