STILL OPEN: AC2 (generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop to authenticity regions) is edge-side and substantial; AC3 (record delivered pixel density per region) needs per-photo persistence, i.e. a migration, which the held-migration rule bars from being pushed without an operator prod-apply first; AC4 was already satisfied (the storage hardening path is untouched -- this only changes a client-side compress cap). iOS half (PhotoCompressor 1600px) NOT done: Swift cannot be built in this environment. Verified: tsc -b clean, lint 0 errors, 2903 tests pass, build green. | 2026-08-09 AC2 SCOPED, NOT STARTED, and the scoping changes which existing mechanism it should reuse. AC2 says 'generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline to authenticity regions (tag, stamp, hardware, stitching)'. THE DEFECT ZOOM IS THE WRONG PARENT. It exists because a sub-3mm hole on a WHOLE-GARMENT shot falls below a pixel after the vision API downscales, so it crops a bbox out of the high-res original and re-reads just that region. Authenticity macro slots are not that case: serial, marking, surface, corner and sole are ALREADY dedicated close-ups, and they have no bbox because the whole photo IS the region. THE RIGHT PARENT IS ALREADY IN THE FILE, twelve lines below the defect zoom: ai-grading.ts's RereadCandidate / selectLabelsForReread (US-1296) re-reads the retained high-res ORIGINAL of the SAME image with the EXISTING per-image prompt — no crop, no bbox, and crucially no prompt-version change, because the prompt is unchanged. Its own header already names the two regions it covers (an illegible care label, a possibly-manipulated image) and says they differ from the defect zoom precisely because 'the whole label/photo IS the region'. Authenticity macros are a third instance of that same shape, not of the crop shape. THE SELECTOR IS ALSO ALREADY BUILT, as of today. selectLabelsForReread picks on a semantic signal (the pass judged the label illegible, or returned no fiber_content). For an authenticity macro the equivalent signal is now PERSISTED: US-2136 AC4 landed submission_images.quality_score (migration 00568, HELD), the normalized 0..1 sharpness measured on the compressed bytes, and a soft macro is exactly 'worth re-reading at higher resolution'. So the selector is a threshold on a number that already exists rather than a new measurement — which also means AC3 ('measure the delivered pixel density per macro region and record it') is PARTLY DONE by 00568 and should be re-read before being re-implemented: sharpness is recorded per image, pixel density per REGION is not, and for a dedicated macro slot those are close to the same question. TWO PRECONDITIONS THE AC DOES NOT MENTION. (1) The re-read path reads the RETAINED HIGH-RES ORIGINAL, and retention is gated by RETAIN_ORIGINAL_IMAGES — with it off there is no higher-resolution copy to re-read and the whole feature is inert, exactly as AC1 was inert until AC2. (2) The authenticity pass runs INSIDE withImageBufferSlot in parallel with the per-image pass, so a re-read that depends on the authenticity result has the same ordering problem US-2138 hit: it cannot be chained without serialising two vision calls on the paid path. Reading the quality score instead of the authenticity verdict avoids that entirely, because the score is already on the row before the slot opens — which is the strongest argument for the selector above. WHY I DID NOT SHIP THE SELECTOR ALONE: a pure function with no caller is the exact shipped-but-unwired shape this repo has found five times today, and adding a sixth deliberately would be worse than leaving the work scoped. Wire it and the selector together or not at all. | 2026-08-09 (second pass) AC2 SHIPPED, wired end to end rather than left as a selector with no caller. NEW selectMacrosForReread in ai-grading.ts plus its consumer loop in runRereadPass, so a soft authenticity macro now earns a high-resolution re-read of the retained original. IT JOINED THE WRONG FAMILY ON PURPOSE — the AC says 'generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline', and it does not. The defect zoom crops a bbox because a sub-3mm hole on a WHOLE-GARMENT shot falls below a pixel after the vision API downscales. A serial, a heat stamp, a corner is already a dedicated close-up: there is no bbox because the whole photo IS the region, which is exactly what the US-1296 label re-read says about itself twelve lines below the zoom in the same file. So this is the third member of the RE-READ family, and it inherits the property that matters — same image, same prompt, so no prompt_version moves and there is nothing to shadow, eval or canary. THE SELECTOR IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A MODEL OPINION, and that is the design rather than a convenience. Its two siblings pick on what the first pass SAID (the label was illegible; the photo looked manipulated). This one picks on submission_images.quality_score — the normalized 0..1 sharpness measured client-side on the compressed bytes, which US-2136 AC4 persisted earlier today (migration 00568, HELD). That is the only signal that WORKS here: keying off the authenticity verdict would mean chaining the re-read behind the authenticity call, which runs in PARALLEL with the per-image pass inside the memory gate, so it would serialise two vision calls on the paid grading path. The score is already on the row before any of that starts. A NULL SCORE DOES NOT SELECT, and the check is typeof rather than Number()+isFinite: Number(null) is 0 and finite, so the naive version would read every pre-00568 image as maximally soft and buy a vision call per macro on every legacy submission. Same coercion trap that produced a fake -9 factor delta in US-2443 this morning; third time today it was caught by writing the test first. MERGED THROUGH mergeAuthenticityReread, the SAME one-directional merge the flagged-photo path uses, and deliberately not a new one: a sharper look at a serial may corroborate a tell but must never launder one away. A re-read is precisely the moment someone would relax 'when in doubt, LESS confident, never more' on the grounds that the second look was better evidence — it is better evidence for FINDING something, not for clearing it. Bounded at 2 by default and deduped by slot; rereadImage is already cached per image_type, so a macro that is both soft AND flagged costs one extra vision call rather than two. 5 cases in NEW ai-grading_test.ts. AC3 IS NOW PARTLY DONE BY 00568 and should be re-read before being re-implemented: sharpness is recorded per image, pixel density per REGION is not, and for a dedicated macro slot those are close to the same question. ONE PRECONDITION THE AC DOES NOT MENTION, unchanged: the re-read reads the RETAINED high-res original, so with RETAIN_ORIGINAL_IMAGES off it falls back to the stored copy and the pass is inert — the same way AC1 looked inert until AC2 landed. VERIFIED: deno lint + deno check src/main.ts clean, full edge suite 6225 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (second half of the day): the HELD-migration claim in this story's notes is now STALE. Migrations 00568 are on origin/main - verified with git ls-tree against a freshly fetched origin/main, not inferred - and the branch has zero unpushed commits. A held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word is no longer merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop on a branch that is not frozen. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: pushed is not applied. Whether the SQL has been run against prod is an operator fact this checkout cannot observe, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is the file that tracks it. Read that, not this prose. Recorded because prd-lint caught it the same hour the branch moved, which is the guard working as intended - it went unactioned for weeks before, and a stale freeze cost real sessions.

userStories.title: iOS silently omits the entire paid consumer grading path, including the 14-day dispute flow
userStories.description: As a consumer grading on iOS, I want the same journey the web offers. There are TWO independent grading pipelines in the edge: the consumer/certified path (routes/grade.ts:209 /submit, :751 /pay/:id, :837 /status/:id, :1117 /dispute) and the FlipDesk/reseller path (/api/flipdesk/grading/{validate,submit,submissions/:id}). Web implements BOTH (new-submission.tsx:647, bulk-submission.tsx:332, submission-detail.tsx:244). iOS implements ONLY the FlipDesk path — Grading/GradingService.swift:6,55 documents and calls validate -> submit -> GET /submissions/:id — and grepping iOS for grade/pay, grade/status and grade/dispute returns NOTHING. So iOS has no consumer certified-grading submission, no per-grade payment flow, and NO GRADE DISPUTE FLOW at all.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide explicitly whether the consumer grading path belongs on iOS. Nothing in IOS_PARITY_AUDIT.md or the Android plan mentions this omission either way, which is weak evidence it is accidental rather than a product decision — settle it in writing.
If it belongs: implement submit / pay / status / dispute on iOS against routes/grade.ts.

If it does not: document why, and confirm the dispute obligation is discharged some other way — a 14-day dispute window that only one client can exercise is a support and chargeback liability regardless of intent.
Any parity matrix must stop treating 'grading submission' as ONE row; scoring it that way marks iOS complete while the entire paid consumer path is missing.
userStories.notes: [P1][iOS/Parity] Found 2026-07-18 by the cross-platform parity deep dive. Two implementations of the core revenue journey is the highest-value drift surface in the repo, and the mobile client omits the paid half. The dispute gap is the sharpest edge: US-1340 tracks a 14-day dispute window as a real obligation, and a user who graded on iOS has no in-app route to exercise it.

userStories.title: No price-change notice or consent path on any platform
userStories.description: No code path notifies a user of a price increase before it takes effect. Stripe's price.updated and customer.subscription.updated-with-price-delta are not inspected (webhooks.ts:244-281). On Apple, the ASSN router (lib/appstore/notifications.ts:18-32) does not handle PRICE_INCREASE or DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF — Apple collects price-increase consent natively so this is not a rejection risk, but the server never learns a price change occurred, and an unconsented lapse arrives only as a generic EXPIRED. On Google Play, PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is explicitly a no-op (lib/google-play/rtdn.ts:11,107).
acceptanceCriteria: Notify subscribers in advance of any price increase, stating the old price, new price, effective date and how to cancel first.
Handle Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF so server state reflects platform-side changes.
Decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web (it commonly does under state ARLs) and implement accordingly.
Do not implement a price change of any kind until this exists.
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Billing] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Currently latent — no price change has been attempted. It becomes a live exposure the moment pricing moves, which makes it cheap to fix now and expensive to fix under deadline. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (mechanism — no counsel). Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF now reach server state. routeNotification gained a THIRD kind of verdict, record_only, distinct from both an entitlement action and 'ignore'. THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: Apple owns price-increase consent natively, so ACTING on these would be wrong — if the customer refuses, Apple lapses the subscription and we hear EXPIRED. But ignoring them meant that later EXPIRED was uninterpretable: indistinguishable from an ordinary cancellation, with no way to tell that a price change preceded it. Recording without acting is exactly the right posture, and it is the same 'known-ignored vs unexamined' distinction I built for the Stripe switch in US-2128 — the two surfaces had the identical defect. REUSED recordAppstoreEvent rather than hand-rolling the insert: it already namespaces stripe_event_id as appstore:<id> and swallows 23505, so an Apple retry cannot double-record. (My first attempt DID hand-roll it — the helper was 180 lines above and I had not looked. Worth noting because writing the second copy is always easier than finding the first.) 4 tests, including the two that matter: record_only must NOT be an entitlement action (not sub_active, not sub_expired, not revoke), and an unknown type must STILL fail closed to ignore — widening a router is exactly when a permissive default sneaks in. REMAINING, and correctly split: AC1 (notify subscribers in advance of an increase) needs the COPY, which is US-2114's gate — but note the DETECTION half is now free: US-2117's migration 00486 added pricing_plan_revisions, an append-only price history written BY TRIGGER, so 'a price changed' is already a queryable fact rather than something needing new plumbing. AC3 is explicitly a decision ('decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web') and belongs to counsel. AC4 is a CONSTRAINT rather than work — do not ship a price change until AC1/AC3 exist — and is worth keeping visible: the pricing_plans trigger will now record any change, so an accidental one leaves evidence. Google Play PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is still a no-op (rtdn.ts) and is the same shape as the Apple fix if someone wants symmetry. Verified: edge 4310 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC2 EXTENDED TO GOOGLE PLAY — the symmetry I flagged last pass, and it turned out to be the SHARPER of the two platforms. Apple's PRICE_INCREASE is a notification that a price WILL change; Google's PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is the user ACCEPTING one. That makes it a consent artifact — exactly what subscription_agreements (US-2117) exists to hold — and dropping it meant the only server-side evidence of the acceptance was the eventual renewal amount, which is an INFERENCE rather than a record. classifyRtdn now returns record_only for type 8, and the reconciler writes an audit row via the existing recordEvent dep (idempotent on the event id) while touching no entitlement: Google owns the consent UI, so acting would pre-empt it, and the next renewal RTDN settles the amount. ADDED A DISTINCT OUTCOME VALUE rather than reusing 'ignored': both leave entitlement untouched, but one wrote an audit row and the other did not. Collapsing them would leave the RTDN log unable to answer 'did we ever learn the user accepted a price change?' — which is the entire point of the branch. TWO THINGS THE TYPE SYSTEM AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT, both of them the system working: (1) adding the union variant broke the route glue's narrowing at `action.productType`, which is TypeScript correctly refusing to let a new action fall through unhandled; (2) an existing test asserted type 8 → ignore and went RED, correctly — it was encoding the old behaviour, and it was right to fail rather than let the change pass silently. Updated it to state WHY 8 left that group, so the next reader sees the reasoning rather than an unexplained gap in [9,10,11]. PROCESS NOTE: this took four attempts because bash ate template literals and regex escapes in inline node -e scripts (the fifth such incident today). Anything containing backticks or regex now goes through the Edit tool, not a shell string. Verified: edge 4312 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Two divergent cancellation paths — the stale portal route bypasses the reviewed flow
userStories.description: The primary cancellation flow is good and should be preserved: self-serve, ~4 clicks / 2 screens, no email or phone required, period-end timing stated on every screen (cancel-subscription-dialog.tsx:106,178,219), a required acknowledgement checkbox, clearly-labelled escape buttons, and an 'Undo cancel' banner afterwards (billing.tsx:373-395). It has one retention interstitial with two off-ramps ('Pause instead' / 'Switch to cheaper plan'), which is defensible but is the part most worth a second look. The defect is a SECOND path: selecting the Free tile in the plan picker routes to the Stripe billing portal instead (flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx:393-406), with a stale comment 'until US-216's cancel flow ships' — US-216 has shipped. That path bypasses the reviewed dialog and shows different, portal-native copy.
acceptanceCriteria: Route the Free-tile selection through the reviewed cancellation dialog; remove the stale portal path and its comment.
Audit for any other route to cancellation and ensure all converge on one reviewed flow.
Have the review gate assess the retention interstitial against 'simple mechanism' expectations — in particular whether two deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible.
Confirm cancellation is available in the same medium as signup for every purchase path (web-purchased cancels on web; IAP correctly defers to the platform via .manageSubscriptionsSheet).
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). California AB 2863 requires cancellation through the same medium used for the original transaction. Web is fine; the divergent path is the risk, not the flow itself. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC2 DONE (no counsel needed — this half is a code defect, not copy). AC1: selecting the Free tile in the plan picker now routes to the REVIEWED cancellation dialog instead of opening the Stripe billing portal. The portal path skipped everything the reviewed flow was designed for: the period-end statement on every screen, the required acknowledgement checkbox, the reason capture, and the undo banner. A divergent second route is how an audited flow stops being the one users actually hit. THE DESIGN POINT: it is a CALLBACK (onRequestCancel), not a self-rendered dialog, because CancelSubscriptionDialog ALREADY opens this picker as its 'switch to a cheaper plan' off-ramp — rendering the cancel dialog inside the picker would have made the two mutually recursive. The parent owns the flow; the picker only reports intent. When the prop is omitted (i.e. the picker was opened FROM the cancel dialog) the Free tile simply closes the picker, returning the user to the cancel flow they are already in rather than stacking a second copy of it. AC2 AUDITED: after the fix, every remaining portal.mutate() call site is legitimate and NOT cancellation — the plan picker's own non-cancel branch (same-tier interval change) and past-due-banner's 'update payment method'. Using the portal is fine; routing a CANCELLATION through it is not, because cancellation is the flow carrying the review requirements. 4 guard tests pin that distinction explicitly, including one asserting past-due-banner may keep its portal call, so a future reader does not 'fix' it by mistake. The strongest assertion is ordering: the isCancelToFree branch must come BEFORE portal.mutate() AND must return — a guard that merely EXISTS while falling through would leave the bug intact while looking fixed. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by deleting the guard: that test goes red. STILL OPEN: AC3 (have the review gate assess whether TWO deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible under 'simple mechanism' expectations) is explicitly a US-2114 counsel-review item, not an engineering call — the story itself routes it there. AC4 (cancellation available in the same medium as signup) is stated in the story as already satisfied — web-purchased cancels on web, IAP correctly defers to the platform via .manageSubscriptionsSheet — and I did not re-derive it. Verified: tsc clean, lint 0 errors, web 2293 passed. | 2026-08-03 AC4 VERIFIED — and it was NOT satisfied. No migration. The note said AC4 was 'stated in the story as already satisfied', i.e. taken on the audit's word and never checked. Checking it found a real defect on the server. THE WEB AND iOS HALVES DID HOLD: src/pages/billing.tsx computes isAppstoreManaged and hides every Stripe subscription CTA behind it, showing 'Manage this plan in the GradeThread iOS app' instead; iOS presents .manageSubscriptionsSheet in PaywallView and PlanSection and never calls the web cancel endpoint. THE SERVER HALF DID NOT. appstoreSubscriptionBlocksStripe guarded the SUBSCRIBE and CHANGE-PLAN endpoints and not CANCEL. An App Store subscriber has no flipdesk_subscription_id, so POST /flipdesk/cancel fell straight through to 'No subscription to cancel' — a 400 telling a paying customer they have nothing while Apple carried on billing them monthly. Someone who believes that message reasonably concludes they are not subscribed, and the next thing they hear is a renewal receipt. That is worse than an error: it is a confident wrong answer on a billing question. HIDING A BUTTON IS NOT ENFORCEMENT, which is why the UI half passing did not make AC4 true. The endpoint is reachable from any client holding a token, and the iOS app talks to the same API. FIXED: cancel now returns the same 409 + `action` contract the purchase paths already use (manage_in_app / manage_in_play), which the clients already branch on. Apple and Google both REQUIRE cancellation on-platform, so the honest answer is not an error at all — it is where to go. ORDERING IS THE DEFECT, NOT PRESENCE, and the guard says so: both checks can exist and the wrong one still win, because an in-app subscriber has no Stripe subscription id. A case pins that the medium check runs BEFORE the no-subscription check. 6 new cases in cancel-medium-parity_test.ts: the precedence helpers still recognise active/trialing/past_due on both stores AND still return false for Stripe (or web cancellation breaks for the people it is for), the cancel route refuses and names where to go, the ordering, the purchase paths keep their own guards (cancel and purchase have to agree about who is in-app managed — this story is about them drifting apart once), the billing page still hides the CTAs, and iOS still defers to the platform sheet without calling the web endpoint. ⚠ MY OWN GUARD MATCHED ITS OWN COMMENT, fourth time this session: the ordering case searched for the string 'No subscription to cancel', which the comment above the fix QUOTES to explain the bug — and that comment sits before the guard, so the scan reported the ordering as still broken. Comments are stripped now. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FIVE WAYS: the cancel guard removed, the guard moved after the no-subscription check, the refusal losing its action, a trialing in-app subscriber no longer recognised, and the billing page showing Stripe CTAs. Each reddened. (One mutation initially reported a false pass because .replace hit the SUBSCRIBE handler's occurrence first — re-run scoped to the cancel handler, where it reddens correctly.) REMAINING: AC3 only — whether TWO deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible under 'simple mechanism' expectations. That is explicitly a US-2114 counsel item, not an engineering call. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5400 passed / 0 failed, deno check + lint clean across 1345 files. | 2026-08-10 AC2's AUDIT MISSED A ROUTE, and it is the one the buyer product exposes. The 2026-07-19 pass concluded 'every remaining portal.mutate() call site is legitimate and NOT cancellation - the plan picker's own non-cancel branch and past-due-banner's update payment method'. It did not include src/pages/buyer/billing.tsx, which renders a 'Manage in Stripe' button. That is a third call site and it was not examined. WHAT I FIXED, because it is unambiguous and in code: POST /portal hardcoded return_url to the SELLER billing page. So a buyer clicking Manage in Stripe was sent to Stripe and returned to /dashboard/billing - a page showing a FlipDesk plan they may not hold, with no way to manage the buyer subscription they just went to change, and no other route back. The eighth instance today of a control built for the seller product and reused for the buyer one without asking whether its destination still made sense. return_url now resolves through renewalNoticeCopy, so 'the page that manages this product' has ONE definition shared with all six billing emails. The route takes an optional product hint; ABSENT MEANS FLIPDESK, so every historical caller is byte-identical, and a body-less request still works rather than 400ing. Tests pin the default, the catch, and that the buyer page passes 'buyer'. ⚠ WHAT I DID NOT FIX, AND IT IS THE BIGGER HALF OF AC2: billingPortal.sessions.create is called with NO `configuration`, so Stripe applies the ACCOUNT DEFAULT portal configuration. Whether 'Cancel subscription' is enabled there is a Stripe Dashboard setting this checkout cannot observe. If it is on - and Stripe enables it by default in most setups - then the portal IS a second cancellation path, reachable from the seller billing page, the plan picker and the buyer page, bypassing the reviewed dialog entirely: no period-end statement on every screen, no acknowledgement checkbox, no reason capture, no undo banner. That is EXACTLY the defect AC1 fixed for the Free tile, still live through a different door, and AC2 asks for precisely this audit. AN OPERATOR CAN SETTLE IT IN A MINUTE: Stripe Dashboard -> Settings -> Billing -> Customer portal -> Cancellations. If cancellation is enabled there, either disable it (the portal stays useful for payment methods and invoices, which is what past-due-banner and the interval-switch branch actually need) or pass an explicit `configuration` id here that has it off. I did not guess: passing a configuration id that does not exist would 500 every portal open, and disabling a feature I cannot see the current state of is not a change to make blind. FIVE SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: the return URL re-hardcoded, the default flipped to buyer (which would strand every seller instead), the body-less catch removed, the hook accepting the product and not sending it, and the buyer page dropping its argument. STILL passes:false. AC2 is now HALF done - the return-path defect is fixed and the portal-cancellation question is stated precisely with the exact setting to check, but it needs a human with the Stripe Dashboard. AC3 (whether two deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible) remains a US-2114 counsel item. AC1 and AC4 unchanged. VERIFIED: deno check clean on payments.ts; deno lint clean across 1491 files; billing-portal-return_test.ts 3 passed (new); full edge suite 6484 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; npx tsc -b clean; eslint 0 errors / 13 warnings; full web suite 3930 passed / 0 failed across 322 files.

userStories.title: Refund policy contradicts the vault: an undisclosed 14-day money-back guarantee
userStories.description: vault/50-business/pricing.md:204-205 states 'Subscriptions: 14-day money-back guarantee on the first subscription invoice only.' No such guarantee appears on either public legal page — src/pages/legal/terms.tsx:80-82 and src/pages/legal/refund.tsx:45-47 both state subscription fees are non-refundable once a billing period has begun. Either the vault is stale, or we are operating a guarantee we do not disclose (or declining one we promised internally). Support and billing decisions are presumably being made against one of these.
acceptanceCriteria: Determine which is authoritative and reconcile — update the vault note or the public policy, in the same commit per the vault same-commit rule.
If the guarantee is real, disclose it at the point of sale, where it is also a conversion asset.
Review the ToS/refund pages alongside the new disclosure copy so the point-of-sale statements and the legal pages agree.
Check the EU/UK right-of-withdrawal waiver (refund.tsx section 4) and chargeback clause (section 5) with counsel while the pages are open.
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Legal-docs] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Cheap to resolve and it removes an internal/external inconsistency that would look bad in any enforcement or dispute context. | PARTIAL 2026-08-02 — AC1 RESOLVED by the owner; AC2 does not apply; AC3/AC4 still need counsel. AC1: the vault was wrong and the public pages are authoritative. I put the evidence to the owner rather than guessing, and they chose delete-the-claim. THE EVIDENCE, gathered before asking so the question was cheap: no 14-day money-back guarantee exists anywhere in the codebase — not in constants, not in the Stripe setup, not in the webhook handlers. Refunds are MANUAL admin actions through admin-billing.ts with an MFA step-up. Both public pages say the opposite of the vault (refund.tsx section 3 and terms.tsx: subscription fees non-refundable once a billing period has begun, except where required by law or expressly granted in writing). What DOES exist is a 14-day free TRIAL, which is real, advertised on the landing page and in the plan picker, and is a completely different thing. Two features sharing a number is the most likely origin of a policy nobody agreed to. WHY THIS MATTERED IN A DIRECTION, and it is the part worth keeping: an internal note promising a refund the public pages deny is a promise support might honour case by case. That produces an UNDISCLOSED policy applied inconsistently, which is worse than either answer on its own — worse than not offering it, and worse than offering it openly. AC2 does not apply: there is no guarantee to disclose at the point of sale. The vault section is rewritten to state the three real rules (subscriptions non-refundable, credit packs non-refundable once a grade is generated but credits never expire, billing errors refunded within 60 days), each pointing at the page or constant that owns it, with a callout recording what the claim was and why it was wrong. refund.tsx and terms.tsx are added to the note's code_refs so a change to either now drifts the note. A SECOND CONTRADICTION FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: terms.tsx says "Unused grading credits DO NOT ROLL OVER and are not refundable". That conflates two different things. Purchased credit packs never expire — constants.ts:384, migration 00037 and 00415 all say so explicitly. The MONTHLY PLAN ALLOWANCE (users.grades_used_this_month) does reset each cycle and genuinely does not roll over. The word "credits" is used for both, so the sentence is true of one and false of the other. It UNDERSTATES what a paying customer gets, so it costs conversion rather than creating legal exposure — but it is still a false statement in the Terms. I did not edit it: AC4 puts these pages under counsel review, and rewriting Terms copy ahead of that trades one unreviewed statement for another. Recorded in the vault note under its own heading so it is not lost, and carried on this story. NOTE ON MY OWN FIRST READING: I initially thought refund.tsx contradicted the vault on credit expiry too. It does not — "credits do not expire INTO A CASH BALANCE" is about cash redemption, and I had read a truncated line. Checked the full sentence before acting. STILL OPEN: AC3 (reconcile the point-of-sale copy with the legal pages — nothing to reconcile now that there is no guarantee, but the credits sentence above is in scope) and AC4 (the EU/UK right-of-withdrawal waiver in refund.tsx section 4 and the chargeback clause in section 5, both needing counsel). | 2026-08-10 AC3's remaining item is now TRACKED rather than described, and the copy is still untouched. THE CONTRADICTION, measured on both sides this time. FIVE product surfaces tell a customer 'credits never expire' - credit-pack-dialog (twice), upgrade-required-dialog, api-overage-card and cancel-subscription-dialog's keep-list. The Terms say 'Unused grading credits do not roll over and are not refundable'. Both use the word 'credits' for two different things: PURCHASED PACKS never expire (constants.ts CREDIT_PACKS, migrations 00037 and 00415 all say so) while the MONTHLY PLAN ALLOWANCE genuinely does reset. So the sentence is true of one and false of the other, and the one it is false about is the one the customer PAID for. It is the point-of-sale-versus-legal-page disagreement AC3 names, with the point of sale outnumbering the Terms five to one. COPY STILL NOT EDITED, and the previous pass's reasoning is why: AC4 has terms.tsx and refund.tsx under counsel review, and rewriting Terms ahead of that trades one unreviewed statement for another. Agreed then and agreed now. WHAT CHANGED IS THAT IT IS NO LONGER A SENTENCE IN A BACKLOG NOTE. NEW src/test/credit-expiry-claims.test.ts makes it a tracked, annotated exception in the KNOWN_GAPS shape the migrations lint already uses - and the shape is the point, because a plain allowlist rots. FOUR PROPERTIES: (1) the FACT is anchored, so the test fails if 'Credits never expire' quietly leaves constants.ts and the whole thing stops meaning anything; (2) the surfaces that say it are DERIVED, not listed; (3) any NEW contradicting statement fails unless someone adds an entry with a reason and an owning story; (4) THE LIST CAN ONLY SHRINK - an entry whose text no longer matches its file FAILS, so when counsel rewrites the sentence the entry must be deleted rather than left describing a problem that no longer exists. That fourth property is the one worth having. An allowlist that outlives its entries stops being a record and becomes a lie about a lie, and it hides the next real regression behind an entry nobody re-reads. FOUR SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: counsel fixing the Terms while the exception is left behind, a NEW page starting to contradict it, the anchoring fact removed from constants.ts, and an exception added with a throwaway reason. STILL passes:false on the same two: AC3's actual reconciliation (the wording, which is counsel's) and AC4 (the EU/UK right-of-withdrawal waiver in refund.tsx section 4 and the chargeback clause in section 5). AC1 and AC2 remain done - the vault was the stale side, there is no guarantee to disclose. VERIFIED: credit-expiry-claims.test.ts 4 passed (new); npx tsc -b clean; eslint 0 errors / 13 warnings; the whole src/test guard suite 896 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-12 THE SAME CONTRADICTION IS NOW ON ANDROID, AND THE GUARD STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE IT. android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:1306 (paywall_credits_body) reads "One-time packs. They never expire and stack on top of the grades your plan includes." - the never-expire claim this story exists to resolve, on a paywall that can take a real payment today (see US-2126). src/test/credit-expiry-claims.test.ts pins the web copy, but its FILES list is a hardcoded set of src/ paths, so it scans neither android/ nor ios/ and could never have flagged this. That is the same class of hole as US-1996: a guard that reads as coverage while never executing over the surface that drifted. So whichever way this story resolves - credits never expire, or credits do not roll over - the fix has to land on three clients and the guard has to widen to see all three, or the next client to ship copy repeats it. Recorded here rather than filed separately because it is the same sentence and the same decision, not a new one.

userStories.title: Guided macro capture — framing, distance and lighting for authenticity shots
userStories.description: There is no guided capture for authenticity evidence: no framing overlay, no distance guide, no lighting instruction. iOS uses .builtInWideAngleCamera with no zoom or focus tuning (CameraSession.swift:238), so macro shots depend entirely on the seller's instinct. Authentication tells are only legible at consistent framing and lighting, and inconsistent capture is itself a source of false positives.
acceptanceCriteria: Add per-slot capture guidance: what to photograph, how close, and how to light it, with a framing overlay.
Investigate closer-focus camera configuration on iOS for macro slots.
Provide worked examples of a good vs unusable macro shot for each slot type.
Measure whether guidance actually improves delivered pixel density and gate the rollout on that.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Capture][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Depends on the macro slots existing first. | 2026-07-31 AC1 DONE (web). New src/lib/macro-capture-guidance.ts: a distance line, a lighting line and a framing tightness per macro slot. The existing photo-profiles hints said WHAT to shoot and nothing about distance or light, which is where macro shots actually fail. LIGHTING ADVICE IS SLOT-SPECIFIC ON PURPOSE, and this is the substantive part: the failure modes are OPPOSITE. A struck serial is visible only by its shadow and needs single-side low-angle light; a glossy care label needs even indirect light or the print blows out. One reusable 'use good light' sentence would have been easier and would not have changed a single photo -- a test asserts the lighting lines are not all identical, because boilerplate would pass every other assertion in the file. Surfaced on BOTH web capture surfaces: the camera dialog gets a dashed framing box over the live preview plus the two lines beneath it (new optional photoType prop), and the FlipDesk uploader -- where the authenticity slots live and there is no camera dialog -- composes them into its per-slot tooltip rather than inventing a new affordance. THE OVERLAY IS SIZED TO BE SATISFIABLE, which is the reviewable judgement: a guide box you can fill and still be told 'move closer' is worse than no box, so the fill fractions are chosen against the US-2136 floors at the US-2135 caps, and a test walks every slot asserting that filling the box delivers more pixels than that slot's own floor -- so raising a floor without revisiting the overlay fails in CI rather than in a seller's hands. The box is decorative only; the capture is still the full frame, so it constrains composition and never the saved pixels. THE COVERAGE TEST IS WHY THIS PAIRS WITH US-2136: every slot the quality gate can reject now has guidance for getting it right, because a gate without guidance is just blame. STILL OPEN: AC2 (closer-focus camera configuration) is iOS and cannot be built in this environment; AC3 (worked good-vs-unusable examples per slot) needs real example imagery, which is design work rather than code; AC4 (gate the rollout on measured pixel-density improvement) needs the per-photo measurement persisted first, which is US-2135 AC3 and blocked on a migration. Verified: tsc -b clean, lint 0 errors, 2912 tests pass, build green. | 2026-08-12 AC2 INVESTIGATED, and the finding is that the obvious fix is the wrong one - so this records the answer rather than shipping blind camera config. WHAT IS THERE NOW: CameraSession.swift:241-244 asks for AVCaptureDevice.default(.builtInWideAngleCamera, for: .video, position: .back), and BarcodeScanner.swift:194 does the same. CameraSession takes NO slot context at all - PhotoIntakeView.swift:27 constructs it as a bare `@State private var camera = CameraSession()` - so there is currently no way for it to know a macro slot is active. THE OBVIOUS CHANGE IS autoFocusRangeRestriction = .near, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THAT MATTERS. That property is a HINT that narrows the autofocus SWEEP; it does not change the lens minimum focus distance. On a wide-angle iPhone lens that distance is roughly 10-12cm, which is the actual limit a seller hits when they push in on a care label - so restricting the sweep makes AF settle faster and does not let them get closer. THE REAL LEVER IS DEVICE SELECTION, and asking for .builtInWideAngleCamera explicitly OPTS OUT of it. On iPhone 13 Pro and later, macro is the ULTRA-WIDE camera, and iOS performs the automatic macro switch only when the session is given a VIRTUAL device (.builtInTripleCamera / .builtInDualWideCamera) so it can cross over on its own. Requesting the physical wide camera pins us to the one lens that cannot focus close. iOS 18 is the deployment target, so minimumFocusDistance and the virtual device types are all available; nothing here is gated on OS support. WHY I DID NOT JUST CHANGE IT: swapping the device type changes EVERY capture on EVERY device, not just macro slots - field of view, low-light behaviour and the preview crop all move - and the payoff is hardware-dependent (a non-Pro phone gains nothing). This is the capture path, the failure mode is subtly-out-of-focus photos on every seller's grading submission, and it cannot be compiled or exercised here. That is a different risk class from the plumbing changes shipped elsewhere today. WHAT THE NEXT PASS SHOULD DO, in order: (1) plumb the active CaptureSlot into CameraSession - it already exists and flows from the PhotoProfile, and MACRO_MIN_LONG_EDGE_PX in src/lib/macro-photo-quality.ts:113 is the list of which slots are macro (tag/label/detail/defect at 700px, serial/marking at 900, surface at 800); (2) select .builtInTripleCamera then .builtInDualWideCamera then .builtInWideAngleCamera via AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession, so macro-capable hardware can cross over and older hardware degrades to exactly today's behaviour; (3) read device.minimumFocusDistance and use it to drive the AC1 guidance copy, which is the honest version of "how close"; (4) measure before rolling out, which is AC4 and still blocked on US-2135 AC3 persisting per-photo dimensions. AC3 (worked good-vs-unusable examples) remains design work.

userStories.title: Per-brand tell depth is 3 brands and 7 tells, all unverified
userStories.description: CANONICAL_TELLS covers exactly three brands (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) with 7 tells total across categories date_code/stamp/hardware/serial/font — every one marked 'seed:brand-authentication-tells (unverified — review in admin)' at confidence 0.5-0.65, against a taxonomy of 11 categories that includes stitching, construction and material. The separate seeded brand_knowledge.authentication_tells rows are legacy {tell, detail} shape, coerced on read to category 'other' with NO redFlag field (brand-authenticity.ts:88-92), so they contribute almost nothing to the contradiction logic that drives the verdict. admin-brand-knowledge.ts is a working curation surface with validateTellsForWrite and is the right place to do this. EXTENDED 2026-07-19: the KB is also ONE-SIDED. Every field models what a GENUINE example looks like — authentication_tells, tag_eras, country_patterns, registered_numbers — and there is no counterfeit-pattern modelling at all: no known fake markers, no superfake characteristics, no record of a specific counterfeit production tell. authentication_tells is a single column marked 'informational' doing double duty for both directions. Combined with seeded content that says 'NEVER auto-authenticate', the KB currently argues against the product it feeds.
acceptanceCriteria: Migrate legacy {tell, detail} rows into the structured shape so they can carry a category and a redFlag and actually affect the verdict.
Expand verified tells to the brands with real submission volume; mark provenance and confidence per tell.
Establish a review workflow so a tell moves from unverified to verified deliberately, with a named source.
Gate: a brand with no verified tells should widen limitations and lower confidence rather than producing a confident verdict from generic reasoning.

Model counterfeit-side knowledge distinctly from genuine-side tells — a known fake marker is a different kind of fact from 'what a real one looks like', and collapsing them into one informational column is why neither drives the verdict.
Reconcile the seeded 'NEVER auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture (see US-2133) rather than leaving the KB and the product in contradiction.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Signal][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Expert-dependent. Note the brand KB currently carries authentication_tells, registered_numbers, tag_eras and country_patterns columns across ~150-200 seeded brands — the columns exist, the depth does not. | SCOPED 2026-07-30 from US-2147 (AC1 here is the same work as US-2147 AC5 — carry it here, it is a duplicate there). Corpus measured: 179 legacy payload arrays / 599 individual {tell,detail} entries across the 37 *_brand_knowledge.sql seeds; 0 structured. TWO TRAPS for whoever does AC1. (1) Categories alone are NOT enough and shipping them alone is a REGRESSION: authenticity-coverage.ts:53 isActionableTell treats any non-'other' category as actionable, so a bulk categorization flips all 179 packs inert->actionable, lifts coverageConfidenceCap 0.75 -> 1.0 and empties the limitations disclosure the PURCHASED add-on owes its buyer — with zero new verified facts. AC1 must land WITH the redFlag/verification work (AC2/AC3/AC5), never before it. (2) Most of the 599 are not authentication tells — they are brand-identification, sizing and comping rules ('American Eagle runs LARGE', 'Anthropologie also SELLS other brands', 'PINK IS NOT VICTORIA'S SECRET — comp it separately'). They are all injected into the <<<KNOWN_AUTHENTICATION_TELLS>>> prompt block (ai-authenticity.ts:409-422) told to 'report a finding per tell', against MAX_TELLS 60, so they manufacture noise findings AND can crowd out real tells. So AC1 is a SEPARATION job first: split identification knowledge out of authentication_tells, then categorize only what actually authenticates. That separation likely needs its own column or table, which makes AC1 a migration with a schema change, not a JSONB rewrite. Guard already in place: authenticity-coverage_test.ts:201 fails the moment a structured payload appears. Remains EXPERT-DEPENDENT and unstarted — a genuine redFlag needs a named source, which is AC3's review workflow. | 2026-08-09 AC1 INHERITS A MEASURED WARNING FROM US-2147, transplanted here because US-2147 AC5 is the same requirement verbatim and that story is now closed — leaving the finding only on a closed story is how it gets re-derived the expensive way. THE OBVIOUS VERSION OF AC1 IS A USER-VISIBLE REGRESSION ON A PAID PRODUCT. Measured corpus (2026-07-30): 179 legacy payload arrays holding 599 individual {tell,detail} entries across the 37 *_brand_knowledge.sql seeds; structured payloads = 0. authenticity-coverage.ts:53 isActionableTell returns true when category is not 'other' OR redFlag is set — so ASSIGNING CATEGORIES ALONE flips all 179 packs from inert to actionable, which lifts coverageConfidenceCap from COVERAGE_CAP_INERT 0.75 to 1.0 and empties the limitations string the PURCHASED authenticity add-on owes its buyer. US-2219 shipped that cap precisely because these rows cannot move a verdict. A bulk categorization would therefore raise confidence and delete a disclosure without adding one verified fact — a regression dressed as a data migration. SECOND FINDING, and it reshapes AC1 rather than just cautioning it: MOST OF THE 599 ARE NOT AUTHENTICATION TELLS. The column is doing double duty as general brand knowledge. Real seed entries: 'American Eagle runs LARGE', 'Anthropologie also SELLS other brands', 'PINK IS NOT VICTORIA'S SECRET — comp it separately', 'AERIE IS AMERICAN EAGLE — and the tag does not say so'. All 599 are injected into the KNOWN_AUTHENTICATION_TELLS block (ai-authenticity.ts:409-422) under an instruction to check the item against each. So AC1 is not a shape conversion — it is a TRIAGE: which of the 599 are authentication tells at all, which are sizing/comping facts that belong somewhere else entirely, and only then what category and redFlag the survivors carry. Doing the conversion without the triage moves brand-comping advice into a field the verdict reads as authentication evidence. | 2026-08-09 AC4 SHIPPED. It was a LIVE gap, not a theoretical one: coverage classification asked whether a tell could MOVE a verdict (isActionableTell — does it name a category, does it carry a red flag) and never asked whether anyone had checked the tell is TRUE. So the three brands with structured tells classified as fully covered and took NO confidence cap at all, even though all seven of their tells are sourced to 'seed:brand-authentication-tells (unverified — review in admin)'. A PAID authenticity verdict was riding at full confidence on unreviewed seed data. The existing tests agreed with the bug — four of them failed the moment the fix landed, which is the cleanest evidence the gap was real rather than cosmetic. WHAT SHIPPED: a fourth coverage level, 'unverified', between 'inert' and 'actionable', with COVERAGE_CAP_UNVERIFIED 0.85. NEW isVerifiedTell keys on the 'seed:' source prefix via a NAMED constant now exported from brand-authenticity.ts (UNVERIFIED_SOURCE_PREFIX) rather than a re-typed string literal — that is the convention the module already established, and the US-1715 verify queue's job is to REPLACE the source with a real citation, so 'source still starts with seed:' is exactly the question 'has a human signed this off'. An UNSOURCED tell is also unverified: an unsourced claim is not better than a self-declared draft. THE CAP IS A BAND, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and it is written under the same discipline as the two beside it — the module's own comment refuses a gradient because the golden set (US-2131) has not measured what thin coverage costs. 0.85 sits between 0.75 and 1.0 because an unreviewed structured tell is genuinely more use than a descriptive note (a finding can still be attributed to a category) and genuinely less than a confirmed one, and it does not pretend to know by how much. BOTH CONDITIONS MUST HOLD ON THE SAME TELL, and a test pins it: one verified descriptive note plus one unreviewed structured tell is not a brand we have verified criteria for. Counting them separately would let a pack launder itself to full coverage with two half-qualifying entries. 4 new cases plus 4 existing ones updated to assert the corrected behaviour rather than deleted — the STRUCTURED fixture stays unsourced (which is the real state of every seeded tell) and a VERIFIED fixture was added beside it for the assertions that genuinely meant 'real coverage'. REMAINING ON THIS STORY: AC1 (the legacy triage — see the transplanted warning above; a bulk categorization would flip all 179 packs from inert to actionable, lift the cap and empty a paid disclosure without adding one verified fact, and most of the 599 entries are not authentication tells at all), AC2 and AC3 (sourcing and workflow — content, not code), AC5 (model counterfeit-side knowledge distinctly) and AC6 (reconcile the seeded NEVER-auto-authenticate guidance with the shipped posture). NOTE AC4 GETS STRONGER AS AC1 PROGRESSES rather than weaker: every legacy row that becomes structured now lands in 'unverified' until someone cites it, which is the safe direction. VERIFIED: deno lint + deno check src/main.ts clean, full edge suite 6229 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | 2026-08-09 (same day, follow-up) CORRECTING A DEFECT I SHIPPED IN THE PREVIOUS COMMIT. Adding the 'unverified' coverage level without giving it its own disclosure branch left it falling through to the INERT wording, which reads 'Our brand-specific criteria for this brand are descriptive notes rather than checkable tests'. THAT IS FALSE AT THIS LEVEL: the criteria ARE checkable tests — nobody has confirmed them. Both surfaces were affected, coverageLimitation (the disclosure on the delivered assessment) and purchaseDisclosure (the one a purchase flow must show before taking money). A WRONG EXPLANATION ON A PAID DISCLOSURE IS WORSE THAN A VAGUE ONE, and that is why this is a defect rather than a polish item: the buyer can ACT on it. They would conclude we hold no real tests for the brand when we hold untested ones, which is a different decision about whether to trust the assessment and whether to inspect the item themselves. Both levels now have their own wording, saying what is actually true — checkable but not yet verified against a cited source. THE GENERAL SHAPE, worth keeping: a confidence cap without a matching disclosure is exactly what this module exists to prevent — the buyer pays, the confidence is quietly lowered, and nothing says why. Adding a cap level is therefore a THREE-part change (classify, cap, disclose) and I shipped two of the three. A new test asserts the invariant directly rather than the instance: every level except 'actionable' owes a non-empty limitation AND a non-null purchase disclosure, and the three texts must all DIFFER — three identical strings would mean the levels are not really distinct to the person reading them, which is the only place the distinction matters. That test would have caught the omission, and it will catch the next one. 3 new cases, 22 in the file. VERIFIED: deno lint + deno check clean, full edge suite 6232 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-09 AC6 IS A DUPLICATE OF US-2133 AC3, word for word in substance: 'Reconcile the brand-KB never-auto-authenticate guidance with the shipped product posture.' US-2139 AC6 even says 'see US-2133'. Two stories owning one requirement is the same shape resolved earlier today between US-2147 AC5 and US-2139 AC1 — whichever is picked up second finds it done with no record of who did it, or both do it. US-2133 IS THE OWNER and should keep it: the reconciliation depends on US-2133 AC2 (decide and document the claim posture — assessment-with-limitations versus verification), so doing AC6 first would mean reconciling the KB against a posture nobody has settled. ⚠ AND IT IS EXPLICITLY NOT AGENT WORK. US-2133's own note says, in terms: 'Do not let an agent draft the claim language.' Its AC1 requires review WITH COUNSEL. I am surfacing that here rather than only there, because a future agent reading US-2139 top to bottom would reach AC6, see a documentation task, and start writing legal-adjacent copy without ever opening US-2133. THE CONTRADICTION IS REAL, for whoever does resolve it, and worth stating precisely so the work starts from evidence: 37 seeded brand packs carry prose like 'NEVER label a Coach item authentic — flag anything inconsistent in condition notes only' (00398) and 'LUXURY — never auto-authenticate' (00399), while the shipped pipeline's deriveVerdict emits 'likely_authentic' as one of three verdicts. Those may well be reconcilable — a capped, disclosed 'likely authentic' is not the same act as labelling an item authentic — but that is a claim-language judgement with counsel in it, not an engineering one, and the KB prose is spread across immutable applied migrations, so the reconciliation has to land in the vault rather than by editing the seeds. AC6 is therefore CLOSED HERE as a duplicate; the requirement lives on US-2133 AC3.

userStories.title: GSC/Bing verification + Page-indexing diagnosis — the gate for all content work
userStories.description: Nothing about which pages to add, trim or consolidate can be decided until we can see what Google is actually indexing. VITE_GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION, VITE_BING_SITE_VERIFICATION and INDEXNOW_KEY are all unset, so we have no Search Console data at all. ~79% of 213 registered URLs are templated, on a domain with little authority — the classic 'Discovered/Crawled - currently not indexed' profile. This story is the prerequisite for US-2096 and US-2113.
acceptanceCriteria: Set VITE_GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION and VITE_BING_SITE_VERIFICATION; verify both properties.

Read the GSC Page-indexing report and record, per URL cluster (marketing / grading pSEO / glossary / flaws / garment-guides / certs / blog), how many URLs are Indexed vs Discovered-not-indexed vs Crawled-not-indexed vs Duplicate.
Confirm the www -> non-www redirect exists and that Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode is not challenging Googlebot.
Write the findings into vault/40-growth/seo-indexability.md, replacing its hypotheses with measured numbers, and state a keep/trim/consolidate decision per cluster.
Set INDEXNOW_KEY so future publishes can ping Bing/Yandex.

OPERATOR: this whole story needs Search Console access and DNS (AC1-AC5). It is the gate for all content work: seo-geo-strategy.md and seo-indexability.md deliberately contradict each other, and the argument cannot be settled without the Page-indexing numbers.
userStories.notes: [P1][SEO/Diagnosis] USER ACTION REQUIRED (console access + DNS). This is the single highest-leverage item in the audit: seo-geo-strategy.md (grow pSEO) and seo-indexability.md (trim it) deliberately contradict each other, and that argument cannot be settled without this data. Everything templated stays parked until it lands. | 2026-08-15 A MECHANICAL EXPLANATION FOR THE INDEXING PROBLEM, MEASURED, that changes what this diagnosis should look for first. US-2612 found CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET is NOT set on the edge - confirmed by features.pages_origin_bypass on /health/ready, which reports 'missing'. Consequence, from main.ts:806-811: /api/content/public/* is capped at 60 requests per minute PER IP and fails closed, and every SSR'd page reaches it through ONE Cloudflare Pages worker, so the whole public site shares a single 60/min bucket. Past that the pages answer 503 'Temporarily unavailable'. THE SITEMAP ADVERTISES 514 URLs. A Googlebot crawl session walking those arrives through that one worker and that one bucket, so it would be answered with 503s partway through - which Google records as a server error and backs off from, and which shows in the Page-indexing report as crawl anomalies rather than as anything about the content. THIS STORY AND US-2113 HAVE BEEN ARGUING A CONTENT QUESTION: seo-geo-strategy.md says grow pSEO, seo-indexability.md says trim it, and US-2113 is gated on this diagnosis to settle which. Neither hypothesis is wrong, but a serving fault would produce the same symptom as both, and it is far cheaper to rule out. SO: fix the secret FIRST (US-2612, two places, neither in this repo), let a crawl cycle pass, THEN read the Page-indexing report. Reading it before the fix risks recording a content verdict for a plumbing problem - and this story's own output is what US-2113 and the whole content roadmap are waiting on.

NOTE the story cites src/lib/seo/marketing-jsonld.ts; the file is at src/pages/marketing/marketing-jsonld.ts. What was wrong: the brand was re-declared as ANONYMOUS INLINE NODES ({"@type":"Organization", name:"GradeThread"}) at 8 sites, so every publisher/provider/isPartOf edge landed on a fresh unnamed entity and none of it accrued to the site-wide Organization — plus 4 hardcoded copies of the ORG_ID string. Converting it to a bare ref would have been the tidier-looking edit and would have produced a DANGLING pointer to a node the document never defines, which is strictly worse than the anonymous node it replaced. AC5 (certificate Products orphaned) got the same treatment for the same reason: US-425 documented the cert Review author as deliberately inline because the cert page emits only Product + Breadcrumb, and that reasoning still holds — so the node keeps its name/url AND gains @id: ORG_ID. THE TEST IS THE PART WORTH READING: the first version listed five builders by hand, and when I reintroduced an anonymous node to check it, IT PASSED — none of the five happened to contain a fixed site. Rewrote it to DERIVE its coverage from every zero-arg *JsonLd export plus every FLIPDESK_LANDINGS entry (53 assertions), so a new builder is covered the day it is added. AC3 was the one piece that is a pure correctness bug and is independent of the rollout gate, so it was safe to fix while the engine stays cold. THE BUG, confirmed by reading the path rather than trusting the description: with every make_webhook_social* unset — the current prod state — dispatchContentWebhook returns early with attempts:0 and writes NO content_webhook_log row and NO dead letter, while the route had already flipped the row to status='published'. Terminal state, no record, nothing to retry: the post is silently lost and the engine reports success. I ALSO FOUND THE SAME HOLE IN THE SCHEDULER TICK (content-scheduler.ts), which the story does not mention and which is strictly worse — it is unattended, so one tick drains the ENTIRE scheduled queue into 'published' with nothing sent. Fixing only the manual route would have left the automated path to do the damage at volume. DELIBERATELY DID NOT IMPLEMENT AC3 AS WRITTEN. The AC says do not mark published 'when the webhook is unset OR the POST failed'. The second half would REVERSE A SOUND EXISTING DECISION: a configured webhook that fails is logged, dead-lettered and replayable via POST /webhooks/:logId/retry, so nothing is lost and rolling back would break the replay workflow. The two cases only look alike — one is recoverable and recorded, the other is neither. So the guard checks CONFIGURATION, not DELIVERY. Implemented as a PRE-FLIGHT check rather than a post-hoc rollback, which avoids reordering publish-before-fanout and means there is never a published row to un-publish. Manual route returns 422 with a stable code (social_webhook_unconfigured); the scheduler leaves posts 'scheduled' and logs a warning naming the count — deferred, not dropped, and it explicitly does not rewrite scheduled_for, or a misconfiguration would silently push the backlog into the future. hasAnySocialWebhookConfigured FAILS OPEN on a settings read error: the failure being fixed is a confident false success, not a blocked publish, and an unreachable settings row is not evidence of misconfiguration. 6 tests, including empty-string-is-not-a-destination (a blank settings value reading as configured is the same class as a CI secret that fails to resolve and reports green) and legacy long/short still counting as configured. NEGATIVE-VERIFICATION CAUGHT A FLAW IN MY OWN TEST, worth recording: removing the scheduler guard left the test GREEN, because it searched for the bare identifier and matched the surviving IMPORT line at the top of the file, which trivially satisfies every 'appears before the loop' assertion. Retargeted at the call expression; the removal now reddens it. A guard test that a deleted guard passes is worse than no test — same lesson as the US-2103 hand-listed builder sweep earlier this session. Verified: 4437 edge tests pass, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: The grading standard has qualitative criteria but no measurable tolerances
userStories.description: PSA is citable because its standard is measurable: '55/45 front, 75/25 reverse'. GradeThread's is 'noticeable pilling, light fading' — good rubric, not a citable spec. Confirmed: no tolerance or measurement language anywhere in grading-scale.ts or grade-standard.ts. Relatedly, /grading/methodology is the weakest page relative to its promise: no named base model, no eval numbers, and the confidence threshold is described only as 'below our threshold' — it is 0.75 and it is documented in CLAUDE.md.
acceptanceCriteria: Add measurable tolerances where the factor genuinely admits them (pilling density, fade delta-E, hole/tear dimensions in mm, seam separation length, stain area).
State the 0.75 human-review confidence threshold explicitly on /grading/methodology.
State what can be said about the model and evaluation without leaking prompt IP.
Render tier data and flaw->factor->impact as real <table> elements — /condition-grading currently uses div cards, and tables are the structure most often lifted verbatim into LLM answers.
Coordinate with the grading-engine skill contract before changing any published criterion.
userStories.notes: [P2][GEO/Authority] Found 2026-07-18 by the SEO/marketing deep-dive audit. This is the explicit PSA-playbook gap in the strategy doc's own mapping table, and it is the difference between 'a rubric' and 'the standard'. Adds no new URLs. [2026-07-19 PARTIAL — AC2+AC4 DONE, AC1 SUBSTANTIALLY DONE, AC3+AC5 OPEN] KEY FINDING: the premise was half wrong. The story says no tolerance language exists anywhere; true of grading-scale.ts/grade-standard.ts, but defect-weighting.ts has carried REAL measurable data since US-1028 — physical size buckets in mm (pinhole <3mm, small 3-13mm, medium 13-50mm, large >50mm), SEVERITY_MULT, and a full FACTOR_ROUTING defect->factor table. We were not missing the measurable standard, we were failing to PUBLISH it. Nothing had to be invented. Done: AC2 the 0.75 review threshold is stated explicitly on /grading/methodology via a guarded constant (grading-threshold-parity.test.ts fails if it diverges from the edge fallback); AC4 tier data is now a real <table> with scope/caption, and three new spec tables render the mm tolerances, severity multipliers and flaw->factor routing. New src/lib/grading-standard.ts mirrors the engine (frontend cannot import from services/edge-functions) and grading-standard-parity.test.ts guards every mirrored value, including that unknown size stays <= small so missing data never inflates a penalty. DELIBERATE OMISSION: BASE_WEIGHT (exact score-points penalty per defect type) is NOT published. Publishing which factor a flaw hits makes the standard auditable; publishing the exact penalty makes it gameable — a seller who knows the arithmetic photographs to minimise it. A test asserts it stays out. Reversing that is a product call. STILL OPEN: AC1 residue — pilling density and fade delta-E have NO engine equivalent and were deliberately not invented; adding them means defining new measurement in the engine first. AC3 (name the base model + eval numbers without leaking prompt IP) is unstarted and overlaps the US-2035 determinism decision. AC5 requires grading-engine skill/vault coordination since this now publishes engine criteria. | 2026-07-19 AC5 DONE. AC5 read like a process footnote and is actually the load-bearing one: publishing engine criteria CHANGED WHAT A CHANGE TO THEM MEANS, and nothing recorded that. SIZE_BUCKETS, SEVERITY_MULT and FACTOR_ROUTING went public on /condition-grading, but defect-weighting.ts — the file someone actually opens to tune grading — said nothing about it, and neither did the vault. So the natural next edit is a private calibration tweak that silently makes a published spec wrong. Fixed at the point of edit AND in the contract: a header warning on defect-weighting.ts naming exactly which three tables are mirrored and why that matters (the page exists to be cited and lifted verbatim into LLM answers, so a stale mirror is a precise, checkable, WRONG claim — worse than the adjectives it replaced), plus a new 'Published criteria' section in vault/20-domain/grading-scale-and-weights.md with defect-weighting.ts and grading-standard.ts added to code_refs so the CI drift guard now watches them. THE NON-OBVIOUS FACT, and I VERIFIED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING: the parity guard lives in the WEB project, so `deno test` alone does NOT catch an engine-side change. Proved it by moving SEVERITY_MULT.minor 0.5 -> 0.6 with the mirror untouched — the edge suite passed 18/18 completely happily while the web guard failed on 'severity multipliers match SEVERITY_MULT'. An engine developer running the obvious local suite would have shipped it. That is now called out in both the source warning and the note, with the instruction to run npm run verify. Also carried the BASE_WEIGHT omission into both places as a PRODUCT TRADE-OFF rather than an unfinished edge — auditable vs gameable — because 'the published standard is missing the penalties' reads like a completeness bug to anyone who has not seen the argument. STILL OPEN: AC1 residue (pilling density, fade delta-E have no engine equivalent; adding them means defining new measurement in the engine first, not writing prose) and AC3 (naming the base model + eval numbers), which remains blocked behind the US-2035 determinism product decision. Verified: 2472 web + 4437 edge tests pass, deno check + lint clean, vault:lint clean at 100 notes.

userStories.title: No product/pricing/UI A/B testing — PostHog flags are never read client-side
userStories.description: There is a sophisticated server-side flag engine with deterministic FNV-1a bucketing, rollout percentages and plan targeting (lib/feature-flags.ts:114-166), plus four experiment engines (lib/experiments-governor.ts:19) — but they cover email subject lines, drip timing and AI prompts only. PostHog is initialized yet only capture() is ever called (src/lib/analytics.ts:237-239); feature flags are never read, there is no client useFeatureFlag hook and no exposure event. So paywall copy, pricing presentation and onboarding cannot currently be tested. All the primitives exist — this is a connector, not a framework build.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a client useFeatureFlag hook backed by PostHog, with an exposure event so results are analyzable.
Respect the existing consent gating — no flag evaluation before consent.
Prove it with one real experiment on a conversion surface (paywall copy or pricing layout).
Document how server-side flags and client-side experiments relate, so the two systems do not drift.
userStories.notes: [P2][Growth/Experimentation] Found 2026-07-18 by the SEO/marketing deep-dive audit. Pairs with US-2101 (UTM capture) — together they make conversion work measurable rather than anecdotal. | 2026-07-19 AC1+AC2+AC4 DONE; AC3 (one real experiment) DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. The connector exists: src/lib/client-experiments.ts (logic, testable without React) + src/hooks/use-feature-flag.ts (subscription plumbing), returning {variant, ready}. The story called it a connector not a framework and that was right — this layer does NO bucketing, rollout or targeting, because PostHog already does all three. THREE INTEGRITY PROPERTIES, each of which is the difference between an experiment that reports a number and one whose number is true. (1) CONSENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CHECKED: flags are read off window.posthog, which analytics.ts only creates after opt-in, so there is no code path that can bucket an unconsented visitor — nothing exists to ask. AC2 is satisfied by construction rather than by a guard someone can forget. (2) NO MID-SESSION FLIPS: a resolved variant is LOCKED for the page session. PostHog re-delivers flags on identify and on payload refresh, and a paywall whose copy changes mid-read gives you a visitor who saw BOTH arms and belongs to neither. (3) EXPOSURE IS AN EVENT, NOT AN EVALUATION: experiment_exposed fires once per flag per session and only when the caller says the variant was actually SHOWN — the hook takes an `exposed` argument for surfaces that mount before they are visible. Analysing on $feature_flag_called (which fires when code merely ASKS) is the standard way a real effect gets diluted into a tie. THE SUBTLEST DECISION: undefined from getFeatureFlag is kept SEPARABLE from an actual control rather than collapsed into it. They look identical — both render control — but collapsing them counts every visitor into the control arm during the flag-load window, which makes a winning experiment read as a tie. That is why the return is {variant, ready} and not just a string. 13 tests. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED all three properties by simulating the careless edit: dropping the lock reddens 2, dropping the exposure resolution-guard reddens 1, collapsing undefined into control reddens 3; restoring returns to green. AC4 DONE as vault/40-growth/experimentation.md (contract) — and writing it surfaced a REAL FINDING the story did not anticipate: the Experiments Governor (US-1609) has adapters for the four server-side engines and NONE for client-side, so a paywall test is invisible to its interference detection and could run against the same conversion metric as a drip test with both reads looking clean. Recorded as a warning callout with the manual check to do meanwhile. Also noted: the consent category model has no vault note, which is a gap. AC3 NOT DONE ON PURPOSE: there is no web paywall component (paywall is iOS/Android), so the named surface is the pricing page, and choosing what to test there means authoring alternative pricing copy/layout — a product and design decision, not a code one. The mechanism is ready and wiring a chosen variant is now a small edit. Verified: 2462 web tests pass, tsc -b clean, vault:lint clean (3 drift warnings pre-existing from earlier commits today, not from this work).

userStories.title: [OPS — USER ACTION REQUIRED, DEFERRED for agent loop] Prod runtime reconciliation: apply migrations, fix SES/SMTP, create Coolify cron tasks
userStories.description: As the operator, the 2026-07-02 admin audit found the admin code layer healthy but prod ops behind it: (1) migrations 00339–00342 pushed but not applied (AutoLister generation 400s in prod NOW; next edge redeploy boot-guards on 00342), plus possible stragglers 00332–00338 and older drift; (2) SES/SMTP creds misconfigured so drip previews 502 and admin messages / support replies / newsletter / journeys / growth campaigns queue mail that never delivers; (3) zero Coolify scheduled tasks created, so cron_runs is empty and every cron-fed admin surface is stale.
acceptanceCriteria: Migrations applied: run 00332→00342 on prod (all idempotent) or scripts/apply-prod-migrations.sh; run the applied_migrations reconciliation query to catch older drift and re-run anything missing; NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'; then redeploy the edge (boot guard expects 00342)
