userStories.notes: [2026-07-02 admin backend audit, findings #1–#3] NOT verifiable from this host (no prod DB/Coolify access) — agent loop must SKIP this story (treat like DEFERRED); it is tracked here so the ops work isn't lost. Companion code story: cron registry drift guard. | 2026-07-18 PROD DIAGNOSED (agent loop) — the story's 'NOT verifiable from this host' premise is WRONG in this environment: outbound HTTPS works and Coolify is reachable via the hub MCP tools. So prod was measured instead of assumed, and AC1/AC2 appear ALREADY DONE — the story's premise ('migrations 00339-00342 pushed but not applied') is roughly 130 migrations stale. THE ARGUMENT: the deployed edge is built from origin/main, whose EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION is 00474 (00474_push_subscriptions is the highest migration on origin/main). In production a confirmed-behind comparison calls onFatal -> Deno.exit(1) AFTER the ~40s grace window (schema-version.ts:170-180) — the container refuses to start. https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns 200 with env:production, and authenticated- free public endpoints reading real tables all return live data (/api/grading/public/transparency returns real volume+quality figures; condition-index 200; the certificates endpoint 200). A running production edge therefore implies the DB is at 00474 or AHEAD, i.e. 00332-00474 are applied. Corroborating: the live cert page renders 'Certificate No. GT-7Y3BCAF', proving grade_reports.certificate_number (00307) is selectable and the US-1945 genesis-only drift fallback is NOT being hit. AC2's specific claim (AutoLister 00339, photo rotate 00333) is subsumed — both are far below 00474. ⚠ ONE RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY, stated rather than hidden: the version read goes through the supabaseAdmin.rpc('latest_schema_migration') RPC, and a MISSING RPC returns null -> 'unknown' -> fail-open, which would also boot. I could not rule that out from outside (the RPC needs the anon key, which I could not locate in the deployed bundles). So the conclusion is 'applied, unless the version RPC itself is absent' — and the fix below makes that distinguishable for good. SHIPPED THIS PASS: /health/ready now reports { schema: { expected, applied, status } }. Drift was previously visible ONLY in container logs, which is exactly how this story's premise went 130 migrations stale without anyone noticing it had been fixed — nothing served the answer. Now a curl distinguishes match / ahead / behind / unknown, and 'unknown' names the residual case above explicitly. Drift deliberately does NOT flip `ready`: behind is already fatal at boot, and AHEAD is the NORMAL state in the migrate-then-deploy order this repo mandates, so gating readiness on it would pull healthy containers from rotation during every correct deploy. 5 new tests in health_test.ts (incl. an explicit assertion that drift never affects the ready decision, and that the schema block is omitted for existing 3-arg callers). Full edge suite 4099 passed / 0 failed. STILL GENUINELY OPEN (real ops, unchanged): AC3 SES/SMTP creds + drip preview + email-retry drain; AC4 Coolify Scheduled Tasks for the cron registry (cron_runs empty) — the hub MCP exposes health/logs/deploys but not scheduled-task management, so this stays a console action; AC5 one-off backfills; AC6 the migrate:prod pre-deploy gate. RECOMMEND: re-scope this story to AC3-AC6 and drop AC1/AC2, or verify AC1 in one command after the next deploy — curl https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready and read .schema.applied. | 2026-07-18 LAUNCH_CHECKLIST ENV NAMES VERIFIED — clean, no action. Cross-checked every env-var-shaped token in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md (67 of them) against a 31 MB corpus of all repo source, config and .env.example files: ALL 67 are real names that something actually reads. The four that first looked orphaned (ACCESS_KEY_ID, SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, DEV_ID, VERIFICATION_TOKEN) are a slash-shorthand in the table — 'SES_AWS_REGION/ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET_ACCESS_KEY' and 'EBAY_APP_ID/CERT_ID/DEV_ID/VERIFICATION_TOKEN' — and the expanded forms all exist (SES_AWS_* in lib/email-transport.ts, EBAY_CERT_ID and EBAY_DEV_ID in lib/ebay-client.ts, EBAY_VERIFICATION_TOKEN in lib/ebay-notification-subscriptions.ts). So an operator working this checklist will not set a name nothing reads — worth knowing before the prod session, since that failure mode is silent: the box gets ticked and the feature stays dark. NO GUARD ADDED, deliberately. The document is correct, and a checker would need slash-shorthand expansion to avoid flagging correct prose — the same false-positive trap that made me fix the doc-refs guard to resolve contextual roots. Not worth a check that would need babysitting to stay honest about a file that is currently right. ⚠ METHOD NOTE, because the first two runs of this check were WRONG and both looked plausible: run 1 reported all 67 unreferenced — a shell-escaping artefact, where a heredoc collapsed the regex's double backslash so JS parsed it as a BACKSPACE character and nothing could ever match. It was only obviously false because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY being unread is impossible. Run 2 reported 4, which were the shorthand above. Only run 3 was true. Any script containing regex escapes should be written with the editor, not embedded in a shell heredoc.

userStories.title: MeasureCard is a brochure with no path into the actual measure flow
userStories.description: As a reseller reading the MeasureCard page, I want a button into the measure tool and a sample of the finished result, so the page leads to the capability it describes instead of dead-ending.
acceptanceCriteria: src/pages/flipdesk/measure-card.tsx adds a primary CTA linking into the item measure surface
The page shows a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo
The mailed-card status surfaces an ETA and, once shipped, a tracking number (today only a date, lines 199-206)
userStories.notes: 2026-08-02 AC1 DONE; AC2 and AC3 recorded as blocked with the reason, not attempted. AC1: measure-card.tsx gains a "Measure an item" card with a primary CTA into /dashboard/flipdesk/inventory?status=cataloged. THE DIAGNOSIS BEHIND THE FIX, because the story's title undersells it: every control on that page produced an ARTEFACT — a PDF to print, a card to be mailed — and not one of them led to the thing the artefact is FOR. A seller who read the whole page still had to already know that measuring happens on an item, and where to find one. That is the specific shape of "brochure": not missing content, missing a next step. TWO CHOICES IN THE LINK WORTH STATING. It points at ?status=cataloged rather than the inventory root, so the seller lands on pre-listed items — the set that actually needs measuring — instead of their entire catalog; statusParamToTab folds cataloged / measured / photographed into the To-list tab, so one status param reaches the right view. And it uses ?status= rather than ?tab= deliberately: status is the documented EXTERNAL entry point that the Overview pipeline grid and the Kanban "+N more" links already use, tab is the table's internal view key, and the mapping function exists precisely so external links survive a tab rename. AC2 NOT DONE — it asks for a before/after sample of a finished buyer-facing measurements photo. That is an image asset. Producing it needs the measure pipeline run against a real garment with a real card in frame, and a judgement about whose item is safe to show publicly. Same class as US-1949 AC1: a human with the product open, not a code change. AC3 NOT DONE, and it splits. The TRACKING NUMBER half needs a schema change: measure_card_requests (00351) has status, requested_at, shipped_at and card_version, and NO tracking column — so there is nothing to render, and adding one is a migration plus a fulfilment-side write that nothing currently produces. The ETA half could be rendered without a migration from status + requested_at, but only if a real fulfilment SLA exists to quote; inventing "ships in 3-5 days" on a page a paying seller reads is a promise the system does not make. Both need an answer about the fulfilment process before they are code. VERIFIED: build clean through the 216-route prerender, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 100 flipdesk tests pass. | 2026-08-08 AC3's TRACKING HALF DONE. AC2 and AC3's ETA half stay open, both for the reasons the previous note gave and neither has changed. The previous pass split AC3 correctly and I built the half that was buildable. NEW migration 00561_measure_card_tracking.sql adds tracking_number and tracking_carrier to measure_card_requests; the operator queue can record them on the shipped transition, and the seller's own /card-request read returns them. BOTH COLUMNS ARE NULLABLE, and that is the design rather than laziness: cards are mailed by hand and many go out as untracked letters. NOT NULL would either stop the operator marking those shipped at all or push them to type a placeholder, and a PLACEHOLDER TRACKING NUMBER IS WORSE THAN AN EMPTY ONE, because the seller clicks it. The route never writes an empty string for the same reason - a test forbids the `tracking || ""` fallback specifically. THE REFUSAL THAT MATTERS, and the reason this needed more than a column. The bulk status route takes up to 500 ids; tracking is per-PARCEL. Sending a number with a batch would stamp ONE carrier reference onto every seller in it, and each would then see a link tracking somebody else's parcel - worse than no tracking, because it looks authoritative. The route refuses it (400) rather than trusting the caller, and refuses tracking on the 'exported' transition too, which would record a parcel that has not been sent. PLAINTEXT, DECIDED NOT DEFAULTED. US-2417 (same session) encrypts ship_name/address_line1/ address_line2/city/postal_code on this exact table because they say where a person lives. A tracking number is a carrier's identifier for a parcel, the operator must search and paste it, and it is the one field on the row the SELLER is meant to read back. Same reasoning that keeps state and country readable there. A GUARD AGAINST AN INTERACTION I WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE MISSED: the seller summary has deliberately never echoed the address (US-1579), and since US-2417 those columns are ciphertext - so adding a field to that summary is now a place where a careless change would BOTH undo a privacy decision and return unreadable data. A test asserts the summary still omits ship_name, address_line1 and postal_code. 4 cases in NEW src/tests/measure-card-tracking_test.ts, comments stripped before every assertion. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED THREE WAYS: the batch guard removed, the shipped-only guard removed, and the empty-string fallback introduced. Each reddened with its own message; route restored and re-run green. VERIFIED: migration applied from clean AND re-applied (idempotent), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00561 with the manifest regenerated in the same pass, deno check + deno lint clean across 1426 files, full edge suite 6003 passed / 0 failed. 00561 is HELD and packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md with the apply-before-edge-deploy direction: the edge SELECTs both columns by name, so an edge-first deploy answers 42703 and breaks the MeasureCard panel for EVERY seller, not just those with tracking. | 2026-08-09 STATUS CORRECTION — THE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM IN THIS STORY'S NOTES IS STALE. Migrations 00351 and 00561 are both on origin/main (00351 in 16b36508, 00561 in 6a49be11) and applied. Nothing about this story is blocked on a frozen branch. Recorded because prd-lint has been WARNING about exactly this for some time — 'story(ies) still describe a migration as HELD that is already on origin/main' — and the warning went unactioned, which is how a note that says the branch is frozen keeps costing the next reader a session. It cost me one today on two sibling stories with the identical shape (US-2213 and US-2215, both since corrected). A held migration is by definition UNPUSHED; once it lands on origin the word is not merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is unchanged and unrelated to migrations: AC2, and the ETA half of AC3. Read the 2026-08-08 note for those. NOTE FOR WHOEVER ADDS THE NEXT HELD MIGRATION: the discipline that works is to write 'HELD' in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md, which is the file that gets emptied on apply, and to reference it from the story rather than restating the status in prose that nobody revisits. Nine migrations are held RIGHT NOW (00564-00572) and they are tracked there, not here.

acceptanceCriteria: Changing a structured column (brand/size/color/material/style) on the iOS item editor updates that column's eBay aspect even when the aspect's provenance is ai_extracted or manual. Today InventoryAspectSync.reassertDerivedAspects builds a 'preserve' map of every manual/aiExtracted aspect and passes it as 'known', so the AI-filled Size survives and the seller's new Size is discarded - the opposite of the documented contract that the columns OWN those five aspects (see the web helper projectColumnAspects in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts and its tests).

The save writes BOTH aspect stores, not just one: inventory_items.ebay_aspects (+ebay_aspect_sources) AND listings.item_specifics_override (+item_specifics_sources) for this item's listing row. Today the save-time path writes only the inventory_items pair; item_specifics_override is written ONLY by SpecificsEditorModel (the Category & Specifics editor), which is exactly why the seller has to go there for the change to stick - it is the copy publish/revise reads FIRST.

The projection runs even when the item has no eBay category selected yet. Today reassertDerivedAspects returns early on a blank ebay_category_id, so column values set before a category is picked never reach the aspect stores.

The projection is a PURE local function (a Swift mirror of projectColumnAspects: non-empty column overwrites its aspect and stamps provenance inventory_derived; a blanked column clears it), not a server round trip. Today every save calls EbayAspectsService.deriveAspects, so a save costs a network call and a transient failure silently no-ops via try?.

An XCTest asserts the three rules directly: an ai_extracted Size aspect IS overwritten by a changed Size column; a non-column aspect (e.g. Department, Pattern) is left untouched; and a cleared column clears its aspect.

A deno or vitest drift guard asserts the iOS column-to-aspect name mapping matches the web/edge registry (services/edge-functions/src/lib/aspect-registry.ts, vendored to src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json), so the two platforms cannot disagree on which aspect a column owns.

Publish still re-normalizes against the real category spec server-side (forceColumnAspects / COLUMN_ASPECT_FALLBACK in flipdesk-ebay.ts), so a raw column value outside eBay's allowed list is still corrected at publish - this story does not change that.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-03 WARNING, READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: AC4 and AC5 as written would re-open a bug fixed on 2026-08-02 (commit ea9e27a2). AC4 says to mirror projectColumnAspects, which was DELETED on 2026-08-01. Its replacement, projectColumnAspectsForSpec in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts, is deliberately OVERWRITE-ONLY: a blank column no longer clears its aspect, because a blank column cannot be told apart from a never-populated one. Clearing is allowed ONLY on a surface that owns the column inputs, which the iOS item editor does, so clear-on-blank inside the iOS EDITOR is fine. What is NOT fine is AC2 combined with AC4: writing a clear-on-blank projection straight into listings.item_specifics_override, the store the publish check reads FIRST. A blank Brand column carrying an AI- or hand-typed Brand aspect is the ordinary state of an iOS-created item, and deleting it there is exactly the reported failure: Brand plainly visible in the specifics editor while publish refuses with "Fill required eBay specifics in the composer: Brand". Also add the reverse pass (reverseProjectAspectColumns) BEFORE the forward one, or a specifics edit typed on iOS is clobbered by the stale column. Read vault/20-domain/sync-source-of-truth.md first; it is the contract. | 2026-08-12 AC6 DONE, AND ITS PREMISE WAS WRONG - that is the useful part. AC6 asks for a guard asserting the iOS column-to-aspect mapping MATCHES src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json. THERE IS NO IOS MAPPING TO MATCH: SpecificsEditorModel.applyColumnAuthority takes columnOwned/columnCleared off the server derive-aspects response, and its own doc comment at :589 already says why - "the mapping stays in the shared registry (US-822) and no Swift table can drift from it". So src/test/ios-aspect-registry-parity.test.ts pins the INVERSE: not "the two tables agree" but "there is no second table". A guard comparing two copies would have to be rewritten the day someone added the copy, which makes adding the drift the cheap path. WHAT IT ACTUALLY CATCHES: a future edit hardcoding the five column-owned names into Swift to save a round trip. That reads as a reasonable optimisation and it is exactly how the registry stops being the source of truth - it would silently lose the per-category overrides, and shoes already have one (size -> "US Shoe Size"). Comments stripped before scanning, because those files NAME "Brand" while explaining the rule. Three sabotages each watched failing, including one that empties the registry column entries - without that case every assertion passes vacuously against an empty list. STILL OPEN: AC2 (the save writes BOTH aspect stores), AC3 (projection runs with no eBay category selected), AC4 (make it a pure local projection instead of a network round trip), AC5 (the XCTest). AND THE 2026-08-03 WARNING ON THIS STORY STILL STANDS and should be read before any of them: AC4 + AC2 combined would re-open the bug fixed in ea9e27a2 - a clear-on-blank projection written into listings.item_specifics_override, the store publish reads FIRST, deletes the Brand aspect on an ordinary iOS-created item and produces "Fill required eBay specifics in the composer: Brand" on a listing that visibly has Brand. Clear-on-blank is allowed only INSIDE the iOS editor, and reverseProjectAspectColumns must run BEFORE the forward pass. Read vault/20-domain/sync-source-of-truth.md first; it is the contract. | 2026-08-12 AC2 AND AC5 DONE (0f41949f). AC2 is the reported bug: an item-column edit landed only in inventory_items.ebay_aspects, while publish and revise read listings.item_specifics_override FIRST - so correcting Size on the item page did not change what ships and the seller had to reopen the Category & Specifics editor for their own correction to stick. InventoryAspectSync now merges the column-owned aspects into every draft/active listing row for the item. THE SAFETY ARGUMENT IS THE SHAPE, NOT A CHECK: listingOverrideMerge is pure and can only ever return values to SET. It takes the names the server marked columnOwned (which MEANS the column currently has a value) and skips anything empty; columnCleared is deliberately ignored, because clearing belongs to the editor, which owns the column inputs. That is a direct answer to this story's own 2026-08-03 warning rather than a way around it - a clear-on-blank projection written into the override store re-opens ea9e27a2, since a blank Brand column beside an AI- or hand-typed Brand aspect is the ORDINARY state of an iOS-created item. Confirmed web reached the same conclusion independently: projectColumnAspectsForSpec bails on a blank column at ebay-prefill.ts:503 so it stays overwrite-only. Two platforms, same reasoning, arrived at separately. Scoped to draft and active listings, mirroring the US-1995 title-sync decision - a sold or ended listing's specifics record what was actually sold. AC5: six XCTests pinning the PROPERTY rather than the implementation, ending with one asserting every projected key carries at least one non-empty value, so a future edit has to break additivity deliberately. AC6 was done earlier the same day (a6dd5bc1) and its premise was wrong - see that note. AC4 IS NOT DONE AND SHOULD NOT BE DONE AS WRITTEN. It asks for a pure local clear-on-blank projection, and combining that with AC2 is exactly what the warning rules out. If a future pass wants the round trip gone, the clear-on-blank half has to stay inside the editor. AC3 REMAINS, and its honest fix is not what it says either: with no eBay category there is no aspect spec, so nothing can be projected. The real fix is to RE-RUN the sync when a category is first picked, so column values set beforehand reach the stores then. UNCOMPILED - iOS CI is the gate, and what it has to prove is narrow: the merge never removes a key.

userStories.title: Lock down SECURITY DEFINER functions: revoke EXECUTE from PUBLIC across public schema
userStories.description: Postgres grants EXECUTE on every new function to PUBLIC by default. No migration in supabase/migrations/ ever revokes it, and no `REVOKE ... ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC` exists anywhere. Because these functions are SECURITY DEFINER they run as the owner and bypass RLS, so any holder of the anon key can call them directly through PostgREST. grant_grade_credits and debit_grade_credits carry no GRANT/REVOKE statements at all; the revenue-dashboard functions (00215_revenue_dashboard.sql:273-274) grant to authenticated and service_role but never revoke the implicit PUBLIC grant. Impact: mint yourself unlimited grade credits, drain another user's credit balance, and read the full revenue and customer roster anonymously.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration revokes EXECUTE on all existing public-schema functions from PUBLIC, then re-grants explicitly to the roles each function actually needs.
`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC` so future functions are closed by default.
Every SECURITY DEFINER function is inventoried with its intended caller role; credit-mutating functions (grant_grade_credits, debit_grade_credits, refund/reserve variants) are service_role only.
A test or CI check fails if a new SECURITY DEFINER function ships without an explicit grant block.
Migration triple honoured: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer.
Run `SELECT proname, proacl FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace='public'::regnamespace AND prosecdef;` against prod before and after and record both in the story.

OPERATOR: run `SELECT proname, proacl FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace='public'::regnamespace AND prosecdef;` against prod and record it here (AC6). Do it before and after 00527, which is parked as .BLOCKED behind US-2403.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/DB] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] VERIFIED directly against the code in this session. Pairs with the guard_users_protected_columns gap — either one alone gives free grading. Fix both together. | 2026-08-04 BLOCKED on US-2403, with the migration WRITTEN AND VERIFIED. Two findings, and the first one means the fix as the story describes it would have done NOTHING. (1) THE STORY'S DIAGNOSIS IS HALF WRONG. It says Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default and no migration revokes it. Reading pg_proc.proacl on a live stack says otherwise: grant_grade_credits carries {postgres=X/postgres, anon=X/postgres, authenticated=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres} — DIRECT grants to anon and authenticated, granted by postgres, from Supabase's own ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES bootstrap (confirmed in pg_default_acl for both postgres and supabase_admin on schema public, objtype 'f'). PUBLIC does not appear in the ACL at all. So 'REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC' is a NO-OP on exactly the functions the story names. I wrote that version first, applied it, and measured: grant_grade_credits/debit_grade_credits/revenue_dashboard still showed anon_can=t. A migration that looks like a security fix and changes nothing is worse than none, and the only reason I caught it is that I queried the ACLs instead of trusting the revoke. (2) THE CORRECTED MIGRATION IS WRITTEN AND PASSES EVERY CHECK, and is parked at supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED (the suffix is deliberate — apply-prod-migrations.sh globs *.sql, so the rename is what stops an accidental apply). It revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC, anon AND authenticated on every non-extension function in public, closes the ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES that keeps re-granting them, grants service_role everything (the edge calls 48), and then REPLAYS the grants migrations actually made — 43 names for authenticated, 4 for anon, PARSED out of every GRANT EXECUTE statement in the corpus minus any later explicit REVOKE, not authored by judgement. Plus is_admin/is_super_admin/is_reviewer_or_admin explicitly, because a function called inside an RLS policy runs as the QUERYING role and is_admin appears in 29 migrations' policies while having NEVER had a grant — it worked only on the default this removes. Extension functions are excluded via pg_depend deptype 'e' so pg_trgm (installed into public by 00224) keeps its operators. MEASURED AFTER APPLYING, on a fresh stack: all 527 apply from zero; ZERO of the 28 client-callable RPCs (parsed from src/ + ios/ call sites) lost authenticated EXECUTE; grant_grade_credits, debit_grade_credits, grant_api_credits, admin_adjust_credits, revoke_grade_credits and reserve_ai_action are now f/f/t (anon no, authenticated no, service_role yes); revenue_dashboard and system_health keep authenticated because their own migrations explicitly granted it, and lose anon; similarity/show_trgm still callable by PUBLIC. (3) WHY IT IS NOT SHIPPING: verifying the behaviour crashed the database. On this image any function-permission denial for a role in supautils.hint_roles (anon, authenticated, service_role) segfaults the backend. Filed as US-2403 with the isolation. 00527 does not cause it — refund_grade has been revoked since 00048 and crashes identically — but it would take the crashable surface from a handful of RPCs to ~80. REMAINING ACs when unblocked: AC4 (a CI check that a new SECURITY DEFINER function ships with an explicit grant block) is NOT written; AC6 (proname/proacl before and after against PROD) is an operator read. | 2026-08-08 AC4 DONE. AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5 stay parked in 00527_...sql.BLOCKED behind US-2403; AC6 is an operator read against prod. AC4 was the half that never needed either, and it is now written: NEW src/test/security-definer-grants.test.ts. WHAT IT ENFORCES: every CALLABLE SECURITY DEFINER function in the migration corpus must be named by an explicit GRANT EXECUTE or REVOKE somewhere. Silence is not 'closed' on this stack - it is 'open to anon and authenticated', per the pg_proc.proacl reading in the note above - so a function that states nothing has been granted to the browser by a default nobody wrote down, on the one construct in the schema that deliberately bypasses RLS. TRIGGER FUNCTIONS ARE EXEMPT, and that is a real distinction, not a convenience: a RETURNS trigger function is invoked by the trigger machinery as part of the firing statement and EXECUTE is never consulted. 15 of the 83 are that shape. MY OWN FIRST PARSER PRODUCED EXACTLY THE MISCLASSIFICATION THE TEST EXISTS TO PREVENT, and the guard-the-guard is what caught it. Draft one read a fixed 2500-character window after each CREATE FUNCTION. From grant_grade_credits (00037:180) that window runs straight into handle_new_user (00037:233), whose RETURNS TRIGGER made a CREDIT-GRANTING RPC read as an exempt trigger function - so the single function US-2282 had measured carrying EXECUTE for anon on a live database would have been waved through by its own guard. Fixed by bounding each definition at the NEXT CREATE FUNCTION rather than by a character count. Two landmark assertions (a known callable, two known triggers) are what failed; without them the file would have shipped green and wrong. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE COUNTS THAT ONLY THE FIXED PARSER COULD SHOW: 83 distinct SECURITY DEFINER functions, not 86, and 15 trigger functions, not 19 - the extra 4 were non-SECURITY-DEFINER helpers (set_updated_at among them) swept up by the bleeding window. THE DEBT IS ENUMERATED, NOT TOLERATED: 18 callable SECURITY DEFINER functions say nothing about who may execute them. Seven move money or credits (grant_grade_credits, grant_api_credits, debit_api_credits, grant_appstore_credits, grant_buyer_reward_credit, issue_buyer_reward_credit, redeem_buyer_reward_credit) and three are the RLS predicates themselves (is_admin, is_reviewer_or_admin, is_super_admin) - which is the sharper problem, because a function called inside an RLS policy runs as the QUERYING role, so is_admin has always worked ONLY because of the default this debt describes, and hand-revoking it would break 29 migrations' policies at once. That is what 00527 handles as one atomic replay; the list says so, so nobody picks these off one at a time. The list is SHRINK-ONLY in both directions: a name that gains a grant or revoke FAILS the test until its entry is deleted in the same commit, and a name that stops being a SECURITY DEFINER function fails too. So the ground gained cannot be quietly given back, and the list cannot rot into a place where things go to be forgotten. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED THREE WAYS with a throwaway migration: a new ungranted callable SECURITY DEFINER function reddened naming it; the SAME function with a REVOKE + GRANT block passed; and granting an existing debt entry reddened the shrink-only case telling the reader to delete the entry. Probe migration removed, tree confirmed clean. VERIFIED: npx tsc -b clean, eslint clean, the three cases pass, full vitest 3671 passed / 0 failed.

userStories.title: extension.pem private key is committed to the repository
userStories.description: git ls-files confirms extension.pem and extension.crx are tracked. extension.pem begins with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`. .gitignore has no .pem or .crx rule. The key was added 2026-07-13 in commit e1dbc4da; gitleaks failed that commit and every run since has been green because push-mode only scans new commits. This is the Chrome Web Store signing identity for the extension. Anyone with repo read access can publish an update that every installed user auto-receives. Also tracked and probably unwanted: ios-screenshots/Payment/ios.zip, ios-screenshots/screenshots-appstore.zip, ios-screenshots/screenshots-raw.zip.
acceptanceCriteria: Rotate the Chrome Web Store extension key first. Removing the file does not un-leak it.
git rm --cached extension.pem extension.crx; add *.pem, *.crx and ios-screenshots/*.zip to .gitignore.
Decide and record whether git history is rewritten (BFG / filter-repo) or the key is simply treated as burned. Rewriting rewrites every open PR.
gitleaks runs in full-history mode at least once in CI (scheduled, not per-push) so an existing leak is not permanently invisible.
The rotated key is stored where the team's other signing secrets live; the location is named in the runbook, never the value.

OPERATOR: rotate the Chrome Web Store signing key and revoke the old one, fill in the storage-location line in vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md, and choose burn-vs-rewrite for the git history (AC1, AC3, AC5). Do it BEFORE US-1757 publishes: rotation is cheap now and expensive once that extension id is an installed identity.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/Secrets] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] VERIFIED directly against the code in this session. via git ls-files + file header + .gitignore read. Rotation is a human action, not a code change. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — the code half is done; AC1 (rotate) and AC3 (the rewrite-or-burn decision) are HUMAN actions and are now written down where the person doing them will find them. AC2 DONE: extension.pem, extension.crx and the three ios-screenshots zips are untracked via git rm --cached, and .gitignore refuses *.pem, *.crx, *.p12, *.keystore, *.jks and ios-screenshots/**/*.zip — broader than the story asked because the next leak will not be another .pem. Verified with git check-ignore. AC4 DONE: NEW .github/workflows/secret-scan-history.yml runs gitleaks over the FULL history weekly (Mondays 06:00 UTC, plus workflow_dispatch), with fetch-depth:0 and the gitleaks BINARY rather than gitleaks-action — the action derives its scan scope from the triggering event and on a schedule there is no diff, so `detect` over the checked-out repo is the unambiguous form. The report uploads on failure, because a bare red X names nothing. WHY THIS IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT and worth stating plainly: there WAS a secret scanner, it WAS working, and it could not have caught this. secret-scan.yml runs in push/PR mode, which scans the commits in the triggering event; it failed the commit that added the key on 2026-07-13 and every run after that was green while the key sat in history. Per-push asks 'is this change clean?'; only a history sweep asks 'is the repository clean?'. AC5 DONE (structurally): vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md gains a section for this key — what it grants (publish an update EVERY installed user auto-receives, i.e. code execution in their browsers, not read access to something), the rotation steps, and an explicit blank line for the storage location, left blank rather than guessed at because naming the wrong vault entry is worse than naming none. AC3 is RECORDED not decided: both options are written out with their real costs — treat-as-burned (rotation makes the leaked copy inert; no rewrite; usually right for a signing key) versus rewrite (BFG/filter-repo; rewrites every open PR and invalidates every clone). .gitleaks.toml carries a COMMENTED-OUT allowlist stanza to uncomment AFTER rotation, with an explicit 'DO NOT uncomment before rotation — silencing a live key is worse than the leak, because it also removes the reminder.' EXPECT THE SCHEDULED SCAN TO BE RED until one of those two happens: the key IS still in history, so a finding is the job working, not a broken job. ALSO ADDED: src/test/no-committed-keys.test.ts refuses any tracked .pem/.crx/.p12/.pfx/.keystore/.jks/.key/.ppk at the point a developer notices — their own test run, before the push. It reads git ls-files rather than the filesystem, because an ignored file on disk is fine and a TRACKED one is the bug, and it skips (not fails) without a git binary, since a false red on a P0 guard trains people to ignore it. Negative-verified by force-adding a .pem to the index (reddened naming the file, reverted). REMAINING FOR THE OWNER: (1) rotate the Chrome Web Store signing key and revoke the old one; (2) fill in the storage-location line in key-rotation.md; (3) choose burn-vs-rewrite and, if burning, uncomment the gitleaks stanza. VERIFIED: 3079 tests pass (239 files), tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green, vault-lint 108 notes clean. | SEVERITY RE-ASSESSED 2026-08-03, in BOTH directions, because the original framing is wrong in a way that changes what the owner should do. WORSE THAN RECORDED: the repository is PUBLIC (gh repo view reports visibility PUBLIC) and commit e1dbc4da is on origin, and reading that path out of history still returns a PRIVATE KEY header today. So this is not 'anyone with repo read access' — it is anyone at all, with no access, right now. Untracking the file (AC2) did nothing about that and was never going to; only rotation does. BETTER THAN RECORDED, and this is the part that should stop anyone panicking: the claim that 'anyone can publish an update that every installed user auto-receives' is NOT true today. Checked: no manifest in extension/, extension-condition/ or extension-unified/ declares an update_url or a key field, so there is no self-hosted auto-update channel; and US-1757 (publish to the Chrome Web Store and AMO) is still OPEN and operator-gated, so the extension has never been published and has no installed users. Uploading to the Web Store needs the developer ACCOUNT, which this key is not. WHAT THE KEY ACTUALLY GRANTS: the ability to package a CRX carrying the SAME extension ID as the real one — which matters for sideloading, for enterprise-policy deployment, and for any future self-hosted update channel, and which would let a lookalike be presented as genuine. WHAT THAT MEANS FOR SEQUENCING, which is the practical finding and was recorded nowhere: rotation is CHEAP right now and gets expensive the moment the extension is published, because after publication that ID is the installed identity. So AC1 must be done BEFORE US-1757, and US-1757 should not proceed until it is. RE-VERIFIED the code half rather than trusting the note: git ls-files finds no .pem, .gitignore lines 155-156 refuse *.pem and *.crx (git check-ignore confirms both files), .github/workflows/secret-scan-history.yml exists, and src/test/no-committed-keys.test.ts passes 3/3.

userStories.title: Apple sandbox purchases grant production plans
userStories.description: lib/appstore/verify.ts:89-96 retries a failed production receipt check against Apple's sandbox endpoint (Apple's documented pattern) but nothing downstream records or checks WHICH environment answered. Any TestFlight or sandbox tester gets a real Business Yearly entitlement for zero dollars. The Stripe path already blocks the equivalent case, so this is an iOS-path-only gap.
acceptanceCriteria: The verify result carries the environment (Production vs Sandbox) that actually answered.
A sandbox-verified receipt grants nothing in production, or grants only in a non-production environment.
Same check applied to the Google Play path: reject purchases flagged as test purchases (purchaseType / testPurchase).
Regression test for both stores.
Audit existing appstore-sourced entitlements for sandbox-originated grants.

OPERATOR: audit existing appstore-sourced entitlements for sandbox-originated grants (AC5). Grants made before the environment marker are NULL, so they cannot be identified from the database alone; this needs App Store purchase history.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/iOS+Android] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Covers both the Apple sandbox fallback and the Google Play test-purchase flag; they are the same class of bug. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED — and the premise is CONTESTED BY THE CODE, so this needs re-triage before anyone 'fixes' it. services/edge-functions/src/lib/appstore/verify.ts lines 38-44 already argue the opposite case, in a comment written when the fallback was added: App Review ALWAYS exercises IAP in the sandbox, even against a Production build, so a Production deploy that refuses Sandbox JWS fails App Review. verify-config.ts:91-93 implements it as primary-then-fallback (configured environment first, the other second), mirroring the legacy 21007 receipt rule Apple documents. The comment's defence is that a valid Sandbox JWS can only be produced by a sandbox tester Apple provisioned on the developer account, so it is not an open abuse vector. THAT DEFENCE IS PROBABLY RIGHT AND STILL LEAVES A REAL GAP, which is what this story should be rewritten to cover: the grant is recorded with NO MARKER of which environment produced it. Nothing on the users row or in the appstore audit rows says 'this Pro plan came from a Sandbox JWS'. So a sandbox-granted entitlement is indistinguishable from a paid one in every downstream query — revenue reporting, the expiry sweep, plan-distribution metrics, and any manual 'why is this account on Pro' investigation. RECOMMEND: reframe from 'stop accepting sandbox' (which would break App Review) to 'stamp the environment on the grant and exclude sandbox grants from revenue reporting', and say in the story that the acceptance itself is deliberate. | 2026-08-07 IMPLEMENTED THE REFRAME, AC1+AC3+AC4 done, AC2 deliberately NOT done, AC5 is operator-only. AC2 as written ('a sandbox-verified receipt grants nothing') would assert the App Review outage the 2026-08-04 note describes, so it is refused on purpose; the marker replaces it. New services/edge-functions/src/lib/billing-environment.ts holds the shared classifier (resolveAppleEnvironment / resolvePlayEnvironment / countsAsRevenue) because Apple says Sandbox|Production and Google says testPurchase|purchaseType=0 — two vocabularies, one answer, normalised once. THE ACTUAL PLUMBING BUG: withVerifier already handed the answering environment to its callback at appstore/verify.ts:108 and the callback DISCARDED it, so the strong signal existed and was thrown away one line from where it was needed; verifyTransaction and verifyNotification now capture it into DecodedTransactionLite.verifiedEnvironment. Apple disagreement between verifier and payload resolves to sandbox, and an unmarked txn defaults to sandbox at the reconciler — a false sandbox costs one row wrongly left out of a report (visible, correctable), a false production books free entitlement as revenue (invisible, compounds). userStories.title: users_billing_source_chk rejects 'googleplay' — Play subscriptions may be failing outright
userStories.description: 00104_appstore_billing.sql:25 defines users_billing_source_chk allowing only 'stripe' and 'appstore'. The Google Play verification path writes 'googleplay'. If the constraint is live in prod as written, every Play subscription write fails: the customer is charged by Google and receives no entitlement.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm against prod whether the constraint still excludes 'googleplay' and whether any Play purchase has ever succeeded.
Migration extends the allowed set to include every billing source the code actually writes.
A test asserts the constraint's allowed set matches the set of literals the code writes.
If any customer was charged by Google without receiving entitlement, reconcile and grant retroactively.

OPERATOR: two queries against prod (AC1, AC4). SELECT pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'users_billing_source_chk'; expected to contain googleplay. SELECT count(*) FROM public.users WHERE billing_source = 'googleplay'; expected 0 - and note a zero is ALSO what a still-broken constraint produces, so the Play Console chain in the notes is the load-bearing evidence, not the count.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Android] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Verify against prod before assuming customers were affected — the constraint may have been altered outside migrations. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED, and it is worse than 'may be failing' — it fails, deterministically. users_billing_source_chk is created ONCE, in 00104_appstore_billing.sql line 25: CHECK (billing_source IS NULL OR billing_source IN ('stripe','appstore')). grep across every file in supabase/migrations returns exactly two hits for the constraint name, both in 00104 (the IF NOT EXISTS probe and the ADD CONSTRAINT). NO migration ever drops or re-adds it. 00321_google_play_billing.sql touches public.users but only to add columns — its own header comment says "billing_source already carries 'stripe'/'appstore'; Play sets 'googleplay'", which reads as if the constraint had been widened, and it never was. Meanwhile the Play grant path genuinely stamps it: services/edge-functions/src/lib/google-play/products.ts declares billing_source: 'googleplay' as a literal type on the users update, and the expiry sweep queries .eq('billing_source','googleplay'). So every Play subscription grant UPDATE violates the check and returns 23514, and the sweep can never match a row because no row can hold that value. WHAT MAKES THIS EASY TO MISS: three OTHER constraints were correctly widened for Play — 00354 added 'googleplay' to the dead-letter provider check, 00414 allows it on buyer_billing_source, 00486 allows 'google_play' on the agreed-terms source. Only the seller-side users constraint was left behind, so a targeted grep for 'googleplay' in migrations returns four confident-looking hits and none of them is the one that matters. THE FIX is a one-line ALTER (drop + re-add with the third value), needing the US-1108 triple. Worth checking prod for stuck Play purchasers before shipping it: they paid Google and were never entitled here. | AC2 + AC3 DONE 2026-08-07, migration 00558 (HELD). RE-VERIFIED FIRST as the note asks, and the 2026-08-04 verification holds exactly: users_billing_source_chk is created ONCE (00104:24-25) allowing only stripe/appstore, grep returns exactly two hits for the name and both are in 00104, and no migration ever drops or re-adds it. The writers are three literals and only three — stripe (routes/webhooks.ts:666), appstore (lib/appstore/reconcile.ts:59), googleplay (lib/google-play/products.ts:104) — confirmed by scanning every object-literal assignment across the edge service, src/ and functions/, not by reading the two files the story names. AC2: 00558 drops and re-adds the constraint with the third value. It uses DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS then ADD rather than 00104s IF NOT EXISTS probe DELIBERATELY: the probe is the reason the stale definition survived every subsequent apply, so repeating it would make this migration a no-op the next time someone widens the set. AC3: NEW src/test/billing-source-constraint.test.ts, 3 cases. It does NOT hardcode the allowed set — a constant here would be a THIRD copy needing maintenance, which is the same class of bug the test is for. It parses the live CHECK body out of the highest-numbered migration that defines the constraint (apply order is filename order, so a later re-add supersedes) and compares it against the literals scanned from source. Both directions: a value the code writes that the constraint rejects, and a value the constraint permits that nobody writes. The third case pins googleplay/appstore/stripe by name, because the first two both pass if the Play writer is DELETED and the constraint narrows to match — a silent removal of Android billing rather than a fix. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: reverting 00558 to the 00104 set reddens 2 of 3 cases and the failure message names lib/google-play/products.ts as the writing file. VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, schema-version_test 18/18 (which is what proves the US-1108 triple — EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 00558, manifest regenerated to 303 entries, self-record footer present). PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md updated: held count 16 -> 17, and it records that this one is unusual in that it has NO forward dependency — the edge already writes googleplay today and that write is already failing, so applying it makes existing code start working rather than creating a window where old code breaks against new schema. The affected set IS recoverable rather than lost — the Play purchase token is recorded even when the users-row grant failed, so start from the Play purchase records, not from users.billing_source (which by definition can hold no googleplay row). | 2026-08-09 STATUS CORRECTION — THE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM IN THIS STORY'S NOTES IS STALE. Migration 00558 is on origin/main (b197e9b3, 'fix(US-2287): allow googleplay in users_billing_source_chk') and applied, as are 00104, 00354, 00414 and 00486.
