userStories.title: Unlimited free trials: handle_new_user grants 14 days of Pro with no abuse check
userStories.description: 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql:102-104 grants every new signup a 14-day Pro trial with no card, no device fingerprint, no email-domain check and no prior-trial lookup. Deleting the account and signing up again resets it. Each trial can consume real Claude Vision spend.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the abuse control: card-on-file for trial, per-device/per-email prior-trial record, or a hard cap on trial grading volume. Record the decision.
A prior-trial record survives account deletion (keyed on something that persists, not on the users row).
Trial grading volume is capped independently of the plan's normal allowance.
Measure current exposure first: count trials started vs converted, and grading spend attributable to trial accounts.

OPERATOR: run §19 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql (AC4). Four read-only queries: trials started vs converted, addresses that normalise to the same mailbox once plus-tags and dots are stripped, what the trials cost in grading, and whether any came from an account since deleted. AC1 is deliberately gated on this - the right abuse control is a different control at two people than at two hundred.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Abuse] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Measure before building — the fix depends on whether this is being exploited today. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED against the LIVE definition, not the one the story cites. handle_new_user has been redefined six times; the current body is 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql, and it grants flipdesk_plan='pro', subscription_status='trialing', trial_ends_at=now()+interval '14 days' to every signup EXCEPT a buyer-only one (v_buyer_only, from a client-supplied account_type of 'buyer'). No prior-trial lookup, no email-domain check, no device or IP signal, ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING — so one auth user is one trial and a second address is a second trial. The claim holds exactly as filed. ONE CORRECTION TO THE STORY'S FRAMING: 00303 is not the live definition, 00401 is, and the difference matters if a fix is written — 00401 already carves out buyer-only signups, so any abuse check has to compose with v_buyer_only rather than wrap the whole grant. A SECOND THING WORTH KNOWING BEFORE FIXING: the whole function body is wrapped in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS RETURN NEW, deliberately, so a profile-row failure can never abort auth signup. Any abuse check added here inherits that — if it raises, the user still gets an auth account and gets NO profile row at all, which is a worse outcome than an extra trial. The check probably belongs downstream of signup, not inside this trigger. | 2026-08-08 AC4 IS NOW RUNNABLE — the measurement this story insists on doing FIRST is written as §19 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, so it rides along with the other operator reads instead of being a separate ask. AC1 stays open ON PURPOSE: the correct abuse control is a different control if the answer is 'two people did this' than if it is 'two hundred', and the story is right that building before measuring picks one blind. FOUR QUERIES, ALL READ-ONLY. (a) trials started per month vs converted vs still trialing. (b) THE ABUSE SIGNAL: addresses that normalise to the SAME mailbox once a Gmail-style plus-tag and dots are stripped. That is the cheapest possible way to take a second trial, so any stem with n > 1 is one person holding several. It returns COUNTS and nothing else - no addresses, not even the normalised stems - because this output gets pasted around and the rest of the file is deliberately secret-free. (c) what the trials COST: grading submissions made inside the trial window, per account and worst-case, which is the number that decides whether AC3's trial-specific volume cap is worth building at all. (d) whether any of it came from an account since DELETED, which is what makes the delete-and-resignup loop measurable rather than hypothetical. A READING GUIDE SITS UNDER IT, because the numbers alone do not imply the fix: (b) and (d) both zero means the hole is real but unexploited and a plain prior-trial record suffices; (b) above zero means it is already in use and the record has to SURVIVE deletion, which is exactly why AC2 asks for it to be keyed on something outliving the users row. TWO BUGS IN MY OWN SQL, both found by EXECUTING it rather than reading it, and both would have hurt the operator rather than me. (1) I wrote subscription_status NOT IN (..., 'incomplete'). There is no 'incomplete' - the enum is none/trialing/active/past_due/paused/canceled/comp - so on prod that is 22P02 and, under ON_ERROR_STOP, it ABORTS THE WHOLE SESSION partway through, taking the other eighteen sections with it. That is precisely the failure mode this file's own header says it exists to prevent. Rewritten to name the PAID statuses positively (active, comp), which is also the safer shape: an exclusion list silently counts any status added later as a conversion. (2) account_deletion_log records requested_at, not deleted_at. THE REPO'S OWN GUARD CAUGHT A THIRD THING I HAD NOT THOUGHT ABOUT: src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts failed because prod-diagnostics-console.sql - the meta-command-free copy for the Supabase SQL editor - was out of sync. Regenerated with scripts/gen-console-diagnostics.mjs and executed separately; both files now run to completion. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by review: the FULL file and the FULL console copy each ran against a throwaway local stack with ON_ERROR_STOP=1, both exit 0, zero ERROR lines, and §19 returned real rows against the seeded data (3 trial-window submissions across 2 accounts) - so the queries execute and shape correctly, not merely parse. prod-diagnostics-safety 9 passed / 0 failed. STILL OPEN: AC1 (the control, once the numbers are in), AC2 (a prior-trial record surviving deletion), AC3 (a trial-specific volume cap). NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS AC2, because there is a real tension nobody has written down yet: US-2005 PURGES email-keyed rows on account deletion, so a prior-trial record holding an address would be erased by the very deletion it exists to remember. The shape that resolves it already exists in this codebase - email_suppressions is deliberately EXEMPT from that purge on legitimate-interest grounds, for the same reason (forgetting a suppressed address harms the person the erasure protects). A salted hash rather than an address would be stronger still. Do not solve this by quietly adding a table to the purge-exempt list without saying why.

userStories.title: Batch grading re-charges on every retry, up to 5 times for one garment
userStories.description: lib/grading-batch-worker.ts:59-124 and :155-176: gradeBatchItem unconditionally INSERTs a new submission (:66-79) and calls runPaymentPrecedence (:97) on every invocation. runJob reclaims a stale job (:167) and calls it again with no reference to the submission a prior attempt already created and paid for. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS is 240s but a single image's worst case is already 3 attempts x 120s = 360s, so a job can be marked stale while the original pipeline is still running and may still write a valid grade. After GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS (15 min) the reclaim cron starts a second paid attempt. MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS is 5. Result: up to 5 credits debited for one payload, plus duplicate certificates.
acceptanceCriteria: The created submission_id is persisted on the job row BEFORE the charge, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission rather than creating a new one.

Payment is charged at most once per job row, enforced by an idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions (the column and partial unique index already exist at 00216_credit_ledger_admin.sql:35-42 and the grading path never sets it).
Item lease duration exceeds the true worst-case runtime (3 AI attempts x timeout + composite), or the work is made cancellable.
Regression test: a job forced through 3 reclaims debits exactly one credit and produces exactly one certificate.
Audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id, and refund affected customers.

OPERATOR: run section 20 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql and refund the customers it lists (AC5). Read-only. It returns the double-charge count, the refund list and duplicate CERTIFICATES separately, because refunding a credit does not withdraw a public certificate.
userStories.notes: [P0][Grading/Billing] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Highest-confidence money bug from the grading audit — the code path is described concretely and matches the reclaim-cron design. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — the double-charge is FIXED at the root (AC1, AC3, AC4); AC2 is defence-in-depth that now needs a migration, and AC5 is an operator action. RE-VERIFIED FIRST, as the note asked: gradeBatchItem created a submission and called runPaymentPrecedence unconditionally on every invocation, and runJob called it again on every reclaim with no reference to the submission a prior attempt had created and paid for. Confirmed the two windows that made it reachable rather than theoretical: GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS was 240s while one garment's worst case is (AI_MAX_RETRIES + 1) x AI_TIMEOUT_MS = 3 x 120s = 360s (ai-config.ts DEFAULTS), so the worker abandoned a pipeline that was still running; and GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS was 360s — EQUAL to that worst case — so the reclaim cron could pick up a job nobody had abandoned. With MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS at 5 that is up to 5 credits and 5 certificates for one garment. AC1 DONE: the submission id is written to the job row IMMEDIATELY after creation and BEFORE any money moves, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission instead of creating another. The ordering is the point — writing it after the charge would leave exactly the window this story is about; writing it before means a container death mid-flight leaves an UNPAID submission, which the resume path declines and starts clean, costing nothing. The fix is deliberately NOT a smarter charge: payment is per-submission, so resuming skips the charge BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard someone has to remember. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/paid-submission.ts holds isPaidSubmissionStatus as its own pure module — it is the hinge the whole fix turns on and keeping it out of the worker means it can be tested without booting the grading pipeline. It fails CLOSED on unknown/NULL/unpaid, and the asymmetry is the reason: a false negative re-creates a submission nobody paid for (free), a false positive skips a real charge or resumes a row we do not own. The paid values are the three grade-billing.ts actually writes — included, credits, paid_stripe — read off the source, not guessed. The resume path also re-stamps status=processing (tenant-scoped, mirroring the charging chokepoint's own .eq(user_id)) and records the API usage the abandoned attempt never got to record, exactly once. AC3 DONE: both windows are now DERIVED from the AI budget instead of written down beside it, because two hardcoded numbers that must track a third are two numbers that drift — which is precisely how the lease ended up shorter than the work it was leasing. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS = (getAiMaxRetries()+1) * getAiTimeoutMs() + 90s composite headroom (450s at current defaults, up from 240s); GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS = 1.5x the lease (675s, up from 360s) so a merely-slow worker is never mistaken for a dead one; GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS is floored above the job window so the batch sweeper cannot fire before its jobs are even reclaimable. The pre-existing assertion (timeout < stale) in grading-batch_test.ts still holds. AC4 DONE: NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/grading-batch-recharge_test.ts, 6 Deno cases pinning the lease-exceeds-worst-case relationship, the stale margin, the sweeper ordering, the derivation arithmetic (asserted rather than the literal, so raising AI_TIMEOUT_MS keeps it green), and both directions of the paid-status rule. VERIFIED: 20 assertions run against the esbuild-compiled paid-submission module plus the timing arithmetic reproduced independently (old lease 240000 confirmed BELOW the 360000 worst case); all four changed edge files parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: (AC2) the idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions. The column and partial unique index exist (00216:35-42) but the credit debit goes through the debit_grade_credits RPC, so threading a key needs a FUNCTION SIGNATURE CHANGE — a migration, which cannot be pushed from this host under the held-migration rule. It is defence-in-depth behind the root fix, not the fix itself. (AC5) audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers — an operator action; the query is: grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. | [2026-08-01] Migration status correction: 00508 and 00509 were applied to prod on 2026-08-01 (operator-confirmed), and everything else this note calls HELD is already on origin/main. Nothing here is holding the branch. | AC2 DONE 2026-08-03, migration 00516 (HELD). The note above said this needed a function signature change and so a migration, and that is exactly what it took. debit_grade_credits gains a TRAILING p_idempotency_key defaulting to NULL, so every existing 4-arg caller is untouched; the old 4-arg overload is DROPPED in the same file, because leaving it would let those callers silently keep resolving to the pre-idempotency body. When a key is supplied and a ledger row already carries it the function debits nothing and returns the current balance — returning rather than raising on purpose, since the caller intent (this submission is paid for) is already satisfied and an error would make a harmless retry look like a billing failure and push the caller into a checkout it does not need. The edge passes grade-batch-job:{jobId}, keyed on the JOB rather than the submission because the job is what a reclaim re-runs. VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, not by inspection: applied to the local stack and exercised in a rolled-back transaction — the same key three times debits ONCE (10 -> 7 -> 7 -> 7, exactly one ledger row), a different key debits normally, and a call with no key debits every time, which is the assertion that protects the existing callers. Storage needed no migration: 00216 already had the column and its partial unique index, unused. REMAINING: AC5 only — audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers. That is an operator action; the query is grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. Edge suite 5155/0. | 2026-08-09 STATUS CORRECTION — THE 2026-08-03 SEGMENT'S 'migration 00516 (HELD)' IS STALE. 00516 is on origin/main (93f8a4b3) and applied; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md's held list is 00564-00572 and names none of this story's migrations. Nothing here is blocked on a frozen branch. HOW THIS HID FROM THE GUARD, which is the part worth keeping: prd-lint DOES warn about a stale HELD claim, and it was silent on this story because it tested the whole notes string for a correction — and an EARLIER segment already carried one. So the first correction a story ever records suppressed the warning permanently, including for a HELD claim written after it. Fixed today: the check now resolves by SEGMENT ORDER, mirroring findUnresolvedDeferrals which already did, because notes are append-only and only a correction at or after the LAST held claim can be talking about it. That one change surfaced three hidden cases at once (this story, US-1880 and US-1996). WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is unchanged and is not a migration question: AC5 only — audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers. AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 shipped. | 2026-08-15 AC5 IS NOW ONE PASTE AWAY, and that is all this pass changes - the audit still has to be RUN, so the story stays open. scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql gains §20 (regenerated into the console variant), four read-only queries: (a) per batch, jobs versus grade_debit rows inside its window, padded 30 minutes past updated_at because the reclaim is a */5 cron and a resumed attempt settles after the batch row last moved; (b) the refund list, one row per affected customer with credits owed and the date range; (c) duplicate CERTIFICATES from the same bug, counted separately because refunding a credit does not withdraw a public certificate and two certificates for one garment is a trust problem rather than a billing one; (d) whether the fix is holding, keyed on idempotency_key LIKE 'grade-batch-job:%' - and the note that a newest_unkeyed later than newest_keyed means some grading path still charges outside the chokepoint. THE KEY IS WHAT MADE THE AUDIT WRITABLE: runPaymentPrecedence is called with 'grade-batch-job:<jobId>' (grading-batch-worker.ts:161-166), so a NULL idempotency_key on a batch-era debit is a pre-fix charge, which is a cleaner fingerprint than trying to match payloads. Pre-fix job rows also never set submission_id, so the queries deliberately join by user plus time window rather than through a link those rows do not have. NOT EXECUTED: Docker is down on this box so there is no local Postgres to run it against, and nothing here has touched prod. Structurally checked instead - 13 statements across §20-§22, every one balanced and every one a SELECT or WITH, and src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts stays 9/9 green, which is what pins the no-write property.

userStories.title: The golden-set eval gate never runs in CI and the live prompt versions have no DB row
userStories.description: Two compounding problems. (1) The grading eval appears in none of the 16 files in .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json. The only eval task there is the agent eval, and CI does not call that either. No build, deploy or PR is blocked by golden-set accuracy. runScheduledEval raises alerts and blocks nothing. (2) The code defaults are per_image_v5 and composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63) but the only grading seed migration (00050_grading_self_improvement.sql:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 and composite_v2, and no migration sets is_active. So the live prompts have no row and were never evaluated. (3) The repo contains no golden-set data at all: zero INSERTs into grading_eval_cases, no seed, no fixture. A fresh database has an empty golden set; runEval throws on empty but grading-monitor.ts:287-294 treats zero cases as a clean skip, so an empty set is silent. Net effect: editing prompt text in ai-grading.ts ships straight to customers without ever touching an eval.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm first, against prod, whether grading_eval_cases has any rows and which ai_prompt_versions rows are active. Record the answer in the story before building.
The golden-set eval runs in CI and fails the build on regression, or the reason it cannot is written down.
Every prompt version the code can use has a DB row with eval results and qualified_model, including the code defaults.
An empty golden set is treated as a hard failure, not a clean skip.
Prompt text in ai-grading.ts cannot ship without a corresponding evaluated version — enforced by a test, not by convention.
EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 (grading-eval.ts:26-29) is reconsidered: on a 1.0-10.0 scale a prompt can be a full grade point off on average and pass.

OPERATOR: two reads settle AC1 and size AC3. §15 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql returns golden-set size and which ai_prompt_versions rows are active with what qualified_model. An EMPTY set is the finding, not a null result: it means the accuracy gate has never run and cannot.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Lifecycle] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. The prompt-lifecycle doc reads as if a pipeline gate exists. It does not. Either add one or correct the doc. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — ALL FOUR factual claims independently RE-VERIFIED and TRUE; AC4 and AC5 shipped, the doc corrected; AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6 need prod access or a migration and are recorded with why. VERIFICATION (mechanical, not by reading the cited lines): (1) NO CI GATE — the golden-set eval appears in no file under .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json; the only match anywhere in those trees is a mention in scripts/ralph/progress.txt. Nothing blocks a build, PR or deploy on grading accuracy. (2) THE LIVE PROMPTS HAVE NO ROW — code defaults are per_image_v5 / composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63); the sole seed migration (00050:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 / composite_v2 with is_active false. Scanned EVERY migration touching ai_prompt_versions: neither v5 nor v4 appears. (3) ZERO GOLDEN-SET DATA — no INSERT into grading_eval_cases in any migration. A fresh database starts with an empty set. (4) EMPTY WAS SILENT — grading-monitor.ts runScheduledEval returned skipped_reason "no active eval cases" and moved on. AC4 DONE, and the reasoning matters: an empty set is the accuracy gate being SWITCHED OFF, not "nothing to check". With no cases the eval never runs, so eval_passed is null rather than false and NO other rule in evaluateAlerts fires — the state where no prompt has ever been evaluated, and none can be, produced complete silence from the only component whose job is to notice. evaluateAlerts now raises golden_set_empty at CRITICAL. Deliberately an ALERT rather than a thrown error: throwing would break the monitor cron on a fresh deploy, trading a silent gap for a noisy one and teaching operators to ignore the job. The message names the remedy AND the anti-remedy ("never synthetic") because an operator reading "the set is empty" under pressure will reach for fabricated cases, which makes every future eval meaningless while reading green. Kept DISTINCT from golden_set_shrank: a 40→0 set is both, and collapsing them loses the deliberate-abuse signal US-2037 exists for. AC5 DONE as a PIN rather than a fix, since seeding rows is a migration this host cannot push: a new case reads both prompt-version constants, scans every migration that touches ai_prompt_versions, and asserts the unseeded set equals KNOWN_UNSEEDED_PROMPT_VERSIONS exactly — both ways. So a FURTHER version bump fails until its author seeds a row or amends the declaration, and seeding one without amending also fails. That converts "nobody noticed for four versions" into "you cannot bump a version without deciding". DOC CORRECTED (the story's own closing note asked for exactly this): .claude/skills/grading-engine/references/prompt-lifecycle.md read as if a pipeline gate existed. It now opens with what the gate does NOT cover — no CI gate, code defaults with no DB row — while stating clearly that the part which IS real (activation and canary refusing an un-evaled version, via checkPromptServingEligibility, US-2300) applies only to versions that go through a DB row. VERIFIED: 4 alert assertions plus the seeding scan run against the real tree in Node (no deno on this host) — the scan reports exactly composite_v4 and per_image_v5 as unseeded, matching the declaration; grading-monitor.ts and the test parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: AC1 (confirm against prod what grading_eval_cases holds and which ai_prompt_versions are active) — operator only, and it should be done BEFORE the rest, as the AC says. AC3 (seed rows for the code defaults) — a migration, push-blocked here. AC2 (eval in CI) — depends on AC1/AC3: a CI eval against an empty golden set would be theatre, and the golden set must grow from REAL human-corrected grades, never fabricated ones, so it cannot be seeded from this host either. AC6 (EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 lets a prompt be a full grade point off on a 1-10 scale and still pass) — a product judgement about acceptable error, with a real cost either way, and it belongs to the owner rather than to a sandbox. | 2026-08-15 AC2 AND AC6 CLOSED; AC1/AC3 remain and are operator/migration work. AC6 DECIDED (owner): EVAL_MAX_MAE default drops from 1.0 to 0.5. On a 1.0-10.0 scale rounded to 0.1, a mean absolute error of a full point is an entire grade - the gap between Excellent and Good - so a candidate prompt could be that wrong on average and still be promoted, on the one number the product sells. 0.5 is one tier rather than two and is still generous. 0.3 was offered and refused FOR NOW with a reason: it is close to the disagreement between two human experts, and the golden set is not yet large enough to tell a real regression from an unrepresentative sample. THIS CHANGES NO GRADE - it decides only what may be ACTIVATED - and the env override means a deliberate exception is one variable while the silent default is the strict one. NOTE THE NUMBER IS PUBLISHED: evalThresholds() feeds accuracy-tracking.ts and src/pages/marketing/transparency.tsx renders it as a promise to buyers, so this tightens a public claim as well as the gate. The page reads it from the code, so nothing was hardcoded and nothing else needed editing - checked rather than assumed. AC2 CLOSED VIA ITS SECOND BRANCH ('or the reason it cannot is written down'), in NEW vault/20-domain/grading-eval-gate.md, and the reason is not 'nobody got to it': every run spends real vision calls on a set that must GROW to stay meaningful, so a per-PR gate scales its bill with the thing that makes it worth having; grading is not temperature-pinned on the default model (US-2035) so the same prompt against the same case moves between runs, and a build gate that fails on noise gets bypassed - a lesson this repo has already written down twice (db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs is advisory for exactly this, and US-1927 records a permanently-red guard being switched off); and the golden set cannot be faked to make CI green, because a synthetic set turns the gate into a test of the fixture. WHAT GATES INSTEAD IS STRONGER: activation. A version cannot go active without a passing eval recorded against it, so the check sits where the change would reach a CUSTOMER rather than where it reaches main. VERIFIED: 4 new cases in src/tests/grading-eval-gate_test.ts including junk/zero/negative overrides falling back to the strict default, and one asserting the agreement floor did NOT move so a later edit cannot take the other half of the gate with it. Sabotage-verified by restoring 1.0, which reddened two cases. deno check + lint clean, tsc -b clean, vault:lint strict clean at 179 notes.

userStories.title: FlipDesk grading drops the label photo the pipeline still blocks on
userStories.description: flipdesk-grading.ts:83 sets REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES to front and back only, with a comment claiming the tag shot is covered by the sub-0.75 review path. That premise is false: lib/image-quality.ts:68 still lists label as required with severity 'block' and there is no carve-out at its only call site (grading-pipeline.ts:1859). A FlipDesk item with no tag photo is charged (flipdesk-grading.ts:591), runs one Claude Vision call per image, then abstains to needs_photos and refunds. Money returns, AI spend burns every time, seller round-trips. iOS and Android both use this path with no local check.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide: either FlipDesk requires the label photo, or image-quality gets an explicit FlipDesk carve-out. Record which and why.
The two requirement lists cannot disagree — one source, or a test that asserts they match.
The client validates before upload so the seller is told up front, not after a round trip.
Measure how often this fires today (submissions ending needs_photos with a refund) to size the wasted AI spend.

OPERATOR: run §26 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql (AC4). It counts FlipDesk grading rows that ended in needs_photos per month and the refunds that followed. Read the two together: rows with no matching refunds is a WORSE finding than the one this AC asked about, because the seller then paid for a grade they never got.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Grading] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | 2026-08-03 AC1, AC2, AC3 DONE. AC4 is a prod query and stays open as the operator half. VERIFIED THE AUDIT FIRST, as its note asked, and every claim held. AC1 DECISION (owner, via AskUserQuestion): FLIPDESK REQUIRES THE TAG PHOTO. THE OLD COMMENT'S PREMISE WAS FALSE, which is what made this worth asking about rather than assuming: flipdesk-grading said front+back were enough because 'the <0.75 → human-review path already covers the weaker-signal case'. image-quality.ts lists `label` in REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES at severity `block`, and grading-pipeline.ts applies it at Step 4b — BEFORE any confidence scoring. The review path it named never executed. So a FlipDesk item with no tag was charged (flipdesk-grading.ts runPaymentPrecedence), ran ONE CLAUDE VISION CALL PER IMAGE, abstained to needs_photos, and was refunded. The money came back and the AI spend did not, every time, and the seller round-tripped to be told something we could have said up front. Requiring it is therefore strictly better for the SAME seller the old comment was written to protect. THE OTHER OPTIONS AND WHY NOT: loosening image-quality would have changed grading for every WEB submission too (more human review, a global product change for a FlipDesk bug); a FlipDesk-only carve-out would have frozen two deliberately-different paths forever. Both were offered to the owner with their costs. ⚠ LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY: the old comment's concern is real — some garments (Lululemon cut size labels, tagless resale) genuinely have no readable tag. That is a product question about what those sellers photograph, and it is recorded at the call site rather than settled by loosening a grading gate. AC2 DONE BY DERIVATION, not by matching two literals: REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES is now REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES.map(gradingImageTypeToPhotoType), so the lists cannot drift apart again. Two tests pin the derivation and the round trip — a wrong entry in the inverse map would make them agree on paper while asking the seller for a photo type the UI cannot produce. A REAL BUG THE TEST CAUGHT, and it would have been a prod outage rather than a wrong answer: REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES is built at MODULE LOAD, and I first placed the GRADING_TO_PHOTO_TYPE map below it. A function declaration hoists; the `const` it reads does not, so the module threw ReferenceError at import and the edge would not have booted. The map is now above its use with that reason written next to it. AC3 DONE: the client already had a readiness mirror (src/lib/grading-readiness.ts) driving the Submit card live, so the seller is told before paying. THE TRAP IN THE CLIENT HALF: REQUIRED_PHOTO_TYPES was doing DOUBLE DUTY — it gates 'may this item advance to photographed and be listed?' AND fed the grading readiness preview. Adding `tag` to it would have blocked the LISTING pipeline for every tagless garment, which nobody asked for and is a different product decision. Added a SEPARATE REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES (front, back, tag); the listing list is unchanged, and a test asserts the two stay different. THE SHARED FIXTURE (src/test/fixtures/grading-readiness-cases.json, asserted by BOTH suites) was regenerated from the rules rather than hand-edited — 13 cases each needing a blocker string and a missingPhotos list is where a typo becomes a cross-project contract both sides then agree on. But a straight recompute BROKE WHAT THE CASES WERE FOR: 'fully ready' had no tag, so it stopped being ready and every case collapsed onto the same missing-tag blocker, testing nothing. Inputs were patched to preserve each case's intent, the case named 'tag photo does not satisfy anything' was renamed (it is no longer true), and a 'missing tag only' case was added for the new rule — 14 total. Also fixed a latent wrong-name in the edge parity test: it passed the GRADING type `label` where the FlipDesk readiness function takes `tag`. It passed either way while neither was required. AC4 REMAINS (operator): count submissions ending needs_photos with a refund, to size the wasted AI spend. It belongs with the other prod diagnostics. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5358 passed / 0 failed, deno check + lint clean across 1339 files, tsc -b clean, web readiness + hooks suites 112 passed. | 2026-08-15 AC4 IS NOW PART OF THE ONE-PASTE FILE. §26 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql asks it in two halves: (a) flipdesk_grading_submissions rows that ended in needs_photos, by month, and (b) the refunds that followed, joined through submission_id - the only link between the FlipDesk bridge row and the credit ledger. Counts and dates only, no ids. THE READING GUIDE MATTERS MORE THAN THE QUERY: (a) non-empty with (b) empty is a WORSE finding than the one this AC asked about, because it means the abstention happened and the refund did not, so the seller paid for a grade they never received. Both empty closes AC4 at zero. And the AI spend itself is NOT recoverable from either number - images-per-submission is the multiplier and these rows do not store it, so the honest answer is a count of occurrences, not a dollar figure. COLUMN NAMES VERIFIED AGAINST THE MIGRATION CORPUS, not assumed: the safety test's required-columns list now covers flipdesk_grading_submissions (status, submission_id, created_at) and grade_credit_transactions (reason, submission_id, delta, created_at), so a rename on either side of that join fails in CI rather than on the operator's prod session. Sabotage-verified by typoing created_at, which reddened it naming the pair. The reason value is 'refund', from 00037's CHECK constraint, read rather than guessed.

userStories.title: Nothing in version control creates or verifies the 73 production cron schedules
userStories.description: There is no scheduling mechanism in the repo. docker-compose.coolify.yml has no cron, sidecar or command (only the healthcheck at lines 70-79); same for the other compose files. .github/workflows has zero /api/jobs references and its only three schedule blocks are lighthouse, staging-smoke and an uptime probe. pg_cron is unused (zero cron.schedule across all 506 migrations). Cloudflare is unused (no crons in wrangler.toml, no scheduled handler in functions/). The sole mechanism is 73 hand-typed Coolify UI scheduled tasks documented in COOLIFY.md:222-255 and CRON_SETUP.md. Nothing creates, applies or verifies them. The only runtime check is cron-fleet-health, which is itself one of the 73 hand-entered tasks — if the operator never created it, nothing alerts about anything.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the mechanism: schedules-as-code (compose sidecar, pg_cron, or a scheduler service) or a verified manifest. Record the decision.
At minimum: an artifact in the repo listing every expected schedule, and a job that compares it to what actually ran and alerts on absence.
Confirm cron-fleet-health itself is scheduled in prod and that its alerts reach a human.

Confirm ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email are set in prod system_settings — both default to empty string (ops-events.ts:78-79), in which case the entire alert path terminates in an admin screen nobody is watching.

OPERATOR: two confirmations against prod (AC3, AC4). (a) Is cron-fleet-health itself a Coolify Scheduled Task, and does its CRITICAL ops event actually reach a human? A watcher nobody scheduled is the joke version of this story. (b) Run the first query of section 11 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql: both ops_alert rows EXIST (owner confirmed 2026-08-03), but a present row with an EMPTY value ends the entire alert path in an admin screen nobody is watching, and that is what section 11 reports.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Cron] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Root cause behind the three dead schedules. Start with the prod verification, not the build. | 2026-08-02 VERIFIED, with two counts corrected. The central claim is TRUE and I checked each half rather than the summary. NO pg_cron: grep for cron.schedule / pg_cron across every file in supabase/migrations returns nothing. NO scheduler in compose: services/edge-functions/docker-compose.coolify.yml contains only a healthcheck block and traefik labels — no cron, no sidecar, no command, no entrypoint; same for docker-compose.yml, .dev.yml and .staging.yml. NO Cloudflare crons: wrangler.toml has no triggers section and no cron key, and nothing under functions/ exports a scheduled handler. NO CI scheduling: zero references to api/jobs anywhere in .github/workflows. So the sole mechanism really is hand-typed Coolify UI tasks, and the repo has no way to create, apply or verify them. CORRECTION 1: the story says the workflows have three schedule blocks (lighthouse, staging-smoke, uptime). There are FOUR — secret-scan-history.yml also runs on a schedule. Immaterial to the conclusion, but the story should not be quoted as an inventory. CORRECTION 2: the count 73 is stale. CRON_REGISTRY now holds 74 entries — 67 recorded:true and 7 recorded:false — of which 2 are marked oneOff. The number moves whenever a job is added, which is itself an argument for AC2's manifest-and-compare over any figure written into prose. CONFIRMED AND WORTH THE EMPHASIS THE STORY GIVES IT: cron-fleet-health is itself entry number N of the same hand-entered list, so if the operator never created that one Coolify task, nothing in the system alerts about anything — the watcher and the watched share a single point of failure. AC4 CONFIRMED AT THE CODE LEVEL: ops-events.ts reads ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email via getSetting with an empty-string default for both, so an unconfigured prod terminates the entire alert path in an admin screen. WHAT I CANNOT DO FROM HERE, and it is the half the story says to start with: AC3 and AC4 both require PROD state — whether the cron-fleet-health task exists in the Coolify UI, and whether those two system_settings rows are non-empty in production. This host has no prod access. Those two are operator checks, not agent work, and should be split out so the buildable half (AC1/AC2, schedules-as-code or a verified manifest) is not blocked behind them. RELATED, same day: US-2312 made every recorded cron run report body-level failures and populate rows_processed, and US-2318's notes measured that the admin dashboard's 2000-row window covers only ~14.2 hours at the current fleet cadence — so the ledger this story would compare a manifest against is more trustworthy than it was, but the screen reading it still hides daily jobs. | 2026-08-03 AC1 DECIDED and AC2 CLOSED. AC3 and AC4 are prod checks this host cannot make and stay open as the operator half — which is what the 2026-08-02 pass asked for. AC2 WAS MOSTLY ALREADY BUILT, and saying so is the honest half of this. The story asks for 'an artifact in the repo listing every expected schedule, and a job that compares it to what actually ran and alerts on absence'. CRON_REGISTRY is that artifact (74 entries, each with a schedule and an endpoint), lib/cron-fleet-governance.ts is that comparison — its own header calls itself 'the diff between the SCHEDULE (CRON_REGISTRY) and REALITY (cron_runs)' — and US-2004's routes/jobs-cron-fleet.ts is the alert. All three predate this story. SO THE REAL HOLE IS THE ONE THE STORY EMPHASISED and nothing had addressed: cron-fleet-health is itself entry N of the same hand-typed Coolify list. If the operator never created that one task, or deleted it, or typo'd its secret, then nothing in the system alerts about anything — and the silence is indistinguishable from health. The watcher and the watched share one point of failure, which means the alerting is not merely unverified, it is unverifiABLE from inside. AC1 DECIDED, and scoped rather than sweeping: THE SCHEDULES STAY IN COOLIFY, EXCEPT ONE. Moving 74 tasks into a compose sidecar or pg_cron is a migration with its own failure modes, and the diff-against-reality job already covers a missing task ONCE SOMEONE IS WATCHING. What moves to schedules-as-code is exactly the job whose absence is silent by construction. NEW .github/workflows/cron-fleet-watchdog.yml invokes /api/jobs/cron-fleet-health every 6 hours from GitHub-hosted runners — infrastructure that cannot fail the way Coolify does. If the Coolify task exists these ticks are near-no-ops (the job takes a lock); if it does not, the alarm stays connected. TWO DELIBERATE DESIGN CHOICES. It SKIPS, exit 0, when EDGE_JOB_SECRET is unset — a watchdog that cries wolf every six hours because nobody configured it gets muted, and a muted watchdog is worse than none. And it checks the BODY as well as the status, because this endpoint can answer 200 with an error payload and this is the one job where a green-looking check that proves nothing is exactly the failure being fixed. NEW src/tests/cron-fleet-watchdog_test.ts, 6 cases, pinning the two halves agreeing: the workflow is SCHEDULED (a workflow_dispatch-only file would look like coverage and provide none), it calls the endpoint the REGISTRY declares, it sends the header requireJobSecret reads, the unset-secret branch exits 0, the body is inspected, and every registry entry still carries a schedule and an endpoint. TWO WEAKNESSES IN MY OWN GUARD, both found by MUTATION rather than by reading, and both the same family. (1) The endpoint assertion searched the whole file — but the workflow names that endpoint in its header comment and its step name too, so it would have been satisfied by PROSE while the actual request drifted. It matches the curl line now. That is the eighth time a guard here has been confused by a comment. (2) Worse, the fixed version used `includes`, and '/api/jobs/cron-fleet-healthz' CONTAINS '/api/jobs/cron-fleet-health' — so a renamed route still passed. It matches with the closing quote now, so the path has to end where the registry says it ends. A substring check on a path is a prefix check, and prefix checks wave through exactly the rename they exist to catch. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS: the schedule removed, the endpoint drifted, the auth header changed, the unset-secret branch made to fail, the body check deleted, and a registry entry stripped of its endpoint. Each reddened on its own case — two of them only after the guard itself was fixed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE STORY carried forward from 2026-08-02 and still true: there are FOUR scheduled workflows, not three, and the fleet is 74 entries, not 73 — which is itself the argument for a manifest over a number in prose. REMAINING (operator, both need prod): AC3 — confirm the cron-fleet-health task actually exists in the Coolify UI and that its alerts reach a human. The new watchdog reduces the cost of getting this wrong but does not answer it. AC4 — confirm ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email are non-empty in prod system_settings; both default to empty string, in which case the entire alert path terminates in an admin screen nobody is watching, and every alert this story is about would be raised into a void. VERIFIED: deno lint clean across 1334 files, full edge suite 5300 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-03: this story's last open AC is now answerable by scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, which the operator runs in ONE psql session alongside the other blocked stories. Read-only, verified by executing against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 — so it cannot fail the operator's session on a wrong column name, which is the failure mode that makes someone distrust the whole file. §11 reports whether ops_alert_webhook_url and ops_alert_email are configured — PRESENCE and length only, never the value, since a webhook URL is a capability rather than a setting. A MISSING ROW is reported separately from an empty one, because ops-events.ts falls back to "" for both and the two look identical from the code's side. If they are unset, every alert this story is about is raised into a void, including the cron-fleet-stalled one. | PROD ANSWER 2026-08-03 (owner ran scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql). §11's second query returned webhook_row_present 1 and email_row_present 1, so both ops_alert settings rows EXIST. STILL MISSING: the first query of §11, which reports whether each row's value is actually non-empty. A present row with an empty value behaves identically to a missing one — ops-events.ts falls back to '' either way — so row presence alone does not answer AC4. That is the one number left on this story. | 2026-08-15 AC1 and AC2 CLOSED; AC3 and AC4 are operator confirmations and are now declared as one. AC1 asked for a DECISION recorded, and it had been made implicitly and never written down: NEW vault/10-ops/cron-schedule-governance.md records a verified manifest rather than schedules-as-code, with the three reasons the alternatives were refused — pg_cron would make the database hold a credential for the API in front of it; a sidecar is a second thing that can be down with no way to alert about its own absence, which is this story's failure moved one layer along; and Coolify tasks already survive a redeploy because they live on the service rather than in the image. It also states the COST plainly: creating a schedule stays a manual step, so a new cron can be merged and never installed, and that is exactly why the drift check is not optional. AC2 was already satisfied and is now written down as such: CRON_REGISTRY is the artifact, scripts/render-cron-docs.ts generates the tables in COOLIFY.md and the launch checklist with a drift test that fails when they diverge, and jobs-cron-fleet.ts compares expected ticks to the cron_runs ledger hourly. THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES A MANIFEST SUFFICIENT, and it is worth stating because it is not obvious: detectMissedTicks computes expected slots from the SCHEDULE rather than from prior runs, so a task that was never created in Coolify reads as stalled from its first elapsed slot. Without that, a never-installed job would be indistinguishable from a job with nothing to do. The note also carries the honest limits: the check cannot see an EXTRA Coolify task hitting an endpoint the registry does not know about, and five registry entries sit outside the ledger (US-2616/US-2617) and are named in the fleet report rather than silently excluded.

userStories.title: Concurrent token refresh disconnects sellers on providers that rotate refresh tokens
userStories.description: No advisory lock, mutex or single-flight guard exists in any token path (no pg_advisory, no FOR UPDATE, no in-flight promise map). The read-modify-write is check expiry, refresh, persist. Four connectors do this and all four persist a rotated refresh token when the provider sends one, which proves rotation is expected: etsy-client.ts:392-396, whatnot-client.ts:347-350, depop-client.ts, flipdesk-google.ts:353-355. Scenario (Etsy, 1-hour tokens): a user opens the Marketplaces page while the sync cron fires; both see expiresAt - now < 60s (etsy-client.ts:368) and POST the same refresh token; Etsy rotates and invalidates the old one on first use; the second call gets 400 invalid_grant; isPermanentEtsyAuthFailure classifies 400 as PERMANENT (:243) so the handler sets is_active:false and stores a reconnect message (:410-416). The user is force-disconnected by a race, not a revocation. eBay is not exposed (its refresh token is not rotated).
acceptanceCriteria: A per-connection advisory lock (keyed on connection id) around refresh, so concurrent callers wait rather than racing.
invalid_grant immediately after a successful sibling refresh is treated as transient (re-read the row and retry once) rather than permanent.

refreshExpiringEtsyConnections (etsy-client.ts:467) scans on a 24-hour horizon but delegates to getEtsyAccessToken which only refreshes inside a 60-second window, so the cron decrypts every active connection every run and proactively refreshes nothing. Fix or delete it.
Confirm whether Etsy/Depop/Google actually invalidate the old token on rotation — that sets the real severity.
Audit prod for connections deactivated with an invalid_grant refresh_error and offer affected sellers a reconnect.

OPERATOR: ask Etsy, Depop and Whatnot whether they invalidate the OLD refresh token on rotation (AC4). This sets SEVERITY, not correctness - siblingRefreshWon already makes the race survivable either way. AC5 is answered: prod section 13 returned no rows, so the race never disconnected a seller.
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Auth] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE for all three affected connectors. AC4 needs a partner answer and AC5 needs prod; both are named below with what to ask. THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT ON THE MECHANISM AND WRONG ON ONE CONNECTOR. Etsy, Whatnot and Depop all do read-expiry → refresh → persist with no coordination, all three persist a rotated refresh token when the provider sends one, and all three classify the loser's failure as PERMANENT — is_active false plus a reconnect message. eBay is genuinely not exposed (no rotation). But there is no flipdesk-google.ts in the repo and nothing under src/lib/google* stores refresh_token_encrypted, so the fourth connector the story names does not exist. Three, not four. AC2 IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIX AND IT WENT IN FIRST, because it makes the race SURVIVABLE rather than rarer. NEW lib/token-refresh-race.ts exports the pure siblingRefreshWon(before, after, now): before deactivating, each connector re-reads its own row, and if a sibling has stored a DIFFERENT and still-valid token then we lost a race rather than the grant — use their token, leave the connection active. It compares ciphertext, which is the right test even though a fresh IV means identical plaintext encrypts differently: the question is 'did this row change', and an unchanged row is byte-identical because nobody rewrote it. AC1 DONE as in-replica single-flight, and the cross-replica advisory lock the AC names was CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. try_acquire_job_lock (00094) would give one with no migration, but job_locks is the cron fleet's table — cron-fleet-governance reads it — and keying it per CONNECTION would put a row per seller per marketplace into a table that exists to describe scheduled jobs. A lock also only makes the race rarer, while AC2 makes it harmless. If duplicate refresh calls later show up as a quota problem, that is what the lock fixes, and it belongs on its own table. Recorded in the module header so the next reader sees a decision rather than an omission. The single-flight entry is deleted in a finally, so a REJECTED refresh is not cached — on these paths a shared rejection would turn one transient provider 503 into a deactivation for everyone waiting behind it. AC3 DONE, FIXED NOT DELETED, and it was worse than 'refreshes nothing': all THREE sweeps (not just Etsy's) select connections expiring within 24 HOURS and then called a getter that only refreshes inside 60 SECONDS. So every run decrypted every active connection and renewed none of them — a cron wearing the costume of a safety net. The getters now take refreshWithinMs (default 60s) and the sweeps pass their own horizon. The single-flight key deliberately IGNORES the threshold: a page load arriving mid-sweep inherits the freshly renewed token, and a sweep landing on a page load's still-valid token simply renews on the next tick. A NEGATIVE TEST THAT PROVED NOTHING, caught and fixed. The 'an unchanged row is not a sibling refresh' case used a 30-second expiry on both sides and stayed GREEN with the unchanged-row guard deleted — the freshness floor rejected it for an unrelated reason. The times are the test: the token now has HOURS left, which is the sweep's world, where refreshWithinMs is the 24-hour horizon and a proactive refresh can fail on a row nowhere near expiry. There the unchanged ciphertext is the ONLY thing between a dead grant and being called a race. NEW src/tests/token-refresh-race_test.ts, 10 cases: six behavioural on the pure helper and the single-flight (including different connections not collapsing, and a rejection not being cached), and four on the wiring — all three connectors wired with eBay's absence ENUMERATED as a decision, the race check running BEFORE the deactivating update by index, and the sweep passing its horizon AND the getter honouring it. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS, each reddening on its own case: the unchanged-row guard removed, the freshness floor removed, the in-flight entry left behind, a connector losing single-flight, a sweep reverting to the 60s window, and the race check physically moved below the deactivating update. REMAINING. AC4: confirm Etsy/Depop/Whatnot actually invalidate the old refresh token on rotation. That sets severity, not correctness — the fix is right either way — so it is a documentation question, not a blocker. AC5: audit prod for connections with is_active=false and a refresh_error matching the reconnect message, and offer those sellers a reconnect. That needs the prod session and is a candidate for scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql on the next pass. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1328 files, full edge suite 5267 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-03: this story's last open AC is now answerable by scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, which the operator runs in ONE psql session alongside the other blocked stories. userStories.title: Marketplace webhooks have no freshness window and one debug flag disables all four
userStories.description: Verification itself is correct everywhere — all four receivers read the raw body, verify before any DB write, fail closed when the secret is missing, and use constant-time comparison (or asymmetric verify for eBay). Three residual gaps. (A) isDebugAllowed('WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG') is checked at flipdesk-webhooks.ts:123, :201, :493, :1229 and skips the whole verify block when true; lib/env.ts:82-85 returns false in production and edgeEnv() defaults to 'production' when unset, so a bare container fails closed — but any staging or preview with EDGE_ENV non-production and the flag on accepts unsigned requests on the account-deletion path (mass seller disconnect) and logs headers plus 2KB of body verbatim. (B) No replay or freshness check anywhere. All four rely on event-id dedupe which is skipped when the provider's id header is absent (:756, :389, :512) and FAILS OPEN on a DB error (:770, :400, :595, :1290). eBay's notification.publishDate is declared in the type at :744-745 and never read; Shopify's X-Shopify-Triggered-At is never read. (C) fetchPublicKeyMaterial (ebay-notification-verify.ts:135-154) does getAppAccessToken plus a call to eBay's public_key/{kid} for any attacker-supplied kid, with no timeout and no negative cache (keyCache at :92 stores only successes), bounded only by the 600/60s limiter at main.ts:1025 — so an attacker can drive 600 unauthenticated outbound eBay calls per minute per replica and burn the app's API quota.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod. If it does, this is live.
A timestamp freshness window (+/- 5 min) on the eBay and Shopify receivers using the headers already sent.
Dedupe fails CLOSED on a DB error rather than open.
Negative cache plus a timeout on the eBay public-key fetch.

Depop's header names (x-depop-signature / x-depop-hmac-sha256 at :495-496, x-depop-webhook-id / x-depop-delivery-id at :512) are unconfirmed guesses. The signature failure mode is safe (401) but the dedupe failure mode is SILENT — if Depop uses neither header, every delivery is reprocessed with no error. Confirm and narrow, including the hex-or-base64 hedge at depop-api.ts:488-491.

OPERATOR: two confirmations that cannot be made from here (AC1, AC5). (a) In staging, check EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod - if it does, the unsigned-request path is live against real seller connections. (b) Get Depop's actual webhook documentation: the header names in the receiver (x-depop-signature / x-depop-hmac-sha256, x-depop-webhook-id / x-depop-delivery-id) are GUESSES, and the dedupe failure mode on a wrong guess is SILENT.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Webhooks] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Secrets at rest are CLEAN: crypto-aes.ts uses a fresh 96-bit IV per encryption, key from env never logged, and v2 binds user_id as GCM additionalData so a ciphertext copied to another tenant fails to decrypt. No plaintext tokens in any log path. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC2 and AC4 DONE. AC3 is PUSHED BACK ON with a reason (see below). AC1 and AC5 need an operator and a partner respectively. AC4 DONE, and it was the real one. fetchPublicKeyMaterial did getAppAccessToken plus a bare `fetch` — no deadline — to eBay's public_key/{kid} endpoint, with `kid` taken from the REQUEST'S OWN signature header, so an unauthenticated caller chose it. Only SUCCESSES were cached, so every request bearing a non-resolving kid produced a fresh token + a fresh outbound call, bounded only by the 600/60s limiter: 600 unauthenticated outbound eBay calls per minute per replica, burning the app's own quota, on requests that were going to be rejected anyway. Added a NEGATIVE cache (5-min TTL — short, because a kid can legitimately start resolving when eBay publishes a key, and a long negative cache would then reject genuine notifications until the process restarted) and a 5s timeout via fetchWithTimeout. The no-bare-fetch guard's declaration for that file went 1 -> 0, which is how I knew the change actually landed. AC2 DONE: NEW lib/webhook-freshness.ts, applied to the eBay and Shopify receivers using the timestamps both providers ALREADY SEND and neither receiver read — eBay's notification.publishDate (declared in the payload type and never touched) and Shopify's X-Shopify-Triggered-At. A signature proves the provider signed a payload; it does not prove the payload is recent, and a captured delivery stays validly signed forever. TWO ASYMMETRIES, deliberate and both tested. ABSENT timestamp -> ACCEPT: a provider renaming a header or shipping a topic without the field must not become an outage on a path we do not control, and freshness is a SECOND line after the signature. PRESENT but unparseable -> REJECT: that is not an omission, it is a value that does not mean what it claims, which is the shape a forged replay has. The window is symmetric because provider clock skew runs both ways and a one-sided window rejects every delivery from a clock running fast — indistinguishable from an outage. The eBay check sits in the ROUTE, not in processEbayWebhookEvent: that function runs detached from the response, so a rejection there could not produce a status and would be indistinguishable from success to the caller. Both checks run AFTER signature verification so an unsigned request is still reported as unsigned rather than as stale. A TEST OF MINE WAS WRONG BEFORE THE CODE WAS: I asserted '0000' is unparseable. Date.parse accepts it as year zero, so it is a valid-but-ancient timestamp and is caught by the staleness branch instead. Rejected either way, but via the honest reason — the test now asserts that explicitly rather than being loosened. AC3 — I AM NOT IMPLEMENTING THIS AS WRITTEN, and the reason should be decided rather than inherited. The AC says dedupe should fail CLOSED on a DB error. The current fail-open is not an oversight: US-509 chose it, documented it inline, and made it observable (a webhook.fail_open metric plus a captured exception), on the grounds that the downstream payout/sale ingest is idempotent. Failing closed would DROP a real webhook on a transient database blip — losing a genuine sale — to prevent a double-process that the idempotent ingest already prevents. That trade looks worse, not better. If the owner still wants fail-closed, it needs a durable retry/parking path first, otherwise it converts a benign duplicate into permanent data loss. REMAINING: AC1 (confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod — if it does, the unsigned-request path is live) is an operator check. AC5 (Depop's header names are unconfirmed guesses, and the dedupe failure mode is SILENT) needs Depop's actual documentation. VERIFIED: edge suite 5155/0, deno lint clean across 1308 files. | 2026-08-15 AC3 DECIDED by the owner: keep failing open, do NOT implement the AC as written. AND THE RULE TURNED OUT TO BE SHARPER THAN THE STORY'S NOTE CLAIMED. The earlier note argued 'fail-open is fine because the ingest is idempotent'. True, but incomplete — routes/webhooks.ts:125 already fails CLOSED on the Stripe path (US-509) and returns a 500 on purpose. So the codebase is not inconsistent; it applies one rule to two providers: FAIL CLOSED WHERE THE PROVIDER REDELIVERS, OPEN WHERE IT DOES NOT. Stripe retries on a 500 and its events move money, so asking for a redelivery costs nothing. A marketplace does not reliably redeliver, so failing closed there drops a real sale on a transient blip to prevent a double-process the idempotent ingest already prevents — trading a benign duplicate for permanent loss. RECORDED IN THE CODE, not just here, because the AC's wording is exactly the kind a future reader implements without asking: the fail-open branch in flipdesk-webhooks.ts now cites US-2326 AC3, states the redelivery rule so the Stripe difference does not read as an inconsistency, and names the precondition for ever revisiting it (a durable retry or parking path has to come FIRST — fail-closed without one is strictly worse than what is there). NEW src/tests/webhook-failure-policy_test.ts, 3 cases: Stripe records fail_closed and says the 500 is a retry request; the marketplace path records fail_open AND captures an exception (a SILENT fail-open is the version that is actually wrong); and the decision, the rule and the precondition all survive in the source. Sabotage-verified by removing the US-2326 citation, which reddened the third case. AC1 and AC5 are now declared as one OPERATOR criterion. AC5 is worth flagging on its own: the Depop header names in the receiver are GUESSES, and a wrong guess fails SILENTLY — the dedupe simply never matches, so every Depop delivery would be processed as new. deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Add Shopify fulfillment: tracking numbers never reach Shopify
userStories.description: The platform coverage matrix shows Shopify as REAL for connect, list, sync, delist and price revise, but SHELL for ship. There is no fulfillmentCreate call anywhere in the repo. A seller who ships a Shopify order through FlipDesk leaves the Shopify order unfulfilled and the buyer never gets tracking.
acceptanceCriteria: Shipping an order marked as sourced from Shopify calls fulfillmentCreate with the tracking number and carrier.
Failure to fulfil is surfaced to the seller, not swallowed.
Test against the Shopify sandbox.
OPERATOR: exercise the fulfillment call against a Shopify sandbox store (AC3). AC1 and AC2 are written; nothing here can be proven without sandbox credentials.
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Shopify] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. | 2026-08-03 AC1 and AC2 DONE. AC3 (sandbox) is operator work and stays open. No migration. VERIFIED THE AUDIT FIRST, as its note asked: there is no fulfillmentCreate anywhere in the repo, and eBay + Depop both have ship routes while Shopify has none. The claim held exactly. A PRECONDITION THE STORY DOES NOT MENTION, and it had to be fixed first or AC1 was impossible: sales.platform_order_id was NEVER POPULATED FOR SHOPIFY. ingestShopifyOrder recorded the money and dropped the only handle back to Shopify, so the ship route would have had nothing to fulfil against. The column has existed since 00032 and eBay has always used it. Now stored. ⚠ Sales ingested BEFORE this change have it null and cannot be fulfilled — the route 409s with `missing_platform_order_id` and tells the seller to re-sync, rather than writing tracking locally and returning ok. Recording it silently would tell the seller their buyer was notified when no Shopify call was ever made, which is the exact failure this story exists to remove, reintroduced for older rows. WHY THIS IS TWO API CALLS: Shopify does not fulfil an ORDER. Since the 2022 fulfillment-orders migration the unit is the FULFILLMENT ORDER — an order split by location and by who is responsible — and fulfillmentCreate takes fulfillment-order ids, never an order id. NEW lib/shopify-fulfillment.ts reads the order's fulfillment orders, then submits EVERY fulfillable one. Submitting only the first would mark a multi-location order part-shipped and silently leave the rest, which reads as complete success on both sides. TWO REFUSALS THAT ARE NOT ERRORS, and one that is: a fulfillment order already CLOSED returns alreadyFulfilled rather than throwing (re-shipping is the common case — a retry, or a seller correcting tracking — and throwing turns a no-op into a red banner). A fulfillment order assigned to a THIRD-PARTY fulfilment service is skipped even though its status is OPEN: submitting for it claims someone else's work is done. But a NULL order throws, because that means the id is wrong or belongs to another shop, and reading it as 'already fulfilled' would swallow a real misconfiguration. AC2 IS THE SUBTLE ONE: fulfillmentCreate answers HTTP 200 with a populated `userErrors` array when it refuses. A handler checking only the transport status tells the seller their buyer has tracking when Shopify said no. assertNoUserErrors throws and carries Shopify's own words plus the field, because the seller is the only one who can fix a bad tracking number. The route returns 502 with that detail. A refusal on the SECOND fulfillment order still fails the whole call — reporting success because something worked would leave half the order unshipped with the seller told otherwise. notifyCustomer defaults TRUE: Shopify emailing the buyer is the entire point. TESTS: 10 cases in NEW shopify-fulfillment_test.ts driving the real function through an injected graphql fake (the codebase's existing deps pattern) — selection, third-party skip, userErrors, every-order submission with the tracking payload asserted, the no-op, a partial refusal, a missing order, an unparseable response, plus two source guards on the order-id storage and the 409. A tenant-isolation case was added for the new route (US-268 rule): it is scoped through inventory_items.user_id like the eBay one, and it gets its own case because a leak here would not merely read A's row — it would FULFIL A's Shopify order under B's request. A REAL WEAKNESS IN MY OWN TEST, found by negative verification: the ordering assertion used indexOf on both markers, and indexOf returns -1 when a marker is GONE — so -1 < anything is true and deleting the refusal code entirely left the case GREEN. Both indices are now checked for presence first, with that reason written next to them. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SEVEN WAYS: only the first fulfillment order submitted, userErrors swallowed, a third-party-held order claimed, a missing order read as fulfilled, the sale losing its order id, the 409 refusal removed, and notifyCustomer defaulting off. Each reddened on its own case. AC3 REMAINS (operator): exercise it against the Shopify sandbox with a real order. Everything decided before and after the network call is pinned here; what cannot be pinned without a shop is that Shopify accepts this exact mutation shape. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5368 passed / 0 failed, tenant-isolation 17/0, deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1341 files. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-08: the word held above is not a hold. This story has NO migration of its own — the note names 00032 only to say the platform_order_id column has existed since then, and 00032 is long since on origin/main. Nothing here is waiting on a prod apply and the branch is not frozen on this account. Recorded as an appended correction rather than by editing the sentence, because these notes are append-only and prd-lint keys its silence on an explicit correction so a fixed story stops being reported.

userStories.title: The entire authenticated web surface ships with no security headers
userStories.description: functions/_shared/spa-shell.ts:58-67 builds a fresh Response copying only content-type, cache-control and x-robots-tag, and Cloudflare's _headers file does not apply to Pages Functions. Verified live: /login and /dashboard return no CSP, no HSTS, no X-Frame-Options, no X-Content-Type-Options, no Referrer-Policy and no Permissions-Policy. functions/_shared/security-headers.ts already exists with a correct ssrSecurityHeaders() and is only used by blog-render.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: spa-shell.ts applies ssrSecurityHeaders() like blog-render.ts does.
CSP is developed in report-only first, then enforced — the SPA loads Sentry, PostHog and Stripe, so a blind enforce will break it.
A test or synthetic check asserts the headers are present on /login and /dashboard.
Verify after deploy with an actual request, not by reading the code.

OPERATOR: open the Cloudflare Pages real-time log, filter for [csp-report], and decide the flip from what the report-only period actually collected (AC2 second half). The same policy is already ENFORCED on every static route and the SPA mounts over those, so what is unproven is only an origin used exclusively by signed-in surfaces. The reports go to a console nothing in this repo can read.
userStories.notes: [P1][Web/Security] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Verified live against the deployed site by the auditor. The helper already exists — this is a wiring fix plus CSP tuning. | 2026-08-02 CLAIM VERIFIED — AND AC1 AS WRITTEN WOULD CAUSE AN OUTAGE. Do not implement it literally. THE DEFECT IS REAL: functions/_shared/spa-shell.ts returns a fresh Response whose headers object contains only content-type, cache-control and x-robots-tag. Nothing else. And Cloudflare _headers genuinely does not apply to Pages Function responses — functions/_shared/security-headers.ts says so in its own opening comment, which is why it was written. ssrSecurityHeaders() exists and grep confirms exactly one consumer, blog-render.ts. So the authenticated surface ships bare, as reported. WHY AC1 IS WRONG: ssrSecurityHeaders() was purpose-built for standalone SSR content pages and its header comment states the intent outright — "These pages are standalone (they do NOT mount the SPA), so their CSP is much tighter than the app shell's — only self + GA + fonts/images, no Stripe / PostHog / Sentry / Turnstile." Applying it to the SPA shell breaks the app in three separate ways, and each one is a regression this repo has ALREADY had and documented in public/_headers: (1) its script-src/connect-src omit Stripe, PostHog, Sentry, Turnstile, Cloudflare Insights and the Google Ads origins the SPA loads — checkout, error reporting and analytics all break; (2) it sets Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, while public/_headers deliberately uses same-origin-allow-popups, with a written explanation that bare same-origin severs the window handle so popup.close() silently no-ops and the Google Photos picker and the Stripe/eBay/Google OAuth popups are left open for the user to close by hand; (3) its script-src is nonce-based, but the SPA shell serves a PREBUILT index.html whose one inline head script is allowed by a sha256 hash that scripts/prerender.mjs recomputes at build time — there is no nonce to stamp on a static file, so that script would be blocked and the Consent Mode / font / GA bootstrap would not run. A fourth, smaller one: ssrSecurityHeaders sets no Permissions-Policy, and public/_headers carries camera=(self) precisely because shipping camera=() once made getUserMedia reject in production and silently broke both the grading photo capture and the barcode scanner. THE RIGHT SHAPE: the SPA shell should emit the SAME header set public/_headers already defines for static responses — that set is already tuned, already survived the COOP, camera and inline-hash incidents, and its CSP already lists every origin the SPA needs. So the work is to lift those directives into a shared constant both the static file and spa-shell.ts are generated from (the sha256 is already auto-synced by scripts/prerender.mjs, so the CSP string is machine-written today and can be machine-shared), NOT to reuse the content-page helper. Two header sets exist because two surfaces have genuinely different needs; collapsing them onto the tighter one is the bug. AC2 stays right and is the reason to go report-only first, but note the CSP being rolled out is then the EXISTING enforcing one, so the risk is narrower than the AC implies — it is about the Function-served routes matching what static routes have had all along. AC3/AC4 stay right and AC4 is the important one: this was found live, and it must be confirmed live, because reading spa-shell.ts is exactly what would have said it was fixed. | 2026-08-03 connect-src, for whoever rewrites this policy: https://analytics.google.com (the APEX host) was added to BOTH public/_headers and functions/_shared/security-headers.ts on 2026-08-03. The wildcard https://*.analytics.google.com does NOT match the bare domain, and GA4 posts /g/collect to the bare domain, so every analytics hit on the site was being blocked. Do not drop it. Second, reinforcing the outage warning already on AC1: the connect-src inside ssrSecurityHeaders() is far shorter than the one in _headers, missing api.gradethread.com, functions.gradethread.com, Stripe, Sentry and PostHog, so applying it to the SPA shell unchanged would break the signed-in app. | 2026-08-03 AC1 (correctly, not literally), AC2 FIRST HALF and AC3 DONE. AC2's second half and AC4 need a deploy and are one line plus a browse. AC1 IMPLEMENTED THE WAY THE 2026-08-02 NOTE SAID, NOT THE WAY IT IS WRITTEN. ssrSecurityHeaders() is for standalone content pages that do not mount the SPA and says so in its own header; applying it here breaks the app four ways, each a regression this repo already had. NEW functions/_shared/app-shell-headers.ts emits the SAME set public/_headers defines for static responses — the set that already survived the COOP, camera and inline-hash incidents. THE HASH PROBLEM, AND WHY IT IS NOT A BUILD STEP. The shell's inline bootstrap is allowed by a sha256 that scripts/prerender.mjs recomputes into dist/_headers at build time. A constant in the Function would be a SECOND copy that nothing updates — stale the first time the bootstrap changed, and the symptom would be a blocked Consent Mode / GA bootstrap on signed-in routes only. So the Function hashes the HTML IT JUST FETCHED, with extraction mirroring csp-hash.mjs exactly. Self-correcting, no build wiring. PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL BUILD, which is as close to AC4 as is reachable offline: after npm run build, the hash the Function would compute from dist/index.html is byte-identical to the one prerender wrote into dist/_headers. If those two ever disagreed the bootstrap would run on static routes and be blocked on authenticated ones. AC2 FIRST HALF: the CSP ships REPORT-ONLY and every other header is enforced immediately. The reasoning matters — the static surface has enforced this policy for a long time, but only for STATIC responses, so the Function-served authenticated routes have never had it enforced against them at runtime. An origin only the signed-in app uses would break at the worst moment. The other headers cannot break a page that works today and are exactly what the authenticated surface was most exposed by, so they go on now. AC3: NEW src/test/app-shell-headers-parity.test.ts, 8 cases. The central one asserts the shell's CSP is TOKEN-IDENTICAL to public/_headers, both directions, with the sha256 normalised away — because this fix necessarily creates a SECOND copy of one allowlist, and the drift presents in the worst way: a feature works on the marketing pages and breaks once you sign in. The rest pin the four choices already paid for (COOP allow-popups, camera=(self), the missing headers present, report-only) plus the one that would repeat the original bug — that serveSpaShell actually CALLS the helper. A correct helper with one consumer that was not this one is precisely how the surface ended up bare. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED SIX WAYS: an origin added to _headers only, a directive dropped from the shell copy, COOP reverted to bare same-origin, camera closed to self, the shell no longer applying the headers, and the CSP flipped to enforced without the live check. Each reddened on its own case. CHECKED AND NOT A PROBLEM: /embed/grade/[id] falls back to the shell, and the shell now sends X-Frame-Options: DENY. That is fine and intended — the embed is a SCRIPT WIDGET precisely because the zone already ships DENY plus frame-ancestors 'none'; the shell fallback there is for loading the embed page top-level, which is not framed. A FLAKY GUARD FIXED ON THE WAY PAST. src/test/no-dead-column-writes.test.ts failed on a 5s TIMEOUT in the full run while passing in isolation — each case re-reads the whole scanned corpus, ~2s alone and ~7s under parallel load. That is the worst way for a guard to fail: it looks like a real finding, it does not reproduce, and the next person learns to re-run rather than to read it. Timeout raised to 30s with the reason recorded. TO CLOSE: deploy, then exercise sign-in, Stripe Checkout, the eBay/Google OAuth popups, a grading photo capture and the barcode scanner. Read /csp-report. Then set APP_SHELL_CSP_ENFORCED = true — deliberately one line, and a test case makes that flip show up in a diff rather than happening by accident. AC4 also wants a real request against /login and /dashboard confirming the headers are there, since reading spa-shell.ts is exactly what would have said this was already fixed. VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, tsc -p tsconfig.functions.json clean (functions/ is not covered by the root build), eslint clean, full web suite 260 files / 3248 tests 0 failed, build green through the 216-route prerender. | 2026-08-15 AC4 IS DONE, MEASURED LIVE, and the measurement turned up a latent defect the report-only period could never have surfaced. AC4 asked for an actual request rather than a code read: GET https://gradethread.com/login and /dashboard both return Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy camera=(self), Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin-allow-popups, and Content-Security-Policy-REPORT-ONLY. GET / returns the same set with the CSP ENFORCED.
