[P1][Buyer/Billing] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. The dead-code sweep called this its top finding. Revenue leak, not just dead code. | 2026-08-02 VERIFIED, and quantified. requireBuyerFeature is defined at lib/buyer-entitlements.ts and grep across the whole edge service (excluding _test files) returns ONE hit — its own definition. Zero callers, exactly as reported. buyerFeatureEnabled has two hits: its definition and the single use inside requireBuyerFeature, so the entire gating helper pair is dead. THE SIZE OF THE GAP: BuyerGateFlags in lib/buyer-plans.ts declares THIRTEEN gated features — extensionSecondOpinion, discrepancyScoring, priceFairness, conditionAlerts, fitPrediction, authenticityAddon, videoGrading, rewards, trustScore, purchaseGuarantee, wardrobePortfolio, demandBoard, prioritySupport. Across the seven buyer route files, exactly ONE reads a gate flag: buyer-authenticity.ts checks ent.gateFlags.authenticityAddon inline. buyer-closet.ts, buyer-purchases.ts, buyer-rewards.ts, buyer-trust.ts and buyer-wants.ts contain no gate reference at all (buyer-profile.ts's only hit is the word "entitlements" in a comment). So one of thirteen flags is enforced anywhere, and the story's specific example holds — buyer-wants.ts, the demand board, has no gate. A DETAIL THAT CHANGES AC2 AND IS NOT IN THE STORY: the one gate that does exist returns 403 with code "not_entitled", while requireBuyerFeature is the 402 upgrade-required guard. They are not interchangeable. Applying requireBuyerFeature to buyer-authenticity as part of AC2 would change its status code from 403 to 402, which is a client-visible change — the buyer web/iOS clients may branch on one or the other. Either check the clients first, or leave authenticity on 403 and say why. Do not assume the helper is a drop-in for the inline check just because both deny. SEQUENCING NOTE on AC4: it asks how many free-tier buyers have been using paid features before deciding whether to grandfather. That is a PROD query this host cannot run, and it should gate AC2 rather than follow it — switching thirteen features on at once for users who have had them free is a support event, not just a fix. Split AC4 out as an operator task so AC1 (the inventory) can proceed without it. AC1 is the cheap half and is mostly done by this note: the thirteen flags above are the candidate list, and what remains is deciding the TIER each belongs to, which is a product call rather than a code reading. | PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE. AC4 is a prod query this host cannot run and stays open as the operator half. AC1, the inventory, is now a FILE rather than a paragraph: services/edge-functions/src/tests/buyer-plan-gates_test.ts lists all 21 buyer routes across the seven route files, each with either the feature that gates it or a stated reason it is open. AC2: TWO ROUTES WERE GENUINELY UNPROTECTED and are now gated. The demand board (POST /wants, PATCH /wants/:id) is Connoisseur-only and had no gate on any of its four routes. The purchase-guarantee claim (POST /purchases/:id/claim) is Guard and up and had none either. Both now call requireBuyerFeature and RETURN its refusal. The claim gate goes BEFORE the ownership read on purpose: a free-tier buyer should be told to upgrade, not told whether some other buyer's purchase id exists. A RULE I HAD TO INVENT, because the story does not state one and the naive reading causes harm: GATE THE PATHS THAT CREATE OR CONSUME A PAID FEATURE, NEVER THE ONES THAT READ OR REMOVE WHAT THE BUYER ALREADY HAS. Gating GET /wants and DELETE /wants/:id would mean a buyer who downgrades cannot see or clean up wants they created while paying — the gate would convert a billing state into data loss. Both are left open with that reason recorded at the call site and in the registry. WHAT I DID NOT GATE, and why each: eleven routes read a flag that is TRUE ON EVERY TIER (wardrobePortfolio, extensionSecondOpinion, rewards, trustScore), so a gate there denies nobody and costs a database round trip — a test case now FAILS if anyone claims a gate on a feature no tier withholds, because a gate that cannot deny reads as protection and is not. POST /authenticity keeps its inline 403 not_entitled rather than being converted: requireBuyerFeature returns 402, and the buyer web and iOS clients may branch on the status. That is a client contract change and belongs in its own story rather than in a sweep — the previous pass flagged this and it was right. AC3: the story asks for a live 402 assertion for a free-tier user. That needs an authenticated request against a seeded buyer, i.e. the database, so I did NOT claim it and built the strongest thing that works without one — six cases asserting the guard is CALLED on the right route with the right feature name, that its refusal is RETURNED rather than discarded, that the declared route set IS the route set, that every ungated route carries a real reason, and that the free tier genuinely lacks demandBoard and purchaseGuarantee (otherwise the two new gates would silently stop denying anyone while every other case still passed). WHY ENUMERATION: dead security code is the worst kind, because the helper's EXISTENCE is what makes a reviewer believe the gating is handled. Nothing about reading buyer-wants.ts said "this is ungated" — the absence was the bug, and absence is what a diff never shows. A new buyer route now fails until its author answers the question nobody asked for thirteen features. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS: removed the demand-board gate (reddened naming the route and flag), kept the call but discarded its Response (reddened on the return), added an undeclared /probe route (reddened as an unlisted route), and re-declared the claim gate against the rewards flag (reddened as a gate that denies nobody). Each restored. A MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: my first route regex was a bare .get( / .post(, which also matched c.get("userId") in every handler and reported a phantom route per file. Over-matching is not harmless here — it would have left the guard permanently red, and a permanently red guard gets deleted. It is anchored to the Routes receiver now and says so. AND A SELF-INFLICTED ONE: I reverted my own uncommitted gate edits with a git checkout while restoring a negative-verification probe, then caught it by grepping for the guard before moving on. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1310 files, full edge suite 5166 passed / 0 failed, tenant-isolation 17/0. REMAINING: AC4 (how many free-tier buyers have been using the demand board and the guarantee claim, to decide grandfathering) is a prod query — it belongs with the other operator diagnostics in scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql. Worth doing BEFORE this deploys, since switching a feature off for users who have had it free is a support event, not just a fix. | 2026-08-03: this story's last open AC is now answerable by scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, which the operator runs in ONE psql session alongside the other blocked stories. Read-only, verified by executing against a real database with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 — so it cannot fail the operator's session on a wrong column name, which is the failure mode that makes someone distrust the whole file. §12 counts free-tier accounts that used the two features that were genuinely ungated — the demand board and the guarantee claim — BY ACCOUNT rather than by row, because '3,000 wants' and '4 buyers' call for very different decisions about grandfathering. A 30-day slice is reported separately: an account that used it once a year ago is not the same support problem as one using it this week. | AC4 FIRST DATA POINT, 2026-08-03 (owner ran the diagnostics): free_tier_accounts_last_30d = 0. No free-tier buyer has used the demand board in the last 30 days, so switching its gate on is NOT a support event for anyone currently active. That is the half of AC4 that decides urgency. What is still needed to close it is the ALL-TIME half from the same section — the demand_board and guarantee_claim rows of the first query in §12 — because an account that used the feature months ago still loses access on the next deploy, and whether that matters is a grandfathering call rather than a code one. | PROD ANSWER 2026-08-03 (owner ran scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql). §12's 30-day slice returned 0. Combined with the earlier reading, no free-tier buyer has used the demand board recently. STILL MISSING: the ALL-TIME half of §12 — the demand_board and guarantee_claim rows of that section's first query — which is what decides grandfathering for someone who used the feature months ago and would lose it on the next deploy. | 2026-08-04 RE-CHECKED — the title is now FALSE and should not be quoted. grep for requireBuyerFeature across services/edge-functions/src excluding tests returns four hits: its definition in lib/buyer-entitlements.ts plus three real call sites — buyer-purchases.ts:301 gating purchaseGuarantee, and buyer-wants.ts:40 and :91 gating demandBoard. Commit 6e3915f7 closed the zero-caller claim, and the story's own worked example (the demand board) is one of the routes now gated. WHAT REMAINS is the count, not the mechanism: the earlier note recorded THIRTEEN flags in BuyerGateFlags, and two of them are now enforced through this helper (a third, authenticityAddon, is enforced inline in buyer-authenticity.ts). So AC1 (the inventory of which routes gate against which tier) and AC2 (applying it to each) are still open for the remaining ten, and AC4 (measuring free-tier usage before deciding whether to grandfather) is untouched. Keep the story, retitle it to something like 'Ten of thirteen buyer gate flags are still unenforced' — the current title will read as stale to the next person and invites closing it by mistake.

| 2026-08-08 RETITLED, as the previous note asked, and the number in the old title was wrong in BOTH directions.

The 2026-08-04 note said to retitle this to "Ten of thirteen buyer gate flags are still unenforced". I checked that number instead of adopting it, and it does not survive. THE REAL ACCOUNTING, measured by grepping every flag name across the whole edge service:

FIVE FLAGS ARE TRUE ON EVERY TIER — extensionSecondOpinion, conditionAlerts, rewards, trustScore, wardrobePortfolio. Nothing withholds them from anyone, so there is no revenue to leak and a gate on them would be decoration plus a database round trip. They were being counted as unenforced. They are not enforceable.

THE OTHER EIGHT ARE DENIABLE, AND ALL EIGHT ARE ENFORCED — just not all in the buyer route files, which is the whole reason the count kept reading wrong. A route-shaped audit of seven buyer files cannot see five of them:
  demandBoard, purchaseGuarantee -> requireBuyerFeature 402 (buyer-wants.ts x2, buyer-purchases.ts)
  authenticityAddon -> inline 403 not_entitled (buyer-authenticity.ts), deliberately not converted
  discrepancyScoring, priceFairness, fitPrediction -> FIELD SUPPRESSION via resolveExtensionGates in routes/public-grading.ts:1107-1122 and :1818 — the extension scan returns, with the paid fields nulled
  videoGrading -> 402 UPGRADE_REQUIRED at routes/grade.ts:617, after the seller plan is checked and the buyer plan is the second way in
  prioritySupport -> NO runtime path by design; lib/plan-gate.ts:52 states it is an SLA/routing attribute

THE SHAPES DIFFER AND ALL OF THEM ARE RIGHT. A 402 on the extension scan would refuse the free feature in order to withhold the paid one; suppressing three fields is the correct answer there. Writing a test that demanded one uniform shape would have pushed three of these toward the wrong one — worth saying, because that is the obvious next move and it would be a regression.

NEW GUARD, the flag side of the question this story was actually filed on: buyer-plan-gates_test.ts already enumerated all 21 ROUTES, which answers "is this route gated?" and cannot answer "is this paid feature enforced anywhere?". FLAG_ENFORCEMENT now maps every BuyerGateFlags key to null / "GATES" / a file path. A null entry must be true on every tier (so "we do not gate it" stays earned, not assumed); a "GATES" entry must appear in the route registry; a file entry is READ and must still mention the flag, so deleting an enforcement reddens here instead of leaving the table describing code that used to exist. The Record type forces exhaustiveness one way; a key-set assertion catches the other.

NEGATIVE-VERIFIED TWICE: flipped rewards to false on the free tier (reddened, naming rewards and free — a paid feature nothing withholds); repointed videoGrading at lib/plan-gate.ts (reddened, naming the file that no longer mentions it). Both restored, 7 passed. deno lint + deno check clean.

STILL passes:false ON AC4 ALONE, unchanged: the ALL-TIME half of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql section 12 — how many free-tier accounts EVER used the demand board or the guarantee claim, which decides grandfathering. The 30-day slice already came back 0 twice. Operator query; this host cannot run it.

userStories.title: Variation listings cannot be revised: resubmit needs an offer id a group listing never has
userStories.description: As a seller with a multi-variation eBay listing, I want Save and resubmit to push my edits to eBay, so that a listing with size or color variants is not frozen the moment it goes live.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/:id/revise on a listing whose listings.variations is non-null and whose platform_offer_id is null no longer returns the 409 "This listing has no eBay offer id" (flipdesk-ebay.ts, the guard above the offerId const) and instead revises through the eBay inventory item group.

The revise resolves its strategy group-FIRST, the same way the end path does via resolveEndStrategy (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8836), and keys the group on the PINNED listings.inventory_sku rather than the current inventory_items.sku, so a SKU rename cannot orphan the live group.

The group branch updates every variant inventory item and then calls createOrReplaceInventoryItemGroup and publishOfferByInventoryItemGroup (both already exported from services/edge-functions/src/lib/ebay-client.ts), so title, description, price, photos and specifics changes reach the live listing.

A single-offer listing keeps the existing offer branch byte-for-byte; a deno test in services/edge-functions/src/tests/listing-variations_test.ts asserts both branches are chosen correctly from a listings row (variations present versus platform_offer_id present).

The composer treats a published variation listing as live: isLiveListing in src/pages/flipdesk/composer.tsx stops requiring platform_offer_id when listings.variations is present and platform_listing_id is set, so the footer shows Save and resubmit to eBay instead of offering to publish an already-live listing. A vitest guard pins that gate.

Tenant scoping is unchanged: the revise route still reaches the listing through an owner-verified parent row (US-268), and services/edge-functions/src/tests/tenant-isolation_test.ts gains a case covering the group-revise branch.

Verified after deploy against a real multi-variation listing, not by reading code: the publish path never writes platform_offer_id for a group (the variation listingPayload in flipdesk-ebay.ts omits it), so unit tests alone cannot prove the round trip.
userStories.notes: PARTIAL 2026-08-03 — AC2, AC4 and AC5 DONE, plus a truthful refusal in place of misleading advice. AC1, AC3, AC6 and AC7 remain, and the reason is scoped rather than vague. VERIFIED THE WHOLE CHAIN FIRST. The revise route really does begin with `if (!row.listing.platform_offer_id) return 409`, eBay really never mints an offer id for a listing published through publish_by_inventory_item_group, and loadListingOwned already selects both `variations` and the pinned `inventory_sku`. The END path already solved the same problem correctly under US-1999 (resolveEndStrategy, group-first, keyed on the pinned SKU) — two resolvers in one file giving different answers to the same question is the shape that made this findable. AC2 DONE: NEW resolveReviseStrategy, deliberately the same shape and the same ORDER as resolveEndStrategy. Group first, because an offer-first resolver reads a group listing as having no mechanism at all — which is precisely the bug. Keyed on the PINNED listings.inventory_sku, since the inventory_item_group was created under the base SKU at publish and a later rename would aim the revise at a group that does not exist. One deliberate difference from the end resolver: no-mechanism is `none`, not `local`. Ending locally is a real outcome — the listing is closed in FlipDesk — whereas a revise with no mechanism has done nothing and must not report otherwise. A test pins both the agreement and that single divergence. AC5 DONE, AND IT WAS THE WORSE HALF OF THE BUG. isLiveListing required a platform_offer_id, so every LIVE variation listing was classified as a DRAFT and the footer offered to "Publish to eBay" something already live. The 409 at least refused; this invited the seller to publish a duplicate of their own listing. The gate now also accepts variations + platform_listing_id — the eBay item id publish-by-group returns — and a test requires BOTH halves, since a matrix alone would call an unpublished draft live. SHIPPED AHEAD OF THE FEATURE, on purpose: the 409 for a variation listing no longer says "Sync from eBay or republish to enable edits". That is advice that CANNOT WORK — republishing does not create an offer id for a group, and republishing a live listing is worse than doing nothing. It now says the truth: group revise is not supported yet, edit on eBay for now. A wrong instruction is worse than a plain refusal, and this one was pointing sellers at an action that could duplicate their listing. AC4 DONE: seven cases appended to listing-variations_test.ts covering both branches from a listings row, the ordering (group wins even when a stale offer id is present), the pinned-SKU key, the two no-mechanism shapes, the revise/end agreement, and the refusal text. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: the resolver flipped to offer-first (reddened on the ordering case) and the composer's variation branch reduced to the matrix alone (reddened on the both-halves case). WHAT REMAINS AND WHY I DID NOT DO IT. AC1/AC3 are the group-revise branch itself: update every variant inventory item, then createOrReplaceInventoryItemGroup and publishOfferByInventoryItemGroup. The machinery exists — publishVariationListing does exactly this — but reusing it means reconstructing a PublishContextOk, PublishItem, policies and photos inside the revise handler, and that function also performs publish-shaped PERSISTENCE which a revise must not repeat. It is a substantial change to the most sensitive file in the service, on the path every seller's Save-and-resubmit uses, and AC7 states plainly that unit tests cannot prove the round trip because the publish path never writes platform_offer_id for a group. Half-implementing it risks breaking the COMMON single-offer revise to fix the rare one. The resolver, the composer gate and the honest refusal are the parts that are safe and testable now; the branch wants one deliberate pass with a real multi-variation listing to verify against, which is what AC7 asks for anyway. AC6 (the tenant-isolation case) belongs with that branch — there is no new query to scope yet. VERIFIED: deno check clean, deno lint clean across 1323 files, edge suite 5245 passed / 0 failed, web 260 files / 3236 tests 0 failed, tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, build green through the 216-route prerender. | 2026-08-09 AC1/AC3 SCOPED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, and there is a SEMANTIC DECISION nobody has taken that the ACs do not mention. Recorded so the next session finds it before writing the branch rather than after. AC3 reads as plumbing: update every variant inventory item, then call createOrReplaceInventoryItemGroup and publishOfferByInventoryItemGroup, both already exported. Traced the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:7650-7740) to mirror it, and the plumbing IS that shape. THE PROBLEM IS WHAT A SCALAR EDIT MEANS TO A MATRIX. The revise route accepts title, description, listing_price, quantity and photos. For a variation listing those split cleanly in two: TITLE, DESCRIPTION and PHOTOS are unambiguous — they live on the group AND on every member item, so a revise applies them to both, exactly as publish does. PRICE and QUANTITY are NOT. The publish path creates ONE OFFER PER VARIANT SKU, each with its own price (the per-variant override, else the base) and its own quantity (variant.quantity). A single listing_price in the revise body has no defined meaning against that: does it overwrite every variant's price, or only the ones with no override, or set a new base the overrides continue to shift from? Each answer is defensible and they produce different money on a LIVE listing. Same for quantity against variant.quantity. Guessing here is not a call code should make — it is the same class of decision as the offer-route-vs-return-route split in US-2227, and the wrong guess silently reprices a seller's whole variation matrix. RECOMMENDED SHAPE, if the decision goes the obvious way: implement the group branch for title/description/photos only, and REFUSE price/quantity on a variation listing with a message naming eBay as the place to change them — the same truthful-refusal pattern this story already used in place of the misleading 'republish to enable edits' advice. That ships the majority of the value with no ambiguity, and leaves the pricing question to be decided on its own rather than smuggled in. WHY I DID NOT IMPLEMENT IT THIS PASS, stated plainly rather than dressed up: this is a mutation path against live eBay listings, AC7 already says it cannot be verified without a real multi-variation listing, and I have no way to exercise it end to end from here. A branch that looks right and is wrong is worse than the current honest 409, because the 409 loses an edit and a bad branch loses a listing's pricing. The unambiguous half is genuinely small once the price/quantity decision is recorded; it is the decision that gates it, not the code. AC6 IS COUPLED, NOT INDEPENDENT: tenant-isolation_test.ts already covers 'B cannot revise A's eBay listing' via loadListingOwned (line ~1930), and a VARIATION-specific case needs a seeded variation listing id the fixture does not have (seed-tenant-isolation-fixture.ts) plus a group branch to actually exercise. Adding it before the branch exists would assert the refusal, not the ownership check. VERIFIED UNCHANGED: resolveReviseStrategy (AC2), the composer's isLiveListing fix (AC5) and the truthful 409 all still in place; full edge suite green this session at 6213 passed / 0 failed. | 2026-08-15 AC1, AC3 and AC6 DONE. Only AC7 remains, which is the check against a real multi-variation listing after a deploy. WHY THIS COULD LAND NOW when the previous pass deliberately stopped: the risk it named was breaking the COMMON single-offer revise to fix the rare one, and the branch as built cannot. The group path returns before the offer path is reached, and it only runs for a listing with variations and no platform_offer_id - which is exactly the set that answered 409 until today. The blast radius is the listings that were already broken. AC1: the 409 is now keyed on resolveReviseStrategy returning none rather than on platform_offer_id being absent, which is the offer-first read that caused the bug. The variation-specific refusal is DELETED, and the test that used to pin its presence now pins its absence - it was honest while the branch did not exist and would be a lie now. AC3: new reviseVariationGroup, placed AFTER the shared assembly so the group push uses the same title, description, aspects, photos and condition the offer path builds; a second copy of that assembly is how the two paths would start disagreeing about what a revision contains. Order is items, then group, then per-variant offers, then publish, and a test pins that order by source position: the group references the items, price and category live on the offers rather than on the item, and the publish call applies the lot. Offer ids are found with listOffersForSku, since a group listing has none stored - that absence IS the bug this story is about. TWO DELIBERATE REFUSALS. Quantity is not pushed: quantity on a group is per variant, and one number applied to every variant multiplies the seller's stock silently, so the response says so instead. A variant carrying its own price_cents keeps it through a base-price edit, or a deliberately-differentiated variant would be flattened by an edit to the listing price. THE PART I CANNOT VERIFY, stated in the code as well as here: publish_by_inventory_item_group is how eBay applies pending item and group changes to an already-published group, and if it instead rejects the call as already-published the error surfaces as a 422 with its own message rather than being swallowed. That is the failure mode worth having - the alternative is reporting success on a listing that did not change. AC7 stays open for exactly this. AC6: a tenant-isolation case for the group branch, and it needed a fixture rather than a classification. Before the branch existed the 409 was doing the isolation work by accident; now the route performs real eBay writes, so the ownership check is the only thing between B and A's live listing. The seed script emits TEST_USER_A_VARIATION_LISTING_ID - a plain insert with variations set, a pinned inventory_sku and no offer id, which is what eBay leaves behind after a group publish. The structural guard caught the new gating id immediately and refused to let it skip quietly, which is the guard working. ALSO EXTRACTED: clearReviseDrift, so both paths clear the same sync_drift and publish_error state. A revise that succeeded through the group and left the marker standing would show eBay differs on a listing that no longer does. VERIFIED: full edge suite 6781 passed / 0 failed / 195 ignored, deno check and deno lint clean on the route, the test file and the seed script, listing-variations 18 passed (7 new). Negative-verified twice: removing the publish step reddens the order case, and flattening the per-variant price reddens its own case; both restored. | 2026-08-15 (same day, second pass) A DEFECT IN MY OWN CHANGE, found while doing the vault same-commit review rather than by a test, and fixed with two guards. THE BUG: the group branch sits inside the block gated on hasTitle or hasDesc or syncPhotos or resyncFields, because that is where the shared title/description/aspect/photo assembly happens. A PRICE-ONLY or QUANTITY-ONLY revise satisfies none of those, so it skipped the block entirely, fell through to the offer-side push at the end, and called updateOfferFields with the empty string a group listing resolves to as its offer id. A malformed eBay write against a live listing, reachable from Save-and-resubmit with only the price changed, and invisible until production. Before this story the same request met the 409 and could not get that far, so the branch introduced it. FIXED IN TWO PLACES because one alone leaves it reachable: the gate now includes groupRevise, so a price-only revise runs the group path (the extra item and group PUTs are the same idempotent ones publish sends, and that path re-publishes the group anyway), and the offer-side push is guarded with !groupRevise so a future early-exit that skipped the branch still cannot send an empty offer id. Two new cases pin both, and the first was negative-verified: removing groupRevise from the gate reddens it. VAULT, which is the rule I had broken: three notes name flipdesk-ebay.ts in code_refs and were left drifting by the first pass. ebay-required-aspect-completeness gains the fourth-path note (the group revise reuses reviseWireAspects rather than assembling its own, which is precisely how that note's original defect would have returned); ebay-listing-lifecycle-reconciliation gains the revise half beside the end half it already documented, including why none rather than local is the right no-mechanism answer; grade-authority-on-listings records that all three grade channels reach a variation listing, and that the silent failure avoided is a group revise skipping stripCertLinks and putting an off-eBay link back on a live listing. draft-snapshot-precedence was re-read against both its drifted refs - my change does not touch publish precedence, and the composer edits on 2026-08-14 were a help link plus US-2593's title write-back, which narrows one divergence case rather than changing the rule - so it gains one linking sentence and a bump. VERIFIED: full edge suite 6783 passed / 0 failed / 195 ignored, listing-variations 20 passed (2 new), deno check and lint clean, vault:lint down from 12 errors to 5 and every one that remains belongs to another commit.

userStories.title: A denied function call from anon or authenticated SEGFAULTS Postgres and restarts the whole database
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a permission-denied RPC to return an error instead of crashing the database, so that anyone holding the public anon key cannot restart production at will.
acceptanceCriteria: Establish whether the PROD Postgres image reproduces it. On the local Supabase image (PG 17.6) it reproduces every time; prod is a separate self-hosted image and this has NOT been tested there, deliberately, because the test is a denial of service against production. The safe check is to read the image tag and the supautils.hint_roles setting, not to call a denied RPC.

If prod reproduces: mitigate BEFORE anything else. Clearing supautils.hint_roles (it exists only to append a GRANT hint to the error message) or upgrading the image are the two candidates; whichever is chosen, prove it with a denied call against a staging copy of the same image.

A regression check that survives an image upgrade: a throwaway-stack test that revokes EXECUTE on a scratch function, calls it as anon, and asserts a clean 'permission denied for function' error with the connection still alive.

supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED is renamed back to .sql, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00527 in the same commit, and US-2282 closed — the SQL is already written and verified, it is only blocked on this.

The 5 functions already revoked from anon before this was known (refund_grade 00048, credit_ledger_reconciliation 00093, release_job_lock + try_acquire_job_lock 00094, reserve_snap/refund_snap 00099, reconcile_payout_link 00117, equity_snapshot_owners) are enumerated in the notes as the CURRENTLY reachable crash entry points, since they are what an attacker could use today.

OPERATOR: run `show supautils.hint_roles;` over psql on the prod database (read-only, one line). If anon is absent, AC1 closes as does-not-reproduce and AC2 is already satisfied, which unblocks 00527 and US-2282. Do NOT confirm by calling a revoked function: that call is the outage.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/DB] Found 2026-08-04 by accident while verifying US-2282 on a throwaway stack, and it is the reason US-2282 is not shipping. ISOLATED, not guessed — four probes on the local Supabase image (PostgreSQL 17.6, shared_preload_libraries includes supautils): (1) a trivial scratch function with EXECUTE revoked, called as anon => SIGNAL 11 SEGMENTATION FAULT, 'terminating any other active server processes', full database recovery; (2) same as authenticated => same crash; (3) same as a custom role NOT listed in supautils.hint_roles => clean 'ERROR: permission denied for function', connection alive; (4) a denied TABLE read as anon => clean error PLUS the supautils hint 'Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT SELECT ON public.applied_migrations TO anon;'. supautils.hint_roles is set to exactly 'anon, authenticated, service_role', which is exactly the set that crashes. So the crash is in the supautils hint path for FUNCTION permission denials specifically; the table path is fine. ALREADY REACHABLE TODAY, WITHOUT ANY NEW MIGRATION: public.refund_grade(uuid) has been revoked from anon since 00048/00093, and calling it as anon crashes the database the same way — verified, not inferred. PostgREST exposes it as an RPC, so the input needed is the public anon key and one HTTP call. WHY US-2282 IS BLOCKED ON THIS RATHER THAN THE OTHER WAY AROUND: 00527 does not create the bug, it multiplies the entry points — from the handful of functions already revoked to ~80. Applying it into an unpatched image would hand an attacker eighty ways to restart the database instead of eight. The SQL is written, verified on a fresh stack, and parked at supabase/migrations/00527_revoke_public_function_execute.sql.BLOCKED; the .BLOCKED suffix is what keeps apply-prod-migrations.sh (which globs *.sql) from applying it. NOT TESTED AGAINST PROD ON PURPOSE. The test IS the denial of service, so running it would be the attack. The safe next step is to read the prod image tag and 'show supautils.hint_roles' over psql — both read-only — and compare against the local image. If prod's image differs enough not to reproduce, this closes as a local-only artifact and US-2282 unblocks immediately. | 2026-08-08 AC3 DONE; AC5 DONE AND THE COUNT WAS WRONG; AC1/AC2 now have a PROVEN mitigation and a safer prod probe. Docker was available on this host for the first time, so every claim below was re-run rather than inherited. REPRODUCED on public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.6.1.106 with all 552 migrations applied: a scratch function with EXECUTE revoked, called as anon, gives 'server closed the connection' and the server log shows 'terminated by signal 11: Segmentation fault' -> 'terminating any other active server processes' -> 'automatic recovery in progress'. ALSO reproduced with public.refund_grade(uuid), a REAL function that has been revoked from anon since 00048/00093 — so this is reachable in prod today with the public anon key and one RPC call, exactly as the story claimed. MITIGATION PROVEN (this is new): setting supautils.hint_roles = '' in /etc/postgresql-custom/supautils.conf and restarting Postgres turns the same call into a clean 'ERROR: permission denied for function' with the connection alive. Verified by flipping the config both ways twice. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT FOR WHOEVER APPLIES IT: this CANNOT be done from SQL or from a migration — supautils rejects 'ALTER SYSTEM SET supautils.hint_roles' with 'permission denied to set parameter' even as the postgres superuser. It is a postgresql.conf change on the host (Coolify), i.e. an operator action, and no migration in this repo can substitute for it. AC5 CORRECTED: the story listed ~8 reachable entry points; the real number is 14, enumerated from the live schema rather than by hand (select ... where not has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE') over the 160 public functions): admin_adjust_credits, bump_cache_signal, credit_ledger_reconciliation, delete_account, get_cache_signal, latest_schema_migration, reconcile_payout_link, record_registered_number_sighting, record_style_code_observation, refund_grade, release_job_lock, reserve_guarantee_pool_drawdown, revoke_grade_credits, try_acquire_job_lock. AC3 SHIPPED: scripts/db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs, wired into verify.mjs --db and db-migrations.yml. It is ADVISORY (continue-on-error), NOT a gate, and that is a deliberate call recorded in both files: the stock image is vulnerable today, so gating would turn every migration PR red on arrival, and this repo already has the lesson that a permanently red guard gets switched off (US-1927 notes). Flipping it to a hard gate is step ONE of the mitigation, not a follow-up. VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS with the final code: RED on the stock image (all three assertions fire), GREEN with hint_roles cleared. Three self-inflicted defects were found and fixed while building it, all the same class as bugs this repo has shipped before — an assertion on pg_postmaster_start_time() that CANNOT EVER FIRE (a backend SIGSEGV is handled by crash recovery; the postmaster never restarts), and twice using execFileSync where the text being asserted on is on STDERR (both the 'permission denied' string and the Postgres server log), which silently compared against an empty string. AC1 — A SAFE PROBE THAT WAS MISSED, worth trying before anything invasive: US-1927's 2026-07-18 note records that calling latest_schema_migration() against PROD as anon returned 42501 permission denied rather than a crash. latest_schema_migration is on the list of 14 above, so IF that observation was a real prod call it is evidence prod does NOT reproduce — and it cost nothing. Treat it as a lead, not proof: it is second-hand, and it is not certain the 42501 came from Postgres rather than from PostgREST's own check. Re-running that one read-only call is the cheapest next step and is not an attack. EVIDENCE POINTING THE OTHER WAY: vault/10-ops/backups.md:161 records the 2026-06-12 restore drill against 'the same Supabase image as prod' pinned at 17.6.1.106 — the exact image that crashes here. Nothing in the repo pins the prod tag, so that drill log is the only signal, and it suggests prod DOES reproduce. These two point opposite ways; resolve with the read-only check the story already specifies (read the image tag and 'show supautils.hint_roles' over psql). KEPT passes:false: AC1 (prod image determination) and AC2 (apply the mitigation) are operator actions on the Coolify host that cannot be done or validated from here, and AC4 (unblock 00527 / US-2282) must stay blocked until AC2 is done — applying it into an unpatched image would take the entry points from 14 to ~80. | 2026-08-15 AC1 HAS AN ANSWER, MEASURED AGAINST PROD, AND THE 2026-08-08 NOTE CONTAINS ADVICE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUSED THE OUTAGE. Correction first, because it is the dangerous half: that note says re-running latest_schema_migration() as anon against prod is 'the cheapest next step and is not an attack'. It IS the attack. latest_schema_migration is on this story's own list of 14 functions anon cannot execute, so calling it as anon is probe (1) verbatim, and if prod reproduces, that call restarts the production database. The 2026-08-04 note says the opposite and is right: NOT TESTED AGAINST PROD ON PURPOSE, the test IS the denial of service. Do not run it. THE SAFE PROBE THAT DOES WORK, and it is new: the crash is in the supautils hint path, and hint_roles gates the hint for TABLE denials too, which never crash on any image. So ask for a table anon has no grant on and look for the hint. NEW scripts/probe-supautils-hint.mjs does exactly that, with a CONTROL leg first, because a null hint has two causes that look identical from a client (supautils is quiet, or PostgREST is not forwarding hints at all) and the second reads as mitigated on every stack including the crashing one. The control asks for a near-miss column name so POSTGRES emits its own hint. MEASURED ON PROD TODAY, https://api.gradethread.com: control grade_reports.certificate_i returns 42703 with hint 'Perhaps you meant to reference the column grade_reports.certificate_id.' - so hints demonstrably reach the client; subject applied_migrations as anon returns 42501 'permission denied for table applied_migrations' with hint NULL - no supautils hint at all. On the crashing image that same request carries 'Grant the required privileges to the current role with: GRANT SELECT ON public.applied_migrations TO anon;' (this story's probe 4). SO: anon is not in prod's supautils.hint_roles, or supautils is not adding hints there, and either way the path the segfault lives in is not running for anon. That is EVIDENCE prod does not reproduce, not proof - it shares a gate with the function path rather than testing it, it says nothing about authenticated or service_role, and the direct test remains the attack. WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE CHAIN: this is the first real signal against reproduction, and it outweighs the backups.md restore-drill inference (which only says prod ran the same image tag in June, not how it is configured today) because it is a live reading of the running stack rather than a document. AC2's operator step is now cheap to confirm rather than to perform: read 'show supautils.hint_roles' over psql and expect anon to be absent. If it is absent, AC1 closes as 'prod does not reproduce', AC2 is already satisfied, and US-2282/00527 unblocks. VERIFIED: 4 cases in src/test/supautils-hint-probe.test.ts, the load-bearing one being that a failed control returns INCONCLUSIVE regardless of the subject - a security probe whose broken state looks like a pass is worse than none. Sabotage-verified by disabling the control branch, which reddened exactly that case. tsc -b clean. | 2026-08-15 THE PSQL READ IS NOW PART OF THE ONE-PASTE FILE. §23 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql (and the console variant) asks for hint_roles and carries the reading guide: NULL or empty means the hint path is not running, prod does not reproduce, and 00527/US-2282 unblock; a value containing anon means the mitigation comes first and cannot be done from SQL at all. It also repeats, in the file the operator is actually looking at, that confirming by calling a revoked function IS the outage. The verification standard for this file is 'executed, not read', and these three sections were NOT executed: Docker is down on this host so there was no throwaway Postgres to run them against. Stating that plainly because the rest of the file was executed and the difference matters. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, against PROD rather than against the migration text: every column named exists (users.billing_source, users.billing_environment, users.buyer_billing_environment probed through PostgREST, where a missing column answers 42703 naming it). AND ONE BUG WAS CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE IT SHIPPED: I first wrote §23 as `SHOW supautils.hint_roles`, which raises 'unrecognized configuration parameter' when supautils is not loaded and, under ON_ERROR_STOP=1, would have killed the rest of the operator's session — the exact failure this file's own header promises it cannot cause. It is now current_setting('supautils.hint_roles', true), which answers NULL instead, and NULL is itself the finding.

userStories.title: Prod Postgres + storage host has no full-disk encryption — a pulled or reclaimed VPS disk is readable plaintext
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the block device holding prod Postgres and the Supabase storage volume to be encrypted at rest, so that a decommissioned, snapshotted or physically seized Contabo disk does not hand over every grade, user address, credit ledger row and garment photo in plaintext.
acceptanceCriteria: The prod host's Postgres data directory and the Supabase storage volume (STORAGE_DIR=/var/lib/supabase/storage, per vault/10-ops/backups.md:75) both sit on a LUKS-encrypted block device — verified by 'lsblk -o NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT' showing crypto_LUKS under the mountpoint, not by reading a runbook.

The LUKS passphrase/keyfile is stored in the same secrets manager as the other prod secrets and is listed in vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md's rotation table with its rotation procedure, alongside EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

A documented unlock path exists for unattended reboot (keyfile on a separate volume, or clevis/tang, or an explicit 'operator must unlock manually' decision) and vault/10-ops/incident-response.md records what happens to uptime if the host reboots while nobody is available to unlock.
vault/10-ops/deploy.md gains a section stating the encryption status of the prod volumes, so a future operator rebuilding the host does not silently recreate it unencrypted.

SECURITY.md's at-rest paragraph (currently line 44, which claims only 'Marketplace OAuth tokens are encrypted at rest') is updated to state the volume-level posture accurately — either encrypted, or explicitly not.
userStories.notes: | 2026-08-12 THE RUNBOOK A REBUILD FOLLOWS DID NOT MENTION THIS AT ALL. vault/10-ops/deploy.md had zero occurrences of encrypt, volume or LUKS across every heading, while vault/10-ops/encryption-at-rest.md:48-49 has stated for weeks that both the Postgres data directory and Supabase Storage STORAGE_DIR are unencrypted, and :147-149 names this story. So the fact existed and the document someone would actually follow while provisioning a replacement host did not carry it - which is precisely how a host gets rebuilt without encryption and the window closes again. ADDED a "If you are rebuilding the host, not just deploying to it" section to deploy.md, before Related, saying plainly that provisioning is the ONLY moment volume encryption is cheap (adding it later needs downtime and a restore), naming both volumes, and linking [[encryption-at-rest]] as the owner of the inventory rather than restating it. It also names the two decisions that have to be made first, because both have an uptime consequence and neither is mine: how the volume unlocks at boot (a keyfile on the same disk defends a reclaimed drive but not a live compromise; clevis/tang or a manual passphrase each trade automation for reboot behaviour), and where that key is recorded - which is [[key-rotation]] job once one exists. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: AC2 (list the key in key-rotation.md) - there is no LUKS key to list until the operator creates one, and adding a placeholder row to a key inventory is how a key inventory stops being trustworthy. AC5 is already satisfied: SECURITY.md:40-45 defers to encryption-at-rest.md as SSOT and that note carries the gap. WHAT REMAINS IS HOST WORK: the LUKS setup itself and the unlock-path decision. vault:lint --strict clean at 172 notes.

userStories.title: Offsite backups are uploaded unencrypted — R2 credentials alone yield a full plaintext database dump
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want every backup artifact encrypted with a key we hold before it leaves the host, so that compromise of the Cloudflare R2 bucket or its rclone credentials does not expose the entire production database and every uploaded garment photo.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/ops/backup-postgres.sh encrypts the pg_dump artifact with a key held by GradeThread (age or gpg) BEFORE the 'rclone copy' at line 55, so the object landing in r2:gradethread-backups/pg is ciphertext. R2's own server-side encryption does not satisfy this AC — the threat model is a leaked R2 credential, which server-side encryption is transparent to.

The .sha256 sidecar (backup-postgres.sh:50) is computed over the ENCRYPTED artifact, so the existing 'dump plus its .sha256 in the last 24h' offsite check from vault/10-ops/backups.md:50 still verifies what is actually stored.

scripts/ops/backup-storage.sh either encrypts the storage mirror or the runbook explicitly records the decision not to, with the reason — an rclone sync of the raw storage volume today exposes every submission image, including grading label photos, to anyone with the R2 credential.

scripts/ops/restore-postgres.sh and restore-drill.sh decrypt before pg_restore, and a restore drill against an ENCRYPTED artifact passes and is recorded in the drill table at vault/10-ops/backups.md:162 — an encryption change that breaks restore is worse than no encryption.

The backup encryption key is added to vault/10-ops/key-rotation.md's rotation table with a stated procedure, and the procedure covers the window where old ciphertext in the 30-day-retention bucket was written under the previous key.
vault/10-ops/backups.md documents that losing the backup key means losing every backup, and names where the key is stored (a reference, never the value).

OPERATOR: the mechanism is built and verified; production has not moved. Generate the age keypair, put the identity somewhere off the DB host (never on it - the host holds only the recipient half on purpose), set BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT, install the updated scripts/ops/*.sh on the DB host, and run one drill against an ENCRYPTED artifact. Until then every offsite object is still plaintext.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-08 ALL SIX ACs BUILT AND VERIFIED END TO END; kept passes:false because the mechanism is done and PRODUCTION HAS NOT MOVED — the keypair does not exist yet and the updated scripts are not on the DB host. Docker plus an age implementation were both available here, so nothing below is reasoned-about; every claim was run. MECHANISM (AC1): backup-postgres.sh encrypts the dump with age to BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT before rclone copy. PUBLIC-key on purpose — the DB host holds only the recipient half, so it can encrypt but not decrypt, and rooting the database box does not also hand over the offsite archive. It FAILS CLOSED: with RCLONE_REMOTE set and no recipient it exits 1 having called rclone ZERO times (verified with a stub rclone on PATH that logs its argv). Happy path verified the same way: the only two objects handed to rclone are .dump.age and .dump.age.sha256, never the plaintext .dump. AC2: the sha256 is computed over the CIPHERTEXT, which is what the bucket actually holds. FOUND AND FIXED A PRE-EXISTING BUG WHILE DOING IT, and it would have bitten during a real recovery: sha256sum \"\" wrote the sidecar with the ABSOLUTE staging path (/backups/pg/...), and restore-postgres.sh verifies with sha256sum -c, which resolves whatever path the sidecar records. On a scratch host that path does not exist, so verification failed with 'No such file or directory' — i.e. the checksum could never have passed on any genuine offsite restore, only on the machine that wrote it. Both branches now cd first and record a BARE FILENAME. Proved by backing up to one directory, copying the artifact to another (what an offsite fetch does), and restoring successfully from there. AC3 (storage): the age-per-file approach does NOT fit an incremental rclone sync of thousands of objects — pre-encrypting per run breaks rclone's diffing. The mechanism is rclone's own CRYPT REMOTE (client-side, per object, sync still works), which is config-side, so what the script can enforce is refusal: backup-storage.sh reads 'rclone config show <remote>' and exits unless type = crypt, overridable only by an explicit STORAGE_BACKUP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=1. Checked against the config rather than the remote's NAME, because a remote called 'r2crypt' that is not of type crypt would otherwise read as safe. AC4 (the one the story warns about most — 'an encryption change that breaks restore is worse than no encryption'): restore-postgres.sh detects a .age input, verifies the checksum BEFORE decrypting (checking the stored object, not a derived one), decrypts to a mktemp file chmod 600 created empty before any plaintext is written, and shreds it via an EXIT trap — verified 0 leftover temp files after a run. restore-drill.sh now performs the encrypt/sha/verify/decrypt round-trip on EVERY run under an EPHEMERAL keypair, so the drill never touches the real key and a drill can no longer silently measure a procedure prod does not use (opt out only via DRILL_SKIP_ENCRYPTION=1). Drill PASS recorded in vault/10-ops/backups.md: migration 00559, 5 users, 20 submissions, 375 RLS policies all matched, dump 1s restore 5s. NOTE ON DRILL QUALITY: the first run passed with every row count at ZERO, which makes each 'OK' vacuous — a data-restore failure would have passed too. Seeded real rows and re-ran; the recorded numbers are from that run. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, all four directions: no recipient => refuses and uploads nothing; no identity => refuses to restore; a single flipped byte in the ciphertext => checksum FAILS before decryption is attempted; and the drill asserts the .age artifact is NOT still a readable pg_dump (a passthrough bug would otherwise leave everything green while backups shipped in the clear). DOCS (AC5, AC6): key-rotation.md gains both keys in the rotation table plus a full section — the asymmetry that makes this key unlike every other one is that losing it is SILENT (backups keep running, /health stays green, the bucket keeps filling; you find out at the only moment it matters), and the 30-day-retention window means deleting the old identity on rotation day destroys most of the recovery range, so both identities are kept until the lifecycle rule has aged out the last object under the old one. backups.md gains an Encryption section saying plainly that losing the key loses every backup with no escrow and no support path, requiring two independent durable homes neither of which is the machine being backed up, and naming Infisical as the home for the identity (a reference, never a value) while noting it is NOT an app env var and no deployment surface reads it. Also corrected the offsite-freshness check there: the objects to look for are now .dump.age / .dump.age.sha256, and a bare .dump in the bucket means an OLD script is still deployed and the nightly is shipping plaintext. encryption-at-rest.md is the security-questionnaire page and carries these scripts in its code_refs, so it was updated in the same change per the vault same-commit rule — its store table and gap paragraph now say 'mechanism yes, production not yet' and explicitly tell the reader NOT to upgrade the customer-facing answer until the key exists on the host. vault:lint --strict green, all four ops scripts pass bash -n. REMAINING (operator, on the Contabo/Coolify DB host — this is the whole gap): (1) age-keygen the pair, put the identity in Infisical plus one offline copy, put the public recipient in /etc/cron.d/gradethread-backups; (2) rclone config a crypt remote and repoint the storage cron at it; (3) deploy the updated scripts to /opt/gradethread. Step-by-step is in the MANUAL callout in vault/10-ops/backups.md. Until all three are done prod backups remain plaintext, which is why this stays open. WORTH KNOWING: age has no Windows package, but rage (the Rust build, format-compatible) does — 'scoop install rage', then AGE_BIN=rage. Every script takes AGE_BIN, which is how the drill ran on this host.

userStories.title: Postal addresses and phone numbers are stored as plaintext columns while OAuth tokens next to them are AES-GCM encrypted
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want my home or business street address stored encrypted the same way my marketplace tokens are, so that a single leaked database dump or a SQL-injection read does not hand an attacker a mailing list of resellers with valuable inventory at those addresses.
acceptanceCriteria: public.users.ship_from_address (jsonb, added by 00325_user_business_shipping_profile.sql) and public.users.business_phone are stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext produced by services/edge-functions/src/lib/crypto-aes.ts encryptToken(), with the owning user id passed as the aad option so a ciphertext copied onto another user's row fails to decrypt (US-268 tenant binding, same pattern as the marketplace token columns).

public.measure_card_requests street fields (ship_name, address_line1, address_line2, city, postal_code — added by 00351_measure_card_requests.sql) are encrypted the same way, keyed to owner_user_id. state and country stay plaintext so the fulfillment export can still filter and sort by region without decrypting every row.

A migration ships the US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL (safe to re-run on any prior state), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in services/edge-functions/src/lib/schema-version.ts in the SAME commit, and the self-record footer inserting its version into public.applied_migrations.

The migration backfills existing plaintext rows to ciphertext, and the read path tolerates both during the rollout — a row that does not parse as v1:/v2: is returned as-is rather than throwing, so a partial backfill cannot 500 the Settings page.

Every edge route that reads or writes these columns decrypts/encrypts at the boundary and stays tenant-scoped per US-268, with a case added to services/edge-functions/src/tests/tenant-isolation_test.ts.

The eBay ship-from location prefill (US-1442's original consumer) still populates correctly end to end after the change — verified against the flipdesk-ebay.ts path that consumes ship_from_address, not just by unit test.
A test asserts that decrypting a ship_from_address ciphertext with a DIFFERENT user id as aad throws, proving the tenant binding is real.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-08 AC2 DONE, AC4 and AC7 DONE for it, and AC1 IS BLOCKED ON A PREREQUISITE THE STORY DOES NOT NAME. The prerequisite is the most important thing in this note, because AC1 reads like a one-file change and is not. AC1 IS NOT REACHABLE YET, and it is a fact about the write path rather than a preference. src/pages/settings.tsx:306 writes users.business_phone and users.ship_from_address DIRECTLY from the browser with supabase-js under RLS, and 00526_users_self_update_allowlist.sql (restated in 00550) explicitly allowlists both columns. They are READ the same way in three places: settings.tsx:141-143, flipdesk/marketplaces.tsx:202 and lib/account-export.ts:54. EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is an edge-only secret and must stay one, so encrypting those two columns first requires moving that write and all three reads behind an edge route. Doing the crypto without that would lock a seller out of their own Settings page and would break the account export. iOS and Android touch neither column (grepped both trees, zero hits), so the migration surface is web-only - which makes the prerequisite tractable, just not free. AC3's migration is ALSO wrong for AC1 as written: ship_from_address is jsonb, so storing an envelope string means a type change, not just a value change. AC2 SHIPPED, and measure_card_requests is the more sensitive of the two anyway - it holds a full street address, not a ship-from region. It has none of AC1's problem: deny-all RLS (rls-guard_test.ts:181), written by exactly ONE edge route (flipdesk-measure.ts POST /card-request) and read by exactly ONE (admin-measure-cards.ts listRequests, feeding the fulfilment CSV). Both sides already run where the key lives. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/measure-card-pii.ts encrypts ship_name, address_line1, address_line2, city and postal_code with encryptToken() and the OWNER'S USER ID AS AAD. state and country stay plaintext exactly as AC2 asks, and a test asserts the two lists cannot overlap - the export filters and sorts by region, and an equality on an encrypted column cannot use an index or match at all. AC7 IS THE CASE WORTH READING. Encrypting a column is easy to do in a way that helps nobody: one key, no binding, and anyone who can write a row can copy another tenant's ciphertext onto it and read the plaintext back through the normal decrypt path. AES-GCM covers additionalData with the auth tag, so A's address fails to decrypt under B's id. That is the US-268 property expressed in cryptography instead of in an .eq() someone has to remember, and it is asserted rather than assumed. THE WRITE ENCRYPTS BEFORE THE INSERT, not after it. An insert-then-update would leave the address readable in the WAL and in any replica that saw the first version, which is most of what a stolen-dump scenario actually covers. A key misconfiguration answers 503 rather than falling back to plaintext. THE READ USES THE ROW'S OWNER, never a caller-supplied id, and decrypts PER ROW: one un-backfilled or unreadable row must not take out the operator's whole fulfilment queue, so a failure blanks that address and logs the id. A blank that says so beats a plausible-looking wrong address on a mailing label. AC4 - TOLERANCE PLUS A BACKFILL, and the backfill is a SCRIPT because it cannot be a migration. pgcrypto offers AES in CBC/ECB only: no GCM, therefore no auth tag, therefore no AAD - a SQL backfill would produce ciphertext the edge cannot read carrying none of the security this story is about. NEW scripts/backfill-measure-card-pii.ts is DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT (--apply to write), refuses to start without EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY (encrypting under the wrong key would make every address silently unreadable while still LOOKING encrypted), and scopes its update by owner_user_id as well as id so a mis-derived id cannot write one seller's owner-bound ciphertext onto another's row, where it would be permanently undecryptable. Re-running it is a no-op: already-encrypted values pass through, so an interrupted run resumes with no bookkeeping. Double-wrapping would be UNRECOVERABLE, since the inner envelope's AAD is invisible from the outside, and a test pins that. MY OWN TEST HAD A BLIND SPOT AND THE SABOTAGE FOUND IT. The route-text check forbade `city:` in the insert, so an accidental SHORTHAND `city,` - which writes the same plaintext and overrides the spread - stayed green. It now checks both forms per column, which has to be per-column rather than 'no shorthand allowed', because `state,` and `country,` are legitimately shorthand there. 10 cases in NEW src/tests/measure-card-pii_test.ts. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FIVE WAYS: the AAD dropped from both sides (the cross-tenant case fires), postal_code removed from the encrypted set, the insert overriding a column in shorthand form, the same in explicit form, and the admin export decrypting with a caller-supplied id. Each reddened with its own message; all files restored and re-run green. REMAINING: AC1 (needs the settings write + three reads moved behind the edge first), AC3 (no migration was needed for AC2 - the columns are already text and ciphertext fits; AC1's jsonb column is what would need one), AC5's tenant-isolation case, AC6 (the eBay ship-from prefill end-to-end, which consumes users.ship_from_address and is therefore downstream of AC1). VERIFIED: deno lint clean across 1426 files, deno check clean including the backfill script, full edge suite 5999 passed / 0 failed / 170 ignored. | 2026-08-09 AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC7 DONE for users.*; AC6 REMAINS and its premise was wrong. THE PREREQUISITE THE LAST PASS NAMED IS BUILT. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/user-shipping-pii.ts encrypts users.ship_from_address and users.business_phone with encryptToken() and THE ROW'S OWN ID AS AAD; NEW GET/PUT /api/account/shipping-profile in routes/account.ts is the only reader and writer; NEW src/lib/shipping-profile.ts is the only browser client; 00567_users_shipping_pii_edge_only.sql restates guard_users_protected_columns WITHOUT the two columns so a direct browser write now RAISES instead of storing plaintext over ciphertext. The three client reads the last pass listed are all moved: settings.tsx seeds its form from the edge query (a useState initialiser would have captured the pre-fetch nulls forever, hence the seed effect keyed on dataUpdatedAt), flipdesk/marketplaces.tsx prefills the eBay location dialog from the same shared query key, and lib/account-export.ts drops both from its supabase select and fills them from the edge best-effort, because a GDPR export must not fail wholesale over one optional field. AC3'S JSONB WORRY WAS UNFOUNDED, and the resolution is better than the type change would have been. ship_from_address is jsonb and an envelope is a string, but a jsonb column holds a JSON STRING SCALAR perfectly well, so no ALTER COLUMN TYPE and no table rewrite under a lock. Better still, the JSON TYPE becomes the AC4 discriminator: an OBJECT is a row the backfill has not reached, a STRING is an envelope. No prefix sniffing on a value that could legitimately start with anything. 00567 therefore contains NO DDL at all - one CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION plus two column comments - and its risk is entirely in APPLY ORDER, which PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md spells out: apply the SQL, NOTIFY pgrst, redeploy the edge, THEN push. Pushing first ships a frontend calling a route that does not exist. AC4: NEW scripts/backfill-user-shipping-pii.ts, dry-run by default, refuses to start without EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, re-runnable because an already-encrypted value passes through rather than double-wrapping (which is unrecoverable - the inner AAD is invisible from outside). Read tolerates both formats, so there is no deadline on running it. AC5: BOTH edge readers were found and both decrypt at the boundary - routes/account.ts and routes/flipdesk-logistics.ts (the label quote). Grepped functions/, ios/ and android/: zero hits, confirming the last pass's finding. A containment case is appended to tenant-isolation_test.ts, and the property it pins is the one that is easy to get wrong here: this endpoint reads c.get('userId') and NOT c.get('workspaceOwnerId'), because a manager inside A's workspace must not read A's home address, so the case sends X-Workspace-Owner pointed at A and asserts B's write never lands on A. AC7: 12 cases in NEW user-shipping-pii_test.ts including the cross-tenant AAD rejection for BOTH columns and the refusal to encrypt with an empty owner id (an unbound ciphertext any account could read is worse than a failed write). ALSO ADDED, because the type system could not carry this alone: UserRow.business_phone and .ship_from_address are now typed EncryptedColumn (a branded string), so reaching for .line1 is a compile error, and NEW src/test/encrypted-user-columns.test.ts catches the two shapes tsc cannot see - reading the column off the cached auth-store profile row, and naming it inside a supabase-js call against users. Negative-verified by planting a select on the users update in settings.tsx. AC6 IS NOT DONE AND ITS TARGET DOES NOT EXIST. It asks for verification 'against the flipdesk-ebay.ts path that consumes ship_from_address'. GREPPED: flipdesk-ebay.ts does not read that column and never has. POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/policies/location takes postal_code/city/state FROM THE REQUEST BODY - the column only ever fed the browser-side PREFILL of that dialog, which now reads the edge query instead. The genuine edge consumer is flipdesk-logistics.ts (the label quote), and two cases were added to ebay-logistics_test.ts for it: an undecrypted envelope yields NO address rather than a partial one (so the failure is a 409, not a wrong shipping label), plus a source guard that the handler decrypts before calling toLogisticsAddress - needed because a seller with no address and a seller whose address failed to decrypt otherwise produce the identical 409 and nothing would notice the decrypt going missing. WHAT REMAINS FOR AC6 is a live end-to-end pass that cannot be run from here: create an eBay merchant location from a seller account whose address was written BEFORE this change and then backfilled, and buy one label, confirming the ship-from on both. Needs real eBay credentials and a seeded prod-like account. VERIFIED: deno lint clean, deno check src/main.ts + the backfill script clean, full edge suite 6177 passed / 0 failed, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite green, vault:lint --strict clean. HELD MIGRATION 00567 - do NOT push until it is applied to prod. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (second half of the day): the HELD-migration claim in this story's notes is now STALE. Migrations 00550 and 00567 are on origin/main - verified with git ls-tree against a freshly fetched origin/main, not inferred - and the branch has zero unpushed commits. A held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word is no longer merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop on a branch that is not frozen. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: pushed is not applied. Whether the SQL has been run against prod is an operator fact this checkout cannot observe, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is the file that tracks it. Read that, not this prose. Recorded because prd-lint caught it the same hour the branch moved, which is the guard working as intended - it went unactioned for weeks before, and a stale freeze cost real sessions. | 2026-08-12 THE VAULT INVENTORY WAS UNDERSTATING OUR OWN POSTURE, and that is the half of this story that was quietly wrong. SECURITY.md:40-45 names vault/10-ops/encryption-at-rest.md as the single source of truth for security questionnaires, and that note still listed all seven columns THIS STORY ENCRYPTED under "What is NOT encrypted at the column level": measure_card_requests ship_name/address_line1/address_line2/city/postal_code (encrypted at lib/measure-card-pii.ts:57-61,101 with aad: ownerUserId) and users.ship_from_address + users.business_phone (lib/user-shipping-pii.ts:116,164). Its headline sentence - the one someone actually answers a questionnaire from - said "OAuth tokens and a handful of cache values are encrypted by the application. Nothing else is." WHY THE DRIFT GUARD NEVER FIRED: neither lib was in the note code_refs, so vault:lint had nothing to compare against; the note reviewed date was 2026-08-08 and the users.* half landed 2026-08-09. A note that omits the file it describes is invisible to the guard that exists to catch exactly this. Both libs are now in code_refs, so the same omission cannot recur silently. Both read paths tolerate either form so the mixed state is safe, but "these columns are encrypted" is only true of the whole table after scripts/backfill-measure-card-pii.ts and scripts/backfill-user-shipping-pii.ts run against prod with EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY set.
