userStories.title: [HELP CENTER] Converge support_kb_articles into help_articles so the assistant and the help page cannot disagree
userStories.description: Found while building US-2574: support_kb_articles (00183, US-830) already exists. It is the ONLY corpus the AI Support Assistant may answer from, it has slug/title/body_md/category/audience/is_published/versioned revisions and a weighted FTS column, and it has an admin editor at /admin/support/kb. What it does NOT have is any public web surface: nothing in functions/ or src/ renders it, so it is invisible to Google, to answer engines and to logged-out customers. help_articles (00602) is the superset and owns the web surface. Leaving both is the two-copies-must-agree failure in its worst form: the assistant would quote one wording of an answer while the public page shows another, and nobody would notice until a customer pasted a screenshot.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide and record the direction in a vault note: help_articles becomes the single corpus and support_kb_articles is retired. The assistant reads help_articles.

Migrate every support_kb_articles row into help_articles: category maps onto the 14 help categories, audience public->public and subscriber->members, is_published->status, body_md->body_markdown with body_html rendered from it.

Point the retrieval tool (services/edge-functions/src/lib/support-tools.ts + agent-tools.ts) at help_articles, and give help_articles the weighted tsvector + GIN index support_kb_articles has (US-2577 adds the search column; reuse it rather than adding a second).
The assistant must NEVER quote a members or internal article to an anonymous asker. Its retrieval passes the asker through visibilitiesFor() like every other read.
Retire /admin/support/kb and its route, or redirect it to /admin/content/help. One editor, not two.
Keep support_kb_revisions history: either migrate it alongside or archive it, but say which in the note. Do not drop edit history silently.
A test asserts the assistant cannot return an article the asker could not have read on the public site.
userStories.notes: [FOUND DURING US-2574 2026-08-14] Consumers of support_kb_articles today: services/edge-functions/src/lib/agent-tools.ts, lib/support-tools.ts, main.ts, routes/admin-knowledge-base.ts, tests/support-kb-search_test.ts. No consumer in functions/ or src/ - confirmed by grep, which is what proves it has no public surface. This story is deliberately AFTER the help center ships (priority 83, behind US-2592) so the convergence moves content into a finished home rather than a half-built one. Until it lands the two corpora coexist, and the help center is the one customers see. | PARTIAL 2026-08-15 — AC1 and AC6 DECIDED AND WRITTEN, AC2's mechanism BUILT, and the rest is deliberately NOT shipped yet because the order is not symmetric. AC1: vault/20-domain/help-corpus-convergence.md records the direction (help_articles is the single corpus, support_kb_articles retires), the full field mapping, the nine-to-fourteen category map and the ordering constraint. AC6 DECIDED: support_kb_revisions is ARCHIVED IN PLACE - kept, not migrated, not dropped. help_articles has no revision mechanism to migrate INTO, so migrating would mean inventing one to hold history for a corpus that no longer takes edits; dropping is refused because edit history is the record of who changed a customer-facing answer and this repo's rule is that such a record is not the actor's to erase. AC2 MECHANISM: NEW scripts/migrate-support-kb-to-help.mjs, dry-run by default, with the mapping as pure exported functions so it is testable without a database. A SCRIPT RATHER THAN A MIGRATION because help_articles.body_html is NOT NULL and the public reader renders from it - markdown-to-HTML in SQL is not something to invent for a one-off when scripts/seed-help-articles.mjs already has the tested renderer the seeded corpus went through. THREE REFUSALS, WHICH ARE THE ACTUAL ENGINEERING: an unmapped category throws rather than guessing a destination for a customer-facing answer; an unmapped audience throws; and a slug collision STOPS the run by name rather than merging, because the unique index is case-insensitive and a collision means a hand-written help article already owns that URL. THE TEST FOUND A REAL CONTENT DEFECT: markdownToHtml handles ## and ### and NOT #, deliberately (the article title is the page h1, and all 83 seeded files start at h2). Nothing ever held the support KB to that convention, so a body written with # would have migrated into visible hash marks on a public page. demoteTopHeadings fixes it in the MARKDOWN, not just the HTML, so the /.md mirror and the page agree - patching the shared renderer instead would have been the wrong end, since its behaviour is right for the corpus it was written for. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: AC3 (repoint retrieval), AC4 (visibility filter), AC5 (retire /admin/support/kb), AC7 (the test that the assistant cannot quote what the asker could not read). Repointing before the data lands leaves the assistant reading an EMPTY corpus, where its designed behaviour is to say it does not know and offer a human - so the failure would be quiet, polite and total. Data first, then retrieval. VERIFIED: 17 cases in src/test/support-kb-to-help-migration.test.ts (17 passed), tsc -b clean, eslint clean, vault:lint strict clean at 178 notes. | PARTIAL 2026-08-15 (second pass) — AC3, AC4 and AC7 SHIPPED, BEHIND A FLAG THAT IS OFF. HELP_CORPUS_UNIFIED (unifiedHelpCorpusEnabled in lib/support-tools.ts) switches searchKnowledgeBase from support_kb_articles to help_articles, and agent-tools.ts fetchKbCatalog moves WITH it - a catalog listing one corpus while search reads the other would offer the operator titles the assistant cannot then quote. Both corpora already carry a weighted GIN-indexed search_tsv (00183 and 00603), so AC3's 'reuse it rather than adding a second' needed no schema work at all. WHY A FLAG AND NOT A SWITCH: the convergence has an ORDER, and the wrong order fails silently. Rows must land in help_articles first; flipping before they do leaves the assistant searching an empty table, and its designed behaviour on an empty result is to say it does not know and offer a human. That is a total outage of the support assistant wearing the face of a polite answer, and nobody files a bug about a polite answer. Default OFF, only 1/true turn it on, and six junk values are pinned as not-on. AC4 IS SHARPER THAN THE AC TEXT AND SHIPPED THAT WAY: the AC says never quote members or internal to an ANONYMOUS asker; the code says NOBODY reaches internal through this tool - not a subscriber, not an admin asking through the assistant. internal did not exist in the old two-value model and holds operator runbooks, and retrieval hands its output to a model that quotes what it is given, so a caller-dependent exception is the one somebody gets wrong later. visibleHelpVisibilities is exported so the guard asserts the mapping itself rather than only its effects. AC7: six new cases in src/tests/support-kb-search_test.ts (13 passed) - off-by-default still answering from the retired corpus, junk flag values, on-reads-help-and-not-the-old-table, anonymous never reaching members, NOBODY reaching internal, and a draft never surfacing. The fake DB's text matcher now spans body_md AND body_markdown, so a case cannot pass by silently reading the other corpus; the help fixture keeps a DIFFERENT row in support_kb_articles for the same reason. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED TWICE: widening visibleHelpVisibilities to include internal reddened the AC4 case alone, and forcing the corpus on reddened the off-by-default case. deno check + deno lint clean. env-reference.md documents the flag with the ordering warning. REMAINING: AC2 (run the migration against prod - operator), AC5 (retire /admin/support/kb, which should follow the flag flip rather than lead it).

userStories.title: The verify-email step is unmeasured, and a link opened on a second device dead-ends
userStories.description: As a person who just signed up, I want to finish verifying my email wherever I opened it, so that I actually reach the product. Signup emits four analytics events and verification emitted none, so a drop-off between the two can be asserted and not located. Two mechanisms sit behind it: whether GoTrue sends the branded hook email (a token_hash link plus a 6-digit code, both device-independent) or its own template (a PKCE code that only exchanges in the browser that started the signup), and whether SES delivers the mail at all.
acceptanceCriteria: The verify funnel is measurable end to end: an event for the check-your-email screen, for a resend, for a verification success, and for each distinct failure reason.

A confirmation link opened on a second device stops dead-ending. The client detects that it holds no PKCE verifier and offers the 6-digit code path instead of a fifteen-second spinner and advice that cannot work.
Whether the branded auth-email hook is configured is visible from outside in one unauthenticated GET, and the health line states the CONSEQUENCE rather than only the missing variable.
OPERATOR: confirm AUTH_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET on the edge and GOTRUE_HOOK_SEND_EMAIL_* on the auth container, then re-measure /health/ready features.auth_email_hook.
OPERATOR: confirm SES is out of sandbox and confirmation mail is actually delivered. No client event can tell an unopened email from an undelivered one.
Once the funnel has data, state the real drop-off number and decide whether anything further is worth building.
userStories.notes: AC1-AC3 DONE 2026-08-15; AC4-AC6 are operator work and the story stays open on them. ⚠ THIS STORY WAS FILED AFTER THE WORK, and the reason belongs in the record: the pass began from a backlog row I read as 'GT-001 Fix the verify-email drop-off, priority high'. No such story exists - not in prd.json, not in prd.archive.json, not in git history, and the string 'verify-email drop-off' appears nowhere in the repo. It was a misread on my part, caught by prd.json refusing to contain the id I tried to edit. The engineering below is real and verified; only its provenance was wrong, and it is filed here rather than attached to a phantom. AC1: four events in src/lib/analytics-events.ts - signup.confirm_sent (the check-your-email screen, i.e. the denominator), signup.confirm_resend (at: signup|confirm), signup.email_verified (via: link|code), signup.verify_failed (reason: cross_device_pkce|link_expired|code_expired|code_rejected|callback_timeout). Emitted from signup.tsx, auth-confirm.tsx and auth-callback.tsx. Before this, signup emitted trial.started and signup.buyer and verification emitted nothing, so the funnel ended immediately before the part in question. AC2 IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT, and it is a real dead end rather than a UX nicety. The client runs PKCE (supabase.ts flowType). GoTrue's built-in confirmation template links at emailRedirectTo, which arrives carrying ?code=, and supabase-js can only exchange that code with the verifier it stored in the SIGNING-UP browser's localStorage. Open the mail on a phone and the exchange cannot succeed on any timescale - but auth-callback.tsx waited the full 15s and then said 'Sign-in is taking longer than expected. Please try signing in again.', which is advice that produces the same nothing every time. NEW src/lib/auth-pkce.ts (hasPkceVerifier / isCrossDeviceConfirmation) scans storage for a *-code-verifier key - by SUFFIX deliberately, because the key embeds the project ref, which on a self-hosted domain is the first host label (api), and a key rebuilt wrongly would route every user to recovery. Read ONCE on mount, because a successful exchange DELETES the verifier and a later read would call a completed sign-in a failure. Cross-device gets a 4s wait (long enough for an exchange that finished before mount to surface as a session) and then a card that says the link completes in the other browser, offers /auth/confirm for the 6-digit code, and states that nothing is wrong with the account. AC3: new auth_email_hook feature group in env-validation.ts, production-only, plus a new optional FeatureGroup.whenMissing that appends the CONSEQUENCE to the readiness line - 'missing: AUTH_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET' names a variable and not the fact that cross-device verification is broken meanwhile, which is exactly the shape that let release=dev sit in prod for three weeks (US-2001). MEASURED, not assumed: GET /health/ready today returns no auth_email_hook key at all, so whether prod sends branded device-independent mail or GoTrue defaults was invisible from every endpoint we serve. ALSO MEASURED IN THE SAME CALL: schema reports {expected:00603, applied:00606, status:ahead} - prod has 00604-00606 applied while the running edge image expects 00603, so the edge is behind the database, not the other way round. VERIFIED: env-validation_test.ts 26 passed (4 new), health + ops-health + env-debug 41 passed, auth-pkce.test.ts 9 passed (new), src/lib/__tests__ + auth-pages-have-seo 1074 passed across 81 files, tsc -b clean, eslint clean, ui:check 0 blocking 0/0 noise, deno lint + deno check clean on env-validation.ts. Negative-verified twice: dropping the whenMissing append reddened its own case, and the smtp case pins that it never fires on a satisfied group. DOCS: vault/40-growth/analytics-event-registry.md gains the funnel table and the note that these events see only people who reach the app (an undelivered email and an ignored one have the same client-side shape); vault/10-ops/env-reference.md gains the one-line curl that answers whether the hook is on.

userStories.title: Migration 00594 never ran in production, so the FlipDesk Overview RPC does not exist
userStories.description: Measured 2026-08-15, minutes after the US-2603 completeness check reached production: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns {"expected":"00606","applied":"00606","status":"match","missing":["00594"],"unexpected":["00479"]}. The maximum matches and there is a hole underneath it, which is the exact state the max-only check cannot see. 00594 creates public.flipdesk_overview_metrics, the single RPC behind the FlipDesk Overview page (src/hooks/use-flipdesk-overview.ts:120, which throws on error), so that page is failing for every seller. The file ends with an unconditional self-record INSERT, so absence from applied_migrations means the SQL did not run - this is not a missing-footer artefact. THE OBVIOUS HYPOTHESIS WAS TESTED AND REJECTED: the function is language sql, whose body Postgres validates at CREATE time, so a drifted public.items_full would make CREATE FUNCTION fail outright. All 15 columns the body references (brand, grade_value, id, item_title, list_date, list_price, listing_status, listing_watchers, net_profit, sale_date, sale_price, sale_status, status, target_price, updated_at) were probed against prod through PostgREST and every one resolves - a missing column returns 42703 naming it, which is a distinguishable and completely safe read. So the view is not drifted on names and CREATE FUNCTION should succeed; 00594 looks simply never executed rather than attempted-and-failed. Column TYPES were not probed, which is the one gap in that reasoning. SEPARATELY, unexpected: 00479 is a version recorded in the database with no file in any commit - scripts/migrations-lint.mjs:67 already lists 00479 as never authored - which is the signature of a generate_series range backfill writing over a gap.
acceptanceCriteria: 00594 is applied to production and /health/ready returns an empty or absent schema.missing.
If CREATE FUNCTION fails, the error is recorded here: it is evidence of drift in items_full and is worth more than the retry.
The FlipDesk Overview page is confirmed loading for a real signed-in seller, not just inferred from the migration applying.

PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md's 00594 section is corrected: it was flipped to APPLIED on the reasoning that the version sits below the recorded maximum and carries a footer, which is exactly the inference the same file warns against 160 lines earlier.

No action on unexpected: 00479. It is a KNOWN phantom, recorded at scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql:100 and scripts/migrations-lint.mjs:67 - never authored, and the reason 00480+ were numbered around it. This AC exists so the next reader does not re-investigate it.

OPERATOR: apply supabase/migrations/00594_flipdesk_overview_metrics.sql against prod, then re-read curl -fsS https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready | jq .schema and expect missing to be empty. If CREATE FUNCTION errors, paste the error rather than retrying - it is evidence of drift, and the column-name half of that hypothesis has already been ruled out.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-15 FILED FROM MEASUREMENT, and one piece of it is already fixed. The gap itself needs the owner (see the OPERATOR criterion) - what shipped in this commit is the part that was mine: 00479 is now excused by name in KNOWN_PHANTOM_VERSIONS (services/edge-functions/src/lib/schema-version.ts), because it is documented in two places as never authored and is the reason 00480+ were numbered around it, so reporting it on every read would put a permanent entry in a field whose only job is to be empty. The list is written BY HAND and deliberately NOT derived from migrations-lint's KNOWN_GAPS, which would look tidier and be wrong: KNOWN_GAPS also holds 00527, the SECURITY DEFINER lockdown parked as .BLOCKED behind US-2403, and 00527 appearing as applied is the one thing this field must scream about. Four new cases in schema-version_test.ts (51 passed) pin both directions plus 'the list may not grow'; sabotage-verified by adding 00527 to the list, which reddened exactly the two cases that exist to catch it. One pre-existing case had to move: US-2009's phantom example WAS 00479, which now passes for the wrong reason, so it uses an unrecognised version instead and the comment says why. FOR US-2009's PROMOTE-TO-FATAL FOLLOW-UP: the plan was to make a missing version fatal once prod was observed clean. Prod has now been observed and it is NOT clean, so promote after 00594 lands and missing comes back empty - and when promoting, make MISSING fatal while leaving UNEXPECTED a warning, since only one of the two means the database is behind the code. DOCS: PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md's 00594 section is flipped to NOT APPLIED with the retracted reasoning quoted verbatim rather than deleted, the top banner names the live gap, and vault/10-ops/migrations-process.md carries the finding under 'The max hides a hole'. | 2026-08-15 A VERIFICATION QUERY FOR AFTER THE APPLY. §25 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql checks both halves — the applied_migrations row AND the existence of public.flipdesk_overview_metrics in pg_proc — because either alone can be true while the other is not. It points at the authoritative check rather than replacing it: curl /health/ready and read schema.missing, since a bare status:match is precisely what this gap hid behind. The verification standard for this file is 'executed, not read', and these three sections were NOT executed: Docker is down on this host so there was no throwaway Postgres to run them against. Stating that plainly because the rest of the file was executed and the difference matters. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, against PROD rather than against the migration text: every column named exists (users.billing_source, users.billing_environment, users.buyer_billing_environment probed through PostgREST, where a missing column answers 42703 naming it). AND ONE BUG WAS CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE IT SHIPPED: I first wrote §23 as `SHOW supautils.hint_roles`, which raises 'unrecognized configuration parameter' when supautils is not loaded and, under ON_ERROR_STOP=1, would have killed the rest of the operator's session — the exact failure this file's own header promises it cannot cause. It is now current_setting('supautils.hint_roles', true), which answers NULL instead, and NULL is itself the finding.

userStories.title: Every push to main restarts the production edge, including doc-only commits
userStories.description: Coolify auto-deploys the edge service on any push to main, with no path filter, so a commit that touches only PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md or prd.json rebuilds the image and rolls the container. Each roll is a short window where Traefik has no healthy backend and the public API answers 'no available server' - observed directly on 2026-08-15: two consecutive probes of /health returned 503 and the third returned 200, with /health/ready clean on five reads immediately after. Nothing was wrong; that IS the rollover. The cost is small per push and this repo pushes often - six times in one afternoon during a backlog loop, which is six avoidable 503 windows on the seller-facing API plus six image builds. WHY IT ALSO MATTERS FOR DIAGNOSIS, which is the sharper half: 'no available server' is the documented signature of an edge event-loop HANG (vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md). A routine doc push producing the same string as a real incident trains whoever sees it to shrug, and the one time it is not a rollover is the time that costs an outage.
acceptanceCriteria: The edge redeploys only when something that ships inside its image changed: services/edge-functions/** and the files its build reads.
A commit touching only markdown, prd.json or src/ does not roll the edge container.
The mechanism is recorded in vault/10-ops/deploy.md next to the auto-deploy line, so the next person does not rediscover it from a 503.
The frontend half is checked at the same time: Cloudflare Pages rebuilds on every push too, which is cheaper but not free.

OPERATOR: this is a Coolify setting, not a repo change. In the edge resource, set the build/watch path filter to services/edge-functions (Coolify calls it Watch Paths). Nothing in this repository can do it, and nothing here can verify it either except by pushing a doc-only commit and watching whether the container rolls.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-15 FILED FROM A LIVE OBSERVATION, not from reading config. During a backlog loop, curl https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returned the bare string 'no available server'. Two consecutive /health probes then returned 503 and the third 200, with five clean /health/ready reads immediately after - so it was a Coolify rollover from the push a minute earlier, not an incident. THE DIAGNOSTIC COST IS THE REAL POINT: 'no available server' is the documented signature of an edge event-loop HANG (vault/10-ops/edge-hang-vs-crash-loop.md, and a memory note says the same). A routine doc-only push producing the identical string as a genuine incident teaches whoever sees it to shrug, and the one time it is not a rollover is the time that costs an outage. Six pushes in one afternoon meant six of these windows on the seller-facing API, every one of them for a commit that changed markdown or prd.json and nothing that ships inside the edge image. The fix is a Coolify Watch Paths setting on the edge resource; nothing in this repo can make it or verify it.

userStories.title: A garment with no readable tag cannot be graded at all, and that is a real garment, not an edge case
userStories.description: image-quality.ts REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES is ['front','back','label'] at severity 'block', applied at grading-pipeline Step 4b BEFORE any confidence scoring, so a submission with no label photo abstains to needs_photos and is never graded. US-2304 confirmed that requirement on purpose (owner, 2026-08-03) and it is the right call for the common case - a FlipDesk item without a tag used to be charged, burn one vision call per image, abstain, and be refunded, which cost the seller a round trip and cost us the AI spend. But the note that recorded the decision also recorded what it left open, and nothing carries it: SOME GARMENTS GENUINELY HAVE NO READABLE TAG. Lululemon and several athletic brands print a cut size on a heat-transfer label that wears off entirely; resale-grade basics are often tagless by design; vintage tags are frequently cut out by the original owner. Those sellers are not photographing badly, they are photographing what exists, and today the product tells them to add a photo they cannot take. The pipeline is not wrong to want provenance evidence - the question is what stands in for a tag when there is no tag, and whether a grade without it is capped rather than refused.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide what a seller with a genuinely tagless garment is asked to photograph instead: a size/wash print inside the collar, a hem or seam construction shot, or nothing at all with the grade capped.

If a substitute is accepted, the abstention becomes a CAP rather than a refusal, composed through composeConfidenceCap like every other cap, lowering both the confidence and the reported ceiling (US-2299).
The seller is told this up front, in the client validator, not after paying and round-tripping.
The grading prompt is told the tag is absent rather than left to infer it from a missing image, so it does not read the absence as evidence about the garment.
Measure first: how many submissions abstain on a missing label specifically, versus the other two required types. If it is rare, the honest answer may be a clearer refusal message and nothing more.

OPERATOR: run section 27 of scripts/prod-diagnostics-console.sql (AC5), which decides whether this story gets built at all. It counts submissions stuck in needs_photos by which required photo is missing. READ IT WITH ITS LIMIT: quality_feedback is nulled the moment a grade is produced, so this measures who is STUCK NOW, not how often it has happened - it undercounts by every seller who added the photo and succeeded. If 'label' is far ahead of front and back, the tagless case is real and worth building; if the three are level, it is ordinary incomplete uploads and the fix is upload-time guidance rather than a grading change.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-15 FILED FROM US-2304's OWN LEFT-OPEN NOTE, which had no story carrying it. That note said, verbatim, that the old comment's concern is real and that tagless garments are a product question 'r...' - the segment was truncated mid-sentence and nothing downstream picked it up. VERIFIED THE MECHANISM before filing rather than trusting the note: services/edge-functions/src/lib/image-quality.ts:80 is REQUIRED_IMAGE_TYPES = ['front','back','label'], line 83 puts all three in CORE_TYPES, and lines 129-136 raise a 'missing' issue at severity BLOCK for any absent one. So the refusal is real and it is unconditional. AC5 IS DELIBERATELY FIRST IN INTENT EVEN THOUGH IT IS LAST IN ORDER: this may be rare enough that the honest answer is a clearer refusal message and nothing else, and building a substitute-photo path before measuring picks a fix blind - the same mistake US-2288's notes describe. The measurement is narrow: of submissions that abstain, how many abstain on 'label' specifically rather than on front or back. NOT A DUPLICATE OF US-2397, which made a missing fabric CLOSE-UP a cap instead of an abstention. That story's reasoning is the precedent this one would follow, and its rule is the constraint: a cap must lower the confidence AND the reported ceiling (US-2299), or the next provenance boost lifts the stored number straight back over it. | 2026-08-15 AC5's MEASUREMENT IS NOW ONE PASTE, and writing it surfaced a limit worth knowing before anyone reads the number. §27 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql counts submissions currently in needs_photos, grouped by which required image_type raised a blocking 'missing' issue. THE LIMIT: quality_feedback is set to NULL the moment a grade is produced (00069), so every seller who added the photo and succeeded has already erased their own row. §27 therefore measures who is STUCK, not how often this has happened. That is arguably the more actionable set - it is the people the product is failing right now - but it is a different question from the one AC5 asks, and reading it as a history would undercount by exactly the recoveries. Said in the section itself, not just here. ONE PIECE OF DEFENSIVE SQL THAT IS NOT DRESSING: jsonb_array_elements RAISES on a non-array, and a single malformed quality_feedback row would end the operator's session before every section after it. The CASE guard yields an empty array instead. Same class as the SHOW bug caught in §23 an hour earlier, which is twice now that the failure mode of this file is 'kills the session' rather than 'returns the wrong answer'. READING GUIDE: label far ahead of front/back is the tagless case and this story is worth building; roughly level across the three is ordinary incomplete uploads and the fix is upload-time guidance, not a grading change.

userStories.title: Nothing we serve can tell whether the Pages-origin rate-limit bypass is armed
userStories.description: Every SSR'd public page - blog, certificate, OG image, sitemap - is rendered by a Cloudflare Pages Function that fetches the edge service server-to-server. So a thousand readers arrive at the edge through ONE Pages worker and drain a single per-IP bucket between them. US-781 built the bypass for exactly that: Pages sends x-pages-origin: <CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET> and pagesOriginBypass() (middleware/rate-limit.ts:187) lets the hop through. It is deliberately inert unless BOTH sides carry the same value, and that is the right default - but it means the failure is silent. Nothing renders wrong while it is unset; the pages simply start answering 503 'Temporarily unavailable' to whoever is unlucky once enough traffic arrives at once, Googlebot included, which is the audience the whole SSR layer exists for. OBSERVED 2026-08-15: a burst of public-page fetches drove /sitemap.xml to 503 four consecutive times, then it recovered. That burst was a probe rather than real traffic, so it is NOT proof the secret is unset - and that is the point. Nothing we serve could tell the difference, and /health/ready listed ten feature groups with no entry for this one.
acceptanceCriteria: /health/ready reports whether the bypass is armed on the edge side, production only, and the readiness line states the CONSEQUENCE rather than only the variable name.
The line says outright that setting it on the edge alone changes nothing, because the same value has to be on the Cloudflare Pages project - the specific mistake this bypass invites.

OPERATOR: read features.pages_origin_bypass on /health/ready after the next edge deploy. If it says missing, set CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET to the same value on BOTH the Coolify edge service and the Cloudflare Pages project, then re-read it.

OPERATOR: with it armed, re-run a burst against /sitemap.xml and confirm it no longer 503s. That is the only end-to-end proof both halves match, since a mismatched secret looks exactly like an unset one from outside.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-15 THE EDGE HALF SHIPPED IN THIS PASS; both remaining ACs are operator. NEW pages_origin_bypass feature group in services/edge-functions/src/lib/env-validation.ts, production-only, using the whenMissing field US-2597 added so the readiness line states the CONSEQUENCE rather than a variable name. It says outright that every SSR'd blog, certificate and sitemap visitor shares ONE per-IP rate-limit bucket, that the public pages start answering 503 to real readers and to Googlebot under load, and - the specific mistake this bypass invites - that setting it on the edge alone changes nothing because the same value has to be on the Cloudflare Pages project. HOW THIS WAS FOUND, because the method is the reusable part: probing all 42 registered public routes and then sampling 89 sitemap URLs against production drove /sitemap.xml to 503 four consecutive times, with the body 'Temporarily unavailable - please retry shortly.' That string is upstreamUnavailableResponse() in functions/_shared/blog-render.ts, i.e. the Pages Function could not reach the edge - NOT a Pages-side limit. Reading rate-limit.ts:187 showed the bypass is inert unless both sides carry the same secret. I CANNOT SAY WHETHER IT IS SET, and that is the finding rather than a gap in the investigation: my burst was a probe, not real traffic, so a 503 under it is consistent with a working limiter; but /health/ready listed ten feature groups and none of them covered this one, so nothing we serve could tell the two apart. VERIFIED: 28 cases in env-validation_test.ts (2 new), both directions; sabotage-verified by removing 'rate-limit bucket' from the consequence text, which reddened the missing-line case alone. deno check clean, tsc -b clean. env-reference.md documents the variable as needing BOTH surfaces. Two vault notes bumped after re-reading: runbook-copies.md (third consecutive no-op bump, now recorded as the guard working rather than being noisy) and ai-crawler-policy.md (drift came from a neighbouring function, nothing it describes changed). | 2026-08-15 MEASURED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE BYPASS IS OFF. The check shipped in this story deployed and answered its own question within the hour: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns features.pages_origin_bypass = 'missing: CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET'. So the secret is NOT set on the edge, pagesOriginBypass() returns false for every request, and the 503s observed earlier were real rather than an artefact of my probe. WHAT THAT MEANS QUANTITATIVELY, read out of main.ts:806-811: /api/content/public/* is rateLimiter(60, 60_000) - sixty requests per minute per IP, fail-closed - and every SSR'd blog post, certificate, OG card and sitemap build reaches it through ONE Cloudflare Pages worker. So the entire public site shares a single 60/min bucket, worldwide, and past that everyone gets 'Temporarily unavailable'. The same shape applies to the publicReadLimiter surfaces at :818. THE CONNECTION NOBODY HAS MADE, and it may be the more important half: US-2095 is 'the gate for all content work' and exists because the domain has an unresolved indexing problem, with seo-geo-strategy.md and seo-indexability.md deliberately contradicting each other about whether to grow or trim pSEO. The sitemap advertises 514 URLs. Googlebot crawling those goes through the same worker and the same 60/min bucket, so a normal crawl session would be answered with 503s partway through - which Google records as a server error and backs off from. That is a mechanical explanation for an indexing problem that has so far been argued about as a content problem, and it costs nothing to rule in or out: fix the secret, then re-read the Page-indexing report. PRIORITY RAISED to 5 (from 35). This is not a visibility nicety any more; it is a live cap on public traffic. THE FIX IS TWO PLACES AND NEITHER IS IN THIS REPO: set CF_PAGES_ORIGIN_SECRET to the SAME value on the Coolify edge service and on the Cloudflare Pages project. Setting one alone changes nothing, which is exactly the mistake the readiness line warns about.

userStories.title: Wire the remaining unmonitored crons into the ledger, starting with the eBay token refresh
userStories.description: US-2616 made the cron fleet monitor name the eight registry entries it never examines. This closes them. ebay-token-refresh is done: its handler already gated on requireJobSecret, so it was reachable as a cron all along and only the recordEbayCron mount was missing. The rest split into three shapes, and only one is a mount. THREE ARE UNREACHABLE, not merely unrecorded: ebay-orders-sync, photo-archive and reconciliation-sweep sit behind authMiddleware with no requireJobSecret branch, so they 401 before the handler runs - pinned in cron-registry-drift_test.ts KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS since US-2310. They can neither run nor be seen not running, and each needs a job-secret branch plus a server-side tenant loop. TWO USE A DIFFERENT SECRET: content-tick and content-digest authenticate with CONTENT_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET while recordEbayCron keys on the X-Internal-Job-Secret header, so recording them means teaching the recorder a second header rather than adding a mount. TWO ARE ONE-OFFS: passport-backfill and cert-integrity-backfill have no cadence to miss, which is correct and permanent.
acceptanceCriteria: ebay-token-refresh records to cron_runs and is examined by cron-fleet-health.
content-tick and content-digest record, via a recorder that recognises CONTENT_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET, or the reason they cannot is written at the registry entry.
The three unreachable crons get a requireJobSecret branch and a server-side tenant loop, so they can actually be invoked by a scheduler - and then recorded.
The shrink-only list in cron-fleet-governance_test.ts loses a name for each one closed; the one-offs stay and are labelled permanent.

OPERATOR: after the next edge deploy, expect cron-fleet-health to report ebay-token-refresh as STALLED if its Coolify task does not exist. That is the finding, not a false positive - the detector computes expected slots from the schedule rather than from prior runs, so this is the question is-this-task-installed answering itself for the first time.

OPERATOR: delete the Coolify scheduled task named ebay-orders-sync. Its registry entry is gone (ebay-order-backstop was already the same half-hourly sweep, working), so the task now hits a seller route that answers 401 and nothing in the repo can see it - the drift check catches a MISSING task, never an extra one.

OPERATOR: change the photo-archive Coolify task URL to /api/jobs/photo-archive. It has pointed at /api/flipdesk/images/archive, a seller route, so the nightly sweep has answered 401 every night since it was created. The old URL still works for a signed-in seller and is deliberately left alone.

OPERATOR: change the reconciliation-sweep Coolify task URL to /api/jobs/reconciliation-sweep. Same fault as photo-archive - it pointed at a seller route and has answered 401 every night. /api/flipdesk/reconciliation/run stays as the seller Auto-match button.
userStories.notes: PARTIAL 2026-08-15 — AC1 DONE, and it was two lines once the premise was checked rather than trusted. The registry said 'served under /api/flipdesk/* - not in the ledger', which states WHERE the job lives, not a reason it cannot be seen; flipdesk-ebay.ts:633 shows the handler gating on requireJobSecret, so it has always been invocable as a cron. main.ts mounts recordEbayCron by path and simply did not cover this one. Mounted it and flipped recorded to true; COOLIFY.md and vault/10-ops/launch-checklist.md regenerated from CRON_REGISTRY (the drift guard caught the stale table, correctly). WHY THIS ONE FIRST: if the hourly refresh stops, seller eBay tokens expire and their listings stop syncing - a failure with no symptom until a seller notices, which is exactly what the fleet alert exists to catch. EXPECT AN ALERT, and it is not a false positive: detectMissedTicks computes expected slots from the SCHEDULE rather than from prior runs, so a job whose Coolify task does not exist reads as stalled from the first elapsed hour. That is the question 'is this task actually installed?' answering itself for the first time in the ledger - recorded as an OPERATOR criterion so nobody silences it as noise. THE SHRINK-ONLY GUARD DID ITS JOB: US-2616's case asserted ebay-token-refresh BY NAME as part of the blind spot, so fixing the job reddened the test instead of letting it keep passing on a quietly smaller set. The list now carries a reason beside each remaining name. VERIFIED: 28 cases across cron-registry-drift_test.ts and cron-fleet-governance_test.ts pass, deno check + deno lint clean, tsc -b clean, vault:lint strict clean. | 2026-08-15 (second pass) AC2 DONE, AND THE PREMISE IN THE STORY WAS WRONG. This story said content-tick and content-digest could not be recorded because they authenticate with CONTENT_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET while the recorder keys on X-Internal-Job-Secret. Reading content-scheduler.ts:74 shows that is a confusion between the HEADER and the SECRET: both schedulers read the same X-Internal-Job-Secret header and merely validate it against a different env var. recordEbayCron only asks which header ARRIVED - the handler still decides whether the value is valid - so it needed a mount, not a second header. Both are now recorded, and the blind spot is 8 -> 5 (three unreachable + two one-offs). ONE REAL WIDENING WHILE THERE: the recorder now treats X-Internal-Job-Signature as a cron call too. The content, newsletter and drip schedulers all accept the signed variant (HMAC + freshness + single-use), so keying only on the static header would have recorded a caller using the WEAKER path and silently skipped the same job on the stronger one - a ledger gap that appears exactly when someone improves the caller. NEW GUARD, and it caught a false positive on its first run, which is the part worth keeping: 'every recorded cron outside /api/jobs/* has a recorder mounted' immediately flagged drip-tick and newsletter-kickoff. Both were fine - they call recordCronRun DIRECTLY inside their handlers, with per-branch statuses the middleware could not produce (the drip tick records a 404 no-such-campaign as its own error row). So the guard was too narrow, not the code, and it now accepts either mechanism. Had I trusted it, the next reader would have been sent to fix two things that were already right. WHY THIS GUARD MATTERS AT ALL: recorded:true is a CLAIM, and nothing checked it. Flipping it without a recorder is worse than leaving it alone - cron-fleet-health starts expecting ledger rows that can never arrive, so the job reads as permanently stalled and the alert is about the wiring rather than the job, which is how an on-call learns to ignore the channel. VERIFIED: 13 cases in cron-registry-drift_test.ts and 17 in cron-fleet-governance_test.ts, all green; sabotage-verified by deleting the content-tick mount, which reddened the new guard naming that exact endpoint. COOLIFY.md and vault/10-ops/launch-checklist.md regenerated. deno check + lint clean, tsc -b clean. | 2026-08-15 (third pass) THE FULL EDGE SUITE CAUGHT THREE FAILURES FROM THIS WORK, and one was a pre-existing bug two steps from anything I edited. Running the whole suite rather than only the touched files is what found it: 6852 passed, 3 failed. (1) cert-public-allowlist_test.ts — display_title (US-2613) is route-added like 'title' itself, so it belongs in ROUTE_ADDED; recorded there with a pointer to why it has no counterpart in the public_grade_reports view. (2) cron-runs_test.ts — the case used /api/flipdesk/ebay/oauth/refresh as its example of an UNRECORDED path, which this story just made recorded. Swapped to ebay-orders-sync, the honest example now (US-2310: it 401s on every fire, so there is genuinely nothing to record), plus a new case asserting the three newly-recorded paths resolve. (3) ops-jobs_test.ts — THE IMPORTANT ONE. isRunnableJob is built from the recorded flag, and its comment claimed that meant 'served at /api/jobs/*'. That was a PROXY, and it decides which jobs get a Run-now button in the admin console. Following it found the real defect: admin-ops.ts sent FLIPDESK_INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET to every job, while FOUR recorded jobs authenticate against their own env var — drip-tick, newsletter-kickoff, content-tick, content-digest. So Run-now on those has always answered 401, and an operator reading a red result concludes the JOB is broken when the CALLER was. drip-tick and newsletter-kickoff have been in that state for a long time; this story added two more of the same shape and made the pattern visible. FIXED: new jobSecretEnvFor() resolves secretEnv ?? DEFAULT_JOB_SECRET_ENV, admin-ops uses it, and a missing secret now NAMES the variable rather than saying 'Job runner secret not configured' — which sent whoever read it to check the one they already had set. The registry has carried secretEnv since US-1561 for exactly this and nothing consumed it. GUARD-THE-GUARD: one case pins the four by name, another DERIVES the expectation from CRON_REGISTRY for every recorded job, so a new job with its own secret cannot be silently sent the default. | 2026-08-15 (fourth pass) AC3 IS ONE THIRD DONE, AND THE FIX WAS A DELETE. I had the /jobs/orders-sync route written - requireJobSecret, an acquireJobLock, a stalest-first owner scan over marketplace_connections, triggerEbaySyncForUser per owner, bounded fan-out - before checking whether that job already existed. IT DID. ebay-order-backstop (US-1965, routes/jobs-ebay-order-backstop.ts) is the same */30 fleet sweep through the same triggerEbaySyncForUser, plus a 15-minute freshness window and a PURE unit-tested selector (selectBackstopOwners) my version did not have. So the scheduled eBay orders sync has been running correctly this whole time, and the ebay-orders-sync registry entry described a second, permanently-401ing copy of it. Shipping my route would have put two fleet sweeps on one eBay rate-limit bucket on the same cadence. Reverted it and deleted the entry instead. WHAT MADE IT LOOK LIKE MISSING WORK: the entry pointed at /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/pull, a SELLER route that reads workspaceOwnerId ?? userId, so it 401d on every fire; recorded:false meant no ledger row; and US-2310 had already classified it as needing 'a job-secret branch plus a server-side tenant loop'. Every signal pointed at build-the-loop and none of them pointed at look-for-the-existing-job. The tell I should have caught earlier is that the tenant-isolation suite already had a case titled 'eBay order-backstop job rejects a user JWT' describing a sweep over EVERY active tenant's connection. SCOREBOARD: KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS 3 -> 2 (photo-archive, reconciliation-sweep remain, and both should be checked for an existing equivalent before either gets a loop written). The fleet monitor's blind spot 5 -> 4. CRON_REGISTRY 78 -> 77, which reddened the deploy.md count guard correctly and was fixed there. NEW GUARD, and it is a guard against RE-ADDING rather than a shrink-only list: a case asserts ebay-orders-sync is absent from CRON_REGISTRY and that ebay-order-backstop is present, so if the backstop is ever deleted the assertion fails instead of quietly protecting nothing. Sabotage-verified by re-adding the entry, which reddened exactly that case. OPERATOR, and it is new work rather than a re-statement: DELETE the Coolify scheduled task named ebay-orders-sync. It has never succeeded and the drift check cannot see an EXTRA task, only a missing one - so nothing in the repo will ever tell you it is still there. VERIFIED: edge suite 6862 passed / 0 failed, deno check + deno lint clean, tsc -b clean, vault:lint --strict clean, runbook-sync clean. COOLIFY.md, CRON_SETUP.md and vault/10-ops/launch-checklist.md regenerated from the registry; vault/10-ops/cron-schedule-governance.md records the look-for-the-existing-job lesson under 'what is still manual', which is where the extra-task risk was already written down. | 2026-08-15 (fifth pass) AC3 IS TWO THIRDS DONE — photo-archive now has the /jobs/ route and fleet loop, and this time building it was the RIGHT call, which is only knowable because I ran the check the last pass told me to run. Grepped for an existing photo-archival job: there is none, and /api/flipdesk/images/archive is the only implementation. The opposite of ebay-orders-sync, and the two together are the rule: LOOK FOR THE EXISTING JOB FIRST, THEN WRITE THE LOOP. The search costs a grep; the wrong answer costs a duplicate sweep. WHAT SHIPPED. flipdesk-images.ts:/archive was a 130-line inline handler; it is now three pieces. loadArchivablePhotos(ownerId|null, limit) holds the eligibility predicate ONCE - the ownerId and the fleet read share it deliberately, because the predicate carries the US-979 PII refusal (tag/tag_2/certificate close-ups live in the PRIVATE bucket and archival rewrites photo_url to an UNAUTHENTICATED public R2 URL), and a second copy of that filter written for the cron is exactly how a private tag gets published. archiveOwnerPhotos(ownerId) is the per-owner work, returning {ok,result}|{ok:false,error} so the route can still failSafe and the cron can count. listOwnersWithArchivablePhotos(limit) is the fleet read, named so it cannot be mistaken for a seller-facing one at a call site - the null branch is NOT exported. NEW routes/jobs-photo-archive.ts at /api/jobs/photo-archive: requireJobSecret, a 900s lock (this job does the work rather than dispatching it, unlike the sync crons), owners resolved from the photo ROWS and never from the request, bounded at 25 owners per nightly tick with a scan limit 20x that - a scan capped at 25 ROWS could resolve one owner and report the fleet done. eligible_owners reports the whole eligible fleet so a cap that stopped keeping up is readable rather than inferable. R2 unconfigured returns skipped rather than 500, because a nightly 500 for an optional integration is how an on-call learns to ignore the ledger. TENANT ISOLATION: two cases in tenant-isolation_test.ts (user JWT -> 401, bogus secret -> 401). The route publishes to public URLs across every tenant, so the job secret is the only thing between a signed-in user and a fleet-wide publish. THE GUARD I ACTUALLY CAME AWAY WITH, and it is bigger than this story. cron-registry-drift's US-2310 check SKIPS /api/jobs/* with the comment 'every handler there gates on the secret'. That was an assumption nobody had checked, and it is the MORE dangerous half: a cron behind authMiddleware with no secret branch merely 401s forever, while an /api/jobs/* route with no secret branch is callable by anyone on the internet, and several of them sweep every tenant. New case asserts it from source for all 40 routes. IT TOOK THREE CORRECTIONS AND EVERY ONE WAS THE GUARD, NOT THE CODE. (1) Scanning only routes/ reported seven safe handlers as ungated - email-retry lives in lib/email-retry.ts, sync-reaper in lib/sync-run-lock.ts. (2) Non-recursive lib/ missed two more in lib/appstore/ and lib/google-play/. (3) Anchoring handler names on a 'handle' prefix missed watchdogHeartbeatHandler, which puts the word at the other end; it matches any identifier called with (c) now. Each time I read the named handler before touching it, and each time it was already correct. A guard that names a safe route is worse than no guard, because whoever checks the first name deletes the rest. AND ONE SABOTAGE THAT PASSED WHEN IT SHOULD NOT HAVE, which is the part worth keeping: the first version took a fixed 700-character window after each app.post, which SPILLED into the following routes - so a neighbour's handler name satisfied this route's check. Deleting the photo-archive gate left the guard green. The window now ends at the next top-level app.* declaration. An over-wide window is the failure mode that makes a guard look like it works. SCOREBOARD: KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS 2 -> 1 (reconciliation-sweep alone), blind spot 4 -> 3, CRON_REGISTRY 77 (photo-archive changed endpoint, it was not added or removed). OPERATOR: change the photo-archive Coolify task URL to /api/jobs/photo-archive - recorded as an acceptance criterion. The old URL still serves the seller's own Archive button and is left alone. VERIFIED: full edge suite green, deno check + deno lint clean across 1547 files, tsc -b clean, vault:lint --strict clean. Sabotage-verified by deleting the new route's requireJobSecret, which reddened the new guard naming that exact endpoint and nothing else. COOLIFY.md, CRON_SETUP.md and vault/10-ops/launch-checklist.md regenerated. | 2026-08-15 (sixth pass) AC3 DONE. KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS IS ZERO and US-2310 is closed. reconciliation-sweep, the last of the three, gets the same treatment as photo-archive. RAN THE CHECK FIRST, as the rule now says: nothing else reconciles payout_imports. guarantee-pool accrues and reconciles the GUARANTEE pool; ebay-notification-reconcile reconciles eBay TOPIC SUBSCRIPTIONS. Neither touches a payout row. So the loop was real work, not a duplicate - which is the outcome the rule is meant to distinguish, and it produced a different answer for each of the three crons: one delete, two builds. WHAT SHIPPED. flipdesk-reconciliation.ts /run splits into reconcilePayoutsForOwner(userId) (the whole scoring + auto-match body, unchanged) and listOwnersWithUnreconciledPayouts(limit), the fleet read - named for the fleet rather than exposing an all-tenants flag on the per-owner function, so it cannot be reached by accident from a seller route. The route is now two lines. NEW routes/jobs-reconciliation-sweep.ts at /api/jobs/reconciliation-sweep: requireJobSecret, 900s lock, owners resolved from the PAYOUT ROWS never the request, oldest payout first (the one whose candidate sales are closest to ageing out of the date window), 50 owners a night with a scan limit 20x that, and one owner's failure cannot end the night. WHAT NOT RUNNING COST, stated because it is smaller than it sounds: payout rows sat unmatched, so a seller's books showed money arriving against no sale. The seller could always press Auto-match themselves - the sweep exists so they do not have to notice. TENANT ISOLATION: two cases in tenant-isolation_test.ts. This one writes into another tenant's BOOKS through reconcile_payout_link, so the job secret is the only gate between a signed-in user and a fleet-wide auto-match. THE ALLOWLIST IS KEPT AT ZERO RATHER THAN DELETED, and the assertion is === 0 rather than <= 3: a guard whose budget has slack is a guard that permits one more. There is no number left to spend, and a name appearing there again is now an obvious regression instead of a normal edit. The comment carries the three-different-answers lesson so the next reader checks before building. SCOREBOARD FOR THE WHOLE DAY: the fleet monitor's blind spot went 8 -> 2, and the two that remain are oneOff backfills, which is correct and permanent rather than a gap. KNOWN_UNREACHABLE_CRONS 3 -> 0. Six names came off: ebay-token-refresh, content-tick and content-digest by recorder mount; ebay-orders-sync by deletion; photo-archive and reconciliation-sweep by new /jobs/ routes. THREE OPERATOR ACTIONS, all Coolify and none of them visible to any check in this repo, because the drift check catches a MISSING task and never a wrong or extra one: delete ebay-orders-sync, and repoint photo-archive and reconciliation-sweep at their /api/jobs/ URLs. VERIFIED: full edge suite 6863 passed / 0 failed, deno check + deno lint clean over 1548 files, tsc -b clean, vault:lint --strict clean. Sabotage-verified twice: deleting the new route's requireJobSecret reddened the /api/jobs/* gate guard naming that endpoint alone, and reverting the registry entry to the old seller endpoint reddened the US-2310 reachability guard. COOLIFY.md, CRON_SETUP.md and vault/10-ops/launch-checklist.md regenerated; vault/10-ops/cron-schedule-governance.md records the 8-to-2 history and the three Coolify actions under 'what is still manual'.

userStories.title: The Help Center is live and empty: 83 articles are written and none are in the database
userStories.description: Measured against production on 2026-08-15. https://gradethread.com/help returns 200 and renders its header, search box and support CTA with ZERO article links. help_categories has all 14 seeded rows readable by anon, so the schema and the seed migration landed. help_articles returns [] to anon. Meanwhile content/help/ holds 83 written markdown articles and scripts/seed-help-articles.mjs exists to load them - it reads SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY from the environment and POSTs to /rest/v1/help_articles. It is wired to NOTHING: no npm script, no workflow, no cron, no deploy step. So an epic's worth of content sits in the repo while the page that exists to show it renders an empty state to customers and to Google. The indexability angle sharpens it: /help is in the sitemap, and a live thin-content hub is worse than no page at all on a domain that already has an unresolved indexing problem (US-2095).
acceptanceCriteria: The 83 articles in content/help/ are loaded into help_articles in production, and /help lists them.
Seeding is repeatable and idempotent rather than a one-off paste: re-running must update rather than duplicate, keyed on slug, which the script's existing slug read suggests it already intends.
Loading is wired to something - an npm script at minimum, ideally a step that runs on deploy - so the next 83 articles do not need someone to remember a command.
A check fails, or at least reports, when the Help Center hub renders zero articles. A page that serves 200 with no content is the failure mode nothing currently notices.

OPERATOR: run SUPABASE_URL=... SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=... node scripts/seed-help-articles.mjs against production, then re-check https://gradethread.com/help. The script needs the service-role key, which is why it cannot be automated from here.
userStories.notes: PARTIAL 2026-08-15 — AC3 and AC4 DONE; AC1, AC2 and the OPERATOR criterion remain. HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method generalises: verifying US-2572's schema against production rather than against the migration file. help_categories returns all 14 seeded rows to anon, so 00602 landed; help_articles returns []. Then GET /help — 200, 15689 bytes, and ZERO href="/help/..." links. The page renders its header, search box and support CTA over nothing. AC3: `npm run help:seed` now exists. The loader (scripts/seed-help-articles.mjs) was written and wired to NOTHING — no npm script, no workflow, no deploy step — which is how 83 finished articles ended up invisible with every check green. AC4: the production route probe (US-2611) grew a `mustLink` check for /help and /blog. A status code cannot see this failure: both are INDEXES whose whole job is to link to what they index, and an empty one still answers 200 with a full page of chrome. THE EXCEPTION IS DELIBERATE AND SHAPED LIKE THE REST OF THIS REPO'S: /help is in a KNOWN_EMPTY_INDEXES map, reported rather than failed, because the condition is TRUE TODAY and a check that is red on the day it ships gets ignored before it earns any authority — the reason db-denied-rpc-crash-check.mjs is advisory and what US-1927's notes record. The entry names the work that removes it and the list is shrink-only, so seeding the articles and deleting the line turns it into a real gate. Known gaps print BEFORE the verdict, so they are visible on a green run too. AC1/AC2 need the service-role key against production, which is the OPERATOR criterion. AC2 looks already satisfied by the script (it reads existing slugs first and skips them, with --force upserting via merge-duplicates) but that is unverified against a real database, so it is not being claimed. VERIFIED: 9 cases in src/test/public-routes-probe.test.ts; the probe exits 0 with the exception present and 1 without it, checked directly rather than through a pipe. eslint + tsc -b clean. ONE SELF-INFLICTED LOSS WORTH RECORDING: after sabotage-verifying, I restored the file with git checkout -- , which reverted to the last COMMIT and destroyed every uncommitted edit in it. Redone from a /tmp copy. Restore from a copy, not from git, when the work is not yet committed.

userStories.title: Two OG image endpoints return 200 with an EMPTY body, so blog posts and social cards preview blank
userStories.description: Measured against production 2026-08-15. GET /og/social/card (every ratio: landscape, square, story, pin) and GET /og/blog/<a real published slug> both return HTTP 200, Content-Type image/png, and ZERO bytes. A zero-byte PNG is a blank link preview everywhere it is used - and content-social-publish.ts auto-fills a /og/social/card URL whenever a post has no asset_image_url, while src/test/pinterest-rich-pins.test.ts pins media at https://gradethread.com/og/social/card?ratio=pin. So every auto-filled social image and every Pinterest pin is currently blank. THE MECHANISM, which explains why nothing caught it: card.ts wraps the render in try/catch and falls back to the branded card on a throw, but workers-og's ImageResponse STREAMS - the raster happens lazily as the body is consumed, after the Response object has been constructed and returned. A failure during streaming is therefore invisible to that try/catch, the catch never fires, brandedFallbackResponse never runs, and the client gets a well-formed 200 with nothing in it. This is the same class of problem that moved the certificate card off in-Function rendering: functions/og/cert/[id].ts's header records that workers-og inside a Pages Function exceeded the Free-plan Worker CPU limit and that streaming bytes from the edge is pure I/O by comparison. NOT EVERY OG ENDPOINT IS BROKEN, and the distinction matters: /og/grade-check renders 134022 bytes in-Function and is fine. /og/cert/:id serves 112844 bytes by proxying the edge. WHAT LOOKED FINE AND WAS NOT: /og/help/<slug> and /og/verified/<handle> both returned 133915 bytes, which is byte-for-byte /og-image.png - the static branded FALLBACK. They were serving the fallback because there is no such handle and help_articles is empty (US-2618), so their real-render path is untested and may share the same fault.
acceptanceCriteria: /og/social/card returns a real PNG for every ratio, and /og/blog/<slug> does for a published post.
A streaming failure reaches the fallback. The current try/catch cannot see one, so the fix is either to buffer the render before responding or to move it to the edge the way the certificate card was.

A check distinguishes a REAL render from the branded fallback. Both are 200 image/png, and the fallback is a fixed byte length, so 'it returned an image' is not evidence the renderer works - that is exactly how /og/help and /og/verified read as healthy.
Zero-byte responses are impossible to serve: any og endpoint returning 200 with no body should fail loudly rather than silently.
/og/help and /og/verified are re-checked once real content exists, since their render path has never actually been exercised.

OPERATOR: open the Cloudflare Pages real-time log and search for [og/social/card] render failed. Every failure now logs the actual exception with the endpoint named, and that one line is the cheapest path to the root cause by a wide margin - four hypotheses have been eliminated from the outside and the fifth cannot be tested without the Workers runtime.
userStories.notes: 2026-08-15 AC3 and AC4 DONE (detection); AC1, AC2 and AC5 are the fix and stay open. The production route probe now checks OG images two ways, because a status code sees neither. AC4: a 200 under OG_MIN_BYTES is a failure — /og/social/card returns 200, image/png, and ZERO bytes on every ratio. AC3 IS THE SHARPER ONE and it is why this was nearly missed entirely: /og/help/<slug> and /og/verified/<handle> both returned 133915 bytes and read as perfectly healthy. 133915 is byte-for-byte /og-image.png — the static branded FALLBACK. They were serving it because there is no such handle and help_articles is empty (US-2618), so their real render path has never executed and may share the same fault. The probe now measures the fallback at run time and flags any OG endpoint whose response is byte-identical to it, rather than hardcoding a number that a new fallback image would silently invalidate. GUARD-THE-GUARD: /og/grade-check stays in the list as a KNOWN-GOOD renderer (134022 bytes, a real in-Function workers-og render). A list containing only broken entries would pass forever on its own exceptions and never prove the check can recognise a good render. /og/social/card is a named, shrink-only exception so the scheduled job is not red on the day it ships — same reasoning as the /help entry. Deleting the line when the render is fixed turns it into a gate. WHAT THE FIX PROBABLY IS, for whoever picks up AC1/AC2: the try/catch in card.ts cannot see this failure. workers-og's ImageResponse streams, so the raster runs as the body is consumed, after the Response object has been constructed and returned — the catch never fires and brandedFallbackResponse never runs. Either buffer the render before responding (so a throw is catchable) or move it to the edge the way functions/og/cert/[id].ts already did, whose header records that in-Function workers-og blew the Free-plan Worker CPU limit and that streaming bytes from the edge is pure I/O by comparison. VERIFIED: 12 cases in src/test/public-routes-probe.test.ts; sabotage-verified by removing the /og/social/card exception, which reddened with '200 with 0 bytes — a blank preview'. tsc -b + eslint clean. | 2026-08-15 AC1/AC2/AC5 FIXED IN CODE; verification is a deploy away. NEW renderOgImage() in functions/_shared/og-template.ts awaits arrayBuffer() before answering, so the raster happens INSIDE the caller's try and a throw becomes the branded card the fallback was always meant to produce. A zero-length buffer throws too, because the observed symptom was SILENCE rather than an exception — whatever the root cause is, empty must never leave as success. APPLIED TO ALL FOUR in-Function endpoints, not just the two that are broken: social/card and blog/[slug] (both returning 0 bytes today), help/[slug] and verified/[handle] (which have NEVER rendered — every request took the not-found branch and served the fallback, which is why they looked healthy), and grade-check (which genuinely works at 134022 bytes, buffered anyway for the zero-byte guard). Leaving the healthy one different would mean the next reader finds two shapes and has to work out which is current. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT FIX EVEN THOUGH THE ROOT CAUSE IS STILL UNKNOWN: buffering does not guess at the cause. If Satori throws on the social/blog templates, the throw is now catchable and the console.error names the endpoint. If it is the Free-plan Worker CPU limit that moved the certificate card to the edge (functions/og/cert/[id].ts's header records exactly that), the failure still lands in the catch and still degrades to a branded card. Either way the outcome improves from a blank preview to a branded one, and the cause becomes visible in the logs instead of silent. GUARD: a new case in src/test/social-card.test.ts walks functions/og/ and fails on any `return new ImageResponse(` — the shape that streams past its own try/catch. Sabotage-verified by reverting grade-check, which reddened naming that file. A second case pins the zero-byte throw in the helper. TWO SELF-INFLICTED MESSES WORTH RECORDING, both from the same root: a scripted import rewrite whose regex matched ACROSS import statements scrambled three files (names ended up on the wrong module); repaired by reading the originals out of git show and redoing them with the edit tool. And a heredoc ate the backslashes in a regex literal, producing an unterminated string. Both are the shell-escaping class already in memory as backticks-in-shell-args — the rule should read 'anything with escapes goes through a file', not just backticks. STILL OPEN: AC3-AC4 detection already shipped, but nothing here PROVES the fix works, because workers-og needs the Workers runtime. The scheduled route probe answers it after the next Pages deploy: if /og/social/card comes back non-zero and not byte-identical to /og-image.png, delete its KNOWN_EMPTY entry and this story closes. | 2026-08-15 THE FIX IS CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION, and the diagnosis was right. After the Pages deploy landed, /og/social/card?ratio=pin and /og/blog/<real slug> both went from 200-with-0-bytes to 200 with 133915 bytes — byte-for-byte /og-image.png, i.e. the BRANDED FALLBACK. That is the mechanism proving itself: the render was always throwing, ImageResponse's streaming just meant the throw landed after the Response had been returned, so the catch could not see it. Buffering moved it inside the try and the fallback now fires as designed. AC1/AC2/AC5 are done in the sense that matters to a customer — no share, pin or link preview is blank any more. AC1 IS NOT FULLY DONE and the story stays open: a branded card is a degradation, not a render. ROOT CAUSE: NOT FOUND, and four hypotheses are ELIMINATED rather than untested, which is worth more than a guess. (1) CSS gradients — all SIX templates use gradient(), including the working one. (2) Images or data URIs — grade-check embeds a QR as a data-URI SVG and renders fine. (3) A CSS property the failing templates use — diffed the property sets: NOTHING appears in both failing templates that is absent from the working one; the only difference runs the other way (the working one uses padding-left/right). (4) Character set — the failing default text is plain ASCII. THE STRONGEST REMAINING LEAD IS DIRECTORY DEPTH, and it is an observation rather than a theory: the ONE in-Function render that works, grade-check, is the only one at the TOP level of functions/og/. Every nested one either fails (social/card, blog/[slug]) or has never actually rendered (help/[slug], verified/[handle], which take their not-found branch because there is no such handle and help_articles is empty). workers-og loads a WASM binary, and how that resolves can differ with the module's path. Whoever picks this up should try moving one failing renderer to the top level, or proxying it from the edge the way functions/og/cert/[id].ts already does — that file's header records in-Function workers-og blowing the Free-plan Worker CPU limit, which is the other candidate this evidence cannot separate. The console.error now fires with the endpoint name on every failure, so the Cloudflare Pages log carries the actual exception — which is an OPERATOR read and the cheapest next step by far. | 2026-08-15 ROOT CAUSE FOUND: font-weight 700, which workers-og cannot resolve. Satori THROWS on an unloadable weight rather than falling back to the nearest one, and ImageResponse's streaming meant that throw landed after the Response had been returned — which is why it presented as a 200 with zero bytes rather than as an error. THE CORRELATION IS EXACT across all six templates in og-template.ts. Weights used: grade-result 500/600/800 — the ONE that renders in a Pages Function. social-card, blog, help and seller all 500/600/700/800 — the two confirmed failures plus the two that have never actually rendered (their requests take the not-found branch, which is why they looked healthy). cert uses 700 too and works, on the EDGE, a different runtime with its own font loading. Every observation fits and none contradicts. FIVE HYPOTHESES WERE ELIMINATED FIRST, each by evidence rather than by opinion: gradients (all six use one, including the working one); images (the working one embeds a data-URI QR); any CSS PROPERTY present in both failures and absent from the success (the diff runs the other way — only the WORKING one has properties the others lack); character set (the failing default text is plain ASCII); and module depth — a temporary top-level probe rendered the failing template from the working directory and still fell back, which killed my own leading theory. That probe has been deleted now it has answered. WHY THE PROPERTY DIFF MISSED IT: font-weight is a property BOTH sides use. The difference is a VALUE, and comparing property names cannot see a value. Worth remembering — the same blind spot would hide a bad colour, unit or keyword. FIX: the eight font-weight:700 declarations become 800. Both 800 and 600 are proven to raster in this runtime, and 800 is the closer reading of the intent (these are headlines). NOT VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION YET — that needs the Pages deploy, and the scheduled route probe answers it: if /og/social/card returns bytes that are neither 0 nor byte-identical to /og-image.png, this closes. If it still falls back, the weight theory joins the eliminated list and the Pages log exception (the OPERATOR criterion) becomes the next step. GUARD: a case in src/test/social-card.test.ts fails on any font-weight outside {500,600,800}, with the reasoning in the failure message, plus a second case asserting the rationale comment survives in the source — a bare allowlist of numbers gets 'fixed' by the next person who wants bold. Sabotage-verified by restoring one 700, which reddened naming the value. | 2026-08-15 A THIRD FAILING ENDPOINT, and a correction to what I said about it. I recorded /og/verified/<handle> as 'never rendered, takes the not-found branch'. That was true of the handle I used — 'nobody' — and false about the endpoint: /og/verified/pearson, a REAL handle from the sitemap, also serves the fallback. So it does reach its render and it does throw. Testing an endpoint with an input that cannot exist proves only that the not-found branch works, which is exactly how this one read as healthy. CONFIRMED VIA A HEADER RATHER THAN A SIZE: the response carries X-GT-Fallback: branded and Cache-Control max-age=300 (the fallback's own short TTL, not the card's 24h). That is the endpoint saying outright that its catch fired — much better evidence than 133915 bytes matching /og-image.png, and it also proves the US-2619 buffering fix is deployed and working. The probe now reads that header first and keeps the byte comparison only as a backstop for a response that serves those bytes without going through the helper. STILL AMBIGUOUS, and stated rather than glossed: the font-weight fix (b538148d) may or may not have reached Cloudflare Pages yet. Both 'not deployed' and 'deployed but the weight theory is wrong' produce exactly this fallback, and there is no marker in the response that distinguishes them. The monitor watching for a real render is what will settle it. Also added the third target to the probe and a case pinning that it uses a real handle: an assertion written as a bare substring initially matched the COMMENT explaining why the made-up handle is wrong, which would have made it permanently unsatisfiable. Anchored to the usage. | 2026-08-15 CORRECTION: THE FONT-WEIGHT THEORY IS WRONG. I called it the root cause in the previous note. It is not, and the change has been reverted. HOW I SETTLED IT, and this is the reusable part: the ambiguity was 'has the fix deployed, or is the theory wrong', and nothing in the OG response distinguishes those. The answer was sitting on the site all along — the SPA bundle is built with VITE_RELEASE_SHA=$CF_PAGES_COMMIT_SHA, so curl the homepage, read the /assets/index-*.js filename out of it, fetch that bundle and grep for a 40-char hex string. It returned 0c24892a3339994e8413a845b1574d10b436e517 — a commit AFTER the font fix. So the fix IS live and /og/social/card and /og/verified/pearson both still answer X-GT-Fallback: branded. Disproven, not merely unconfirmed. REVERTED PROPERLY rather than by a blanket 800->700: several 800s were always 800s, so the restore walks the pre-fix file's weight sequence positionally and refuses if the count differs. 8 sevens and 19 eights, exactly as before. THE GUARD IS REPLACED, NOT DELETED. A test that asserted 'weights must be 500/600/800' had no basis and would have blocked a legitimate 700. In its place, a case asserting the source still RECORDS the disproof — the correlation was real (of six templates, the only one rendering in a Pages Function was the only one without a 700) and it is exactly the kind of thing the next person rediscovers and re-implements. ELIMINATED SO FAR, six now: gradients, images/data-URIs, any CSS property present in both failures and absent from the success, character set, module depth, and font weight. Each on evidence. WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE DIFFERENTLY: I shipped the weight change and announced a root cause in the same breath, when the deploy-state check that disproved it was available before I wrote either. A correlation across six samples is a lead, not a finding. THE NEXT STEP IS NOT ANOTHER GUESS FROM OUT HERE. Every failure logs its exception with the endpoint named; the Cloudflare Pages log has the actual error, and that is the OPERATOR criterion.
